Mahayana Mahayana Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha Sutra of the Ten Chakras Teachings

Monk Tham's lecture

Translated by: Buu Quang Tu disciple Nhu Hoa

Justify: Duc Phong and Hue Trang

About the old monk Mong Tham

Old magician Mong Tham (1915-2017), nicknamed Luu Thuy Dinh, dharma name Giac Tinh, self-titled Mong Tham, meaning "neither enlightened nor awake". Because of a dream, he became a monk, so he called himself that. The monk was born in 1915 in Kaitong County, Heilongjiang Province, as the eldest child in the family. In 1928, the Master applied to become a railway police officer at the Changchun Railway Bureau. In 1930, the Master entered Phung Thien military school and became an officer in the Phung Thien brigade. When the leader of the Phung Thien warlord, Truong Tac Lam, lost the battle and had to withdraw his army to Beijing, the Master followed his army to Beijing. When assigned to patrol duty in Shijiazhuang later that year, while spending the night in an abandoned factory, Su dreamed of becoming a monk. Waking up, the Master went to ask to become a monk with the old monk Tu Lam at Tu Suat Pagoda, Thuong Phuong Mountain, Phong Son District, Beijing City. The monk shaved his head at the Duoc Vuong Temple in Di Hoa Vien post-mountain, and was given the Buddhist name Giac Tinh. Due to self-humility "not enlightened, not awake", and because of dreaming to become a monk, the Master took the title Mong Tham.

After becoming a monk, he dreamed of a monk telling him to go to Cuu Hoa mountain. Waking up, the Master suddenly discovered that the monk in his dream looked exactly like the portrait of Venerable Nhan Dung (Patriarch Lien Tri was also enlightened by him). Chinese Buddhism often considers Venerable Nhan Dung to be an incarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He came to Cuu Hoa Son, on the right occasion to open a stupa to worship the physical body of Kim Ksitigarbha (Mr. Kim Kieu Giac), so he especially believed and worshiped Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. While staying at Cuu Hoa, the Master dreamed that someone told him to go to Dung Tuyen Pagoda in Co Son. Therefore, the Master asked to enter Co Son Buddhist Academy to study the Avatamsaka Sutra with the old magician Tu Chau. Because his educational level was too low, the Master did not understand anything when he heard the lecture. He was about to leave Co Son, but in his dream he saw a monk teaching him to study the Samantabhadra Vows first to open up his wisdom. The monk obeyed, and sure enough, his wisdom increased. The monk again went to Zhanshan Temple in Qingdao to study Thien Thai Four Teachings and calligraphy with shaman Dam Hu.

In 1937, the Master obeyed his master's orders, went to Xiamen, and invited Dharma Master Hoang Nhat to Tram Son Pagoda. The Master worked as an attendant for Hoang Nhat for half a year, then requested the master Hoang Nhat to create a set of Wheel Forms in the exact manner as taught in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra. Master Hoang Nhat not only created the Luan Xiang, but also taught many of the essential meanings of that sutra, and also personally copied the Pure Hanh chapter of the Avatamsaka Sutra as a gift. This precious calligraphy was treasured at the Phap Nguyen Temple in Beijing, but was destroyed by the Red Guards during the Cultural Revolution.

In 1940, due to supporting the Anti-Japanese army, the Master was arrested, had to hide, and changed his clothes to become an attendant of a lama at Ung Hoa Palace. Wanting to understand more about Tantra, the Master went from Beijing to Shanghai, to Hong Kong, then took a boat to India via Tibet to seek dharma. In Tibet, the monk instructed Rinphoche Ha Ba of the Gelugpa sect at Sera temple to study the Bodhisattva Path and practice the Second Dharma with the dharma name of Can Khuoc Do Dang.

When the People's Republic of China was founded, Mao Zedong's government tried every way to destroy Tibetan Buddhism in particular, and Chinese Buddhism in general. Most monks were imprisoned or had their freedom of action restricted. Many temples were confiscated and turned into cooperatives or food warehouses. Monks were sent to the countryside to "work closely with the masses", essentially forced labor. In 1950, the Master was in Gandan district, Sichuan province. Due to his resolute refusal to return to secular life and not wanting to follow state officials into Tibet to carry out the work of assimilating the indigenous people to eliminate Tibetan culture, he was thrown into a "re-education" camp. In the camp, because the Master still insisted on not returning to the secular world and refusing to deny Buddhism, he was imprisoned in a criminal prison camp. In prison, the Master still propagated Buddhism, helping many people turn to Buddhism, so the Chinese Communist government charged him with being a counter-revolutionary and was imprisoned for fifteen years. Later, the Chinese government sentenced him to eighteen years of hard labor, meaning he was imprisoned for thirty-three years. Many times, the miserable, oppressive, and deadlocked circumstances made the Master frustrated, attempting suicide, and always dreaming of someone pushing him up to the stage to preach and asking him to preach the sutras. The monk knew that he still had the important responsibility of propagating Buddhism, so he tried to be patient. The monk often recites the verse "If the iron wheel is hot, at the top of the dharma, you will never be able to try suffering, and you will lose the Bodhi mind" (suppose the hot iron ring, rotating on the top of your head, will not lose the Bodhi mind because of that suffering) to encourage and persevere in difficult situations.

It was not until 1982, when the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party and the State Council (prime minister's office) of China decided to relax religious policies, that Mr. Mong Tham was released. Returning from Sichuan to Beijing, the Master was invited to teach at the Chinese Buddhist Academy, specializing in teaching the Four Parts of Law. In 1984, the Master was invited by the monks Dieu Tram and Vien Chuyet to Nam Putuo Pagoda in Xiamen to help restore the Min Nam Buddhist Academy, holding the position of Head of Teaching Department. In 1987, the monk was invited by Venerable Tuyen Hoa to the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to preside over the Water and Luc Dharma conference, creating a predestined opportunity to later propagate the Dharma overseas. In 1988, accepting the invitation of the American Bodhisattva Golden Heart Association, the Master and his attendant, shaman Hoang Giac, settled in New York and began teaching the Contemplation Sutra and Ksitigarbha dharma for five years in the United States.

From then on, the Master successively spread his staff to Canada, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. In 1995, while staying at Hoang Phap Pagoda in Vancouver, after discovering he had rectal cancer, the Master decided to give up his fate and single-mindedly recite the Buddha's rebirth. Accepting his disciples' earnest request for survival, the Master agreed to have surgery in 1996 at Changhua Hospital, Taipei. In 2004, accepting the invitation of the four monks of Pho Tho Pagoda, the Master began preaching the Avatamsaka Sutra from the second day of the second month and Mahayana sutras. In 2006, he accepted the invitation of the Phuong Quang Van Hoa organization to preach the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra at Pho Tho Pagoda. In 2007, the Master went to Thong Giao Tu and Cu Si Lam pagodas in Beijing to propagate the Dharma. In 2009, the Master participated in Dharma propagation activities organized by the Taipei International Conference, each lecture had several thousand listeners. At the end of that year, the Master returned to Ngu Dai Mountain and preached the Shurangama Sutra. In 2014, due to the request of his monastic disciples, the Master returned from Mong Tham Tinh Xa in Shenzhen (Guangdong) to rest at Chan Port Pagoda on Wutai Mountain. On November 27, the Master passed away at Chan Dung Pagoda, at the age of 103.

All his life, the Master always considered himself unworthy of being a monk, just a monk who wandered around, did not transmit the Dharma (did not establish a sect), and did not establish any ashram (even the Mong Tham Tinh Xa in Shenzhen was only built by his disciples and after many times of earnest request, the Master approved the naming). All his life, he only had the idea of ​​propagating the Dharma, trying to explain the profound meanings in the sutras so that everyone could understand. The Master's teachings were simple and simple. There are many people who admire the Master, have the heart to practice, or become monks. It was thanks to the Master's influence that the Pho Tho pagodas at Ngu Dai, Nang Nhan at Nhan Dang mountain, and Chan Port at Ngu Dai were all restored and flourished. Although he teaches many different dharmas, the dharma that the Master especially focuses on is the Ksitigarbha dharma, especially the Contemplation Sutra.

Mahayana Mahayana Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha Sutra of the Ten Chakras Teachings

* Mantra of the Ten Rings Sutra

Before starting to preach the Mahayana Sutra, Earth Store Ten Wheels, I chatted with everyone for a bit. When we study a set of sutras, we must study them thoroughly and understand how? After studying the sutras, you must practice, combine with your own body and mind, and also understand the dharma of cause and effect. The fate is complete, all things will come true. If the fate is not perfect, it will not be possible! My friends and I parted ways for half a year. During that half year, I went to many places, such as Taipei, Mainland China, and the United States; that's fate. The meaning of cause and effect is that whatever we do, there is definitely a “predecessor” (previous cause), depending on whether the condition is complete or not? If fate is not complete, it will not be possible to achieve it! No matter what, it cannot be achieved. But all causes and conditions are false, so it is said "the dharma of causes and conditions has no real substance". We will also talk about "emptiness of dependent origination". On this issue, this sutra teaches a lot.

Before we study the Mahayana Sutra, Earth Store Ten Wheels, everyone needs to develop their mind, what kind of mind? Develop a mind to repent! I hear a lot of people say: "Even though I don't understand anything else, I still don't understand myself?" I said: "Even though I have been a monk for more than sixty years, I still don't understand myself!" Surely everyone who hears this will feel very strange! I'm not the only one who doesn't understand myself, I'm afraid of you, except for the saints and Bodhisattvas, there are many people who don't understand themselves! Most people don't understand themselves! Do you know what you did in the past? Those who did not understand the cause in the past now have to suffer the consequences without even realizing it. Why do I have to suffer like this? Why did this accident happen to me? Surely every Dharma friend has an experience like this: Falling into an unjust situation, being wronged. That matter basically has nothing to do with me, and in the end it falls on me! You think "so unfair", that's because you don't know the cause in the past, don't understand yourself!

There are also people who chat with me, saying: "In this world, there are too many unfair things!" I said: "That is your view." They said: "Master! How do you feel?" I replied: "There is not even a single point of unfairness! It's very fair, especially fair." If I say these words, everyone probably won't be able to accept them! Everything you have to endure is because of what you did. You did it yourself, you suffered it yourself; How can that not be fair? Because we don't have wisdom and don't see many things clearly, we think things are too unfair. In the past, when you wronged others, did you understand? I said: "Now that you are being harmed by others, do you know that in the past, you also harmed others?"

Let's talk about a slightly bigger problem. The Japanese invaded China, killing many Chinese people. Currently, the Japanese are still living very well, the economy is very developed, while the Chinese are suffering so much. They asked me how I feel? I replied: “This is very fair!” They asked: “How can this be fair?” I replied: "The people who were killed at that time have all been forty or fifty years old. Currently, those people are reincarnated to live in Japan, going there to enjoy blessings, while the Japanese murderers are reborn in China. Everyone changes their position to look, and will accept it immediately!" If you look at it from the point of view of countless lifetimes of cause and effect, it will be extremely fair. I say these words, hoping that when studying the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, my Dharma friends will use such a repentant mind to study. This sutra has one chapter, the Repentance chapter, which hopes that we will repent of our past sins, to purify our sins. As long as you have wisdom, you will know. Everyone must prepare their thoughts in advance. You don't know what [yourself] did in the past! The Ten Rings Sutra teaches you: What things have you done in the past, and what tribulations must you endure now? Why were you born at this time? When Śākyamuni Buddha was in this world, you were not born, you were not born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, you were not born in Tusita Heaven, nor were you born in the world of the Eastern Medicine Master Lapis La Light Tathagata, but were born in the Saha world at this time. Why is that? Because you created that karma. Since we have that karma, we ourselves have to bear it. That's very fair, there's nothing unfair! Therefore, the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra is like a screen that lets us know our own crimes and mistakes, so there will be no more resentment in our hearts!

This time, when we were studying the Mahayana Sutra, Ksitigarbha Ksitigarbha, I had no faith [in myself], because I couldn't find the explanations of the ancients, I couldn't find reference documents, so it's very likely that I'll say many things wrong! The sutras we have taught before have all been taught many times by ancient people, and there are reference materials to look up. If you say something wrong, you can still push it a bit: "The Venerable Ones all say so, it has nothing to do with me!" But this sutra has never been mentioned by anyone else, so it is impossible to push it away!

First, I started talking about the one thousand Buddhas, making everyone realize what era we are in now. Among those one thousand Buddhas, now is the Dharma Ending era of Śākyamuni Buddha. In this age, we are very miserable. The cause that causes us to suffer is due to very heavy karma in the past. During the time of Śākyamuni Buddha, humanity's lifespan was especially short, only one hundred years. Compared to the era of the Seven Buddhas, [it will be seen] that our era is the best, because only Śākyamuni Buddha has such great vow power, He came to be born here. If Śākyamuni Buddha had not appeared in this era, we would not even know this principle. Therefore, once we are clearly aware of the suffering we are experiencing in this age, the mind will calm down. Until you learn, you won't know how to learn!

In addition, this sutra is quite long, the time we study will be a bit longer. Unlike the Diamond Sutra, the Amitabha Sutra, or the Heart Sutra, which can be learned very quickly, this cannot be the case! However, the number of chapters is not much, there are only eight chapters in total, including ten volumes. Everyone can open the first volume to see: The chapter on Non-Yanh Hanh and the chapter on Yes Y Hanh occupy five volumes. In addition to the previous Tu chapter and Hoach Ich Chuc Luy chapter, except for the Ten Wheels chapter, the number of volumes of the intermediate chapters is not many. Chapter Ten Wheels teaches: Use the Buddha's Ten Wheels to treat the ten wheel karma of ordinary people. Next is the Repentance chapter, the Good and Evil Karma chapter, and the Phuoc Dien General chapter. Although the number of volumes and chapters is not many, the principles in them are still very complicated.

In the Tu chapter, the Buddha praises the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva bows to the Buddha and praises the Buddha's merits. Therefore, in the Tu chapter, there is no great principle that can be said [in detail], but the general idea of ​​the Ten Wheels chapter is completely different! Use Buddha's Ten Chakras to counteract the Ten Chakras in our present!

We must have a method when studying this sutra; must be integrated into your daily life. This sutra teaches us how to live. In everyday life, don't create karma anymore, don't do wrong things anymore. Because after creating it, when you have to suffer it, you will not be able to bear it, you will be very miserable. If you can combine it with daily life to study, the sutras often say the Ten Wisdoms or Ten Powers of Buddha, you must compare, study Buddha's karma, use Buddha's karma to transform our karma into Buddha's karma. This means that every sentence, every action, when speaking, when the body acts, when the mind thinks, uses [Buddha karma] to compare. You must learn from everything in everyday life. After you have finished studying, you will compare with yourself to gradually make changes, the more you study, the more you will penetrate, you will not get bored, you will be able to enter very quickly!

If you don't learn like that, you won't be able to progress. Speaking in our everyday language, this sutra was translated by Master Xuanzang. Compared to the Ksitigarbha Sutra, or the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, the text of the translation is different. Because there are great virtues who use “translating meaning”, which means basing on our lifestyle, emotions, language, and all our habits to express [the meaning of the sutra]. Master Huyen Tsang believes that such an expression may lose the true nature of [the original sutra], perhaps it will be different from the original meaning spoken by the Buddha in India. Therefore, he translated according to the text, and also based on the meaning. Most of the texts [in this sutra] originally came from India, and at first glance are a bit strange. Famous generals often found in scriptures, such as Buddha and the World-Honored One, in this series will be called Bhagavat.

Just like when I first went to Tibet to study Dharma, not only [felt] the sentences in the scriptures were very difficult to study, but even the words were very strange, taking a very long time and not being able to correct them. For example, if we want to invite you to dinner or tea, we won't say "rice" or "tea", but "tea" or "rice". When you hear it, it feels very strange, and it's very awkward to say it. The vocabulary in this sutra has many places similar to that. Understanding how to use words, when we speak, will reverse and transform the meaning contained in them. When viewing this sutra, you should also view it the same way.

In the scriptures there are places “bilateral” (comparison, example). Saying “the other direction” means considering the meaning in Buddhism. I'm afraid you won't understand, so we use another meaning as an example, then we will understand. But once through the “bilateral” way, the meaning is eighty-four thousand miles away! For example, when talking about Emptiness, Buddhism often uses Emptiness to illustrate the Dharma Nature, the Self, and the True Form. We completely misunderstand it, saying "if it is Emptiness, then nothing exists"; Therefore, falling into Duan Kien. “Emptiness” in Buddhism is not empty like that! It is not separate from matter, because it displays matter, that's why it is said to be Empty! That Emptiness can be understood through concrete matter. Just like you say “person” is concrete, still exists, [but based on nature, according to harmonious causes and conditions, person] “is Emptiness”. The meaning in Buddhism is like that. It's not like saying "No" will mean nothing! Here, just giving examples, there are many similar cases.

Again, it is like saying that the Self chapter of the Ten Rings Sutra refers to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, because this sutra mainly takes Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as the main preacher of the Dharma. But in the sutra, Ksitigarbha came with joy, [before he arrived] there were Bodhisattva Sangha, Arhat Sangha, and ordinary Sangha. Everyone gathered to recite the Moon Tripitaka Sutra. When that sutra was finished, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva happily came, not at all to request a sutra (to ask the Buddha to teach a certain sutra), or to preach the Dharma. The Buddha immediately spoke of the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva because of that cause, and Ksitigarbha also praised the Buddha's merits. The causes and conditions of this sutra arise from that. Before preaching this sutra, the Buddha was preaching the Mahayana Sutra of the Moon Pitaka. The Lunar Store Sutra had just completed, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva arrived. When the Bodhisattva arrives, everyone who reads the scriptures will know immediately.

While collecting documents, Hong lay people collected sutras related to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva such as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows sutra, Mahayana Bodhisattva's Sutra, Ksitigarbha's Ten Rings, Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, Ksitigarbha Ten Kings Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Dalai Lama's Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Sadhana Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Sadhana Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra. Bodhisattva Store of the Three Kingdoms, Bodhisattva Repentance, and Dharma Repentance Contemplation. These collections all belong to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's dharma. You only need to communicate with one ministry, the other ministries are all related.

The Ksitigarbha Sutra and the Ten Chakra Sutra are similar, but the difference is that the method of transferring karma to sentient beings is slightly different. In the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, practicing Samigarbha and the Ksitigarbha Sutra, you only need to create an image, worship, and be able to recite the holy name Ksitigarbha, then you will be considered to have practiced. The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, I have not yet explained the part related to our practice, that is, the second half of the Sutra of Contemplation. The Ten Rings Sutra initially teaches you how to practice to attain Zen. If you do not enter Meditation, you will not attain enlightenment. Just starting out, the sutra teaches you a method from the shallow to the deep. After listening, it seems very simple, but using it will not be easy! It's still the six words Sequence, Dependence, Meditation, Contemplation, Transference, and Purity. If you start practicing, it won't be very easy. In general, we know that the methods taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva all have those methods and are included in those documents.

However, there is one thing in it: “Khula mountain is the Pure Land of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”; As for that expression, we don't quite think like that. Because at that time, the Buddha was preaching at Khu La mountain; When he was about to finish speaking, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva from the South arrived there. This shows that Mount Khu La is not His Pure Land. If it was His Pure Land, why would He need to go there from the South? Furthermore, the Contemplation Sutra and Ksitigarbha Sutra both point out that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came from the South. From which South? At that time, it was the South of Dao Loi heaven! “Undetermined direction” (There is no certain direction).

I think: Wherever there is hell, wherever there is an era without Buddha, wherever people are most miserable, there must be Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to save sentient beings. That is His wish. No matter where He goes, that place will be His Pure Land. When we see the word Pure Land, we think that place must be like the world of Ultimate Bliss, the world of Immobility, the world of Lapis lazuli, the world of Perfume Tich to be the Pure Land, but the Pure Land of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is "wherever there is hell, that place is the Pure Land, that place is the Pure Land for Him to save sentient beings". Are we required to explain like that? Here is a discussion, each person has their own method of practice. Sometimes the way to practice is to follow the Dharma of Contemplation and Repentance to bow to Contemplation and Repentance.

This is just the first step in practice, it's not just that we worship, it's practice! Of course, it is also considered practice, because first you have to eliminate karma. Once karma has been eliminated, only then can there be wisdom; Only with wisdom can one practice.

Currently, we are still unable to practice. Whenever we observe the breath going in and out, once we contemplate it, we scatter, how can we enter Concentration? But through repentance, karma disappears. Once karma is eliminated, wisdom will arise, making it easier to enter practice. Therefore, any basic practice method considers repentance as the first priority and must first eliminate karmic obstacles. Studying Tantra is the same! First of all, you must bow ten thousand times[1]. That way of bowing is not like our bowing, but a great bow! First of all, you must eliminate karma, these are all pre-means (means of preparation). If I keep bowing like this all my life, will I be able to achieve anything? It is definitely possible to achieve it, because your wisdom will increase! When you bow, you start to visualize: "The nature of the offering, the nature of the ceremony is not passed away" (The person making the offering, the one being offered the offering, have both the nature of not passing away). Regularly visualize like this, over time you will be able to enter. At that time, cultivating Concentration will enter very quickly!

But the methods of practice in each sutra, each treatise, and each Bodhisattva are also different. There were also Dharma friends who asked me like this: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came to this meeting, why are there so many people who do not know him, and still need to find someone to introduce him?" I said: "Not only Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is like that, even Śākyamuni Buddha, but there are also many people in his Buddha realm who do not know him!" Master Hoang Giac once joked: "There is no need to mention any other Buddhist country, even this country, as disciples of Śākyamuni Buddha, they only know how to recite Amitābha Buddha, not knowing that their teacher is Śākyamuni Buddha." There is nothing else, we can only say "no fate". There are also magicians who do not know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. I have also heard someone say: "I have never heard of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, have not studied Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teachings, and do not know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at all!" Likewise, at present, there are also many people who do not know Bodhisattva Manjushri. Why is that? It's because of Duyen as I just told everyone. Many lifetimes in the past have never had a relationship with a Bodhisattva, so naturally they will not understand His method.

Many people have the habit of commenting on teachings, any sutra that talks about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, whether it is Ksitigarbha Sutra or the Ten Rings Sutra, whenever it talks about hell and the human world, it doesn't seem to be Mahayana! Whenever we talk about Mahayana, we must know that it is very big. They think that it must be like the Mind Only method to be Mahayana, or like Mahamudra (Mahāmudrā) of Esoteric Buddhism “instantly become a Buddha”, thinking that this is Mahayana. They think that the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, and even the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra are Hinayana. As for [the title being] Mahayana Mahayana Sutra, which specifically indicates that this is Mahayana, there are those who only write Mahayana Mahayana Sutra, without the word Mahayana, even though the translation by the magician Xuanzang clearly states Mahayana!

This sutra was translated twice, once in the Sui Dynasty, and whoever translated it is unknown, because the name [translator] was missing in that translation. The second translation was translated by master Huyen Trang. Everyone saw Him noting the time, place, and conditions. Master Xuanzang translated this sutra during the reign of Vinh Huy[2] of the Tang Dynasty, that is, sixteen years after he returned from India to China, he translated this sutra.

In the sutra, in addition to praising the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also praises the Buddha in turn. The purpose of the Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva creating a feud with each other is mainly to eliminate our Ten Evils. The Contemplation Wheel section in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra also focuses on the Ten Evils. Ksitigarbha Sutra teaches: The reason you have to fall into hell is because of the Ten Evils. What are the Ten Evils? "Killing, stealing, and lust" arise in the body, "lying, embellishing, double-talking, and evil speech" arise in the mouth, and "greed, anger, and ignorance" arise in our mind. Those are ten karma. Karmas created in the body, karmas originating from the mouth, karmas arising from the mind, these are the ten karmas. Not creating those ten evil karmas, doing all the good things, that is the Ten Virtues. Speak beautiful words, do not speak evil words, do your best to promote harmony for everyone, do not destroy others, that is, do not commit the Double Damage. Speaking without ever uttering impure words, that is called "not speaking evilly". Always praise; In addition to praising the merits of others, try your best to say pleasant words and utter words that make others happy, this is the treatment of Evil Mouth. Don't say any words that are not virtuous. All day long, from morning to night, don't talk nonsense; No more talking about "I'm right, you're wrong" anymore. Not saying such words means "not saying lies". Do not say meaningless words, deceive people, deceive, and even less say false words, then your speech karma will be pure. Whenever the word Emptiness is added before the [Ten Evils], it becomes good karma. Without the word Emptiness, it is evil karma, also called Evil Wheel. In the mind, greed arises, anger arises, and wrong views arise. Ignorance is wrong view. Wrong view is not understanding clearly, being confused, the karmic cause of ignorance is caused by "greed, anger, ignorance". If in our mind there is no greed, anger, or ignorance, it is good karma. Not killing, stealing, or committing sexual misconduct is good karma.

Visualizing those ten good karma is the Virtuous Wheel. If you commit a crime, you will become an Evil Wheel. What effect does Luan have? Everyone knows: Luan means “to launch, to move continuously”. Luan means “transformation”, constantly rotating. Why do we reincarnate in the six paths forever without stopping, forever circulating? Because of karma. Karma makes it impossible for you to stop. If you create good karma, good karma will make you unable to stop. But the Ten Wheels also have ultimate and preliminary:

- Making good karma reach the Ten Wheels of Buddha is the Ten Wisdoms.

- Converting the evils of sentient beings into the Five Evils, the Ten Evils are the most evil Ten Evil Wheels. The Chapters of Non-Importance and Existence of Virtue also teach about the Ten Evil Wheels.

First of all, it is said to use Buddha's Ten Chakras to counteract the Ten Evil Chakras of sentient beings. Therefore, the name of this sutra is Ten Wheels. Why must Ksitigarbha Ten Wheels be added? At the end of this sutra, the one who is instructed to transmit and protect this sutra is Void Store Bodhisattva. In the chapter Praying for the Fall of Humans and Heavens of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it is also the Void Store Bodhisattva. Everyone knows what the Void Store Bodhisattva means? In the Avatamsaka Sutra, Void Store Bodhisattva denotes “tolerating all, embracing all”. The word Tang in the Void Tripitaka means “treasure”. Emptiness is not empty, but the image of Him attaining Emptiness, attaining the true mind, and attaining the ten characteristics of the Contemplation Sutra. “No” is not “nothing”. Emptiness includes all dharmas and is not empty. Instruct him to propagate this sutra, instruct him to propagate it.

Those ten wheels never stop, whether they are good or bad, when can they stop? Wait until your own mind calms down. Every Buddha has witnessed the cessation of the Ten Wheels and attained that nature. In order for us to achieve that goal, it is called Mahayana.

“Great” refers to our mind. Dai Phuong Quang Buddha Hoa Nghiem Sutra is also the word Dai. Mahayana Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra is also the word Great. The word Dai clearly states our mind, or our whole being. The Essence of all dharmas, the great general of the dharma is Dai. “Excess” means transportation. If you rely on those ten good karmas, they will be able to transport you to ultimate Nirvana. “Can pass away” is Buddhahood. The connotation of Emptiness in Sanskrit is Tranquility, or Tranquility, both intended to visualize Emptiness; But don't say No! Because Chinese does not have that word, we cannot translate it, so we use the word Mu instead. But using the word Mu, we misunderstand it as "nothing". As soon as they say Mu, there are many people who immediately fall into the View of Annihilation, because they think Mu is “nothing”! “No” is not “nothing”. That word Emptiness includes all Dependent Origination dharmas, their essence is Emptiness. That Emptiness includes all the dharmas of Dependent Origination, how to display that Emptiness? Use dependent origination to display that Emptiness. How to attain that Emptiness? “Dependent origination and complete destruction” is the realization of that Emptiness.

There are two ways to explain the word “Dai Tap”:

1) One is that in that dharma assembly, many sentient beings were gathered. How much? Countless! If you look at the scriptures, you will know: How many Thanh Van Sangha are there? Exceeded quantity! That means using numbers to calculate, it will be impossible to calculate! That's called “excess quantity”. How many Bodhisattva Sangha are there? Exceeded quantity! Whenever it comes to Ksitigarbha dharma, except for the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, the country has two places: One is in Dao Loi Thien, the other is between the seven ranges of Kim Son mountain, that is Khu La mountain, between the Desire Realm and the Form Realm, which ordinary people cannot reach. That is the land of victory. Only by gathering in that place can we tolerate it!

In Buddhist scriptures, when it comes to numbers, we do not use numbers in the human world to calculate, [that is, we do not] use one, two, three, four, five, six to calculate. How many briskets? How many thousands? How many million? We cannot calculate; Therefore, the Buddha used a simile, that is, he used the sand of the Ganges River as an example. “Ganges River sand” (sand of the Ganges River): The Ganges River is seven or eight thousand miles long, how much sand is in it? Human intelligence cannot be counted. So, for the numbers here, you should interpret them like that!

2) Another explanation: You may have heard that the Ten Karmas can transport you, reveal your mind, achieve your own Nature, achieve your own Vairocana, which means you can reach Greatness. Therefore, the great masses gathered in this Dharma conference are all predestined people. Now that we can study this sutra together, circulating it until now, we have fate. Without that fate, we wouldn't be able to meet!

For this issue, I also thought many times. At any time, I think: "If you say it is unconditioned, it seems like it is predestined. When you say it is predestined, it seems like many years have passed, and no one has ever had the heart to preach the Ten Rings Sutra". When I haven't yet developed that mind, I just honestly say: "This sutra, unless I have the opportunity to study it with everyone, I will only read it." Before, I had never read it. Although we have mentioned Ksitigarbha Three Sutras, I have never read the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra from beginning to end. On the contrary, shaman Hoang Giac had read and researched before me. The monk read it once, he held the sutra with a red cover, meaning he not only read it once, but also commented on the mantra.

Previously, I had no desire to preach this sutra. Now, because some Dharma friends have suggested: "Everyone study this sutra together." I don't have the slightest bit of faith; If you study this sutra, will anyone listen? They replied: "How could it be that no one listens? Because very few people know that this sutra exists!" Perhaps the fate is ripe. Currently, there are quite a few people coming to listen, there are still people listening, it's not like no one is listening! So, when we study, if anyone has any questions, please ask. We have to spend a long time to learn. If you have made up your mind to learn, you must study carefully. What is thorough study? We must use! No matter what you learn, you must apply it. Learning to write is because you have to use it. When you learn English, you also have to use it, use English to speak, that means we have to use it. So what is the point of learning the method taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Become a Buddha!

If you develop a slightly bigger mind, of course you won't fall into hell! Once you study the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, you will no longer fall into the three realms, will no longer fall into hell, will no longer fall into evil spirits, and will never fall into the animal world! Let's see if that has been achieved or not? Not yet! You must definitely become a Buddha. Being able to be born in heaven is the same, enjoying happiness is the same, but at a certain point, we will not be satisfied. Just like before, life and customs in Mainland China are in no way comparable to those in the United States, nor are they in any way comparable to Van Ca Hoa (Vancouver) of Canada, we often say life in those places is paradise. But having come here, having reached paradise, do you feel happy or not? Impossible! Because the requirements are more advanced! The result is that this place is not right, that place is not right, either way is not satisfactory. We have been born into heaven, are we satisfied or not? Even if you are born in heaven, you will not be satisfied, even though it is a happy realm. When you have a happy state, you have another request, the wish for immortality! How to achieve? If we talk about happiness, our minds swell. If you suffer, your brain will swell. In heaven, enjoy blessings and joy, your mind will swell! If you don't do anything and enjoy all the blessings, what should you do? Therefore, we must definitely follow the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra to study.

We vow to become Buddha. This method teaches us step by step how to become a Buddha. If we apply this method, we will achieve success. When you first studied the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, did you feel there were any problems? Please bring it up for discussion. We follow the half-study, half-study nature, we should not just listen, just using our ears to listen will not be enough! You need to use your mind, you must use your wisdom, and the six senses interact with each other to learn!

When studying, there will be obstacles. What's the obstacle? Your family has problems, or there is this cause or that cause, it's very difficult to say! First of all, you make a vow, hoping that "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless you, so that you can study completely, from beginning to end without missing a single session." Such good roots are also very difficult to have. Therefore, you must make that first vow. Next, make the second vow: “May I end the suffering in the present”. Wanting to minimize obstacles is not that easy! Falling ill will not happen, or right when you are about to go to the lecture, just out the door, a guest will come to visit. If you refuse that person and say you have to go listen to a lecture, you won't know how to treat him. If you entertain that person, you will miss a lesson tonight.

You see that problem at first glance is a small matter, but in general, it will not be small! If obstacles arise in my body, I cannot preach and must interrupt. Therefore, at present, whenever I have the opportunity to preach sutras and study a set of sutras with everyone, I will personally vow to recite those sutras, and also recite the holy name Ksitigarbha to pray for blessings. If you don't ask for blessings, you will be interrupted midway. One thing is interrupted, everything is interrupted. From the time I preached the Sutra until now, until now, the thing I regret most is that the time I preached the Avatamsaka Sutra at Nam Putuo Pagoda was not completed! I preached the chapter on Separation from the World and then left there. I still wish to return and explain the completion of that sutra, but I will never be able to complete it! You go back to the lecture, the people who heard the sutras at that time and the people who listen to the sutras now are not the same. They've already left, and no matter how I go back to lecture, I can't add to that lecture! How to do this? I can only repent, the other sutras have been preached from beginning to end. I hope to teach the Ten Wheels of menopause. Otherwise, in the future, when you die, you will be entangled and will be very miserable! Therefore: Let's all make a vow to study very well.

Everyone must learn to understand the sequence, don't learn half-heartedly. What is understanding? Can be used! When in use, there are no obstacles. When you practice visualization, there is nothing that causes obstacles. This sutra is not the same as the Ksitigarbha sutra used for reading and reciting. The Ksitigarbha Sutra encourages you to read and recite it, just like we read the Heart Sutra or the Diamond Sutra, which teaches us to read and recite. The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra tells you to practice! How much you can do is not certain! Now we begin to teach the scriptures.

I. Self - Pham DENt

(First element: Self)

(Sutra) As Thi Van: For a while, Bac Gia Pham at Khu La De Da mountain, MAu-ni's abode of immortality, the vast assembly of great Bodhisattvas, exceeds the number of great Shravaka Sangha. (Sutra: I heard this: At one time, Venerable Bac Gia Pham lived at Khu La De Da mountain, where the robes of the Immortal Munis and the great upsattvas gather, that is, the great Shravaka Sangha who cannot be counted. There are Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, that is, the great Bodhisattvas and Sangha who have finished speaking the Moon Store Sutra).

This is a passage of scripture. Due to the harmony of causes and conditions, at the time of contract and opportunity, the Buddha preached the Dharma, what kind of Dharma was that? The Menstrual Sutra. We do not study the Moon Tripitaka Sutra in the Tripitaka, so we do not mention it. At the time of that contract and agreement, the World-Honored One resided at Khu La De Da mountain (Kharādīya). That place is the place of those who practice Tinh Tinh. Mau Ni (Muni) translated [into Chinese] is Tinh Tinh. The immortals practice Tinh Tinh in that place, it is the place where they take refuge to practice. At that time, there were many Bhikkhu Sangha who received the Bhikkhu ordination, how many were there? “Over quantity” means that quantity cannot be used to calculate. Not thousands, tens of thousands, billions, millions! There are many more than those numbers, it is impossible to know the quantity! There are also Bodhisattvas, Ma Ha Tats, Bodhisattvas who are enlightened sentient beings. Those are sentient beings who have developed great minds, are all great Bodhisattvas, and have achieved achievements, whose number cannot be counted.

The incumbent in that sutra is the Moon Store Bodhisattva. When [Buddha] preached that sutra, I (Anan) myself heard it. “Like Thi” refers to this method. The Buddha said such dharmas, I personally heard them. This is called “the six achievements of self-confidence” (the title of the certification includes six achievements), that is, there are six things to prove in order to achieve this method, it is absolutely not false. “Thus” refers to this dharma, “self” is Ananda talking about himself. According to the Mahayana dharma, the sutras were compiled by Ananda. He said: "I heard it myself, it is not fake." When to listen?

“Momentary”: Every time the Buddha preached was a time of contract and agreement. Because the Buddha sometimes spoke in heaven, sometimes in the human world, sometimes in this location, sometimes in another location. Conditions of place and time are different. We can give examples to illustrate. Currently, it is half past eight here, the time in Taiwan will be different, the time on the Mainland will also be different. New York is three hours earlier, both are different times. “Time has no definite substance” (Time has no definite essence): It is an indeterminate dharma, not to mention the Buddha preached the Dharma throughout all worlds, both human and heavenly, everywhere, so where does time take as the standard? Therefore, it is estimated that it is “temporary”, that is, the time when causes and conditions are in harmony, the agreement is fulfilled, the opportunity is fulfilled. That is the Time of Achievement.

“Van Thanh Tuu”: Who said? Bodhisattva Pham, that is, the World-Honored One, was also said by the Buddha. This is called Master of Accomplishment. Where to say? Kharādīya Mountain. The location of Khu La De Da mountain is one of the seven Golden Mountains, very close to Mount Tu Di. Surrounding Mount Meru is a layer of Kim Son, a layer of fragrant water sea, [there are seven layers like that]. “Kim SGrateful” is said in Buddhist scriptures to be equal to iron, because iron is a metal, not necessarily gold, so it is said to be Kim Son. “Hai” is the fragrant sea of ​​water surrounding Mount Tu Di. If we speak according to the Chinese pronunciation, it is called La Lan Son. Because there is no human fire or smoke, only immortals with supernatural powers and pure virtues can go there to practice. That is the residence where the Muni immortals reside.

Buddha preached the Sutta Pitaka there. Are there any members of the public attending the dharma conference? They are the Sravakas and Bodhisattvas. There are no ordinary monks there either, because ordinary monks cannot come. Without supernatural powers, it will be impossible to get there. Therefore, only two groups of Shravakas and Bodhisattvas listen to the Dharma. We can rely on the two words Dai Tap to explain. If it is a Great Practice, the congregation of Shravakas and Bodhisattvas who will attend will be extremely large. Shravakas study Bodhisattvas, that is our way of looking and thinking, which also means that Shravakas who listen to the Dharma will enter the Mahayana and become great Bodhisattvas. Therefore, the sutra is called Mahayana Mahayana.

When that sutra is complete and the dharma assembly has not yet been dissolved, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will come to rejoice. He knew that the cause for propagating the dharma in the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra of Śākyamuni Buddha was ripe, so he came there at that time. If sentient beings like to kill living beings, even if there are those who love wrong views, because of the light shining on them, they will all love to stay away from wrong views but all achieved. Thanks to the light, all sentient beings in the Buddha realms are suffering all kinds of suffering, no one can rest or stop, all are happy and enjoy mysterious joy

Seeing again in such Buddha realms, touched by this light, all dark clouds, mist, dust, fierce winds, raging rains, unwholesome sounds, and all rotten, filthy things, bitter evil tastes, evil touches, fear, far away from all evil karma, evil speech, evil intentions, evil tendencies. It's not cold, it's not hot, it's quiet, it's calm, the ground is as flat as the palm of your hand, all kinds of things that create mysterious joy are filled there.

“Mass of monks” are the Shravaka Sangha, the Bodhisattva Sangha, and also the newly arrived monks. When Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva arrived, there were also people who followed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva from other worlds. The great assembly had not yet dispersed in that Dharma assembly when they all saw those clouds pouring down treasures. At the same time, I also saw and heard the Dharma sounds from those precious clothes and decorations. No matter what color or treasure you like, you will see precious ornaments falling from the sky and automatically wearing them on your body. Therefore, the sutra says:

“The heron is like the Dharma of sounds, mocking at will” (Also listen to sounds like that, depending on what you like): Depending on what you like, you will see your body adorned with all kinds of incense, flowers, precious jewelry, and clothes. The clothes offered to you are all suitable sizes, large, small, long, and short, and the tailoring is even more precise than a tailor! Depending on your wishes, one is due to the Bodhisattva's vow power, the other is due to your mental power.

Not only that, at the same time, everyone can see in both hands holding the Nhu Y Jewel Pearl, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva holds the Nhu Y Jewel Pearl in his hand. The effect of the Nhu Y Treasure Pearl is that whatever you think of in your mind, the jewel will immediately appear, satisfying all your needs. That is, for each person attending the Dharma conference, not only will the body's needs be satisfied, but all the desires in the mind will be satisfied. As for clothes, hundreds of flowers, and ornaments, some people like red, some people like blue, none of them are exactly the same, naturally worn on your body, solemn and perfect.

But there is one thing that is equal, that is, everyone holds the Nhu Y Bao Chau in their hands. We see a statue of Ksitigarbha, holding a staff in one hand and a Nhu Y Pearl in the other; He gave alms to Nhu Y Bao Chau. In the hand of every gathering attending the gathering is a Nhu Y Pearl. Not only does it exist, but countless treasures are born from Nhu Y Chau. That pearl emitted light. Not only can treasure be poured out, but it can also shine. How big is the light radiating from those pearls? Bigger than the light of a lamp, even brighter than the light of the sun, because the light of a torch or the sun cannot reach other Buddha realms. Their light is completely different.

“Canga sa” means sand of the Ganges River. There are countless Buddha worlds, each grain of sand is a Buddha world. That is, the light radiating from Nhu Y Chau illuminates the worlds that much. Every world has Buddha preaching the Dharma. Then each light shines through all the Buddha lands as much as the sands of the Ganges River. Every grain of sand is a Buddha world. Every world has a Buddha, manifesting in light. At the same time, in that assembly there is no discriminating mind, nor is there any distinction between which Buddha this is and what the name of that Buddha is? At that time, they had no discriminating mind.

“Human light is clear” (Because of the light), all the Buddha realms are illuminated, and each Buddha is seen to have countless Bodhisattvas and countless masses surrounding that place. Countless Buddhas are preaching there. As soon as I saw this, all karma was eliminated. If karma is not eliminated, you will not see it! Because of that light, we can see all sentient beings in the Buddha realms. Not only can we see the Buddhas preaching the Dharma, but we can also see all sentient beings in their lands. Because wherever Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's light shines, those who are sick are immediately cured and all diseases are eliminated. Or the person who is about to be killed, just as he is about to go to the execution ground, will also be liberated and will not be killed. Or being imprisoned in prison, will be released. Why?

“Light shines” (Due to light shine), that is, because the Ruyi Pearl of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the hands of sentient beings radiates light. The light from [the pearls in hand] all the masses shine together, so they are all liberated. However, we can only see the Body of the luminous realm.

Speaking of the light in our nature, due to the karma of each of us, even though it is still not pure, relying on the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, along with the blessings of the Buddha in the Dharma Assembly, we will immediately have the appearance of that realm. Is there freedom or not? Yes! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva comes here, illuminating the entire earth. [In the next passage, it will be said that the Earth Element in the body of the masses is heavier and more solid], do you want to lift your arms? It cannot be lifted up, because [the light has] fully illuminated all Earth Elements. That is just a momentary phenomenon, that is the power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Called Self-Quality means Self-Theory (explanation for introduction). Self-explanation will not be able to explain deeply. If everything has been explained in the Self chapter, the following texts do not need to be said anymore. If the Tu chapter is extremely long, it means incorporating the sutras from the next part of the lecture into the Tu chapter to preach. Because everyone learns together, it is difficult to teach in order. But we made a few mistakes, because of intentional violations!

[Why do you say that?] I myself study [Thien Thai] the Four Teachings, which means using the Four Teachings to classify and judge teachings. That is, regarding the Tang, Thong, Biet, and Vien, determine which sect this sutra should belong to. First of all, you must like the name (explain the name of the sutra). After explaining the name of the sutra, we still have to explain its meaning (that is, talking about the Form). After explaining the meaning, talk about the Beast Sect. After explaining the Tong Beast, we still have to clearly state the purpose (ie the Power of Use part). It is necessary to follow that rule. That is the rule established by the great monks in Chinese Buddhism, called the Five Mysterious Meanings (five levels of mysterious meaning). If we had to explain those five levels one by one, it would take ten days to explain all five levels of profound meaning.

But I initially studied Five Teachings; If you preach according to the Five Teachings, in addition to Tieu, Thi, Chung, Don, and Vien, you must also preach the Ten Mysterious Mons. Before explaining it in the scriptures, we must definitely explain the Ten Mysterious Gates. Teaching the Ten Mysterious Mons, I'm afraid that explaining the mystical part will take half a month or a month. Currently, we only preach for an hour and a half each day, why do we have to do that? Because when the great monks of ancient times preached the Sutra, for example, I wanted to preach the Lotus Sutra, the people who came to attend were all to study the Lotus Sutra, study the Lotus Sutra, and the people who came to listen also came because they heard the Huyen Nghia, and came because they heard the teachings. After learning these things, they will leave without listening to the lecture on the scriptures. Here, everyone is a beginner. If I start with Huyen Dam, I'm afraid everyone will float, like a car flying into the sky, making everyone unable to understand and not knowing where to fly!

Now we rely on the scriptures to explain the meaning, but this is the wrong way! If you preach the sutras, “revealing the meaning based on the text” means relying on the text to explain the meaning. If you don't say it according to the text, but say it with other meanings, "The three worlds of Buddha are unjust!" That is the unjust confrontation of the three worlds of Buddha, impossible! “Leaving the sutra with one word” (Leaving the sutra with one word), if the magician leaves the sutra and blindly speaks nonsense, it is impossible for him not to fall into hell, “that is, the same demonic theory” (it is just like a ghost speaking). That's not what Buddha said, it's what a ghost said. Everyone, think about it, what should a magician do? To leave the sutra, to leave one word, is to make a mistake. If you don't leave the written word, if you only rely on the written word to speak, you will be unjustly confronting Buddha. That's one thing!

Corresponds to the basis for preaching the Dharma, depending on [the nature of] the listener to teach. Today, I am destined to be with everyone, but my wisdom is just that, giving everyone a little bit of understanding like that. More than that, I don't have the mental capacity either. If you say it wrongly, you will only fall into hell. I can't help but fall into hell, there's no way! For a long time now, no matter what I preach or conduct, I always think like this: "Prepare to go to hell at any moment." Is it possible to escape? We have to see if Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has blessings or not? If Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses me, I will definitely not fall into hell for the time being; or fall into hell, I will repent first and then do it. Wait until I finish, then I repent. That's the only way! Otherwise, the sutra will be interrupted. If no one preaches, the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra will become extinct. It's really almost extinct! In the Tripitaka, there are many sutras that are extremely wonderful and very good for us, but no one talks about them! If no one says anything, it's like breaking up! Only in the Tripitaka, it's like being left out there! There are also many temples and shrines that do not let people see or touch the Tripitaka. They say that touching the Tripitaka is a crime. They think that the Tripitaka should be worshiped! Each side has its own arguments. To me, the sutras spoken by the Buddha are intended to teach us to learn. Viewing is not allowed, what is the point of piling it there? Over time, everything deteriorates. It's all ruined and everyone doesn't know!

When we learn, we must authenticate our learning. When studying the main text, you must really understand the logic, not go against paradoxes. In addition, we must enter the world, which means it must be integrated with daily life, which means we must be able to use what we have learned, and after learning it, we can use it immediately! Currently there are afflictions, after studying the Ten Rings Sutra, afflictions disappear, meaning it can be used! It's very painful, your mind can't think clearly. If you take the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, read it, listen to it, study it, you'll also understand it clearly. Being able to use it like that would be great!

In the previous part, I had a conversation with you, now we officially preach the sutra, not repeating it, but saying it from the beginning. This sutra is called the Mahayana Mahayana Collection of Ksitigarbha Ten Wheels.

“Mahayana”: Buddhism is divided into three vehicles, i.e. great, middle, and small, because the Buddha preached “to the basis”, that is, in accordance with the listener's ability. To the Mahayana Bodhisattva, or to those who have developed a great mind, he spoke the Dharma with a very profound meaning. For middle and lower abilities, depending on their preference or need, [the appropriate dharmas] will be mentioned, so that we can gradually introduce them to the dharmas of the Middle and Hinayana. The meaning of the great and small dharma, I have explained in the previous section. The word Great is explained very simply, it is a normal thought in our present time. Whenever we talk about Dai, ultimately we want to clearly point out your mind, understand that your mind is completely complete.

Dharma has no greatness, but also no smallness. Some people, because they endure suffering and know suffering, hope that all sentient beings can leave suffering. That's Dai. Even though the Buddha spoke about the dharma nature and the physical body, for those who only think of themselves and do not think of others, the great dharma also turns into a small dharma! The Dharma is neither great nor small, just establish it according to your mind! The Dharma itself refers to the Essence. Because living beings have all kinds of natures, Buddha [preaching the Dharma] also has all kinds of natures. Dharma is a method, a path, a rule, it depends on how you understand it. Therefore, there is no need for dispute between Mahayana, Hinayana, Hierarchy, Tantra, Four Teachings, and Five Teachings. Any dispute will become an argument. Therefore, first of all we must clearly understand the two words Mahayana.

“Great Practice”: A very large crowd attended this dharma conference. “Volume” means many. Gathering in one place for what? To explain the Mahayana propaganda.

“Ksitigarbha”: Ksitigarbha is the mind of each person, the mind, and how to use that mind? “Earth” is a representation of our mind, because the great earth contains everything. Everything we need comes from the earth. Whether gasoline, coal, or thermal energy, it all comes from the soil. Dia means “concealed” (contains), and also has the meaning “birth”. Everything we eat or use comes from the earth. “Tang” is hidden, it also “contains a lot of meaning”, but we do not know. Why don't you know? Because we are deluded, it also means that our mind is deluded. These two words can both be explained as our mind. Because of our mind, body, speech, and mind karma are born; From body, speech, and mind karma, three things in the body, four things in the mouth, and three things in the mind, in turn, are born, forming ten karma. Those ten karmas are eternal and endless, like a spinning wheel, never stopping, forever rotating. At the same time, the wheel has the function of crushing, which can help us crush Obstacles, Karma, and Suffering, giving birth to pure Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom.

According to us Buddhist disciples, if we take refuge in the Three Jewels and study Buddhism, we will turn the wheel upside down. [Currently], not only is it impossible to move in the right direction to eliminate the three karmas, but on the contrary, it also increases the three karmas a lot, why? Because we already have a lot of suffering, we should believe in Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to eliminate suffering, but they are not like that. In Buddhism, they create discrimination, destroy harmony with the Sangha, and even create karma, defame the Dharma, and destroy Buddha. They think they are praising Buddha, but actually they are sabotaging Buddha. This sutra specializes in that phenomenon.

Therefore, in this sutra, for Bhikkhus who break the precepts, as long as they still wear their kasa, they create their own karma, you do not need to care about them. As long as they show the appearance of the Three Jewels, you must still respect them. Respecting them will be your blessing. If you destroy it, it means committing a crime. No matter how corrupt they are, it's not up to you. Therefore, the Buddha did not approve of kings and ministers using the law to punish bhikshus and bhikshunis. I give this example to make it clear: The Ten Chakras is using the Ten Chakras of Buddha to treat our Ten Chakras.

“Sutra” means “throughout”, like we string flowers together. In India, they use thread to string flowers [into garlands]. Because the meanings preached in the sutras are meant to speak to this sentient being, or to correspond to other sentient beings, spoken first, spoken later, explanatory, secret, all are gathered in one place, causing the meanings in the sutra to be gathered. That is the title of the sutra.

Pham Tu is the introductory part to initiate this sutra. In the Self chapter, one is to praise the merits of the Buddha, and the other is that the Buddha is praising the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Why did the Buddha praise Ksitigarbha's merits? In [when teaching] the Ksitigarbha Sutra, we also said it. In [when teaching] the Contemplation Sutra, it was also said: It is to make those who do not understand the practice on the human ground of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and those whose faith and reverence are not yet complete, thanks to the Buddha's praise, will give rise to liking: "This great Bodhisattva is so wonderful, I must be close to Him, to hear His name, worship His statue, I will achieve many good things." Then if you come to study, you will be able to enter very quickly. The mind of living beings is like that. If you hear someone else say that person is very good, and you haven't met that person yet, you already trust that person with all your heart. Suppose we meet, it feels even better. But there are people who are liars, their names are not worthy of their truth, hearing their voices is not as good as meeting them face to face. Meeting in person seems to be better than hearing. Some people we meet, [realize that that person] is not as famous as they are. When you meet that person, you will truly despise him, and you will understand even more clearly, knowing that he or she is bad and an impostor. Bodhisattva is different! For all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas mentioned in the sutras, you study and meet, immeasurable reverence will arise.

Some Dharma friends asked me: "People like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva or Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), aren't everyone who hears about them and has a heart of reverence? Why do we still need to introduce them?" The Buddha addressed the assembly and introduced this Dharma assembly. Let us consider this issue from the realm of thought. In this world, among the fifty or sixty billion people, there are too many people who do not know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Because they are not close to the Three Jewels, they do not know. There are people who have been close to the Three Jewels, there are even people who have been monks for many years, there are still people who do not know the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, much less need to mention the Ksitigarbha Sutras, the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, and the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutras. I know this myself, I'm not talking nonsense. There are people who have taught the sutras for many years, but still do not know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, have never studied it, have never been close to it, and have never seen it. Therefore, an introduction is necessary!

Even in that dharma conference, there were many people who did not see or know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Therefore, you see in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, even Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Void Store Bodhisattva, Universal Bodhisattva, all turned to the Buddha to ask questions so that the Buddha would teach about the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Think about it: Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has such great divine power and supernatural powers, does he not even know Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Each teacher teaches a different direction, each Buddha's fate is different. Although it is said “Buddha and Buddha's path is the same”, each Buddha preaches a different Dharma, each Buddha world is different. Therefore, it is necessary to introduce a little, the meaning of the title Tu is like that.

In this assembly, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva uses his supernatural powers and vows to bring joy. He knew he had a predestined relationship with this Dharma conference, so he came to rejoice and praise. In the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the Buddha emitted wonderful light. Quang symbolizes sound, light and sound are similar. In the previous section, we roughly explained thirty-nine types of sounds. Every type of object that is thrown down, such as falling clothes, or especially splendid jewels falling, is preaching the Dharma. It contains sound, all movements have sound, but we cannot hear it.

Why? Because we have not yet attained full understanding of the Ear Organ. Therefore, He needed to use this method to express. The sound of preaching [has appeared] even though the person has not yet arrived, meaning Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has not yet appeared, the sound has come first. In addition, the fallen things that He evokes, such as treasures and clothes, are all things in life, things that everyone needs to use, and everyone feels they automatically wear them.

Why is that scene? This is due to the vow power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, which is the cause of practicing for countless eons to bring about the results. He had just moved and had not yet arrived at that place. As long as living beings have a relationship with Him, He will come there. This is praising the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva [based on] the hopes and desires related to the masses. The things said in this sutra are related to daily life, as said in the above section: We always have needs. Do you need wealth or not? Even though we don't have that need right now, we are still in darkness, ignorance, and ignorance. Ignorance is ignorance.

We have a lot of wrong views, that is, incorrect views, looking at any problem incorrectly. Because you don't look at the problem correctly, you easily make mistakes. Business capital is in the hope of making a fortune, but due to not looking at it correctly, the investment results in a loss of capital. I originally wanted to go for entertainment, but when I got there I fell ill, because the climate was not suitable for you. If you want to travel, there will be problems with the plane, and all kinds of persecution. That is because of darkness and ignorance. If you keep doing things that shouldn't be done, you will be in danger. If you had wisdom, you wouldn't go. If you are illuminated by the light of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will have wisdom. Once you have wisdom, you will clearly understand: What should not be done, you will not do; Where you shouldn't go, you won't go; What should not be said, you will not say, regarding the things we ourselves will do like that!

But regarding all kinds of merits, even the sounds of preaching here, some friends ask: "Why can't I find one thing?" Because there is no such fate! Now we are teaching this sutra, explaining the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, that is, you are destined to meet. In the future, you recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, worship the Ksitigarbha statue, or study the Ten Rings Ksitigarbha Sutra, including the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva [Original Vows of Merit], all of which are related to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. After you have meditated many times, you will gradually be able to achieve it. At that time, in that Dharma assembly of the Buddha, the people in that Dharma assembly all achieved it. Now we will also achieve; In the future, when we meet this fate, we will also be blessed.

Here, there are two types [of blessings]: One is what we see clearly, or in our mind we feel it. The other type is that you can't see or feel. There are phenomena that are blessed by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or by reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra, you will feel that your own affairs are a little better than before. That is called “minh gia” (hidden blessing). “Ming family” means it does not appear, but sometimes it actually dreams, and there are also people who dream of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva coming to initiate initiation. After drinking the water of empowerment, a person who was originally very stupid will turn into a very strong memory and restore his memory. Some children are inherently stupid, or born unable to hear or see, and have a dull mind. Because he recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, [or because] his parents prayed for him and recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, he recovered. It is true that such things exist, I know many cases. These are the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, but these are all small causes. Our greatest hope is to become Buddha. Because of this, there are people who can clear their minds and see their nature. As soon as they saw it, they immediately opened their minds and understood it, all karma was gone. This is because each person's nature is different.

When listening to the Dharma, the great assembly was together in the Dharma Assembly at that time, some people attained Shravaka fruition, some people developed Bodhicitta, but there were also people who had not yet achieved the benefits, and there were also people who created seeds for the future. When Śākyamuni Buddha preached in India, maybe we will be there too! Even though you hear it, you don't get any benefit, it's still stuck in circulation, that's called "far from death". If the Buddha preached the Dharma and could save everyone, then the Buddha would not need to instruct Maitreya Bodhisattva to save sentient beings! You see: After speaking each sutra, the Buddha had to entrust a Bodhisattva: "You must skillfully propagate this sutra, so that sentient beings who have not yet attained salvation will be saved, and those who have been saved will be increased, making them all become Buddhas." Every sutra is like that. We need to think like this: As long as we hear, just as long as we hear, the seeds have been sown, forever incorruptible. The Buddha will bless us at any time, causing us to gain benefits.

In the Tu chapter, the Buddha preached about the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Every career, every merit that He did, was accomplished by Him. Just like today, everyone has the heart to practice, practice in different ways or methods, and follow a certain way to practice, the forms are different, the effects are also different. Using a very sincere, passionate mind, using a very sincere heart, will achieve both quick and great results. If your mind just listens casually, like going to school, you will only achieve far-reaching people, in the future you will not be like other people, and will gradually mature in a certain life, so you can meet again and grow again. It takes many lifetimes to ripen and grow. Even within an individual's lifetime, after you listen to the Dharma, you will gradually grow and change. However, you should not give birth to wrong views. If wrong views arise, the previous merits will be like pressing the Cancel button on a computer, immediately eliminated, no more! If you give birth to wrong views, you will not achieve anything. The most notable thing here is wrong view. You must definitely stay away from all evil karma and evil speech.

I specifically explain to everyone a little about evil karma, especially the karma of killing. Of course, we Buddhist disciples don't open brothels, but I'm afraid we still can open Karaoke, it just depends on how you do it! You work as a butcher, specializing in killing living beings, that is called evil karma. Wrong speech is even worse, saying inaccurate words, saying words that go against one's own conscience. Why? For the sake of a small profit in front of me, I also know that it is not right, I also know that I cannot say that, but in order to protect my own interests, I must promote it, I must do so. There are so many stories like that, I'm afraid everyone has said those words!

Evil intentions are even more miserable! Evil intentions lie right in our hearts. For unrighteous thoughts that arise, you must always contemplate and not lose mindfulness. Finally, we must stay away from all wrong karma, wrong speech, and wrong views. Because you can choose your career, you can control your speech and shape your thoughts. If you yourself do well and take refuge in the Three Jewels, you will no longer need to look for the East or the West to find the means! Some people learn Qigong to keep their bodies healthy. However, no matter how you preserve it, you cannot preserve it, because that is not right action. I see people who have been hit by a car or died in an accident, and I don't see that their bodies [before the accident] were not good. You cannot control this. You must believe in the Three Jewels. If you want to exercise, you can bow more. If you can't bow in the normal way, then bow with your whole body to the ground. After bowing less than twenty or thirty times, my whole body was drenched in sweat. That is also movement, that is also right action.

However, I see that many people, after listening, do not feel very comfortable. They think that taking care of the body is not a bad thing. [Ask yourself] why do we need to maintain our body? What is the meaning of the body's existence? They do not research and instead arrogantly pursue the five desires. All day long, from morning to night, he went to bars and got drunk. I hope my body will take good care of me, but I end up doing drugs. I hope my body will take good care of me and have sex with men and women promiscuously. How do we maintain this body, for what purpose? Maintain it to create karma! That's called evil karma.

Wrong speech is caused by incorrect main thoughts. The greatest relationship of wrong views is that it directs your body and speech. After speaking indiscriminately, one often brings great harm. We often say: In every thought, we recite the Three Jewels. The Three Jewels are your refuge. If you leave that place of refuge and wish to take refuge elsewhere, it will be a wrong refuge. Taking refuge in the Three Jewels, you will attain eternal purity until you become Buddha. If you take the Three Refuges and can keep them firmly, you will not fall into the three realms and will forever belong to humanity. Even if you practice for a lifetime without success, if you practice slowly, you can still attain enlightenment. If you originally believed in the correct teaching, you would have taken refuge in [the Three Jewels], but you feel that this is too slow. When you hear others say there is a method to immediately have magical powers, you abandon the Three Jewels and leave the Three Jewels. I hear about this situation a lot, it is also everyone's karma!

I just arrived in New York, and there were lay people who came to take refuge with me. After that, they took refuge in Thanh Hai again. After that, he felt that Thanh Hai was not fast enough and wanted to find another faster method. Ultimately, it leads to demons. That demonic symptom has appeared, there is no way to cure it! If you want to save it, you can't save it. Once destroyed, it is very difficult to save. Having broken the precepts, one can still repent. If one breaks the view, it will not be one or two lifetimes, but countless lifetimes. If one day you fall into wrong wisdom and wrong views, it will be very difficult to recover! Suppose that person has great good roots and meets Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He radiates light to illuminate that person, that person will let go of wrong views, let go of evil karma, but are there many causes and conditions like that? Very little! Is there anyone who has been illuminated by the light of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? I don't think there is yet. I think everyone will definitely benefit, but this depends on each person's fate!

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, they naturally gather together, the earthly realm strengthens, and is difficult to resolve. When he signed the letter, he was startled and skeptical: "Ha people, rivers of fate, are you showing signs?" In the gathering of the assembly, the right celestial De Thich, the name of Uncapped Sanh, past the Silver Age Brahma non-retirement seat, immediately rose on the throne, bowed to the World-Honored One, joined his palms towards the Buddha, and recited the question and wrote:
(Sutra: At that time, the assembly suddenly saw the earth element in their bodies increasing strongly, solidly, and heavy. It was difficult to move.
