(Sutra: Throughout the sentient world, always abiding in great compassion, although attaining wonderful Bodhi, never leave give up one's vow).

This is praising the Buddha in the sentient world, often giving rise to great compassion. Seeing the suffering of sentient beings, although the Buddha attained supreme Bodhi, his original vow was to benefit sentient beings, not letting go of his inherent vow power. Therefore, I still come to this world to save sentient beings. If we speak according to reason, Buddha saves all sentient beings, but there are no sentient beings that can be saved. Now we first talk about Facts, not according to Principles, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva praises Buddha, starting with things that we living beings can comprehend. Why are we born into this world? The reason we are born into this world is because of the Ten Wheels.

The Ten Wheels are the wheel of suffering. To cut off that wheel of suffering is to cultivate the Buddha's wheel of wisdom. Use the wheel of wisdom to counteract the wheel of suffering, two opposing sides. When Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva praised the Buddha, he gave a very simplified noun. Why didn't He say [in detail]? He knows that all dharmas are empty and false, but sentient beings do not know. For sentient beings, that is real suffering.

(Sutra) Depending on sentient beings, urgent in their suffering, depending on arising requires diligence, courage and gentleness.
(Sutra: Whenever you see sentient beings, oppressed by suffering, immediately strive diligently, to be strong help).

He saw all sentient beings suffering and suffering, exactly in the midst of suffering. That's why the Buddha was brave and diligent in saving those suffering sentient beings. Therefore, He immediately set an example for them, hoping that they would diligently practice almsgiving, maintain precepts, be patient, be diligent, practice Concentration, and seek Prajna wisdom.

(Sutra) The spirit needs to practice Thien, Precepts, Forbearance, Diligence, Concentration, and Prajna child's mind and nurture.
(Sutra: Encouraging the diligent practice of Love, Precepts, Forbearance, Patience, Concentration, Prajna, like a mother just one child, raised with kindness).

“Like a mother, one child, nurturing from the heart”: Like a mother giving birth to only one child. All of a mother's body and mind are for that child, loving, protecting, and raising that child. That is mother's love. As for today, there is a mother who kills both her children and throws them into the sea; that is a special phenomenon. In today's society, karma is too heavy, so that phenomenon arises. That is especially heavy karma! In general, a mother's love for her child is 100% genuine and passionate. For current people, it has to be reduced a bit.

Some people point out cases where mothers kill their children a lot, but children kill their parents even more. This shows that the five impurities of evil life and karma have reached their peak and severity. Therefore, the Buddha was diligent, diligent, honest, and earnestly wished to become a Buddha, because he wished to save sentient beings.

(Sutra) All sentient beings, always abiding in universal kindness, strive to quickly attain Bodhi, immeasurable liberation. them.
them).

Because of sentient beings, the Buddha practiced Buddhism, because of sentient beings, he became a Buddha. Become a Buddha to easily save sentient beings.

(Sutra) The original practice of Bodhicitta, no one is sentient, no sentient being, no renunciation Luc Luc Degree. Earn money at the end of the world, pray for Supreme Bodhi, attain gold at the end of the world, quickly attain Supreme Enlightenment.
(Sutra: Originally practicing Bodhi, always for sentient beings, now towards sentient beings, never abandoning Luc Do. In the past, in the Mat dynasty, he prayed for Supreme Bodhi. Now in the Mat dynasty, he quickly attained Supreme Enlightenment).

Buddha never stops saving sentient beings, diligently and diligently. Because of living beings, he practiced Bodhi; Because of sentient beings, he practiced Buddhism. Having attained Buddhahood, he still hopes to save sentient beings and liberate countless sentient beings. When Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva praised the Buddha, the Buddha was absolutely not like Śākyamuni Buddha that we all often see: From generating the mind, achieving Bodhi, to saving sentient beings, becoming Buddha, entering Nirvana [in just one life]. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva did not see that, [but saw that the Original Master] had become a Buddha and saved sentient beings, the sentient beings were saved to become Buddhas, became Buddhas and then appeared as sentient beings. As sentient beings, practice again, practice and become Buddha again. It is a Buddha who constantly saves sentient beings. These sentences have that kind of meaning.

(Sutra) Subdues evil views, heavens, dragons, people, yaksha, abiding energy, or, like the holy vajra religion.
(Sutra: Subduing evil views, gods, dragons, people, yaksha, abiding in eliminating Or, like needles holy path).

Evil views are evil views that are very difficult to overcome, and we often encounter them nowadays. You say good things to them, but they don't listen. Their evil views are inconceivable. What is evil view? We can often hear it. We say "killing people is not right", they retort: ​​"Why is killing people not right? If I don't kill him, he will kill me". Or that person doesn't kill people, he kills people to steal money. We see headless corpses, or anonymous bodies, we don't know who killed them! Kill and throw away. You have to find out the reason why?

In Taiwan, there are young people racing cars, riding in cars, shooting at cars other people are driving. When you see someone you don't like, immediately swing your knife and kill them, no grudges left! What karma is that? That is the collective karma of sentient beings in the present time. Is that kind of view an evil view or not? You ask them why they have raised that view, what is the benefit to themselves? They also don't have any wishes, isn't it because they consider killing people to be fun? That's called evil views. If you want to subdue those evil views, everyone should consider whether they are easy to subdue or not? Do they listen to advice? Very difficult! Yaksa (Yakşa) is Yaksha. We often talk about Duoc Xa. Yaksha is a devil, but there are still good ghosts and good beings. There are Yaksha Great Generals who protect the Dharma. Humans, heavens, and dragons also have evil people, all have good and evil. Subdue evil views, subdue heavens, dragons, humans, Duoc Xoa belongs to the evil type.

“An abiding can cut off Or” (An abiding, can cut off Or): To make them cut off evil views, abide in the good path, abide in the vajra holy path, how great a force is needed? Therefore, only Buddha and great Bodhisattvas can control it. This also requires a predestined relationship, and must also have good roots.

In the Buddhist scriptures, there are so many Bodhisattvas, there are so many Buddhas, [yet] there are people who do not even hear the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and do not even have the causes and conditions that pass by their ears. How can we tame them? Just like we are surrounded by six relatives, everyone loves us, and especially loves our children, but it's not just what you say that they will listen to. If it were that easy, there would be no more evil beings! I went to Tho Thanh Prison in Taiwan and saw that the serious prisoners were all young! Throw them in there, discipline them like that, but they don't listen. You advise them with kindness, do they listen to you or not? If you hope they will listen to you, you must have great power, and you yourself must cultivate full virtue. Virtue is not enough, it will not work! “Virtue is not enough to conquer others, power is not enough to rule others”. How can they listen to you? Therefore, we must rely on ourselves to practice. Buddha cultivated himself first. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva praises this.

(Sutra) Enjoy the life of limitless sentient beings, overcome the Bodhisattva, become the master of the Dharma Offering, the supreme Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) and blessings.
the healthiest).

That's nice. If countless sentient beings develop the mind to practice the Dharma and diligently practice the Six Paramitas, the Buddha will predict that they will attain supreme Bodhi, that is, in the future, that person will definitely be able to become a Buddha, in the future they will definitely be able to become an Offered One, a Perfectly Enlightened One, a Perfect Wisdom and Virtue, to be a guide for all sentient beings, to cultivate the best fields of merit for all sentient beings, which is also to become a Buddha.

(Sutra) The World-Honored One is incomparable traveler, universally rich in all sentient beings, countless great famous texts, abundant in the ten worlds.
(Sutra: The World-Honored One has no equal, protecting all sentient beings, immeasurable fame, filled with realm).

All equals who can be compared to the World-Honored One must be all Buddhas. No one is better than Buddha, and no one is equal to Buddha! Only Buddha can save all sentient beings, that is, all sentient beings. Buddha can protect them everywhere.

“Universal wealth” (covering all over) means being able to cultivate them, causing them to grow, become Buddhas, have a reputation like Buddha: The roar is heard throughout the ten directions, all the lands in the ten directions know Śākyamuni Buddha. That is the Buddha's great reputation, up to the ten names of Buddha, which are Tathagata, Saṅgha, Perfect Enlightenment... every Buddha has those ten names.

(Sutra) Thi Co, Bodhisattvas, Because of his achievements, he took refuge in the future, Dai Mau Ni took refuge.
(Sutra: Therefore, Bodhisattvas, in order to achieve their own affairs, all along to Quy y, at the feet of Dai Mau Ni).

Bodhisattvas are Bodhisattva (Bodhisattva), or Enlightened Beings, are Bodhisattvas who develop great minds in the ten precepts, hoping to benefit sentient beings, that is, those who hope to make all sentient beings enlightened, develop great Bodhisattva minds, achieve themselves, achieve the cause of Buddha, skillfully save sentient beings, are all directed to Śākyamuni Buddha. “Ham Cong Lai takes refuge, Dai Mau Ni submits” means “all surrender to the feet of the World-Honored One, that is, Śākyamuni Buddha”. Great Passover is the great Nirvana, Mau Ni translates as Complete Passage.

(Sutra) The text preaches the wonderful Dharma, the stage of giving birth to a joyful mind, giving rise to the highest right effort, practicing the Bodhisattva conduct.
(Sutra: Hearing that the Dharma is miraculous, all give rise to joy, the right initiation requires monks, practice Bodhi conduct).

Go for refuge to Buddha to pray for the teachings of the miraculous Dharma. What is magic? The Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra is also a wondrous dharma, the Diamond Sutra is also a wondrous dharma. “Magical” is inconceivable, very wonderful. In our minds we cannot think or discuss, then it is called Magic. The law, the rule, that is Dharma, is what makes understanding clear. In other words, [understanding] is enlightenment. Without enlightenment, Buddha will not speak. We don't understand clearly. As soon as the Buddha spoke, we immediately understood. That is called “miraculous dharma”. We don't know where suffering comes from, so the Buddha taught that suffering comes from practice, that is, feeling. If there is a cause, there will be suffering. What if you want to escape? He taught us to practice the Way. Cultivating the Way and attaining Nirvana, suffering is immediately ended. That is a wonderful dharma.

If you don't have wisdom, start contemplation, start thinking a lot. For all things, if you don't understand, you must learn: How is this flower born? Why is it yellow? If you casually point out something, [you'll see] there's so much we don't know! Using Buddha's wisdom to teach us, these things are called “wonderful dharma”. That is inconceivable! These wonderful dharmas only refer to the dharma to escape birth and death and attain Nirvana.

Hearing the Buddha speak that kind of wonderful Dharma immediately gave rise to great joy. Sentient beings who have a joyful mind will be diligent and enthusiastic in their studies, and will give rise to the highest right effort (right diligence), that is, “to increase the highest right effort”. Nowadays, although we are diligently cultivating righteously (right effort), we still do not have enough to attain higher levels. We must put in more effort, increase our mind of victory, increase our mind of diligence. You already have the mind of renunciation, plus the mind of monks, what will happen? Cultivate enlightenment and develop Bodhi mind. That is also the practice of enlightenment. What should be done?


(Sutra) Due to the master of magic power, accelerated attainment of Bodhi, the ancient master of alchemy, the Great Ascetic Master property.
(Sutra: Due to the master's magic power, everyone quickly attains Bodhi, so now the master, Dai Tap has never yes).

Due to the magic power of the master, those Thanh Van Sangha and Bodhisattva Sangha all very quickly attained ultimate results. Bodhi is the ultimate fruit. Therefore, now I praise Buddha, the present great Dharma conference is truly unprecedented, so I come to rejoice.

(Sutra) Thirteen million Yoc Xoa, nourishing all flesh and blood, releasing all negative karma, speeding up the great Bodhisattva Topic.
(Sutra: Thirteen million Yoc Xoa, always eating flesh and blood, all eliminating negative karma, quickly toward the great Bodhi).

Is there anything to prove [those who are guided by the magic power of the master will quickly attain Bodhi] or not? Here, let's bring up a case: As soon as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva arrived, he immediately knew that in this Dharma assembly there were many people who had attained enlightenment, many people who had heard the enlightenment Dharma, in this Great Assembly, they would attain Bodhi. He stated a number: “Thirteen million Yoc Xa”. Those Yaksha demons are flesh and blood eaters, always eating the flesh of living beings. In this Great Assembly, thirteen million Yaksha heard the Buddha's wonderful Dharma, they no longer created killing karma, and no longer had the thought of harming living beings. “Let go of all evil karma”: Let go of all evil karma. “The Speed ​​Beast Great Bodhi” (Quickly approaching Bodhi): This is what we often say: “Let go of the butcher knife, and on the ground become Buddha” (Let go of the butcher knife, immediately become Buddha). In this Great Assembly, there are thirteen million Yaksha ghosts who no longer create killing karma, no longer flow with karma, eliminate karma, and move towards Buddhahood.

corrugated iron.
(Kinh: Dac Tong Tri is victorious, patient and calm, forever free from defilements, successful Worshiping the World-Honored One).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has just arrived here. Due to the power of his wisdom, he has clearly understood in the incalculable Sravaka Sangha, incalculable Bodhisattva Sangha, how many people have attained Bodhi, how many people have developed Bodhi mind, how many people have abided in the Four Noble Truths. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's wisdom is very great. As soon as you arrived here, you already know how many people are like that! We alone don't know, we don't have wisdom, so we are still miserable beings. Seen from the narrative in the scriptures, in the previous section, the Buddha praised the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came here, also praising the Buddha's merits, and also speaking about the superiority of Buddha Dharma.

Buddha preached the wonderful Dharma here, there were thirteen million Yaksha let down killing karma, from the most evil to the most good. There are also many people who have attained Da La Ni (General Tri), attained many Da La Ni fruits, attained very deep Meditation, and are completely free of all defilements. Some people become Buddhas.

“The World-Honored Offeror” (The Offeror who is respected by the world): In this Great Assembly, there are many people who have become Buddhas, many people who have laid down their butcher knives, many people who have attained the Absolute Master, many people who have attained the Six Paramitas. There is such a wonderful cause and effect. We still have not attained enlightenment, so we rejoice a little, hoping that everyone will achieve the victory of the General Tri.

According to Patience, one attains the Perfection of Action, one attains the wonderful eye of wisdom, one abides in No Birth Forbearance, it is due to the power of the teacher.
Those who abide in Patience, those who attain Perfection of Action, those who attain the wonderful eye of wisdom, those who abide in No Birth Forbearance, all rely on the power of the Guru).

These are beautiful words to praise the Buddha of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. From those praises, we can see the wisdom of the Bodhisattva. Normally, we follow the scriptures to praise Bodhisattvas and Buddha. If we compose our own words of praise, we are afraid that we will not be able to praise them. That praise includes many meanings, sometimes it is [praise] the Buddha's practice while cultivating the cause, sometimes it is the manifestation of the virtue, sometimes it is the praise of the cause, sometimes it is the praise of the fruit, saying this mysterious Gia Da, are inconceivable words of praise.

“The Four Immeasurables” means the four immeasurable minds of “love, compassion, joy, and equanimity”. Tu Nhac means that while cultivating, the Buddha used the most beautiful words to receive blessings from all sentient beings. When they heard His words, their hearts were filled with joy. After that, enter Buddhism. Either He appears to work with them, or He appears to give alms. Therefore, in each verse of praise, it captures what the Buddha did in countless millions of eons. When we hear those nouns, it seems too easy. However, when we do it, it will be very difficult, because we have jealousy. Seeing others doing good things, jealousy arises in the mind. Not only do they not praise, but when others praise, they still want to interject disruptive words: "What's so good about it? Anyone can do it!" When we read these words of praise, we often think like that in our minds, giving rise to shame, and we must learn how to praise Buddha and Bodhisattvas.

If while praising a disciple so that people can have feelings of superiority and learn from them, be skillful in using appropriate words of praise and praise for that disciple. We always feel that when Bodhisattvas praise Buddha, it is an incomplete praise. Except for people like Ksitigarbha, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Maitreya, and Avalokiteshvara, if these great Bodhisattvas praise, they will be able to fully highlight the Buddha's merits. But we don't understand that deeply! If you want to praise the Buddha's merits, you will not be able to praise him, and your praise will never end.

In the praises of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, what have they always been praising? He said: “The Buddha is wonderful, I see that everyone in this Mahasamadhi Assembly achieves benefits from the dharma”. He praised the Buddha for educating them. Isn't this conference the Great Assembly? Can the Shravaka Sangha and the Bodhisattva Sangha both be counted? In this Dharma assembly, there are people who have been taught by the Buddha, there are people who practice the Four Immeasurable Minds; There are people who, taught by the Buddha, practice the Four Dharmas. There are people who, because of the Buddha's teachings, are in this association cultivating the Four Unobstructed Comparatives.

What is Tu Nhiep? These are Almsgiving, Loving Speech, Loving Action, and Collaboration. What is Tu Bien Tai? The Dharma is unobstructed, the meaning is unobstructed, the word is unobstructed, the argument is unobstructed. Here, there is also “Sustainment of Actions”, Actions of Actions is the Shurangama samadhi. The noun Dhammapada is related to each sutra. You should see for yourself what meaning each sutra has, because those meanings are not the main meaning we want to say. What is the main meaning? If we want to practice according to the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, how should we practice? “Practice” means how should we visualize? How can one practice Concentration? How to open wisdom? In particular, although there are only six words “record, depend, meditate, contemplate, move, and purify”, the meanings in them are too many, we can start practicing from the beginning until we attain Concentration. “Magical Wisdom Eye” (Mysterious Wisdom Eye) is a praise to the Buddha, meaning: In this assembly, there are many people like that who have also achieved the wisdom eye, that is, achieved the magical wisdom eye in the Dharma eye store. There are people who attain the Dharma of Non-Birth forbearance. Non-Birth Dharma Forbearance is to attain the nature of the Dharma, to attain the Truth, to understand and enter all non-born dharmas. The word Nhan can be understood as “approval”. Some people stay in the No Birth Dharma of Forbearance due to what powers? Why do the friends in the association have such strength? It's all due to the power of the Teacher, that is, the power of the Buddha's teachings.

(Sutra) The World-Honored One is majestic dearc, destroy evil spirits, subdue pagans, ninety-five different types.
type).

In this Dharma assembly, whenever there are obstacles and are harassed by enemies, due to the Buddha's majesty, these things will all be eliminated. “Ninety-five different kinds” are also [ninety-five kinds of] pagans.

(Sutra) To the depths of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, non-celestial beasts, truly sentient beings, the ultimate refuge lower.
(Sutra: All hells, animals, hungry ghosts, non-heavenly paths, sentient beings true, all refer to the World-Honored One).

There are also hells, eagles (animals), hungry ghosts, non-celestial beings (not deities), [“non-celestial”] that is, sentient beings who do not belong to the heavenly path, nor are they human beings, here we are referring to Asura. Although they have the same blessings as the gods and belong to the heavenly path, they are not like the gods. [Therefore, this verse] talks about the six realms of living beings: Hell, demons, animals, gods, humans, and Asuras. That includes all six paths. All the assemblies in the Mahayana Assembly took refuge at the Buddha's feet. “We all take refuge at the feet of the revered one,” [“revered one”] that is Buddha.

(Sutra) The fake gold is the sword warrior, the epidemic, the fate of calamity, the delusion of the righteous path, the intelligent monks. love.
(Sutra: Now put an end to sword soldiers, famine, epidemics, save those who love the righteous path, dark and blind sentient beings).

If there is a kalpa of swords and soldiers (war), due to the might of Buddha, the kalpa of swords and soldiers will end. If there is widespread illness or suffering, or famine, or during the destruction of kalpas, many sentient beings become confused and lose the right path, the Buddha will save them. “Manh minh sentient beings” (Dark sentient beings) are those who are in darkness. The word Ming originally refers to darkness. These people, due to abnormal nerves, seem to be forever in darkness. Such sentient beings are in darkness and are often said to have "eyes but cannot see", because there is no light in their bodies. Saying “manh minh” is a way of imagining it.

Ton).

There are also troubled and hysterical people. The word “hysteria” includes many meanings, not believing in the right path, not having right views, and wrong views, not a few. [Buddha] causes those people to abide in the path of nirvana, that power is very inconceivable. Because I see that in this Mahayana Assembly there are so many merits, so many inconceivable benefits.

“Try to let go of all conditions” (So I let go of all conditions): Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: “I let go of all causes and conditions, let go of all other conditions to worship the Buddha”. This has the meaning of asking for blessings, “to pay respect and honor” (to worship at the feet of the revered person).

(Sutra) Boundless Buddhalands, present masters, widely praised by the World-Honored One, future writers.
(Sutra: Infinite Buddha lands, current masters, all praise the World-Honored One, all listeners come here).

This is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's praise: I see limitless Buddha lands, there are many lands of Buddha's teachings, each Buddha in those lands praises the inconceivable merits of Shakyamuni Tathagata, all praising the World-Honored One. Why? He is in the most miserable place, aiming at the evil world of the five turbulences to save sentient beings, so everyone who sees and hears will not feel great joy.

(Sutra) Self-literature of the Sea of ​​Enlightenment, true boundless virtue, liberating sentient beings, with a heart filled with joy and reverence. Cultivate immeasurable blessings, attain golden reverence, pray for countless eons, and practice many offerings.
(Sutra: I hear the Sea of Change Tri, virtue truth truth infinite boundary, salvation escape all sentient beings, with a heart of joy and reverence. I have practiced immeasurable blessings, now I can worship the World-Honored One, praying in immeasurable for many lifetimes, often practice many offerings).

When I worshiped, there were a few sentences like that. Before, I couldn't find the origin. Later, when I read the Ten Rings Sutra, I found out the origin: Great Master Nguich Ich excerpted from here, but in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it doesn't exist, and the Contemplation Sutra also doesn't have it. “Bien Tri sea” (sea of ​​Right Enlightenment) is the Buddha way. I understand the Buddha, know the Buddha's wisdom, and the Dharma spoken by him can relieve the extreme suffering of all sentient beings. Buddha has true virtue, [the merits mentioned] in the previous section are Noble virtue, that is, merit that arises in accordance with Truth, so it is called “true virtue”. Because the nature is all-pervading everywhere, that virtue is also all-pervading everywhere, boundless. In the sentence “rescue sentient beings”, “rescue” is the Buddha who teaches, “escape” is sentient beings who are free from suffering and can be saved. Those sentient beings have escaped suffering, enjoy joy, their minds are filled with great joy, and they can worship the Buddha. It's not easy to see Buddha! If you don't cultivate countless merits, you won't be able to pay homage to Buddha!

“Increasingly cultivating immeasurable blessings, earning golden reverence” (Once cultivating immeasurable blessings, now worshiping at the feet of revered ones): The reason we can worship is because of many lifetimes of practice! Don't say we worship every day, even if we only go to the temple to bow once, it's still inconceivable! The Lotus Sutra teaches: "A weak person in a tower or temple, with a single palm, a small dike, can attain Buddhahood" (If anyone in a tower or temple, just raises one hand to bow and slightly bows his head, has already attained Buddhahood). Sometimes it is said that “Buddha path is achieved” (All Buddha paths have been achieved), while the Lotus Sutra says “Buddha path is achieved”.

There are those who only speak according to the written word, [saying] that just by going to a tower or temple, clasping hands and bowing one's head, one can attain Buddhahood. A professor at Xiamen University (Amoy) once asked me about this issue. He asked: "I worship Buddha every day, not just raising one hand, but clasping both hands, still not becoming a Buddha! Those words have flaws." I explained: "Those words have no shortcomings at all! Anyone who comes to a stupa or temple can only raise one hand [to pay homage], bow slightly, and have already become a Buddha. This confirms: Now that you have come, can see the Buddha statue, only raise one hand to pay homage, in the future, you will definitely become a Buddha. It is not just that you have become a Buddha now. In the past, Buddhas sowed good roots, while cultivating people, they sowed them like that. So They have achieved Buddhahood, proving: In the present, anyone who can see a Buddha statue and can raise one hand to pay respect and slightly bow his head, in the future, will definitely be able to become a Buddha. From the past, prove the present.

Therefore, if you have not cultivated countless blessings in the past, you will not be able to worship Buddha now. That's what that sentence means. We not only worship Buddha, we also worship Buddha and repent every day, proving: In the past, we have cultivated countless blessings. Therefore, one must make the "vow for countless lifetimes, often practice many offerings" (vow for countless lifetimes, often practice many offerings) in order to be able to make offerings to the World-Honored One.

(Sutra) The World-Honored One learned the metal, made it according to his vow, while testing impurities, attained Supreme Bodhisattva. Topic.
(Sutra: I now study the World-Honored One, make this vow, and in this impure world, I will attain Supreme Bodhisattva. Topic).

“Self” (Son) is the self-proclaimed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In the past, the World-Honored One made such a vow. At first, Śākyamuni Buddha heard the names of the fifty-three Buddhas. He one by one turned to others to recite them. [Those] are now the three thousand Buddhas, also the three thousand Buddhas in the Stellar Future Kalpa, the Present Noble Kalpa, and the Past Adorned Kalpa when we recite the sutra [Three Thousand Buddha Names]. Three thousand Buddhas in three kalpas initially heard the names of the fifty-three Buddhas, planted good roots, gradually practiced, and all became Buddhas. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva humbled himself, He said: "Now I also study according to the Buddha, and make the same vows as the Buddha's Mahasamadhi Assembly at the present time. I myself also practice in the impure realm during this evil life of the Five Defilements, not in the pure land, [enduring] with all my might many obstacles. Practicing there, I attain Supreme Bodhi. Śākyamuni Buddha made the vow, and achieved it through many lifetimes of cultivators.".

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva both bows and praises, that is, he both praises and bows. Just like when we worship Buddha, we also praise and pay respect. We cannot compose verses, so we take the verses praising the Buddha of Bodhisattvas to recite. As in the recitation of Samantabhadra chapter, there are many verses praising the Buddha, which can all be used to praise the Buddha. There are also articles that can be used to recite and repent for sins, not simply praising the Buddha's merits, but also repenting for one's own sins, everyone must eliminate their own karma. While we bow to the Buddha, while bowing, we think: “I pray to eliminate the three hindrances and afflictions, I pray to attain true and clear wisdom, I pray that all sin obstacles will be completely eliminated, and in this world I always practice the Bodhisattva path” (I pray to eliminate the three hindrances and afflictions, I pray to be fully understood by true wisdom, I pray that all sin obstacles are eliminated, I practice the Bodhisattva path forever and ever). While reciting and worshiping, he praised Buddha, repented of his sins, and made vows. These are all verses composed for us by great Bodhisattvas.

You can also compose verses and write verses, depending on your own wishes. You study a lot of sutras, and when you wish for something, you compose verses to praise it yourself. We see the verse in praise of Bodhisattva Manjushri by the great master Tsongkhapa (Tsongkhapa)[7]. Currently, the verses that Dharma Master Hoang Giac read when preaching the Second Bodhi Path were composed by the great master Tsongkhapa, wishing that all sentient beings would become Buddhas. Although it is just a chant to recite, it is actually a practice. These are Bodhisattvas praising each other. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came to this Dharma assembly. While bowing to the Buddha, he spoke a total of thirty-four verses. He started with praise, using a total of thirty-four verses to praise. After praising, worshiping, and making offerings.

Such a large number of relatives use incense, magical flowers, and other precious decorations to worship the Buddha. At that time, in the assembly there was a Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat named Hao Doubt. If he had doubts, he asked. In the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, the originator of that sutra is Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva who first raised the question is named Kien Tinh Tinh, indicating that we all do not have faith, but He has very steadfast faith, hoping to make everyone [have faith] steadfast like Him. Now the great Bodhisattva who arises here is the Good Questioner. Great Question Great Bodhisattva himself had thoroughly understood Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so he represented the assembly in the assembly, because others did not have the wisdom to ask questions. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva also asked for the same reason. Sometimes, when no one asked, Manjushri Bodhisattva asked, as in the sutras, it was all asked by Manjushri Bodhisattva. While asking each other questions, meanings will arise, causing the masses in the Dharma Assembly to gain many benefits. This Good Questioning Bodhisattva immediately asks questions.

I remember that Master Vinh Gia had a few sentences like this: “The teacher is heartless” (The teacher has no way of speaking according to ordinary sentiments), [meaning]: The teachings of perfection are inconceivable, ordinary people will not be able to understand it! It is impossible to speak with ordinary feelings, there are no ordinary feelings to speak of (that is, not because of doubts but afraid of offending others, or afraid of being criticized as stupid or foolish, but still holding on to doubts). "If you have doubts, don't argue directly" (If you have doubts you can't decide, just argue frankly): I have doubts that you can't decide, "If you have doubts you can't decide" means it's okay to argue like that! Don't listen to what others say, that's what other people say, that's what other people say, that's what I hear! That's not right, you need to ask. "If you have doubts, don't decide to practice directly, but the monks and nuns fight over the ego" (Whenever you have doubts but can't be decisive, just argue frankly to resolve the doubts, it's not a dispute between me and the monks): It's not like I'm arguing about right and wrong. “Practice is terribly lost and ends with eternal khanh” ([If you don't resolve doubts], you are afraid that practicing will fall into the trap of Doan Kien and Perpetual View): People who practice don't understand that principle, if they don't fall into Duan Kien, they will also fall into Perpetual View. Good Doubt Bodhisattva saw that scene and change, so he stood up, turned to the Buddha and asked.

(Sutra) Uplifting the child's throne, adjusting the clothes, one's birthday, worshiping the Buddha with duality, existence before the ground, He raised his palm towards the Buddha and spoke to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! Are you a good man? Are you a good man? Are you in the Buddha's country? Are you in the Buddha's land? Have you achieved countless virtues and good roots? Do you praise the Buddha's race? Serve the Buddha's inconceivable merits and merits in the ocean? The future of the self is the same, the knowledge and wisdom are only the same, the only wish is the theory."
(Sutra: Stand up from your seat, straighten your clothes, undress one shoulder, bow under both feet Buddha, with his right knee placed close to the ground, clasped his hands facing the Buddha, said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! Where did this good man come from? Is the Buddha-land he lives in far or near? What kind of merit and good roots have he achieved that the World-Honored One praises in every way? [Why] can he praise the Buddha's ocean of inconceivable merits and virtues? We have never seen, heard, and respectfully please tell us before."

First of all, the Buddha praised Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, "the World-Honored One's race and lineage praised and praised the inconceivable Buddha's ocean of merit and virtue" (having been praised by the Buddha for all things, [he] was able to praise the Buddha's ocean of inconceivable merit and virtue). Praise like that, praise is inconceivable, ordinary people will not be able to praise. Why have [we] never heard it before? We have never heard of such a great Bodhisattva, never before. “Prayer-only doctrine” [means] please, World-Honored One, please explain and enlighten us. Sometimes when we finished repentance, a fellow monk said: "Master! Please explain." Reveal what? What questions do you have? Please ask questions. Whenever you pray to the Buddha for guidance, or pray to the Buddha statue, you must have a vow and a purpose. First of all, you must have questions, you can't be confused and say "Buddha bless me"! Just like if you have any disease, you need to ask a doctor and clearly state the disease. You must have a question before asking it.

(Sutra) The Buddha wrote: “Only! Good man! Such as the great sage's merit and good roots, the great multitude of people in the world cannot be measured and profound. The Tathagata's teachings are such that the great sage's merit and good roots must necessarily be confused with the world's people. oldn, or unbelieving”.
(Sutra: The Buddha said: “Stop it! Thien Nam Death! The merits and good roots of such a Great Being, all the great multitudes of gods and humans in the world cannot understand the shallowness or depth. If they heard the Tathagata speak so generously of the merits and good roots of such a Great Being, all the great multitudes of gods and humans in the world would be confused, confused, or not believe”).

The Buddha answered the Bodhisattva's Good Doubt: “Just” (Stop it), that means I won't answer you, there's no need to ask anymore! Why didn't we tell you? “Like the Great One”, the merits of this great Bodhisattva, the good roots that he has cultivated, all the great assembly of gods and humans in the world cannot believe and accept, they will not be able to measure how shallow or deep he is! Suppose we explain his merits and virtues in detail, there will be people who doubt and slander, or become confused and confused. “Confusionn” is inexplicable!

(Sutra) Time, Good Nghi Van restores the saying.
(Sutra: At that time, Hao Nghi Van requested again as follows).

Good Doubt asked the Bodhisattva, but the Buddha did not answer. He still wants to ask, please ask again.

(Sutra) “May only the Tathagata be sensitive theory”.
(Sutra: “I hope the Tathagata will mercifully say for”).

That being so, [I still] pray that [Tathagata] will have mercy on all sentient beings, speak for all sentient beings. Whenever you say it, sentient beings will be blessed, “blessed” that is, free from suffering and happy. He asked again. If we ask once without saying anything, we will ask again. At one point, even though the Buddha was invited again, he still did not speak. The third time, the Buddha will definitely speak. One then two, two then three times, in many sutras, all requests are from one to three times. The same goes for the Lotus Sutra; First of all, the Buddha responded. As soon as he responded, he said, the five thousand people present all withdrew, they did not listen! Before the Buddha preached the Dharma, they withdrew. Friends who have read the Lotus Sutra must know this story.

(Sutra) Buddha's words: “Hearing! Good thoughts.
(Sutra: Buddha taught: “Listen! Meditate well).

Once again, please “listen” (listen). In the previous part it was “true language, true view” (truly speaking, true seeing), here it is “true hearing”. Every time the Buddha answered, he taught “true hearing”. “Hear the truth” is true, [implies] listen to the truth as it really is, listen with your heart. Don't use your ears to listen! If you use your ears to listen, it will go from one ear to the other, don't do it! “Dear listening” is asking you to think. Just listening is not enough, you still have to meditate skillfully and observe skillfully.

(Kinh) Ngo reigns as a minor theory.
(Sutra: I will summarize a few parts for you).

If I want to describe the full merits of this Great Being, I'm afraid I can't. Now just a little summary. “Minority” is very little.

(Sutra) Like the Great Sir, immeasurable achievements are beyond compare. virtue.
(Sutra: Such a Great Being achieves immeasurable, inconceivable merit and virtue).

This Great Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha has achieved inconceivable merit. Next, [Buddha] pointed out the merits of the Great Being.

Tam-ma-ground, capable of enlightening to enter the realm of Tathagata, capable of attaining the ultimate Non-Birth Dharma of Forbearance, of all Buddhas, attaining freedom, capable of enduring the All-Wisdom position, capable of transcending the Sea of All-Wisdom, capable of abiding in the Lion Tan Tan Trang sama-ma-ground, capable of rising to the Mount of All-Wisdom, capable of subduing heretical heresy, the mature desire of all sentient beings, residing only in the Buddhaland of all stages. Like the Great Master, depending on where to abide in the Buddha lands, depending on where to abide in the samāma-grounds, generate immeasurable outstanding merit, mature countless sentient beings.
Lai, having attained the supreme Non-Birth Dharma of Forbearance, having attained freedom in all Buddhist dharmas, being able to endure the position of All-Wisdom, being able to cross the ocean of All-Wisdom, being able to abide in the right concentration of Lion Phan Tan Trang, being able to ascend the mountain of One-Tie-Wisdom, being able to suppress and subdue the heretical teachings, for the sake of reaching maturity, all sentient beings can abide in the Buddha realms. Whenever such a Great Being abides in the Buddha realms, If you abide in all the disciplines of right concentration, you will generate immeasurable merits and mature countless sentient beings who have been taught by you.

In the previous part, [Good Doubting Bodhisattva] wondered: Where did this good man come from? Which Buddha realm is he from? How far is it from Sa Ba world, the teaching land of Buddha [Shakyamuni]? He asked like that, the Buddha replied: "In whichever country this Great Being resides, that country is where he resides". Therefore, He does not necessarily come from the South. The Ksitigarbha Sutra says that he comes from the South, but according to this sutra, as long as there is a hell in any Buddha land, as long as there are three disciples, he will be there. Wherever he abides, he abides in samadhi. Samādhi is Concentration, wonderful concentration. We continue to talk about His outstanding merit.

“ Shurangama Samadhi (Śūraṅgama) overcomes samadhi” i.e. Shurangama samadhi. In the past, the old translation was Shurangama. Dharma Master Huyen Trang followed the original intention to translate, so he translated it as Thu Lang Gia Ma Thang Tam-ma-Di. Kien Hanh Dinh in the previous section can also be translated as Kien Tuong Dinh, [implying] having completed those things. “The Ultimate Concentration” is the ultimate. Regarding the samadhi attained by the Buddha, according to the Nirvana Sutra, volume twenty-seven, Shurangama samadhi has five names. The first name is Shurangama samadhi. The second name is Prajnaparamita. Prajnaparamita is the Shurangama samadhi, which is also the Shurangama Demon who overcomes Samadhi as we have just read in this sutra. The third name is Vajra Samadhi, this is the noun used in Tantra. The fourth name is Lion's Roar Samadhi. The fifth name is Buddha Nature samadhi.

Any karma done, that is, any karma performed by the Buddha, is called samadhi, every action is called that. But among the one hundred and eight samadhis, there is one general samadhi. The Bodhisattva has stayed in that samadhi, which also means staying in this Concentration.
