Sometimes when you recite, you get a fever, or feel cold. This is a normal phenomenon, don't feel panic. While you recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the people who come to you are all your relatives. Otherwise, they won't be able to come before you. They look forward to being saved and listening to the Ksitigarbha Sutra. If you recite for two days, or several times, that phenomenon will no longer exist and will disappear. That's natural.

Demon and god roads have existed from ancient times to present. In any country, in any region, there are cases of unstable and especially strange houses. Today, I saw [the scriptures said] these kinds of demons, and remembered that when in New York, there was a Dharma friend who had not yet taken the Three Refuges. Her husband was Japanese and worked for a Japanese company. She had an extremely stinky house; it's because of the devil mentioned above. The devil's body is especially stinky. After that, she recited the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and also recited the Ksitigarbha sutra, inviting us to come and meditate. After that, the devil also disappeared. Before that, any perfume she applied was ineffective and could not [eliminate the stench]. This is indeed true, everyone must be sincere. We are disciples of Buddha, we must believe in the Buddha's teachings: The path of ghosts is one of the six paths. It's still not easy for a dead person to turn into a ghost! You still have to be reincarnated into the devil destinies. Which path to reincarnate into, like reincarnating as a human, reincarnating into the animal path, [there must be a cause in that path], must be reincarnated into the devil destinies to become a demon.

(Sutra) Depending on the place, sentient beings, the Yoc Xoa, Rakshasa, Hungry Ghosts, All Xa Gia demon, Bo DatNa demon, Cuu Friend Do devil, Yet Tra Bo Dat Na ghost, absorbing ghost energy.
ghosts, Tat Xa Gia ghosts, Bo Dat Na ghosts, Cuu Ban Do ghosts, Yet Tra Bo Da Na ghosts, semen-sucking ghosts).

There is a book Translating Famous Generals to explain

The names of the devil, I roughly follow the order of reading a few paragraphs. Piśāca is a blood-sucking demon (blood-sucking demon). This type of demon feeds on human essence, but does not appear. You don't see it, and it doesn't appear to threaten you. It sucks your blood and absorbs your essence. It doesn't follow your body to absorb it. If your excreta has blood in it, for example in the hospital, especially when a mother gives birth, those demons eat that taste. It's not like you actually eat it, you just smell it and you eat it.

Next is the demon Pūtana. Dad Dat Na is “stinky”. Its body smells strangely, but it doesn't eat this or that. Wherever there is a stench, it immediately runs to eat that stench. Currently, I'm afraid that toilets in America and Canada don't have this ghost because they don't stink. It heads down to the ground, searching for stinky places to absorb the stench. But among the demons, among the hungry ghosts, they have the greatest blessings. Since he is a ghost who specializes in sucking up bad smells, why does he have the greatest blessing? It specializes in teasing people or animals, making them bloated, and specializes in eating your stink. It is eaten while other hungry ghosts are not eaten. Therefore, it is said to have great blessings.

Yak Xoa, Raksa: Yakṣa is a Yaksha, specializing in drinking human blood, specializing in eating human essence. We often mention Yaksha and Rākṣas[11] at the same time, this type of demon is extremely evil.

Cu Cuu Companion (Kumbhāṇḍa) means the Unseen Demon because it [is shaped] like a vase. In the past, there was a man who had a great reputation and was a very upright person. When he went to the bathroom, he encountered the Unholy Ghost. He is a man of great reputation and light. Ung Hinh Ghost wanted to avoid it, but couldn't run away, he stopped him. He came in from outside the door and told Ung Hinh Quy: "Don't run!" That demon didn't dare run. Because at that time, when going to the bathroom there was no electric light, so you had to carry an oil lamp. He said: "You wait here!" He immediately placed the lamp on the Ghost Ghost's head. Neither afraid nor frightened by that Unholy Ghost. Waiting for it to finish, he took the lamp and said, "You go." In history, there are records of this type of demon. If you want to read stories about ghosts, there is a book called Duyet Vi Thao Duong Bu Ky written by Ky Hieu Lam. That book was written entirely about ghosts, writing stories he had heard, completely different from Lieu Trai Chi Di. Lieu Trai Chi Di is a story composed, while Duyet Vi Thao Duong But Ky was mostly written when Ky Hieu Lam was exiled to Xinjiang. In the border areas, these stories are especially numerous. He heard old stories and wrote them down. Duyet Vi means hidden. I bring up a few stories to prove that demons really exist.

Ba Dat Na Demon (Kaṭapūtana): This type of demon has an extremely ugly appearance, often entering and leaving the grave. They don't go to normal places because they specialize in eating corpses, [rather] smelling corpses. When the corpse rots, the devil will absorb the smell of the corpse. Why is it that when a monk eats rice, he must give food to those demons? When making offerings to Ngo, making offerings to all living beings, those demons are also included. Whenever they do that, they can smell the smell and taste of the food.

(Sutra) Reciting tigers, wolves, lions, evil beasts, ancient poisons, evil spells, resentment Bandits, military battles, and the remaining species of the chaplains, the hindrances of the body and mind, the loss of life and death, the desire for life and death, the desire for happiness and suffering, the able-minded mind to name, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, must be able to separate from the chaplains, preserve the body and life, follow the time, attain heavenly birth, the path of Nirvana.
(Sutra: And tigers, wolves, lions, evil beasts, ancient poisons, curses, uncles, evil magic, resentment, military battles, and other fear-bound things, the body and mind are panicked, afraid of losing one's life and life, hate death, greed for life, hate suffering, seek happiness, if one can wholeheartedly confess the name, chant, worship, respect, make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, all will be free from fear, preserve one's life, and according to the foundation that should be saved, one can rest in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana).

“Avoid evil spells”: (Evil spells, evil spells): These are evil spells to curse people they hate very much. There were also armies on both sides fighting, and in the hostile battle between the two sides, all kinds of terrifying things arose. All kinds of things entangle and entangle you, making your mind and body unpredictable, frightened, lost, and afraid of losing your life. Everyone wants to live and does not want to die. That is human common sense. Everyone does not want to suffer, they all wish for happiness, that is “despite suffering, seek happiness”. If, faced with that dangerous moment, you can single-mindedly confess the name, chant, admire, respect, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will be able to let go of all fear, but also be able to keep your own life intact, gradually enter the path, and depending on your nature, you will be able to rest in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana. This represents the great kindness, great compassion, and great vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He is not afraid of many things, specializing in taking care of all the trivial matters of all living beings, because He has made that vow. There are people who are very afraid of worrying about many things, especially old monks like us, always thinking "One more thing is better than one less thing", just practice yourself!

In this Sa Ba world, the most compassionate are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), they specialize in many matters! Even though it's a big deal on their side, you still have a predestined relationship with them. What is considered predestined? You can recite their names, you can recite their holy names, it's predestined. It is not easy to hear their names and still be able to recite them. When I encounter times of urgent suffering, I think of them. You should not call mother, calling mother has no effect at all! We often call our mother when we are in pain. Tibetans call their mother A Ma. I have heard so many languages, the word Mother has not changed, the word Mother has understood since birth, they all seem to be the same. Whenever you have difficulty, when you are suffering, always call your mother. However, you must change to calling Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or calling Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, but calling mother cannot solve the problem. If you call Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, He becomes your mother, the problem will be solved, He can really save you.

(Sutra) Depending on the place, all sentient beings, or one of great learning, or one of pure faith, or one of pure precepts, or one of Jing Lu, or one of supernatural power, or one of Prajna, or one of liberation, or one of wonderful form, or one of wonderful sound, or one of wonderful scent, or one of wonderful taste, or one of wonderful touch, or one of benefit, or one of famous literature, or one of merit, or one of skill, or one of fruit, or one of forestry, or one of court, or one of tools, or one of path, or one of wealth, or one of medicine. medicine, or the monk, or the story, or the beauty, or the rain, or the water, or the price, or the waft, or the wind, or the fire, or the far away, or the man and woman, or the means, or the cultivator, or the warm, or the cool, or the memory, or the species of worldly pleasures, the pursuit of time, the urgent and powerful source of sorrow and suffering The mind confesses the name, chants, respects, and makes offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Mahasattva, testing the good man of his wonderful merits and divine power to strive and endure, to completely abandon suffering and suffering, to fulfill his wishes, to fulfill his wishes at any time, to attain heavenly rebirth, the path of Nirvana.
(Sutra: Anywhere, if sentient beings, or for the sake of literature, or for pure faith, or for pure precepts, or for Jingdhi, or for supernatural powers, or for Prajna, or for liberation, or for wonderful colors, or for wonderful sounds, or for wonderful scents, or for wonderful tastes, or for wonderful touch, or for nourishment, or for fame, or for merit, or for skill, or for fruits, or for forests, or for beds, seats, or for carpets, or for roads, or for wealth, grain, or for medicines, or for houses doors, or for servants, or for colors, or for sweet rain, or for praying for water, or for crops, or for breezes, or for cool breezes, or for praying for fire, or for cars, or for children, or for means, or for cultivating blessings, or for warmth, or for coolness, or for memories, or for all kinds of worldly and extra-worldly benefits, while pursuing, are oppressed by all kinds of suffering, if one can single-mindedly name, chant, and admire, Respect and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, due to the merits, wonderful concentration and majestic power of that good man, causing everyone to be free from suffering and suffering, their wishes are satisfied, and according to their nature, they should be saved and placed in peace in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana)..

Those things can be satisfied. What is said in the latter part is worldly dharma, while in the previous part it is worldly dharma. I hope to listen to many sutras and understand the Dharma. Because of being well-versed, one will surely attain Wisdom. Like when we listen to the sutras and the Dharma here, it's as if there is a place where the sutras are preached, and it's very easy for us to go and listen, not very difficult. But for me, I find it extremely difficult, very difficult! Currently, in Mainland China, there are many people who believe in Buddha, hoping to hear the teachings of the Three Refuges but have not heard it. “Isn't there a Buddhist Academy?” The Buddhist Institute in Mainland China does not allow auditions. Lectures on sutras and dharma teachings can only be done in temples and shrines, and cannot be taught in gatherings. Laws in mainland China do not allow this.

Perhaps we feel that multi-literacy seems to be very easy. Actually, it's very difficult! If you want to listen to a sutra, it's not that easy. You need to have a predestined relationship. The person who speaks and the person who listens must have a predestined relationship. If you want to preach the Dharma, you also have to have a place. The place is very difficult. If listening to the Dharma can give rise to pure faith and mind, it is even more difficult! I say so, everyone, don't worry, pure faith is very difficult. [Difficult to develop] pure faith also includes monastic masters like us! Hearing the Dharma, giving rise to pure faith and mind [is not an easy thing]. If we speak in terms of division of dignity, we must reach the status of the Five Grades to hear the Dharma in order to be pure. If our mind can be pure, then we can listen to the Dharma!

Arising pure faith is very difficult, it must be that in our thoughts, the slightest bit of fame, gain, greed, anger, ignorance, love, all jealousy and obstacles are absent. If you cannot achieve pure faith, recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name and pray for pure faith. Now we believe in Buddha, but there are many mixed motivations, so the effect is not very good, we cannot be enlightened. Even though you listen to so many sutras, you still understand very little. If the Dharma you hear does not agree with your own mind, you will not be able to give rise to truly pure faith. Pure faith is not something we casually say and it will be pure faith. If you can enlighten to incorrect ideas, then immediately stop them. Recognizing that "evil thoughts arise before" and being able to prevent "next thoughts from arising", you will have faith. The Dharma friends who have faith in protecting and upholding the Three Jewels would rather sacrifice their lives and lives, without thinking about their own lives, they worry about the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Do we have such pure faith? In that case, as soon as they hear the Dharma, they can enter it. If you can enter, you can attain Concentration. If you can Concentrate, you will be able to give birth to Wisdom. They definitely make a vow, and after making a vow, they need to carry out exactly what they vow. That is the manifestation of pure faith.

To talk a little more deeply, believe that you are Buddha! That is pure faith. When you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you must believe that you are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Or turn back to the Hearing, contemplate the opposite, contemplate your own mind and the unified mind of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: Our mind is the Buddha's mind, but also the mind of sentient beings. Not only do you have pure faith like that, but you also make all sentient beings become pure faith. That is asking Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for blessings. When we sincerely recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, that is called “pure faith”. When you single-mindedly recite Amitābha Buddha, you must know that you yourself have become Amitābha Buddha. Must build faith like that! If you seek the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's blessings are your own mind blessing your own mind! There is also “pure precepts”. Regardless of whether you receive the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, the Eight Precepts, up to the two hundred and fifty monk precepts, the three hundred forty-eight bhikshuni precepts, and up to the Bodhisattva main precepts. In general, the Three Convergence Pure Precepts, i.e. the Precepts of Self-Discipline, the Precepts of Good Dharma Precepts, and the Many Useful Friendship Precepts, because you keep the precepts pure, you will be pure.

“Or because of Tinh Lu”: Tinh Lu is Concentration, another name for Concentration, also samadhi. Sitting still in thinking is cultivating thinking.

“Or because of miraculous powers”: Everyone knows miraculous powers: Others can't, but you can. Here, when you pay attention, you immediately go to Beijing, and when you pay attention, you immediately go to Taipei. Wherever there are sword soldiers, if you raise your hand here, the sword soldiers will disappear, the fight will not be successful! It's like a great monk saw a big fire burning, so he borrowed someone else's wine to drink, sprayed the wine into the air, and extinguished the fire. The fire was extinguished, but the smell of alcohol was present. At that time, he was in Xi'an, extinguishing the fire in Bac Binh Phu. That's called magic power. However, such magical powers are still minor magical powers. Great supernatural power means having wisdom and wisdom nature that can communicate with everything. As for the natural mind, restore the natural mind you already have. That's called God. The divine mind is divine, the heart is the self-nature. The mind is very natural, intelligent and wise, with boundless wonderful uses, that is called "magic power". But usually small realms appear, that's not some great magical power! When Bodhisattvas use their supernatural powers, they will definitely change the karma of sentient beings, eliminate the karma of sentient beings, and increase their pure faith.

“Or because of Prajna”: Prajna is wonderful wisdom. We read the Prajnaparamita Sutra, Vajra Prajna Paramita Sutra, and then read the Heart Sutra, achieving wisdom. That wisdom is not ordinary wisdom, but the wisdom of Prajna, Six Paramitas, or the path of liberation.

There are two ways to explain the word “miraculous”:

- His appearance is very dignified, far superior to ordinary people. Thirty-two generals, eighty types of goodness, all are wonderful colors.

- There are also the formless, the formless, the formless.

Magical form, wonderful sound, wonderful scent, wonderful taste, wonderful touch, that is, Form, Sound, Fragrance, Taste, Touch, Dharma, plus the word Magic, would be inconceivable. Called Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, that is not Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, but called Form, Sound, Scent, Taste, Touch, Dharma, that is Magic. If you don't reach that level, you can't call it Magic. Magic is inconceivable. It is clear that they are blue, pink, red, and yellow, but all forms are not forms, because judging by their nature, we will know that they are dependently arisen, not real. From their form, their nature emerges, which is Magic. Form, non-form, flower, non-flower, flower is not a flower!

I remember reading a parallel sentence: “The color of the paint, the color of the water, the color of the river, the color of the river Khong” (The color of the mountains, the color of the water, smoke color in the afternoon, every color is Emptiness), meaning: There is no Form, it is created by your mind. “Wind sound, Vu sound, Chung Khanh Thanh, Thanh Thanh free” (The sound of the wind, the sound of rain, the sound of bells, every sound is free). There's no sound either.

Therefore, wonderful colors, wonderful sounds, even wonderful scents are all like that. This is not a normal realm. If you want to reach this realm, you must single-mindedly recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind, transforming your own mind into unity with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind. Only if you are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can you reach this wonderful realm. For fame, for benefit, for wanting to make merit, you can also [recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva].

“Or for the servant”, to put it briefly. If you want to hire a few servants at home, or if you want to open a company or hire a few employees, they are all considered "servants". Or the family must hire a nanny, who is also considered a servant. In such situations, ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for blessings, as if Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is in charge of everything. The goal is that you must single-mindedly recite His name, waiting until you recite the spirit and your thoughts will change. The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra aims to transform your afflictions. The first is Self-Pan to talk about the outstanding merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so that you can give rise to faith, so that we can trust Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If your mind can believe in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, your mind will match Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind; After that, your mind transforms into Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind is the great vow, and you will always follow it and make the great vow. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva obeys the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and makes great vows.

We learn from Him and make great vows. For the sake of our achievements, He makes our vows and minds agree with His, Buddha and Buddha's path. If you can be single-minded, faithful in reciting, worshiping, and respecting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the above wishes can all be achieved. Why? In the above section, I said that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva entered miraculous samadhi as much as that. From those Concentrations, so much wisdom is born, He can transform our minds. When He blesses you, it is not He who gives it to you, but it is your own mind that gives rise to wonderful, completely natural effects. Don't think that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will give us anything, but it is your own mind that generates merit, arises supremely, is the power from your own mind, combined with the wonderful concentration and inconceivable power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so you can leave suffering, leave all sadness, compassion, and suffering; Therefore, your wishes and desires will be satisfied. Not only that, but it can also place you in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana.

(Sutra) Depending on the place, whether there are sentient beings, whether there are seeds, truly desolate fields, or mature fields Faithful, weak in business, or not in business, with the ability and determination to name, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, test good men, merit and concentration, majestic divine power, and be flexible, it is truly windy. The reason why it's fake? The good man has passed through countless countless great kalpas, exceeding the number of Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, developing great diligence and steadfastly vowing. By testing the power of the will, the desire to mature all sentient beings, often accepts to hold all the great earth, often accepts to hold all the seeds, often all sentient beings to use it at will. Test the good man's majestic divine power, great spiritual energy, all herbs, roots, cultivators, roots, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, all-growing stages, medicinal grains, cat price, real fruit, mature laxatives, incensepure beautiful.
(Sutra: Anywhere, if sentient beings, take the seeds and sow them in the wild, or in the fields mature, or diligently fertilize, or not fertilize, but can wholeheartedly recite, chant, worship, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, due to the merit, wonderful concentration, and majestic power of this good man, causing all the seeds to grow abundantly. Why is this good man who has gone through countless countless kalpas, in a place where Buddhas and World-Honored Ones cannot be counted, making a vow of great diligence?

Due to that force of aspiration, in order to mature all sentient beings, it often sustains all the great earths, maintains all the seeds, and makes it available to all sentient beings at will. Due to the divine power of this good man, he can cause all the plants and trees in the great earth, roots, tendrils, sprouts, trunks, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, to grow, herbs, grains, grains, fruits to be luxuriant, dense, ripe, fresh, clean, soft, delicious and beautiful.

This paragraph is about people who grow crops, hoping that the crops they have planted will grow very well. Or if you want to plant flowers, hope for the potted plants in your house to grow a little more lushly, chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in front of those flower beds, circumambulate them (don't laugh, [doing so] is really very good). Potted ornamental plants are about to die, especially our favorite orchids and orchids, they are about to die. Return, worship, pray, and it grows lush again. But if you consider the effectiveness of those small things as holy results, holy results, it will be ruined. We study Buddha, pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and must naturally practice and worship. You don't think about those things, but if you do, the flowers and grass are also very lush, unimaginable.

In my hometown, there is a story like this: There was a woman who had only one child. She thought about missing her child, someone taught her a method: "You stand on the doorstep, one hand holding the latch, the other holding the rice basket. Eat rice in the basket, try your best to knock on that horizontal latch. In a few days, your child will return." The old woman kept knocking every day, but in less than ten days, her son actually returned. For what reason? Her daughter was not at peace, thinking that some great disaster had happened in the house, and when she returned quickly, nothing happened, she was just longing for it. That is an example showing the [effect] of single-mindedness.

Another example of determination: There is a mother who remembers her child, remembers her immensely, but that child is extremely unfilial to her mother. However, his mother loved him very much and was very dedicated. One time, her son met a group of people who wanted to worship Pho Da Son, and he also wanted to follow them to worship. Someone said: "If you are so unfilial, going to the mountain to worship Buddha will affect us." It said: “No, I have changed.” He immediately followed everyone up the mountain to worship Buddha. When arriving at Putuo Mountain, iron lotus flowers appeared on the sea surface. The sea surface is full of iron lotus flowers, the boat cannot move forward. Everyone immediately chanted the iron lotus flower with sincerity, and it also chanted along with everyone. It saw Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and said: "You don't need to worship me, just go back home. If you go back, there won't be any more iron lotus flowers, go back!" He said: "I have come to worship Bodhisattva." Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva said: "When you return, you will see that the person who opened the door for you is me." So, it returned, the iron lotus also disappeared, and everyone continued to sail to Putuo Mountain. It did not succeed in worshiping, so it returned home. When he got home, it was twelve o'clock at night, his old mother was already asleep, so he knocked on the door. Mom heard her son's voice, immediately put on her cotton coat and opened the door for him. That is Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara's salvation for mother and child. He returned to repent to his mother, truly repented. Because it worshiped Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva was moved by its sincere thought and transformed [its mind] into filial piety. The mind has a very big relationship!

The above types of determination are small, not the type of determination we need to develop. We must vow to “become Buddha and save sentient beings”. Everyone must remember: Every one of us, Dharma friends, should vow to “become Buddha and save sentient beings”. That is our ultimate wish. Regardless of the Pure Conduct chapter or the Samantabhadra Vows chapter, the vow that has been made is to save sentient beings, every vow is to become a Buddha, to make all sentient beings become Buddhas. Read the Prajnaparamita sutras, those sutras that are relevant to us for the sake of Prajna wisdom. In addition to these things, even pure faith and pure precepts are necessary. As for the things in life, you don't need to pray for them! The more they are, the more disturbing they are; the less they are, the more pure they are. Therefore, talking about “seeds” and “wild fields” (wild fields) in this passage is talking about Prajna, it can be explained like that!

“The reason why it is so” (Why): Why does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva have so much merit? The Buddha again praised Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. “Testing the good man” (This good man) means Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. “I have gone through countless, countless great kalpas” (Having gone through countless, countless great kalpas): It has been a very long time, time that cannot be counted.

“Over the number of Buddhas, World-Honored Ones” (Where it is impossible to count Buddhas, World-Honored Ones): Using numbers to calculate, there is no way to calculate the places of Buddhas, World-Honored Ones. “World-Honored Buddha” is the Buddhas. The Bodhisattva made a vow of great diligence and steadfastness. Not only diligent, but also steadfast, absolutely unshakable. I vow to not waver, I must definitely reach my goal. Everyone should check for themselves whether their own vows are wavering or not? While you are suffering, or when you encounter an unsatisfactory realm, or while you are repenting, obstacles arise, or while reciting sutras, obstacles arise, do you still remember? You worship but don't succeed, do you still worship? If you can't overcome those small things, how can you hope to become a Buddha? Therefore, the vow must be solid. Encountering any hardship or difficulty, once you have made your vow, do not let the external realms change, persevere, and do not interrupt midway.

You make the smallest vow to receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts. When taking refuge, the transmission master will tell you and teach you to “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”. If you can recite it many times a day, it will be even better. If you really don't have time to recite, keep reciting morning and evening, at least ten times. Can you do it? Even if you can't fulfill such a vow, how can you avoid disaster? It is impossible to avoid immediate disasters, there is no need to talk about avoiding disasters from countless lifetimes up to now, [nor is there a need to talk about] eliminating disaster karma, attaining Prajna wisdom, and even becoming a Buddha!

Suppose that the current realm brings loss to us, but is very useful to others, would we be willing to suffer losses to help others? Each person should ask their own mind and they will immediately know and understand clearly. Due to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow and vow to mature sentient beings, he often maintains the entire earth, not just the Sa Ba world. In the above section it is also said, “depending on the place, depending on the season” (anywhere, according to the nature), wherever He is, there will be benefits, causing the entire great earth to benefit all sentient beings. That is the transport function of the earth. If there was no earth to support us, we wouldn't be able to survive! Without the great earth that gives birth to all things, we would not be able to survive! If the oil under the earth is now exhausted, if no electricity is generated, how will we live? Especially in developed countries, if there is no electricity, you won't even have food to eat. Currently, winter is coming, the weather is very cold, if there is no electricity, how will the heating system work? It will make you freeze!

“Usually maintain all great earths” (Usually maintain throughout all great earths): “Great earths” refers to the mind of all sentient beings, creating seeds to become Buddha for all sentient beings. “Usually universal abbot maintains all seeds” (Usually maintains all seeds). In terms of worldly appearance, it will be the great earth containing all the seeds. All food, which is necessary for life and helps us sustain life, comes from the earth. Now let's raise our eyes and see, our eyes are covered with glasses, the clothes on our bodies, even the tables, chairs, benches, you say: Is there anything that does not come from the earth? Is there anything that does not grow from the earth? Therefore, it is said that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva made a vow, He maintained all the great earth, maintained all the seeds, allowed all sentient beings to enjoy them at will, satisfying the wishes of sentient beings.

Due to the divine power of that good man, it is possible to make the earth, grass, roots, tendrils, sprouts, trunks, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, all grow, even herbs, grains, rice, fruits luxuriantly, densely, growing fresh, fragrant, pure, soft, delicious, in places Wherever he is, he matures all sentient beings. These are things that help life. It is said that living beings themselves have everything and can eat anything!

(Sutra) Depending on the place, sentient beings are weak, greedy, angry, ignorant, evil, destructive, and destructive. birth, or non-attachment, or evil desires, or corrupt speech, or coarse and evil speech, or broken speech, or impure speech, or greed, or anger, or subjugation to wrong views, the Ten Evil Karmas.
(Sutra: Anywhere, if sentient beings, greed, anger, ignorance, etc. are strong force, killing, or taking without giving, or wanting to commit evil deeds, or speaking false words, or harsh words, or slanderous words, or impure words, or greed, or anger, or wrong views, ten evil karma paths).

Killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, these are three karma in the body. Killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct are the three karmas of the body, plus lying, speaking harsh words, embellishing words, and double-talking are the four karmas of the mouth, and adding greed, anger, and ignorance are the karmas of the mind, forming the Ten Evil Karmas. The Ten Evil Karmas, greed, anger, and wrong views are extremely strong. Wrong views are sometimes ignorance, very strong. Because of the intensity, the anger is heavy. Therefore, killing, stealing, not giving but taking, people don't give, you just take, or raping, or stealing, all belong to the category of theft. “Tao” is to use force to take, “confiscate” is to steal. Those who do not believe in the Three Jewels do not have this predestined relationship and their evil karma is very heavy. The more people like that, the more difficult it is to see and hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) A powerful mind recites the name, chants, pays homage, makes offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, one Eliminate all afflictions, abandon the Ten Evils, and achieve the Ten Goods. All sentient beings, develop a compassionate mind and gain a beneficial mind. Try the good man to achieve such achievements as merit, wonderful concentration, mighty power, courageous diligence, one real moment, immeasurable energy of countless Buddha lands, one middle level, one real moment, the level of liberation from immeasurable amounts of Ganga, the transformation of sentient beings, the spirit of separation from all suffering, attaining peace and happiness, at any time, attaining peace in heavenly birth, the path of Nirvana.
(Sutra: Can single-mindedly recite the name, chant, worship, respect, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, all afflictions were destroyed, he separated from the Ten Evils, achieved the Ten Virtues, and developed a mind of compassion and benefit towards sentient beings. That good man achieved such merit, wonderful concentration, and majestic power, with great diligence, in the span of one meal, in countless Buddhalands, in each realm, in the span of one meal, he was able to save countless sentient beings who were as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. causing them to leave all sufferings, be at peace and happy, and, depending on their nature, deserve to be saved, and rest in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana).

If you can hear about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you can wholeheartedly recite his name, chant, worship, and respectfully make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and all afflictions will be eliminated. Why? Because of his sincerity, he recites the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The appearance of that realm and your mind can match, the mind and the realm are one, of course the Ten Evil Karmas can be eliminated. The Ten Evils turn into the Ten Goods, which can turn into the Ten Good Karmas. The Ten Goodnesses are the root to give birth to heaven, and are the source of food (thought in the path of karma) to be born to heaven. If you don't have the Ten Good Karmas, you won't be able to be born in heaven, you won't have that blessing! On this basis, it is possible to develop a mind of compassion towards all sentient beings, to eliminate all the suffering of sentient beings, to give joy to all sentient beings, to benefit all sentient beings, without considering ourselves. If you make a vow to be like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and practice according to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and can achieve such merit, wonderful concentration, and divine power, exactly like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

When it comes to courage and diligence, it's very difficult! If we can practice (strongly, diligently) for five or six hours every day, we will feel that our practice is very wonderful. Holding on to time in the East, holding on to time in the West, I'm afraid I won't be able to reach eight hours, which is still not enough to be brave! Courage is day and night, six periods of time, for twenty-four hours with a single-minded and courageous mind, not caring about one's life, truly courageous and single-minded, earnestly reciting the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, thinking of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Due to his miraculous concentration and mighty, diligent spirit, he was able to enter infinite and endless miraculous concentration within the span of one meal, that is, “one moment of real food”. In the previous section, we said “endless realms”. He can abide in countless Buddha lands. Everywhere, in countless Buddha realms, in millions of Buddha realms, He can save countless, countless, countless sentient beings, save that many sentient beings, make that many sentient beings be able to leave suffering, no longer suffer pain, and make those sentient beings be at peace. "According to the occasion", that is, following the basis to preach the Dharma, depending on the basis to give the Dharma for salvation, that is, according to the basis of how that person should be saved, placing them in the path of heavenly birth, Nirvana.

(Sutra) Test the good man, achieve the inconceivable theory of merits and virtues, firmly vow wish, be brave and diligent, and mature all sentient beings in desire, in the ten directions.
(Sutra: This good man accomplished the inconceivable meritorious dharmas as I said, I swear. vow to be steadfast, courageous, and diligent, in order to mature all sentient beings in the ten directions.

For causing countless sentient beings to leave suffering and be happy, causing them to attain Nirvana, what inconceivable power does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva have? What are the dharmas of salvation? Next, clearly state His salvation method. "The meritorious dharmas are inconceivable as I say" (The meritorious dharmas are inconceivable as I said): Vow to be steadfast, courageous, and diligent, hoping to mature all sentient beings. How does He do it? The Buddha said that he is in the worlds of the ten directions, for the benefit of sentient beings, and manifests as companions. [That is] whatever species of living beings you belong to, He appears in that species to save you, a total of forty-two types.

(Sutra) Or at the present time the Great Brahma King himself, sentient beings like him, preach the Dharma, or recreate the work of the Great Brahma King. The heavenly body, or the creation of the Desire Realm Alienation and Freedom, or the creation of the Blissful Transformation God body, or the creation of the Do Su Da God body, or the creation of the Da Ma Celestial body, or the creation of the Emperor Thich God body, or the creation of the Four Great Kings, or the creation of the Buddha body, or the creation of the Bodhisattva body, or the creation of the Pratyekabuddha body, or the creation of the Shravaka body.
currently in the body of the Great Self in the Heaven, or in the body of the Thach Hoang Tu in the Desire Realm, or in the body of the Lac Vang Hoa Thien, or in the body of Do Su Da Thien, or in the body of Da Ma Thien, or in the body of Emperor Thich Thien, or in the body of the Four Great Kings, or in the body of the Buddha, or in the body of the Bodhisattva, or in the body of the Single Enlightened One, or in the body of the Sravakas).

“Or sometimes present as the body of Great Brahma King” (Or sometimes present as the body of Great Brahma King): The body of Great Brahma King is the body of Emperor Thich Thien[12], because sentient beings say dharma. Or the incarnation of the Great Self at Heaven, that is, Ma He Thu La Thien. She appeared in the form of the Great Self at Heavenly King to preach the Dharma to those living beings. Either it is the incarnation of Tha Hoa Tu In Thien in Desire Realm, or it is Lac Vang Thien, that is, Hoa Lac Thien. Or the incarnation of Do Su Da Thien, that is, Tu Suat Thien, is Luc Duc Thien. Or appear in Da Ma Thien, the third heaven. Either appearing in the form of Emperor Thich Thien, or in the body of the Four Great Heavenly Kings (also the body of the Four Heavenly Kings), or incarnating the bodies of the gods up to Brahma, Great Brahma, Six Desire Heavens, manifesting in the body of heaven to be their fellow beings, or manifesting in the body of Buddha. Bodhisattva only needs to be able to manifest Buddha's body after ascending to the first level. Until in the Avatamsaka realm, as long as one develops Bodhi mind, as long as one abides in the Non-Regression, one can manifest. Seven Pillars Bodhisattva can manifest Buddha's body.

“Or Bodhisattva body” (Or Bodhisattva body): How many Bodhisattva statuses are there? Sometimes he appears as a great Bodhisattva, sometimes he appears as a minor Bodhisattva. Say “little Bodhisattvas”, that is, ordinary Bodhisattvas, such as Bodhisattvas of the Tam Hien status. Or manifest the Two Vehicles, that is, Single Sense and Thanh Van. Single Enlightenment and Pratyekabuddha belong to the same status. Being born at the time of Buddha, relying on the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions to attain enlightenment, is Pratyekabuddha. Being born at a time when there is no Buddha, contemplating and seeing material changes: Spring is born, Summer grows, Autumn harvests, Winter stores, sees all things change, and attains enlightenment, is called Single Enlightenment. Shravaka means listening to the sound of the Buddha's sermon and attaining enlightenment. The Four Noble Dharma Realms are Buddha, Bodhisattva, Shravaka, and Pratyekabuddha. Above is the display of the four holy dharma realms.

(Sutra) Either the body of the Wheel-Turning King, or the body of the Kshat-de-benefit, or the body of the Brahmin, or Bodhisattva body, or Thudatta body, or husband's body, or woman's body, or man's body, or female companion's body, or Kien Phat's body, or Ato Lac body, or Khan Nai Lac body, or Mo Ho Lac Giay body, or Dragon body, or Medicine Rubbing body, or Rakshasa body, or Save You Dou body, or Tat Xa Giac body, or The body of the hungry ghost, or the body of the Bodhisattva, or the body of the Bodhisattva, or the body of the Viet Do Ha Lac ghost, or the body of the lion, or the body of the incense statue, or the body of the horse, or the body of the ox, or the body of the race of animals, or the body of the Demon King, or the body of the good hell, or the body of the sentient beings in hell.
Brahmin, or the body of Phiet-sham, or the body of Thu-datta, or the body of a man, or the body of a woman, or the body of a boy, or the body of a girl, or the body of Kien Dat Phuoc, or the body of A To Lac, or the body of Khan Nai Lac, or the body of Mo Ho La Gia, or the body of a dragon, or the body of Yak Xa, or the body of Rakshasa, or the body of Liu Bang Do, or the body of Siddhartha, either in the body of a hungry ghost, or in the body of Bo Dat Na, or in the body of Yet Tra Bo Da Na.

HOr take the body of the demon Viet Do Ha Lac, or take the body of a lion, or take the body of a statue, or take the body of a horse, or take the body of a buffalo, or take the body of all kinds of animals, or take the body of King Yama Ma, or take the body of a good devil in hell, or take the body of sentient beings in the underworld hell. Happears immeasurably, countless numbers of different kinds of bodies like that, for sentient beings to preach suitable Dharma, depending on their natural nature, they are placed in the path of the irreversible position in the three vehicles).

Next, the appearance of the human world appears. Or become the body of the Chakravartin-raja, or become the body of Kshat-di-li, or become the body of a small king. Kṣatriya is the seed nature (varṇa). Either it is the nature of Brahman (Brāhmaṇa), or it is Phiet-xa. Phiet-xa (Vaiśya), also known as Phiet-xa, i.e. work, agriculture, trade, is also the third of the four types of race-nature (varṇa) of India. Brahman is the most noble, Kshatriya is the second type, belonging to the royal family. Work, agriculture, and commerce are Phiet-xa. Śūdra is a slave, slaves are the lowest people.

Or the embodiment of a man, that is, the body of a man. Either the incarnation of a woman, or the incarnation of a boy or girl. Or Kien Dat Phuoc (Gandharvas, Gandharva, song god), that is, a relative of the eight classes of demons (Aṣṭasenā, the eight classes of heavenly dragons). Either Asura, Asura, or Kiṃnara, Khan Na La, musical god), or as Mac Ho Lac Gia (Mahoraga, Ma Hau La Gia). Either the body of a dragon, or the body of Yaksha, or the body of Rakshasa, or the body of Kumbhāṇḍa, or the body of Siddhartha (Piśāca), or the body of a hungry ghost, or the body of Bo-Dat-na (Pūtana), or the body of Yet-Tra-Bo-Dāna (Kaṭa-pūtana), or the body of the demon Ha-Lac, or the body of a monk. death. Next are the bodies of animals, hell, etc. Either as the body of an incense stick[13], or as the body of a horse, or as the body of a buffalo, or as the body of all kinds of animals, or as the body of Diem Demon King, or as the body of a good hell in hell, currently doing countless and countless different bodies like that.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears in many bodies in hell. He also appears in many sentient beings who have committed sins. At that time, he appeared to preach the Dharma to those who suffered that tribulation, and they would listen and accept it. In prison, there is still an epiphany and sermon. Here, we talk about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, it doesn't matter if you chant Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the most important thing is your sincere heart. Reciting Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is fine, but so is reciting Ksitigarbha. Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Manjushri, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, chant any Bodhisattva at will, as long as you can recite it at the same time. Many people at that time could not recite. Especially at the time of death, you can recite, whether you recite the name of a Bodhisattva or a Buddha, or even recite a verse from the Mahayana scriptures.

In Touch Luc, there is a passage like this: There was a person who came to the gate of hell, he only recited half a sentence "If human desires are fully understood, all three times are Buddhas" (if anyone wants to know clearly, all three times are Buddhas), hell is no more, he is also saved. Many people, when they are about to die, after falling into hell, or falling into the realm of hungry ghosts or animals, unfortunately completely forget the Buddhadharma. You can use dreams to experience, see if you still have Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha in there or not? As long as you have a thought, you can recite it and immediately wake up from the dream. Did everyone try it or not? Or recite the Great Compassion Mantra, no matter what you recite, then wake up. The unfortunate thing is that in your haste, you forget all about Buddhism. At that moment, you should chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, but the chanting will not succeed! At that time, there was no thought, only when I woke up did I think about it. Normally you don't put in any effort, so what can you do when that happens?

Therefore, it is said that when Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva wants to save sentient beings, depending on which Dharma he should listen to, which body he should use to save, He will appear in that body, also incarnate in hell, also incarnate King Yama, and even incarnate the sentient beings who are guilty, into the oil pan, up to the mountain of knives. Or when he appears, he will chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will also chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva still have to bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Let me tell you a story.

To Dong Pha and Zen master Phat An, two people came to a large temple. Su Dongpo saw the statue of Avalokiteshvara holding a rosary in his hand and immediately asked Zen master Phat An: "What is the statue of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva holding a rosary for? What else do you have to recite?" Zen master Buddha An said: "Why don't you need to recite?" To Dong Pha asked: "Who do you remember?" "He recites Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara". Hearing that, [To Dongpo was surprised]: "Does Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva still have to recite Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's name?" Zen Master Buddha An said: "That's right! Avalokiteśvara recites Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva." Su Dongpo asked again: "Do you bow to Buddha or not?" The Zen master replied: "Yes!" “Dear to whom?” Zen Master Buddha An said: "O Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara". Everyone, please think about what the meaning is? At that moment, Su Dongpo became enlightened, was it a great enlightenment or not? A little enlightenment, praying to others is not as good as praying to yourself!

Therefore, I tell you again: You reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is reciting yourself. Your mind is Ksitigarbha mind, Ksitigarbha mind is your mind. You have forgotten yourself, you have not put yourself into it. Just reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's blessing will be quite small. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Prajna wisdom shines upon you, your Prajna wisdom and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Prajna wisdom combined, your self-nature will be called Ksitigarbha self-nature. Every thought originates from the mind, every thought returns to the mind. Therefore, praying to others is not as good as praying to yourself.

However, when you yourself are not spiritual, you still have to pray to others. When praying to others, think of yourself. When you pray for yourself, you are praying for others. You have to think a lot, meditate a lot, and have a decent amount of effort to be able to produce equivalent effects. You often think like that, reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is reciting yourself, reciting yourself is also reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In this way, your dreams will be even better, your dreams will be extremely victorious. What dream? Awakened from the dream, all dreams are awakened. Now we are in a dream, I am here talking in my sleep, you are here listening in my dreams. Wait until I don't talk in my sleep, you don't listen in your dreams, everyone will have achieved it. Wishing everyone good luck and success soon.

(Sutra) Good man! Like the Great Being who accomplished such inconceivable meritorious dharmas, like those who conquered the virtuous and virtuous treasures, like those who liberated the precious treasures of origin, like Bodhisattvas who clear their eyes and eyes, and like Nirvana's beasts of merchants and Taoists, like those who have the power to turn the great wheel of dharma, like this, it is preached like before.
(Sutra: O good man! Such a Great Being accomplishes inconceivable meritorious dharmas such as Therefore, it is the treasury of supreme merits, the birthplace of liberating treasures, the clear eyes of Bodhisattvas, the guide for businessmen to reach Nirvana, to the point of being able to turn the great wheel of Dharma in vain like that, as extensively stated above).

Those are the forty-two types of bodies of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as mentioned above, which body should be used to attain salvation, so he manifested that body to preach the Dharma. Here, only the great types are mentioned, in each of which there are also countless bodies. It's like appearing to make sentient beings in hell, too many hells. When we recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, [we will see] so many hells, He can manifest all kinds of bodies. It can only be said that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's merits are inconceivable. Praise the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to make all of us turn towards and seek Bodhisattva's blessings. In the previous section, I said: This is also asking for your own mental power to bless you. But it is necessary to confront the situation and the mind to confront the situation to arise. Regarding the scene, that is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, if you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, your mind will transform into Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. What will the effect be? According to my understanding, the sincere heart becomes spiritual.

In the past few days, friends in Taiwan have called me twice, saying that two people are extremely sick, and the doctor thinks there is no way to cure them. The father of a lay person was hospitalized and needed surgery, but the doctor did not dare to operate, saying it was too dangerous. That lay person called me and I said: "You yourself should sincerely recite and recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva." At that time, there was only reciting the holy name. Because as said in the previous text, just recite the holy name, with one mind and one mind, with all your heart and mind, chanting the holy thoughts, the effect will be good. There was another lay person whose sister had to be taken to Truong Canh Hospital in Lam Khau. Her condition was also very dangerous. The doctor did not dare to operate, but surgery was needed. She is in Taipei and has followed me to repent many times, but in this situation, I asked her to stop and dedicate it to her sister. In the last two days, they all called to report: "The results were very good, after the surgery they were very safe." You say: Is it effective or not? Does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva really appear? Doesn't show up! In the end, they finished the surgery, were safe, and were cured. That's the truth. In the past, we talked about too many types, even grains, flowers, and trees. This is not because the Bodhisattva is in charge of too many things, but because our minds begin to change. While your own relative is in danger, if he or she is a disciple who believes in Buddha, the effect will be even better. If they do not believe in Buddha, they must rely on other blessings, the effect will not necessarily be authentic or certain. But if you have an urgent mind, you can still get results. Therefore, saying “asking the master for blessings”, which master can bless it?

In the above section, we said: “Praying for others is not as good as praying for yourself”. Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) also bows to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, which means this. Is there blessing or not? Of course there is. When you invite several masters to recite sutras, or invite your own master to take refuge while worshiping, it is also okay. But that merit is not necessarily from the master, but mostly from one's own relatives, as well as one's own concern. If that master's great compassion is not complete, like me, I don't necessarily care about that person very much, and someone else called to introduce me, I have never met before, even if I am interested, I can only think of that person's full name, chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's compassion, pray for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's blessings, visualize [like this], it is absolutely not as good as asking for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva himself. If you can wholeheartedly recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, pay homage to and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, all afflictions, all illnesses, sufferings, and disasters will be eliminated. Pointing out these things is only to increase everyone's confidence!

That merit comes from cultivating countless lifetimes, that is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. “Such a Great Being” (Such a Great Being) refers to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He achieved such inconceivable merit, benefiting all sentient beings, skillful means. We all benefit because of the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. To what extent does he have inconceivable merit? Like a treasure, like a hidden treasure, you just need to dig it up to find it. How to excavate? When claiming the title, it means excavating. As long as you sincerely recite “Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”, you can recite it with all your heart and mind.

To say “use your heart and mind” means that when reciting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you recite it to the point of clarity, clearly, not dull, not distracted, your mind is clear and lucid, reciting every word like that. While you recite, you will connect with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and your wishes will arise effectively. Who should you thank? We must thank Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. “This is a treasure trove of superior merits virtues and virtues” (Is a treasure trove of superior merits): That is to say, visualize His superior merits like a treasure. That treasure contains merit that benefits sentient beings.

“The origin of the treasures of liberation” (The birthplace of the treasures of liberation): Liberation itself is the treasure. This thing is invisible, formless, what must it be like to be liberated? Emptiness, Formless, Wishless, ultimate liberation. While we pray, there is no need to pray (the subject of prayer) and to seek (the thing we wish for). At that time, we will be liberated, just like a precious treasure. “Treasure” is a figurative expression to visualize liberation. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is the birthplace of the treasure of liberation. If we wish for precious treasures, for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, it will be like when Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva just arrived at this assembly, all sentient beings in the Mahayana assembly saw the Ma Ni jewel appear in both hands. The Ma Ni jewel appeared with countless precious gems. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is all the precious treasures of liberation.

“The eye of the Bodhisattvas is pure” (The pure eyes of the Bodhisattvas) is the pure dharma eye. Let's consider this problem: The eye is a cloudy thing, not clearly distinguishing right from wrong. If you receive a parcel and know it is a bomb, you will absolutely not open it. Because I didn't know whether it was a disaster or a blessing, [that's why I opened it]. When we see good things, our hearts are filled with immense joy. Actually, that is a disaster. Like in Taiwan, they pay great attention to having children, thinking it is happiness. When it matures, it causes you trouble and causes your family to go bankrupt. That's the root of disaster! How do you know? Basically don't know! Because there are no pure eyes, that is speaking from a worldly perspective.

According to Buddhism, what dharma allows you to be enlightened, liberated, and accomplished? I don't have that kind of dharma vision, I don't know what we practiced in our previous lives. Therefore, I groped. This master preaches sutras, you also listen. The other master told you to recite the Buddha's name, so you also recited it. Another master told me to recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you should also practice it. Reciting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, you also recite. Which Bodhisattva is suitable for your ability? Just try, because you don't have that insight.

“Minh” means to have wisdom, “pure” means pure. That is the dharma eye, but also the pure dharma eye. With a pure Dharma eye, you can see the essence of all dharmas. This is also very deep, all dharmas are inherently unborn, undying, unchangeable, impure. This kind of realm must be reached for it to be ultimate; That is pure eye-eye. So Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is all Bodhisattvas. You want to end life and death, want to pray for Buddha Dharma, want to seek enlightenment, want to attain liberation, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will help and bless you, making your eyes bright and your heart bright.

“The Nirvana Trader Taoist Market Beast” (The one who guides traders to Nirvana): Nirvana means “no birth, no death”. Now everyone is looking forward to Nirvana. Towards Nirvana is the will of birth and death. Through birth and death, one will attain ultimate liberation, just like a merchant who wants to go into the sea to collect treasure, must have someone to guide and help him. If you want to move towards Nirvana, you must have a guru (guide, guide). Who are you looking for? Find Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is the one who guides you towards Nirvana, like a merchant entering the sea to collect treasures [with an experienced person to guide you].

“It is useless to turn the great wheel of dharma, as it was previously preached” (So it is possible to turn the great wheel of dharma without any use, as detailed in the previous section): Why do we stay in this precious place of liberation, hoping to achieve Emptiness, Formlessness, and Wishlessness? Because when Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does those things, He does not rely on merit, does not rely on cultivation[14], but can make what we desire be achieved. We pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, even claim the holy name, achieve what we desire, and transform our circumstances. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also does not release light, nor does he appear. Some people say they will emit light, they will manifest themselves, they will see their true form, but they don't exist, they just need to achieve their desired goal. That's called “useless”. When we practice, it is possible to achieve things naturally without relying on our own merits. That is very difficult! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva turns the great Dharma wheel without any intention. In one thought, in countless worlds, He manifests countless bodies, saves countless sentient beings, and quickly appears at the same time. That is “useless”. Because a lot has been said in the previous section, it is said “as before advertised”.

(Sutra) Good man! Suppose a sentient being in the Maitreya period, attains Miraculous Auspiciousness, pure Avalokiteśvara, Samantabhadra, the child of the upper hand, the Ganga Sa class of great Bodhisattvas, Mahasattvas, in the middle of hundreds of eons, wholeheartedly takes refuge, names, chants, worships, makes offerings, prays for all the wishes, no matter what the sentient beings are like in the real moment, wholeheartedly takes refuge, names, recites, worships, makes offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, prays All wishes, quickly attain fulfillment.
(Sutra: Good man! Suppose there is someone in the place of the great Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas like Maitreya, and Miraculous Cat Tuong, along with Avalokiteshvara and Samantabhadra, are the foremost beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges River. In a hundred lifetimes, if in a hundred lifetimes, wholeheartedly taking refuge, naming names, chanting, worshiping, making offerings, wishing for prayers, is not as good as someone who, in the span of one meal, wholeheartedly takes refuge, confesses names, chants, worships, and makes offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, their wishes will be quickly fulfilled.

“Good man” is the name the Buddha used to call the Immaculate Conception of Thich Thich. The Buddha told Sakyamuni Buddha: Suppose there is a man who has a good mind and, when wishing for liberation, prays to Maitreya Bodhisattva, or to Manjushri Bodhisattva (Magi Tuong is Manjushri Bodhisattva), or to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), or to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Not just praying to one or two, but praying to Mahasattvas Mahasattvas as many as the sands of the Ganges River, praying to that many Bodhisattvas for how long? Pray for a hundred lifetimes.

If you wholeheartedly take refuge, name, chant, and make offerings to those Bodhisattvas like that, it is not as good as “the one real moment”, “the one real moment” is the time it takes to eat a meal, wholeheartedly take refuge, name, recite, worship, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. What that person prays for will be quickly fulfilled, without the need for hundreds of lifetimes! The Buddha was still afraid that the Uncontained Being Thich Thich would be skeptical, so he explained again. Why do we say that? That is the comparison of merit, that is, the comparison between Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Maitreya Bodhisattva, Manjushri Bodhisattva, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), or Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. If compared, praying to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will be fulfilled faster, due to what reason?

(Sutra) Why is it fake? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva benefits all sentient beings in peace and happiness, and all sentient beings' souls have their wishes fulfilled, as Yī says, the heron is like the organ. Like the Great Master, the desire to mature all sentient beings, the nine cultivating steadfast great vows, great compassion, courage, and diligence, is beyond the Bodhisattvas. The ancestors and the elders are making offerings.
(Sutra: Why is that? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva benefits the peace and happiness of all sentient beings, making them The wishes of sentient beings are satisfied, like a wish-fulfilling treasure, as well as a treasure. Such a Great Being wants to mature sentient beings, so he has practiced great vows and great compassion for a long time, and is stronger and more diligent than other Bodhisattvas. Therefore, you should make offerings.

“What's the reason?” (Why) has the meaning of asking: Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva benefits and brings happiness to all sentient beings, causing the wishes of sentient beings to be satisfied like the Nhu Y Bao Chau, like the “restore organ” (treasure) mentioned in the previous section? He stores countless wishes. This Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva "has matured all sentient beings in their desire, has cultivated steadfastly great compassion, courage, and diligence" (in order to mature all sentient beings, he has cultivated great compassion and great compassion for a long time, steadfastly, courageously, and diligently), he cultivates great compassion and great diligence. “Exceeding Bodhisattvas” means going beyond the Bodhisattvas mentioned in the previous section such as Maitreya, Dieu Cat Tuong, Samantabhadra.

“ Thi co, like you should make offerings” (Therefore, you should make offerings), we explain this sentence more. Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, up to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), these are the four great Bodhisattvas we are most familiar with. The Dharma we learn, speaking according to this world, that is, the Sa Ba world, is not of Maitreya Bodhisattva, it is also of Manjushri Bodhisattva, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), or Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Why did the Buddha use these four great Bodhisattvas to compare? Because now we are talking about the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, not talking about the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra. If you preach the Maha Prajnaparamita Sutra, there is only Miraculous Bodhisattva, that is, only Manjushri Bodhisattva is shown. If you preach the Maitreya Sutra, there will only be Maitreya Bodhisattva. Now we are talking about the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, so when preaching a sutra and wanting to highlight a Bodhisattva, the Buddha will use other Bodhisattvas to compare, that is Hien, in order to make you give rise to the mind of superiority, because the discrimination in the minds of sentient beings is especially heavy. Whoever has great merit, people will look for him, that's what they think.

Actually, praying to others is not as good as praying to yourself, you should understand this principle. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva compared to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) and Manjushri Bodhisattva, which one has greater merit? Manjushri Bodhisattva became a Buddha in the past, but now [appears] has not yet become a Buddha, appearing as a Bodhisattva. Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) in the past also became Buddha, they are all Ancient Buddhas. But in the human mind, we will have a discriminatory mind.

When teaching this sutra, the Buddha especially praised Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying that he had strong vows and strong compassion. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is the Great Compassion Avalokiteśvara, the same great compassion. Because we are currently studying the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the Buddha especially appreciated the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Sentient beings are saved by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the place where he comes, the place where sentient beings are saved is in the three evil destiniess, this is very sublime, is it possible that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is not like that? Isn't the hungry ghost Diem Nhien Dai Si in the Diem Khau worshiping ceremony manifested by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva? Buddha and Buddha are in the same path. Amitābha Buddha is not higher than Śākyamuni Buddha, nor is Medicine Buddha higher than Śākyamuni Buddha. If there was no Śākyamuni Buddha, we would not know what Medicine Buddha is, what Amitābha Buddha is? Some people chant Amitābha Buddha and forget all about Śākyamuni Buddha. Some people only know Amitābha Buddha, even Śākyamuni Buddha doesn't understand it very well! Buddha has no obstacles of jealousy, unlike ordinary people. We will say: "I introduced it to you, but you forgot all about me. You only remember that person, not bothering to remember me!" That's not called Buddha!

My point is that while reading and reciting this sutra, wholeheartedly take refuge, name, chant, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva vows to be steadfast, courageous, and diligent, far surpassing Maitreya, Miraculous, Avalokiteshvara, Samantabhadra. The Buddha also spoke truthfully, never lying, but in this sutra, he specifically mentioned Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If we speak according to the Ksitigarbha Sutra, even Manjushri Bodhisattva, Void Store Bodhisattva, and Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) all praise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you recite the Universal Gate chapter, [you will see the scriptures teach] making offerings to sixty-two millions of Ganga Sa Bodhisattvas that much, is not as good as making offerings to Avalokiteshvara in about one meal, the meaning is the same!

The reason I say so is because there are Dharma friends present here reciting the Universal Gate chapter, and there are also people reciting the Samantabhadra Virtue Vows. If we say: "Just reciting the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra is enough, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's merits are so great that they surpass those of others." Mistake is gone! Bodhisattvas are all the same, their merits are all the same. Regarding this Bodhisattva, if we learn a little, we will be able to enjoy and achieve achievements.

(Sutra) At the ear of the time, the great assembly of the ten directions, Bodhisattva and Mahasattva of all places, the Shravakas, Gods, people, Yak Xa, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the stage of the pine tree, depending on the power of the force, the lineages of gold and silver, the assembly of flowers, incense, and phoenixes scattering Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. Pmaintain the strains of superior wonderful clothes, mani jewels, mandarin pearls, jade pearls, and gold. Silver treasure floods, fields, phan, one level, worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. Surrendering to immeasurable wonderful music, all kinds of people praise and respectfully make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.
(Sutra: At that time, a great assembly came from the ten directions, all the Bodhisattvas, Mahasattvas and The Shravakas, gods, humans, Yaoc Xoa, Kien Dat Phuoc, etc. all stood up from their seats, each holding various pieces of gold, silver, etc., precious flowers, incense, and offering them to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. They also held the best clothes, Manhini jewels, pearl garlands, pearl necklaces, precious strings of gold and silver, rosaries, phantoms, parasols, etc., and offered them to Ksitigarbha. Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat also uses countless wonderful music and all kinds of praise to respectfully make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

“At that time, great assemblies from ten directions came” (At that time, great assemblies from ten directions came): This Great Assembly cannot be counted in number, nor can Bodhisattvas be counted in number, it is not possible to use numbers to know how many Bodhisattvas, Sravakas, and Pratyekabuddhas there are in it. The Buddha's sermons are all like that. The great assembly from the ten directions came to attend the meeting, that is, all the Bodhisattvas, Mahasattvas, as well as Shravakas, devas, Yaksha, eight groups of ghosts and spirits, hearing the Buddha praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva all stood up from their seats. “According to your strength” is to do your best, whatever your strength is, you will make offerings to it. What offerings? It is “metal, silver, equal elements, they treasure flowers, incense, and phoenixes to scatter Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat” (pieces of gold, silver, etc., incense, precious flowers, offered and scattered to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat), making offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva with all their might. In each dharma assembly, Bodhisattvas and Buddhas will make offerings. In the assembly, at that time, the Buddhas coming from other directions all made offerings to Sakyamuni Buddha, and also made offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Standing up from his seat, hearing the Buddha praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, he immediately, according to his ability, did not return [to his own realm] to make preparations, but also offered whatever he had brought with him. “Depending on the power of action” this is how offerings are made, everyone uses things like gold, silver, and jewels to make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

There are also people who “keep the race of superior and wonderful clothes” (hold good clothes). The wonderful clothes are as stated in the Ksitigarbha Sutra and in all other sutras. When you are about to wear new clothes, make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva first. When you are about to eat delicious food, you should make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva first. Even making offerings to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva are all like that. Even a newly purchased toy is offered to the Bodhisattva first. Whatever you think is good and want to use, you should first offer it to the Bodhisattva. If you cultivate that habit, your merit will be inconceivable.

Next, there are also mani (mani) jewels, garlands of pearls, beads of pearls, strings of gold and silver, garlands, phantoms, and parasols, offered to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. There are also countless wonderful music and musical instruments, either singing songs, or singing praise songs, or all kinds of praise to respectfully make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. But after Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva receives those offerings, what will he do? In the Universal Gate chapter, Endless Mind Bodhisattva offered alms to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), but Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva did not accept it.

Infinite Mind Bodhisattva again requested, after that, it was necessary to ask the Buddha to remind Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to have mercy on Infinite Mind Bodhisattva and the masses attending the Dharma assembly, then Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) would accept. After receiving it, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva immediately divided the offered object into two parts, one part was offered to the Many Treasures Tower, the other part was offered to Śākyamuni Buddha. In this assembly, only the Buddha was present, so Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva brought all the offerings, that is, all the belongings of everyone, to the World-Honored One. Not only making offerings, but also saying verses of praise.

(Sutra) At the ear time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, reciting the sublime lineage of worship The old man, returned to worship the World-Honored One, and recited and wrote: "The gods, humans, dragons, gods make offerings, the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions come and go. Van Cuu Thas great merit, only the wish to receive the supreme self is superior."
(Sutra: At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva again held the most sublime offering The World-Honored One, then recited verses: "Heaven, humans, dragons, and gods have made offerings, Bodhisattvas from ten directions have come to offer, hearing the Savior's great merit, respectfully accept the supreme offerings."

The offerings I hold in my hand are offered to me by heaven, humans, dragons, gods, and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, and I respectfully offer them to the World-Honored One. Everyone knows that the World-Honored One is a savior of great merit, and I respectfully look forward to receiving your supreme offering. They made offerings to me, so I made offerings to the World-Honored One.
