After Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva recited that verse, he bowed at the Buddha's feet and returned to his seat. At that time, the Buddha recited verses to praise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) “Initiation solidity Hui Thanh Purify the mind, destroy all sentient beings with immeasurable suffering. Give them wonderful happiness like a guard, destroy the net like a diamond, initiate great compassion and diligence, and maintain the wonderful wisdom of worshiping the World-Honored One.
(Sutra: “Raise a pure mind, solid wisdom, eliminating immeasurable suffering for sentient beings. Like a precious hand offering wonderful pleasures, like a diamond cutting the net Or, arousing great compassion, being diligent, skillfully making offerings to the World-Honored One, using the ocean of wisdom to save suffering beings, and save all paths. shore of fearlessness”).

Buddha said: "You make offerings very skillfully. You have steadfast wisdom

unchanging, attaining all dharma-natures." Are we not talking about the realm of One Truth? The mind in the realm of One Truth is the true mind, but also the wonderful wisdom of the true mind. At the same time, he can destroy countless sufferings of all sentient beings, giving away extremely wonderful music. “Conservative” (The precious hand) is the mysterious hand that plays music, but can also eliminate all the doubts of sentient beings like vajra. Vajra wisdom can cut off all the nets of afflictions. "Starting with great compassion and diligence" means having great compassion and wisdom to save sentient beings

“The skillful holding of magical offerings to the World-Honored One” (Skillfully holding miraculous offerings to the World-Honored One): His offerings are very wonderful. When this great Bodhisattva made offerings to the Buddha, all the offerings underwent a transformation, combining all the treasures into a treasure parasol, or a phantom, which was not the original material. Like everyone making offerings to Buddha, we only see apples, fruits, or pears, or incense or flowers, but through the transformation of offerings, the flowers and incense fill the ten directions of the world. If you make offerings and have read the third great vow in the Samantabhadra Vows chapter, which is “extensive practice of offerings”, then when you put the garland in the flower basket to make offerings to the Buddha, if you know how to make offerings, you will definitely practice visualization. Fellow Dharma friends, you should practice like that. If you have never practiced, I will remind you a bit.

You have to visualize that garland, don't think it's only that big. Use your mind power to make the entire emptiness and the entire dharma realm turn into that garland. At first glance, that flower garland seems to only be offered in this Sa Ba world, or offered in On Ca Hoa (Vancouver), but it has spread throughout the Sa Ba world, will go to the Pure Land world to make offerings to the Pure Land world of Amitābha Buddha, and also to the world of Medicine Master Lapis la Light Tathagata in the East. If we don't know much, we only know Amitābha Buddha in the West, everyone is very familiar with that place, or the Oriental Medicine Master Lapis La Light Tathagata, because we often recite the Medicine Master Sutra, or the Buddhas in the upper or ten directions, and even bow to Chiem Sat Sam, among which are the names of fifty-three very familiar Buddhas! Imagine the flower garland covering every Buddha realm, every Buddha and Bodhisattva. That is “offering intention”. Thus, the flower garland is not just the state it is in front of the eyes, but everything will arise and change. Who initiates change? Due to the blessing of the practitioner, that is, the practitioner. It is also because of the four groups of disciples, monks, nuns, upasakas, and upasakas, when making offerings, they rely on their mental power to make offerings. That is called “miraculous offering”. That way of offering is inconceivable.

At the same time, your wisdom is as deep as the ocean, as big as the ocean, forever saving sentient beings who are suffering, infinitely, endlessly. The sea water will never dry up, thousands of rivers and canals flow into the sea, and the sea water will never increase. The wisdom of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is as deep as the sea, as wide as the sea, and can accommodate everything, allowing all sentient beings, that is, sentient beings in all paths, to reach the other shore and to become Buddhas. We can't even say verses of praise. When Buddhas and Bodhisattvas praise, they use very wonderful language and writing, with enormous transformations. We know: “Reaching the other shore” is becoming Buddha, but He did not say “the other shore”, but “the shore of fearlessness”, or “the shore of wisdom, the shore of Prajna”. That is the cleverness of writing.

(Sutra: At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva immediately stood up from his seat and said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One! Con will protect the disciples of the World-Honored One in these four great continents, all the monks, Bhiksunis, Upasakas, Upasakas, causing them all to increase in thinking, increase in keeping in mind, increase in longevity, increase in body, increase in freedom from illness, increase in beauty, increase in reputation, increase in things needed, increase in friends, increase in disciples, increase in pure precepts, increase in learning, increase in wisdom, increase in wonderful concentration, increase in patience, increase in means, increase in holy awareness. the enlightenment of the truth, the growth of entering the Mahayana holy path, the growth of Dharma insight, the growth of maturity in sentient beings, the growth of great compassion, the growth of all the white dharma, the growth of mysterious praise throughout the three worlds, the growth of the rain of Dharma that permeates the three worlds, the growth of the quintessence of the flavors of all the earth, the growth of the quintessence of the well-done career of all sentient beings, the growth of the virtuosity of good deeds of the Dharma, the growth of luminous wisdom, the growth of the wonderful conduct of the Six Paramitas Secret, growth of the five eyes, growth of empowerment, growth of Nirvana”).

“At that moment, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, on the throne, arose and spoke to the Buddha" (At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva immediately stood up from his seat and said to the Buddha): After making offerings to the Buddha, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva returned to his seat, and the Buddha again praised: "You have made a very good offering!" Reciting the verses, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva again stood up from his seat, paid homage to the Buddha, turned to the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One”. Call the Buddha “Great”.“Great” means immeasurable. In all the sutras, whenever the Buddha talks about the Great, it means talking about our Body, the realm of One Truth, or saying “wonderful true mind”, or saying “Tathagata organ nature” is fine. Although the names are different, they are all fake names. But in reality, it is just one word Dai. The Great Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra and the Mahayana Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra are both Great. This word Dai means “substance” (its own essence).

Praising Buddha's merits as “great virtue” has such a meaning. World-Honored One! You should follow the Buddha's teachings. For this world, that is, as we often say “the four great continents”, [also translated by Huyen Trang as] “test the four continents”. “World-Honored One” (disciple of the World-Honored One) means a disciple of Śākyamuni Buddha (“four groups” including O-so, O-soni, O-ba-sach-ca, O-ba-tu-ca, these are two monks and two lay people. Monks are monks, bhikshunis, lay people are male lay followers and female lay followers, as well as are the Male Attendants and the Female Attendants), you both help them increase their memories.

“Growing memories” means growing wisdom. Is it true that we have no memory? In chapter twelve of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it is said: Read the sutra without memory, after reading it you will forget it, teach it once and you will not be able to remember it, teach it several times and you will not remember it. That means having no memory, having learned but not being able to remember. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: "You can help them and make them increase their memories." The growth of memory here of course refers to reciting Buddha, reciting the Dharma, and reciting the Sangha. Therefore, "they have faith and have learned the Dharma, I will help them grow." That is called “the mind of higher growth”, it is necessary to recite the thoughts of growth, the thoughts of higher growth. The more you grow, the greater your wisdom, the heavier your blessings, that's the meaning.

“Growing and protecting memories”, must preserve memories, why? When sleeping, you must recite “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, or early in the morning, as soon as you open your eyes, recite “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, protect the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha of the Three Jewels, thousands of times, don't lose them. That is the meaning of “guardian”, just like we protect property.

“Increase life span”: First, from shallow to deep. That is following the wishes of living beings. No one wants to have a short life, unless they are so sad and miserable that they don't want to live anymore. There are still people who commit suicide, why? Because it's so miserable, I can't bear to live anymore, I have no interest in continuing to live. Therefore, saying “increase longevity” is everyone's wish. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately turned to the Buddha and made a vow to help the disciples who were taught by him in the four great continents, saying “four continents” specifically refers to the Southern Thiem Bo Chau, Northern Cau La Chau (North Cau Lu Chau), Dong Thang Than Chau, and Tay Nguu Ha Chau (Tay Nguu Hoa Chau), referring to those four great continents.

“Body growth”: There is an explanation for this story, either hoping for a healthy body, or hoping for a body that is very ugly and rough, hoping to become a little more beautiful, a little more handsome. Or maybe you feel too small and wish you were a little bigger. Therefore, “physical growth” has many types, which is also what you wish for. You are inherently disease-free. If you grow your body, you will never get sick. That is “diseaseless growth”. “Increasing your physical strength” is the growth of your physical strength.

“Growth in famous writers” is what we long for, everyone hopes to have a good reputation. “Increase in personal belongings”: “Instruments” are the necessary items in life that help you survive, including houses, cars, necessary items, etc., which can all be complete. “Growing disciples”: Refers to the Buddha or the four great disciples of the Buddha. Regardless of whether they are monks or lay people, everyone wants to have a slightly larger group of disciples. Some people don't necessarily wish to have many things. The large number of disciples is very troublesome, and the children and grandchildren are also very troublesome; but that is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow, not the same as what follows below.

“Growing pure precepts”: You receive the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, up to the monks and nuns. At home, there are the Five Precepts, the Eight Precepts, there are six major precepts, twenty-eight minor precepts [in the lay precepts of Bodhisattvas], all of which can be pure and forever maintain pure precepts.

“Growing multi-literature”: Multi-literature is listening to the superior Dharma. The one who increases in hearing is Da Van. Having heard it, one is born in wisdom.

“Growing the wisdom of forgiveness”: [The wisdom of forgiveness] is almsgiving. Letting go a little deeper means letting go of the Ego, don't cling to the Self, but this requires wisdom. Discharge is very difficult. A person with wisdom can let go of everything, even his own life and life. This depends on wisdom.

“Magical growth”: What is magical growth? It is Concentration right in all actions. This is inconceivable. Currently, when you listen to the sutra and enter Concentration, you are not completely asleep, but you are truly entering Concentration, listening to the sutra and staying in Concentration. Therefore, when great Bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings, they are all in Samadhi. We see them flying back and forth, actually entering Concentration. Therefore, at the beginning of this sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva early in the morning entered that much Samadhi, all of the time, all of the places were in Samadhi.

“Grow with patience”: Patience is patience, but why didn't He say “patience”, but “patience”? Speaking from our side, we mostly do not comply with our duties. Forbearance can preserve your duty. The matter of maintaining one's duty includes many things. Because you have wisdom and wonderful Concentration, you will be able to preserve Concentration and Hue without losing it. You can harmonize and consider, making Concentration and Hue balanced. That's called An Nhan. From patience, skillful means can be born, like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva who has entered Samadhi so much and used so many means to benefit sentient beings. That is skillful means. There is wisdom, so wisdom of means is born. Because you have wisdom, all means are liberating. If there is no wisdom, the means will be bondage. For example, no matter what we do, we encounter obstacles on all sides. You also have the mind to save sentient beings, but you cannot save them. Even so, many kinds of troubles still arise, troubles arise in all directions. That's because you don't have skillful wisdom, so you don't handle it properly!

“Growing the enlightenment part of the noble truth of light”: The enlightenment part is the Bodhi path. The Seven Sense Parts are separate. Growing Bodhi means growing one's own enlightenment. That enlightenment can make your holy truth clear. The Holy Truth is to be able to rely on the True Truth and Truth Body to attain sainthood, even becoming a Buddha is possible. The Bodhisattvas of the Ten Grounds are also saints, and according to the original teachings, the Four Fruits of Arhats are also the Holy Truths; That dharma is called the Four Noble Truths. “Increasing the light of the holy truth” means [increasing] wisdom; The Emperor himself is light.

“Growing and entering the Mahayana path”: Being able to transport your own mind is Mahayana. We say "all things cannot be separated from our mind", that is the true Bodhi path. In true Bodhi, there is no dharma outside the mind, and outside the dharma there is no mind. All dharmas are manifested by your nature. That is the true Mahayana path.

“Increase dharma clarity”: Willow dissolves the nature of all dharmas, do not make distinctions in appearance. Understanding the nature of all dharmas, this is called wisdom, called true “wisdom”.

“Growing in sentient maturity”: It's okay to say it's deep or shallow, what kind of maturity is that? Master all sentient beings; Increase your private education (ideological education). Isn't that a vow to benefit sentient beings? So, is it possible for sentient beings to mature? Is it possible for doctors to serve it? Is it possible to follow the teachings and practice to attain enlightenment? For example, the four disciples follow the Buddha's teachings to one by one transform sentient beings, so that they can all believe in them, can all follow the teachings, can all practice, and can all mature. Once you mature, you will be able to escape, allowing all sentient beings to mature. Growing the mind of great compassion is growing the Bodhi mind. Bodhi mind includes many things, great compassion is Bodhi mind.

“Grow all white dharma” (Grow all white dharma): [White dharma] means pure dharma. What is pure dharma? All the Precepts, Concentration, Wisdom, all the dharmas taught to us by the Buddha. White dharma is pure dharma, eliminating black dharma. Black dharma is the dharma of pollution. The scriptures of the chapters Vo Y Hanh and Huu Y Hanh in the following section will talk in detail about the morality of black and white. All of the above dharmas are general theories, and will be explained clearly in the following section. In the previous section, we only gave a little general overview.

“Essential growth of sentient beings' vitality”: Having spirit, having vitality. “Tinh” is pure, “qi” is temperament. Because we are Buddha's disciples, we make the four disciples all pure, so that everyone who looks at them can see the different temperament of Buddha's disciples. Everyone who sees the temperament of Buddha's disciples is very respectful, and at the same time "skillful in doing things".

“Grow the wonderful conduct to the other shore” (Grow the wonderful conduct to reach the other shore): That is, Six Paramitas, almsgiving, precepts, patience, diligence, Meditation, wisdom; These are all wonderful and inconceivable actions that can reach the other shore and become Buddha.

“Growing the Five Eyes”: The Five Eyes are the physical eye, the heavenly eye, the wisdom eye, the dharma eye, and the Buddha eye. From the status of ordinary people until becoming Buddha, we are all flesh-eyes. Nowadays, everyone is a disgrace. There are obstacles in the physical eye. If someone else uses their hand to block it, you won't see anything. Without light, you cannot see. The physical eye has obstacles and cannot communicate. The physical eye has obstacles and is not clear, but the heavenly eye is clear and unobstructed. Thien Nhac is a reward (acquired by karma), can see everything. They can see us, but we cannot see them. The eye of wisdom illuminates all the conventional truths. The conventional truth is the means of wisdom. If you have the wisdom eye, you will contemplate the Tutu. The fourth type of eye is the dharma eye. The Dharma eye clearly understands True Emptiness, [sees clearly] the two principles of the Conventional Truth and the Ultimate Truth. The Buddha's eye illuminates everything. As for the five eyes, we now stop at the physical eye stage. But there are some special people who, due to karma, can see when they are born. That is what is currently called “special ability”. They can see things under the ground; that is good news. Animals also have this kind of ability. For example, there are foxes, weasels, [often said] “yellow willow bean fox”, sometimes snakes, that is, four types of “fairy” fox, yellow willow, willow, bean [15], and there are demons like the great ghosts and spirits we just read about in the above section. They all have magical powers, but they are not ultimate! They are still hindered, do not have eyes like the gods, [just] see a little clearly. That's called "knowledge of retribution" (magical powers come from retribution). The gods [have heavenly eyes] because of karma. The eye of wisdom and the eye of dharma can both be cultivated. The Buddha eye is the ultimate achievement. That's the Five Eyes, we'll simplify it a bit.

“Growing empowerment”: Initiation has many interpretations. Receiving the empowerment is a ritual from India. In the past, in India, [this ritual] was intended to bless the newly born baby. [That child] was born to be the Crown Prince of the king, so [the king] sought someone to practice the religion. People who practice Buddhism are not necessarily Buddhas, [monks] belonging to the six pagan sects can all use water from the four seas to sprinkle on the Crown Prince's head to eliminate disasters. When we seek the dharma, [the teacher transmitting the dharma] will use the method of pouring dharma water onto the top of the head. Currently, we learn how to practice according to Tantra, Empowerment is a specific term. There are many types of Empowerment (Abhiṣeka); Here it is said “increase empowerment” in the sense of blessing. That's talking about empowerment.

When we practice contemplation, we must also initiate initiation for ourselves. Either the Medicine Buddha contemplation, or the Amitābha Buddha contemplation is sitting on top of your head, and blesses and increases your chances of entering Nirvana. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's blessings enabled Buddhist disciples in the four great continents to gradually grow from their own existing foundation. If the capital is nothing, how can it grow? Growth based on available capital. If one has learned the method of cultivating the path, the chances of attaining the Tathagata's status will increase, or it will cause that person to escape the three paths. After that, you will be able to be born in heaven, enjoy happiness, and also be able to listen to the Dharma.

Earth Element has a solid nature. Increases the solid nature of the earth element, preventing it from breaking and causing earthquakes. The Four Great Growths are to increase the happiness of sentient beings, to increase wealth for sentient beings, to increase superior strength, and to increase the use of all things needed for life. In the above section, it was said “increase in personal tools”, repeat it here. The meaning of the repetition is that by reciting this mantra, these things will increase. This dharani can make wisdom strong and sharp, eliminating enemies' afflictions. This mantra has such great merit. That is called “dharma of cause and effect”; Whenever it meets causes and conditions, it will arise. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva wants to provide support for sentient beings, achieve us, make us leave suffering and be happy, but we do not have that cause.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses all around, but among the more than sixty billion people on this earth, I'm afraid there are too many people who have never heard the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even though I heard His name, I did not have the mind to believe in Him, I did not pray to Him, and I did not have that wish. Without that predestined relationship, how can we achieve it? Even the title is not heard! Therefore, in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught: "If you do not have a single mind, even if you recite my name, it is the same as not reciting. Even if you hear my name, it is not called 'hearing', it is the same as not having heard". Implication: You do not establish karma with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even though you hear His name, you don't have any faith or desire, and don't feel that He brings any benefit to you. Therefore, it is said that “is not called hearing”. Even though you hear it, it's like you didn't hear it! No matter how much merit He has, benefiting all, if [the listener] does not give rise to the mind of belief, to the point of not being able to believe, then is there no merit at all? That's not true! Even though you hear the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or you worship and repent without having the will, even the lower ones don't have the will, you only sow far-reaching causes. The merit has been sown, the seeds have been sown, [in the future] you will meet again, a mind of trust and love will arise, a mind of diligence will arise, and gradually you will mature!

The reason why everyone can worship like this is not in one lifetime or two lifetimes, but because of predestined relationships that have been established over many lifetimes. From now on, you can grow more and more, in this life you can leave suffering and be happy. You yourself have a place to understand the Buddha Dharma. You should always pay attention to such issues. Having met fate, you must definitely shoulder it. Regardless of suffering or joy, the cause and effect has ripened, now you accept it and must shoulder it. Whatever has passed, has no cause or condition, let it go, that is called "liberation". When encountering predestined conditions, you should receive the retribution yourself. You don't want to receive it. Even if you push it to others, it won't work. It will only increase your troubles and cause more accidents. If you bear the burden, [retribution] will be minimized. Whatever has passed, let it go, don't always be nostalgic or remember, that is, in each person's heart, whatever is in the past, let it go, if you keep lingering on it, it will cause great harm to yourself. Therefore, we must know that "dharmas born from causes and conditions" are all false. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has revealed to us a general direction. If you have such a mindset and understand this principle to study the Dharma, you will easily understand and enter. Otherwise, it will be very difficult to enter!

At the same time, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning and recited and wrote.
(Sutra: At that time, the masses heard that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva The Bodhisattva Mahasattva has accomplished countless merits worthy of praise and praise. He feels rare and unprecedented. He respects and respects him. He is filled with great joy. He meditates carefully on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. At that time, to clarify that meaning again, the World-Honored One recited this verse.)

Everyone feels a real desire, “a miracle plan” (all feel rare) that is, a feeling of victory. “Winning the position of a friend” was unheard of in the past. For Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, respect and reverence arise, and great joy arises. “The sole mind contemplates Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the eyes do not temporarily let go” (The single mind contemplates Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva carefully, eyes never leave): Observe the virtue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva entered that assembly, everyone observed him like that, carefully observing his virtues, regardless of whether he was practicing the Quan Yin method, or practicing the Manjushri method, practicing Samantabhadra Contemplation Dharma. The last chapter of the Lotus Sutra is the contemplation of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. We practice every dharma like that. Here, you must contemplate the physical appearance of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Regardless of whether you request a statue painted on paper or a porcelain statue, or even a statue cast in bronze, for any statue, as long as you feel very dignified and have a feeling of superiority, you should visualize it. Contemplation starts from His throne, or from the lotus throne, or just the contemplation from the dog named Thien Thinh in front of the seat of Nine Hoa Son Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the contemplation starts from that dog's body. It is best to meditate from the lotus seat, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sitting on the lotus, meditate on the light of that lotus flower, until the light from where Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sits cross-legged. Observe the light radiating from His body, observe the light from His head. Meditate from bottom to top, often visualize like that, so that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's halo shines on the top of your head, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's face enters your heart. In your heart there are lotus petals. Visualize yourself and visualize maturely. First, save you, then, become one with you.

You visualize like that, and also recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, for many days or months, as long as you pay attention, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is right in your mind, others see you, or you are speaking, helping others, dedicating to others, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless you. You yourself do not have any power, but because you visualize Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva like that, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will enter your body and mind, and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's power will merge with you as one. Therefore, others can gain benefits. The audience attending this dharma conference are all great Bodhisattvas. They saw the Buddha praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva like that and felt it was very rare, never heard of it, never felt it before. Therefore, respect, reverence, great joy.

Contemplating Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's technique, "not temporarily leaving" (eyes do not temporarily leave), that is, the eyes do not blink, focusing on one scene, the mind is focused. “No temporary release” and “unblinking eyes” have the same meaning. The Buddha was afraid that the audience would not fully pay attention, so he repeated it again. Below, there are a total of twenty-four chants. Each chant has four sentences, intended to praise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva again. Now we are explaining the Self chapter as the arising part, which has not yet been mentioned in the main text of the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra. It's just that before starting to preach this sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva first praised the Buddha's merits, and both sides chanted, causing the masses attending the Dharma assembly to give rise to pure faith and mind. The Buddha was afraid that the crowd still could not hear clearly, so he used the Verse Chanting technique to recite it again.

(Sutra) “Great Master Ksitigarbha, He achieved many merits, manifested the form of Thanh Van, and returned to the great master
(Sutra: “The true Great Master Ksitigarbha, with all his merits in eliminating defects, appears in the form of Thanh Van, and comes to pay homage to the Great Master).

This is the first chant. “True Great Master Ksitigarbha”: The true Great Master is neither an impersonation nor a fake. “Truth” means that He has attained the realm of One Truth, has attained the mind of Truth, has attained the nature of the Dharma. The word Chan means that. “Great Master” is a title of honor.

“Do Da”[16] means able to “eliminate all impurities, can eliminate all afflictions, transform all afflictions into success virtue”. In us is affliction, in Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is merit. He uses this to save sentient beings. But Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears in the form of Thanh Van, why does he appear in the form of Thanh Van? Thanh Van must maintain the monks' precepts and pure precepts, but he also displays many signs, which were talked about a lot in the previous section. However, in this Dharma assembly, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva manifested the form of Thanh Van. “Lai Khe Thu Great Master” (To pay homage to the Great Master), that is, to pay homage to the Buddha. Great Master is the self-proclaimed Buddha.

(Sutra) Giving to all living beings, saving the three beings of suffering, countless universes of universes, the one who makes offerings to the great master.
monk).

Give all happiness to sentient beings. This is called “evil pleasure” (bringing joy), which is the mind of great compassion. “Love” can give joy and give happiness to all sentient beings. All sentient beings are in suffering, how can they be happy? If sentient beings eliminate their suffering, they will be happy. When we walk at night, there are no lights, we hear strange, strange sounds, we are both afraid of ghosts and wild animals. In the previous section, [the scriptures] said: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva displays light like the moon, [passersby] will not be afraid, nor will they step into the wrong alley. Isn't that very happy? The Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm are three living beings, all in suffering. “Immeasurable Vu” does not mean pouring heavy rain, but pouring down countless treasures and clothes like the sky pouring rain. Why? “The one who makes offerings to the great master” means to make offerings to the Buddha.

(Sutra) Heavenly Emperor Wu Cau Sanh, observe the four directions, hold the palm together respectfully, and invite the great master.
(Sutra: Divine Emperor Wu Cau Sanh, after observing the four directions, clasp your hands, stand respectfully, praise Thank you, great master).

This is what the Buddha said in the great assembly that there is the Immaculate Conception of the Heavenly Deity. He saw all the people coming from all over to attend the conference. He was a little skeptical about this matter, but also did not understand the meaning. Therefore, the Immaculate Conception Thich Thich saw that everyone in the four directions wished to understand, so he clasped his hands, respectfully stood before the Buddha, praised him, and asked the Buddha to teach him why such inconceivable [kinds of offerings] were poured down from the sky. Each person has a Nhu Y pearl in their hand. Why are there such strange and special appearances? We respectfully ask the Buddha to preach the Dharma.

(Sutra) Self-view of the World-Honored Ones, MArni treasures bright light, illuminating all Buddha lands, without any level of clarity.
(Sutra: I see this great assembly, precious Momni radiating bright, illuminating all Buddha realms, no realm is unknown).

These are the words of the Immaculate Conception of Thich Thich towards the Buddha: "I see [in the hand] of each sentient being has the Manhni jewel (as the wish-fulfilling jewel). The mani jewel radiates light, until that light illuminates the lands in the ten directions. All lands are visible as if right before the eyes", which also means that That light clearly illuminated the appearance of the world in those Buddha lands.

(Sutra) Luc Thong illuminates the world, the golden future is determined, the mighty name Ksitigarbha, appears majestically as a monk.
(Sutra: Luc Thong illuminates the world, now the one coming here, the mighty one named Ksitigarbha, appears majestically family).

Usually there are five magical powers, i.e. Thien Ear Thong, Thien Nhat Thong, Tha Tam Thong, Tuc Mang Thong, and Nhu Y Thap; However, here there is also Lau Tat Thong, forming Luc Thong. Now Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is here. “The brave one is called Ksitigarbha” (The brave one is called Ksitigarbha), meaning: His career of practicing to benefit sentient beings is extremely brave and diligent. But he did not appear as a Bodhisattva, but instead appeared in the majesty of becoming a monk. That is the meaning of “The Little Turns to the Great” episode. Because in this Great Assembly, it is impossible to count the mass of Sravakas, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva manifests the form of Sravakas mainly to save suffering sentient beings in the three existences, and the Second Vehicle Sravakas have not yet returned to the Small Way towards the Great. Therefore, He appeared to be of the same kind as them.

(Sutra) The Seven Noble Treasures restore the treasure, the fearless Buddha's sound, the Bodhisattvas win the field, the path of sentient beings.
(Sutra: Treasure of the seven holy treasures, the Buddha's voice is completely fearless, the victory field of the Bodhisattva, the guide living beings).

The Seven Sacred Treasures is sometimes also called That Tai, which means "seven treasures". Sometimes called That Virtue Tai, or That Phap Tai. In general, there are seven types of holy dharma. “Holy Dharma” is the supreme Dharma, what are the seven things? That is, Faith, Precepts, Mindfulness, Preciousness, Literature, Giving, and Concentration. A mind that is not scattered is Concentration. The mind is not distracted, not dull, this in itself is a wealth that cannot be bought, so it is called Wealth. This wealth is called Phap Tai. The mind is not scattered, nor is it without clarity, and can illuminate all dharmas, [that is] using Prajna wisdom to illuminate all dharmas. The seventh gift is Concentration Hue Tai, which not only does not cause confusion, but can also illuminate everything clearly, illuminating all dharmas. These are called the Seven Holy Gifts. Where is the treasure containing the Seven Sacred Treasures hidden discreetly? Buried in the minds of living beings. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can help us excavate. Or it can be understood that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva contains these seven treasures. Living beings only need to respectfully make offerings, be sincere, and earnestly worship, and they will be able to achieve it.

The first item is Faith. “Buddhism can only be entered by faith”. Without Faith, it will be impossible to enter. Faith must be powerful. Without strength, the blessings you gain will be worldly blessings. If Faith gives birth to strength, it will be able to produce effects. I have told everyone many times, at least you can understand yourself. If afflictions arise, you can immediately recognize and control them, causing those afflictions to disappear and not be turned around by the afflictions. That means Faith has power. Realizing that the idea is not correct, immediately stop that idea, do not let it continue. Recognizing that evil thoughts arise in the past can prevent future thoughts from arising again. That's powerful. However, that is only the complete initial faith. If you are a person who has good roots from many past lives, even though in this life you have never heard the Buddha Dharma, suddenly you hear someone else preach, or someone tells you, the pores on your body open wide, showing that you have good roots in the past that are deep and thick, and as soon as you hear it, you can enter. That's called "having Faith". During the Buddha's time in the world, the great Arhats heard the Buddha's Dharma, immediately their hair and beard fell off, they became monks, their minds were opened, their thoughts were understood, they attained Arhatship, and all their negative thoughts and afflictions were eliminated. That is truly the full power of Faith. If we don't have the appearance of that realm, we must practice.

If you want to attain that faith, you have to practice for a lifetime, it takes a lifetime. For example, using small kalpas to calculate, a person's lifespan is eighty-four thousand years, and every hundred years it decreases a little, and after the next hundred years, it decreases a little more. Decreases until humans only live ten years. After passing another hundred years, life expectancy increases a little. Every hundred years, it increases [year by year. Over and over until he lived eighty-four thousand years. The cycle of "one increase, one decrease" is counted as one kalpa. Speaking in terms of small lifetimes, if you want to gain faith, you must practice for that long a period of time. Don't think it's too long! Compared to a human's lifespan, one day in the Four Heavenly Kings is fifty years in the human world. The lifespan of the Four Heavenly Kings is five hundred years. The second heaven is Dao Loi Thien. One day in Dao Loi Thien is equal to one hundred years in the human world. Dao Loi Thien's lifespan is one thousand years. The third heaven is Da Ma Thien. One day and night on Da Ma Thien is equivalent to two hundred years in the human world. Da Ma Thien's lifespan is two thousand years. The fourth heaven is Tushita Heaven. Four hundred years in the human world is one day and one night for them. Their lifespan is four thousand years.

Currently, Śākyamuni Buddha has entered nirvana for three thousand years, in just eight days on Dao Loi Thien! Therefore, when lawyer Dao Tuyen received an offering from a god, he asked: "Buddha Shakyamuni has entered nirvana, where is he now?" The god asked: "Which Śākyamuni Buddha are you talking about?" Everyone, please listen to the meaning in that question: There are hundreds of thousands of billions of Śākyamuni Buddhas, which Śākyamuni Buddha are you talking about? The Patriarch said: "The Buddha is in this Nam Thiem Bo Chau, in this Sa Ba world." The god replied: "I see that Śākyamuni Buddha has not yet entered nirvana, he is preaching the sutra."

The gods see differently than we do; Therefore, we feel very long, like living a hundred years is a very long time, but compared to the Four Heavenly Kings, it is only two days. One hundred years in the human world is only two days, their two days and nights. Regarding the issue of time, everyone should be aware of that. While practicing, even if we practice for twenty-four hours, they see that it is only a moment, a very short time. Therefore, the gods see us relaxing all day long, from morning to night, wandering around for hundreds of years, but do not see you practicing. The gods do not come into contact with you, they see that the human world is dirty. That god came down to offer rice to Lawyer Dao Tuyen, because he saw that the place was pure. The place where religious people live is pure. It is very difficult to see with our eyes, but we see that the Buddha hall is very pure and very sublime. People who do not believe in Buddha come to this place and will find it very dreary and very depressed. Just like the big pagodas are built deep in the mountains, there is no smoke from human cooking, so you have to climb to get there. We worshiped Ngu Dai Mountain, feeling very victorious. Those who do not believe will feel so torn. We see that the guardian deity is of course very solemn. We see that the statue is very solemn and carved, and we are very moved. When they saw it, they exclaimed: "Oh, this statue was carved with very high artistic value." They see with a different perspective! All things each person sees differently.

The treasury contains the treasures of the Seven Holy Wealth including Faith, Precepts, to Tam Quy, Dinh Hue; These are all holy talents, worthy of being called Dharma Jewels. “Fearless Buddha Sound” (Buddha's Fearless Sound): The Buddha's sound is the Four Fearless Fears, which are immeasurable and endless. These are the dharmas praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also has all the sounds of the Buddha. “The Bodhisattva's winning garland” (The Bodhisattva's winning garland): The treasured parasol and phan phan are similar to the national flag symbolizing a country. Bodhisattva is the supreme dharma field, he established the dharma field, is the guide of all living beings, has this meaning. “The leader of the path of living beings” means one who is respected by all living beings.

(Sutra) Liberation is the treasure of refuge, blessed with diligence, compassion and mockery, and relief from suffering. love.
sentient).

Imagine liberation as a precious thing. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is the refuge for all the treasures of liberation. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is the one we can rely on to seek liberation. We who seek the treasure of liberation must rely on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. His strength of diligence, courage of diligence, merit and desirable wisdom are as deep and wide as the ocean. “ Compassion mocks, understanding ”: Compassion is His great compassion. Compassion is great insight and great wisdom. We always think that compassion can end suffering, we hope that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will eliminate the suffering of sentient beings, we hope that we ourselves can listen to the Dharma and gain wisdom. “Clear insight” means wisdom, but we must associate with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is compassionate and bestows wisdom on all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to have wisdom. Only with wisdom can one be free from suffering and be happy. Only then will He come to save us. When sentient beings encounter tribulations, only then can sentient beings believe, admire, and be able to accept and maintain.

We try our best to study the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, some people study for a long time, but it is possible that even the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma still cannot be used. Even if it can be used, it is not compatible. Because they do not have a sincere mind. I have told everyone: Study the first half of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, you must read the sutra many times, then plant the Contemplation Wheel. Without looking at the scriptures and just sowing, it will be like sowing copper coins, or sowing the Luc Hao hexagram, which cannot correspond. Must worship, must praise the title. If there is no correspondence, worship again. That is eliminating karma. Regardless of whether it corresponds or does not correspond, you can still worship. When you recite the holy name Ksitigarbha, your sins will disappear.

All Buddhist teachings teach us a method on how to leave suffering and be happy. I'm very short of money, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can fulfill your wish. As for the necessary items for life, if you wish to have a Western-style villa, bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva more. You want to have a Bao Ma car (BMW), or a Bon Tri car (Mercedes-Benz), as long as you like it, or want to achieve your goal, worship and pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will be able to give it to you. He is not determined to give it to you through a certain method. On the Mainland, there are many people who hope that an American relative will fall from the sky to save them, give them a lot of money, and help them open a shop. Is this a thing or not? Not only is it true, but it's also quite true. But that's just immediate happiness, once it's over, it won't be there anymore.

Praying to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to give you happiness is not like that at all, but [desiring] the willow of birth and death, making you enlightened. If you are clear, by bowing to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, in your dream, you will feel what the outcome of that event will be in the future, but you cannot say it. If you speak out, you may be punished by the guardian deity. Because it was not you who attained it, but the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Because of claiming the holy name, he was blessed. In your mind, clarity arises in a single thought, but you yourself obscure that clarity. Therefore, when you achieve it, you usually don't say it. Only then will your mind achieve it. Continue to pray, He will be able to save your suffering, give you wisdom, and make you understand everything.

(Sutra) The data of the Buddha is like a city, like the clear moon path, giving birth to good roots like the ground, destroying Or like gold cang.
Cang).

“Terrorism” (Create a stronghold for those who fear): “Terror” is a descriptive word. Currently there are no citadels, the citadels are all destroyed. The current war has no distinct front and rear. No matter how high the wall is, it cannot stop bombs and bullets from falling from the air, do you know? Planes dropped bombs from the sky. “Thanh” mentioned here has a different meaning. In our hearts there is a citadel, what does the citadel look like? Suppose you recite the holy name Ksitigarbha, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva creates a citadel, making you not afraid, without a feeling of terror, as if protected by a wall.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is like the bright moon that lights the way for you. That is the recitation of the Truong Hang section. In the previous section, it was said: Causes you to give birth to good roots that do not waver, like the great earth, because we do good deeds but have no roots. Do it now, maybe don't do it next time. You can do it and then regret it. Is there such a thing? Yes! There's so much more! There are Dharma friends who develop a strong and kind heart, “letting go of self-care” means letting go of your house, completely turning it into a monastery. Later, when he didn't even have a place to live, he didn't even have food to eat, he immediately regretted it, thinking that at that time he should keep some of it. So the previous work has been lost! Is there merit or not? Yes, yes, but still no liberation! Do you regret it or not? There is regret. The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra specializes in this issue!

If we give alms to the Three Jewels; Later, when you personally saw that the monk was evil, you became very worried and thought: "Why did you give alms to such a monk at that time?" Thinking like that, merit is gone! No matter what he is like, you have made offerings to the Three Jewels, he represents the Three Jewels. Śākyamuni Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva specialized in discussing this issue. You have made offerings, the conditions are ripe, all the things you have done are finished, just let it go, don't hold on to it. What has passed is past, merit has been achieved. Just like when you practice, you reach the first step, the first step has been accomplished, you have to let it go, you must take the second step. If you keep holding on to the first step and don't let go, you won't be able to move on to the second step! You must let go before you can move on to the second step. Once the second step has been accomplished, you must also let go of the second step to move on to the third step, until it is finally accomplished, everything is complete. Don't do anything and then regret it.

Whenever you enter into something, don't regret it later, the merit has been achieved. What your opponent is like has no effect on you. You make offerings to the Three Jewels and make offerings to that temple. Just as I made offerings, war suddenly broke out, bombs destroyed everything. In your mind, think to yourself: "I just made an offering, why was it destroyed?" [Know] that the cause and condition of the new offering has ripened and the merit has been completed. When you make offerings, as soon as you've finished making offerings, it's already accomplished, the palace in heaven for you has already been built, bullets and bombs can't destroy it, you just don't see it! Therefore, do not reconsider, because you have already moved forward, it is complete!

If you are born in Da Ma Thien, you should not be attached to the Four Heavenly Kings and Dao Loi Thien, because Da Ma Thien is more open than the Four Heavenly Kings and Dao Loi Thien. Merit and solemnity are completely different. If you are born in the Pure Land world and still think about the Sa Ba world, it is a completely different story, because you hope to return to save sentient beings. Because in this world, there are still many people who have a predestined relationship with you, and they still don't understand. Until you understand clearly and return, the Sa Ba world is no longer the Sa Ba world, but exactly the same as the Pure Land world, depending on whose perspective it is. Is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vision of hell a scene of hell? No! He saves hell. Therefore it is said: “Born good roots are like earth, destroy Or like diamonds”. All delusion comes from vajra wisdom[17]; Once destroyed, once illuminated, there will be no more [enchantment], it will be resolved. With the light of wisdom shining in, can darkness still exist? If we turn off the lights, the house will be dark. Turn on the light, the darkness is destroyed, that has such a meaning.

(Sutra) The ability to liberate treasures, like floating waters Or, afflictions, heat, and disabilities like a good doctor.
(Sutra: Donating treasures liberates, like water flowing through the Ores, prevents heat and afflictions, cures diseases like food y).

“Ability to give” means being able to give alms. People who can give alms are extremely liberating, which means “seeing clearly, letting go”. Liberation is very difficult, because money is necessary for life. People with wisdom see and know and use it to benefit sentient beings. You must be a liberated person to give alms. In the Six Degrees, all virtues and alms-giving come first. Giving alms is giving. You have to let go from the heart, don't just focus on material things. Only by giving alms can one be liberated. The hardest thing to let go of is your own body. The most precious thing is also your own body. Currently, if three people come to me asking for alms, either asking for their eyes or asking for their hearts. At present, we cannot give it to them, because we do not fully have that equanimity, nor have we yet reached that spiritual power. Therefore, there can be no liberation. If you are a great Bodhisattva, whatever you pray for, they will grant it to you. Even their own bodies were sacrificed, let alone their country, their wives and children? Samantabhadra Hanh Nguyen Pham said: Things like treasures can be given away to all sentient beings. That is liberation.

Or our karma is like water swept away, don't think it's real. Many people have the attachment: “My karma is too heavy!” If you often talk like that, you won't be able to practice! Either something doesn't work out, or there's an accident, the first thing to think about is that your own karma is very heavy! Karma is your Or karma, starting Or, creating karma, like water washing away, not real, don't think it is real. If you repent, your karma will disappear.

Don't think your own karma is still very heavy. If you think hard, Or your own karma is still very heavy. If you think like that, it will always be very heavy, oppressing you, forever unable to be freed! It's the same with giving alms, it's the same with keeping the precepts, always thinking that your own karma is heavy: "Oh my God! How can I do this! My karma is so heavy!" The sentence "karma is very heavy" becomes a reason to give up, don't! Karma has no roots. Whenever karma arises, you must recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Recite with sincerity. If you don't practice other methods, then you should worry about maintaining your reputation. You also do not recite the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, nor do you recite the Contemplation Sutra, but you can still recite the holy name, but you must recite it to the point of your mind.

Affliction is brain heat. How many types of brain heat are there? Due to afflictions, resentment arises, or due to not thinking clearly, one cannot sleep. The more I lie down, the more I lose sleep. The more I lose sleep, the more I toss and turn, the restlessness in my heart is unbearable, it's all heat. Any affliction will always cause frustration, just like covering up a cotton blanket. “What” includes the Five Hindrances and the Ten Hindrances. There are afflictions that block you. If it is a phan phan, a treasured parasol, that is, the Buddha's treasured parasol, that is a holy scene. And What is here is affliction. Afflictions cause restlessness and dizziness, making you unable to breathe, unable to get through, unable to be liberated! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva eliminates afflictions, like eliminating heat in the brain, [like] removing a layer of concealment. If you are sick, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is like a very good physician. Take a dose of medicine and you will no longer be sick!

(Sutra) One day, Ksitigarbha's merits are great, he overcomes the mid-life, and he claims to be virtuous. Able to solve all sentient beings, all afflictions and afflictions are bound to arise, even if one attains the level of Concentration, all the branches of Concentration are on the shore. The twelve pure conditions, all wisdom is like space, breaking the boundless Buddhaland, all sentient beings are haunted.
(Sutra: One day proclaiming Ksitigarbha, merit, great name, more than in verses of kalpas, claiming the name of a master Other wisdom. Remove all afflictions that bind sentient beings. Reach the Pure Dharma of the Twelve Conditions, all wisdom is like space, destroying the darkness of sentient beings, in the boundless Buddha realm.

One day you will claim the title Ksitigarbha and it will be complete. When you recite one word, one complete word of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy name. Reciting for ten hours is enough to complete the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for ten hours. If you sincerely recite like that, just reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name for one day will be much better than reciting the names of other virtuous beings in an entire lifetime, including reciting the names of other great Bodhisattvas.

“Twelve pure conditions”: Twelve causes and conditions belonging to the dharma of Cause and Effect: Ignorance is conditioned by Action, Action is conditioned by Name and Form, Name and Form are conditioned by Six Entrances, Six Entrances are conditioned by Contact, Contact is conditioned by Love, Craving is conditioned by Attachment, Conditioned by Existence... Those are the Twelve Causes and Conditions, rotating like that. Just recite Ksitigarbha's holy name and learn from Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the twelve causes and conditions will be pure. Our karma, due to the origin of Or, creates karma, karma will bind you. Whenever you are bound, you will suffer. Now, karma is not created, it does not start, Or, karma cannot bind you, you can control it yourself. Not only can he liberate himself, but he can also enlighten all sentient beings who are covered by afflictions. Listen to the Dharma for yourself and want to tell it to others. As the Dharma friends introduced many friends, they made them believe in Buddha and listen to the Dharma. There

is to help sentient beings achieve liberation.

“Sustainment of Concentration” is the name of a discipline of Concentration among one hundred and eight types of Concentration, there is Sustainment of Concentration, Sustainment of Virtue Concentration... These are all names of subjects of Concentration. As long as there is one discipline of Concentration, one can reach the other shore, but the Nine Concentrations and Six Desires Thien Concentration cannot. This type of Concentration (Concentration of Action) is holy concentration. In the Holy Concentration, as in the following section, we will talk about the six dharmas: Record, Dependence, Concentration, Contemplation, Transfer, and Purity; and in the Thien Thai sect, it is So, Sui, Chi, Quan, Hoan, Tinh, meaning “reverting to purity”. The Six Noble Gates explain at a shallow level, while the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra explains at a deep level. Whether shallow or deep, we will tell.

The reason this sutra is long is because there are many methods of practice. Because it is a practice method, we must do it exactly like that. Learn to understand, you will be able to solve problems. What problem does it solve? In everyday life, every day we encounter many problems. In your contemplation mind, your perception and your senses are different. You must know what to do, you must contemplate like that, how to solve that problem? Just like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has such wisdom, we still cannot achieve it.

The sentence “wisdoms are like emptiness” (wisdoms are like emptiness) can be understood as “emptiness is wisdom”, but it can also be said the opposite. We can compare Emptiness with Prajna. In Buddhist scriptures, we only need to mention the meaning of Emptiness, then use nothingness as an example. Actually, that is not nothingness. Nothingness can accommodate everything. You have wisdom and have destroyed the Ors, but it is not just about destroying those Ors and matter. If a vase is Emptiness, completeness is not breaking it and throwing it away to become Emptiness. Completeness is not like that, but knowing that its essence is Emptiness, due to the harmony of causes and conditions. The flowers [in that vase] were not originally grown from a single flower tree, but because the flower arranger wanted to offer flowers, so they placed them in the same place. For each flower, it contains water, it has matter, it is all a combination of causes and conditions, no dharma is real. Causes and conditions combine to arise, causes and conditions to separate then disappear. When fate arises, accept it. When fate disappears, the flower disappears, it's all gone, then let go, there's no more, throw the flower away! Don't be attached or regretful anymore, like that! Family is also like that, parents, wife and children, have fate to gather together, everyone is like that. If I say it's a long time, it's a hundred years, until then, we have to separate. Once separated, let go, don't insist on attachment. I can't let go of this life, I'm attached to the next life. In the next life, you can't let go, so you can't be liberated. For this reason, liberation is impossible. Not knowing the wisdom is like space!

“Destroying the boundless Buddhaland, the dark sentient beings gather” (Destroying the darkness of the sentient beings in the boundless Buddhaland): Mainly all sentient beings in the infinite Buddhaland, darkness gathered together in one place. “Darkness” is karma. Too much karma, afflictions, greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, Personal Views, Boundary Views, Wrong Views, Views of Holding on to Views, and Forbidden Views of Holding on to Precepts, these ten bonds combine, making it impossible for you to escape! Those ten karma give birth to a lot of karma, infinite and endless. Greed, greed for anything, is greed. Regarding Buddha Dharma, if you can truly enter, the wisdom of Prajna just shines, Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, Consciousness, all are Emptiness. Everything that has form, form, language, writing, is all False, all is Emptiness. But when we have not reached that level, we still need language. Only after you understand the text clearly can you destroy it. While we have not yet attained that realm, we cannot leave our family. If you don't need your family and leave your children alone to listen to the sutras, then it's not okay! If you come to listen to the sutra that way, you will not gain any benefit. People in this place, their minds are worried about other places, they can't pay attention! Whatever you have to do, you should do it.

But “the dharma flavors of the world and the dharma flavors, the world often coexists” (the dharma flavors of the world dharmas often exist in the world). You must understand this principle! Therefore, if you understand "wisdoms are like nothingness", then you can destroy the dark gathering (“gathering” means gathering) of sentient beings in the boundless Buddha realm, and you can eliminate all karma born of causes and conditions. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not reside in any [certain] Buddha realm, but rather resides in an infinite [Buddha realm].

brain heat).

Due to the karma of sentient beings, they feel storms, floods, and fire disasters, which are the three great disasters. Currently, war, water, fire, and famine are the three disasters. Due to the karma of sentient beings, these kinds of disasters are especially numerous at present. More and more later, that's just the beginning! I have lived for more than eighty years, and since I understood this, I feel that this world has never had a good day. At that time, in the Northeast, bandits and warlords fought each other. After the battle, the North and South started war. Then, it was the Japanese who were aggressive again. Everyone reflect back and see if there is a day of peace or not? That's just swordplay.

Is anyone not sick? There are many diseases that cannot be cured. Famine, pestilence, some places are harmed and people know, some places are not harmed, others don't know. Diseases, war, famine, each includes countless harmful effects. If you recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will both be liberated. This is the Buddha praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for his immense and ultimate merit. No matter what accident you have, if you pray to Him, everything will be fine.

(Sutra) Sentient beings in the five animal bodies, suffering urgently, rely on Ksitigarbha, all suffering is eliminated.
(Sutra: Sentient beings in the five realms, oppressed by sufferings, as long as they respect Ksitigarbha, the sufferings all except).

“Beings born in the five beasts, suffering urgently” (Beings living in the five paths, suffering from pressing sufferings): Originally “six beasts”, the six paths, here it is said to be “five beasts”, [it seems] one path is missing. When our lives are over, we will enter hell, hungry ghosts, animals, gods, or humans. Asura is included in the five paths, there are human Asura, heavenly Asura, and demon Asura. Sometimes the six paths are said to be five paths, which means the Asura path is included in the other five paths. They are neither heaven nor humans. Every sentient being in the five realms will be forced to suffer hardships. If you pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, “all suffering will be eliminated” means all suffering will be eliminated.

(Sutra) Beings who inherit the wheel of suffering, develop harm, pay homage to Ksitigarbha, the stage of patience and compassion mind.
(Sutra: Living beings rely on the cycle of suffering, one after another, harming each other. Whenever one respects Ksitigarbha, one's mind is stable. from rings).

We rely on bad moral principles, they are evil moral principles, which in turn oppose and harm each other. If we take refuge in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we will not harm each other. I don't hurt you, you don't hurt me, you can all develop great compassion and help each other. The sages of the past thought very well, they said: “The people rule, the people enjoy”, but who does it? Does that mean it won't harm or contradict each other? Rich and poor are the same, everyone enjoys the same happiness. As a result, you suffer a little, I enjoy a little, mostly the situation is like that! Does anyone know how to think of others? They're all thinking for themselves, they're all contrary, they're harmful to each other! More and more they contradict each other, harm each other, suffering becomes deeper and more severe, never ending. After paying homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the heat in their hearts will stabilize and arise from the mind.

(Sutra) Twelve predestined conditions, pursuing suffering, reverence Ksitigarbha, fearless abiding in peace.
(Sutra: The twelve terrifying conditions, the more miserable the pursuit, rules glasses

Ksitigarbha, all stay calm and fearless).

In the previous section, we talked about the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions. Regardless of whether it is a past life or a future life, in general, whenever your mind moves, you start a career; That's called Karma General. That form of Karma will not stop, it will change. That transformation is called Transformation. It is the appearance of the realm in the mind. Karma, Transformation, and General (realm of appearance) have been completed, so grasp (attach, hold) continuously. Attachment to the name then creates Or, creating karma. Therefore, the cycle of suffering will [create] mutual persecution. That is a scary thing (chaplain). Therefore, do not start a business. Without creating karma, there will be no fear, nor will there be fear. The reason we create karma is because we have a body. The body needs to eat, it needs to wear clothes, and at the same time, it also wants to be comfortable. Everyone wants themselves to be comfortable. Whatever you do to feel comfortable, just do it, regardless of whether other people are comfortable or not! “Just make me comfortable!” Everyone calculated like that, competing with each other. The more you pursue, the closer suffering gets to you. You originally pursued happiness, but the more you pursued it, the more miserable you became. If you want to leave suffering, you must practice the Dharma. Śākyamuni Buddha taught us this method, that is, reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will be fine, you will not be afraid anymore!

(Sutra) Disadvantages of cultivating blessings, mindfulness, precepts, wisdom, respecting Ksitigarbha, seeking perfection complete.
(Sutra: If you like to practice blessings, mindfulness, precepts, and wisdom, whenever you respect Ksitigarbha, seek for are satisfied).

If you pray for blessings and wisdom, you must give rise to mindfulness. What's that chant? Reciting the precepts, reciting the Dharma. Reciting the Dharma is listening to the Dharma. Listening to the Dharma can give birth to wisdom, that is also mindfulness of wisdom. As long as you pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom that you desire will all be satisfied, you will leave suffering, and you will be happy.

(Sutra) Ridicule most of merit, skill, medicine, seeds, respect Ksitigarbha, seek fullness.
(Sutra: Appreciate every merit, skillful craft, medicine, seed, whenever you respect Ksitigarbha, all needs are satisfied).

You like to make merit, or you want to be a doctor, a scientist, or you want to be a teacher of good techniques, but if you don't have wisdom, you won't be able to do it! Then ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to bless you and give you the wisdom to be able to invent and create. When a Bodhisattva wishes to benefit sentient beings, he must understand the Wisdom of Consciousness, Wisdom, Inner Wisdom, External Wisdom, and Human Wisdom. That is called the Five Insight Bodhisattvas. Bodhisattvas who practice the Five Insights will understand all worldly arts, and will also use the great compassion of Buddhism to study. If you pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will gain wisdom, and as soon as you learn, you will understand.

(Sutra) Praying for valleys, medicinal fields, men, women, medicine, historical records, respecting Ksitigarbha, seeking perfection complete.
(Sutra: Pray for rice, fields, medicine, children, clothes, servants, as long as you respect the Earth Organs and desires are all satisfied.)

All of these are things we hope for in the present, such as farming and hoping for grain to grow well, planting medicine and hoping for herbs to grow very well. Going to the mountains to pick medicine, Ganoderma, ginseng, such precious and rare medicinal herbs are obtained. Longing for someone to help you, or longing for clothes or a devoted servant. “Story” is a servant. When you open a company, finding good assistants, workers, or officials is very difficult! Which worker or employee doesn't think about stealing, doesn't want to correct you, doesn't think about harming you? As long as you respect Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, all your wishes will be satisfied.

(Sutra) Assemblies of appropriate virtues, diligently accept the great earth, cultivate the medicinal herbs, and nourish the children. puree.
(Sutra: Enough of the corresponding virtues, or maintaining the earth, therefore, grain, medicine, freshness and soft and smooth).

Why? Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has all the virtues, he maintains the great earth, all of which are born from the great earth. Therefore, those cereals and medicinal herbs are cultivated and grow extremely well.

(Sutra) All afflictions are endowed with wealth, mocking the Ten Evil Karmas, respecting Ksitigarbha, eliminating evil afflictions.
all minus).

You are covered by afflictions. “Phú” is a cover-up, you don't think about doing good things, in your heart you are determined to do bad things. The ten main evil karmas are "killing, stealing, sexual misconduct" in the body, "lying, embellishing words, speaking harsh words, double-talking" in the mouth. If you don't curse others, you won't be able to speak! It must be necessary to curse another person for that person to speak. When I was in Sichuan, I felt that if they didn't scold others, they wouldn't be able to speak! It's not really cursing, children and the elderly keep saying "you turtle", which has become their catchphrase! I heard it was very annoying, they said: "It's our habit, it doesn't mean anything!" They won't be able to say "you turtle"! Every time you open your mouth, you say "turtle", it seems to have become a habit, but we hear it very harshly, both men and women say it like that!

There is also the Northeast region, at first, when I was a child, there was an area called Lap Cap tribe, maybe people have never heard of it. Their language is simple to the extreme, young people call older people “old fire keke”, older people call young people “little fire keke”. The words “fire keke” are not pronounced like “fire keke”[18] in Chinese. I asked what those two words meant, but they had no way to explain. I call both my father and my mother “scheming old man”. Parents also call their children “little firecracker”. The language is so poor, I can't even hope to say more than a few sentences! If you become that ethnic group, will speaking be painful? Is there any difference between buffalo and horse? Therefore, the sutra says "no different from animals, no different from wood or stone"; Those who do not understand the Buddhadharma are no different from wood, stone, and animals, no different from buffaloes and horses!

birth).

In the previous section, it was said that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears in all kinds of bodies, which everyone has seen. In total, He manifested forty-two types of incarnations.

(Sutra: Suppose in a hundred lifetimes, praising His merits, still cannot complete them all, we should all make offerings”).

Finally, Śākyamuni Buddha told the gathering of people attending the Dharma Assembly: Talking about the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, even if we talk about it for a hundred lifetimes, we still cannot praise it completely. "Because of the inexhaustible power of God, the ancients are making offerings" [meaning]: Everyone should make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, chanting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.
