Because of existence, there is birth. Due to the fate of birth, there is old age, death, sadness, suffering, great misfortunes gather in the body, all sufferings arise.

This shows that all things are dependently arisen. Relying on other things to initiate virtue is all dependent on conditions for birth. Of the twelve causes and conditions, [in terms of] past, present, and future, Ignorance and Action are two causes of the past connected to the present. This is called a causal layer. This level of cause and effect includes two causes and five effects: Due to the cause in the past, one experiences the effect in the present. These results include Consciousness, Name and Form, and Six Sense Bases; But Luc Xu, due to contact, receives five results in the present. Taking or leaving in there, [that is] there is Attachment and Equanimity. Because there is Love, there is Attachment, and there is birth and death (that is Existence). Those are the three causes. Those three causes (Love, Attachment, Being) create the suffering of Birth and Lao Tzu in the future. These are called three causes (Love, Attachment, Existence) and two effects (Birth and Lao Tzu).

Birth, Aging, Death: If there is Birth, there will definitely be Old Age, if there is Old Age, there will definitely be Death. Sometimes they even skip levels, [which means] they didn't wait for him and died first. Some people, due to different karma, only suffer, and die immediately at birth. There are even cases where the fetus dies in the womb. The karma is different, [that is] the cause in the past is different, so the results are also different. To practice the Wheel of Karma Concentration, the Wheel of Karma Concentration includes ten types. When cultivating Concentration, you must observe and observe the six realms of your body.

We just talked about the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination; Here, [the scriptures] only talk about six types of realms, that is, speaking according to the internal realm. In that, there also arises the Self and the Self, which means considering oneself as the master. Attachment belongs to ignorance. Each of us, because we do not understand clearly, do not have wisdom, think that we are right, that we are the best, and are attached to that view. Looking at the problem, it's clearly not right, but everyone has their own attachments. That is due to each person's own personality. When each person examines and analyzes the problem, it is not accurate, but you just assume that it is correct; Actually, I was wrong! Just like when we buy stocks, we buy this stock thinking that we will definitely get rich, and the price will definitely increase. As a result, you have to buy stocks to give money! Without raising prices, the opportunity to live a better life has passed away! You see people making a lot of money, you feel envious, so you go buy it. That is Ego Clinging. They think they can definitely make money; In fact, it is definitely a loss of money! I was so lost that I had to jump off a building to commit suicide. Is this a situation or not? Sometimes when he recognizes the right opportunity, at that time, he is sure to make a fortune, he has invested in the right place.

These things all belong to Ego Clinging and Ego View, but speaking according to the principles of Buddhist scriptures, speaking according to the dharma of birth and death, once achieved, they will also be lost. When you don't achieve it, you have to suffer. After achieving it, you will suffer again. It's the same if you achieve it, but it's the same if you don't achieve it, it's all illusory! Whatever you achieve will be destroyed in the end, it is all illusory and not real! But they didn't realize it, they thought it was real. Actually it's an illusion. Wanting them to think about selflessness is extremely difficult! Without eliminating the cause, without preserving the fate, how can this be done? You must practice. The Buddha wanted to establish and practice the wheel of karma; First of all, you must observe the Stream of Karma, the Stream of Defilements, and the Stream of Suffering.

(Sutra) Like the three streams, karma is the field of food, ignorance is the cause, love is the gain, children gain birth. Desire is dry crane, karma is the field of food, ignorance is the cause, love is the profit, the three streams of accumulation, the Five Thu Aggregates, contemplating impermanence, suffering, no-self, stupidity, motionless, like an illusion, like a flame, like water in the middle of the moon, like a dream with views, emptiness, non-existence, formless, wishless, non-created, non-born, non-starter, non-existence, non-existence image, tranquility, remoteness, no origin. With the Five Hand Aggregates, as you observe, you can follow Emptiness Forbearance, follow Formless Forbearance, follow No Desire Forbearance, and according to desires, contemplate the Five Hand Aggregates.
(Sutra: Three types of saving like that, good farming karma, ignorance as the cause, love as watering, then Because we want to dry up the three streams of "good karma, ignorance as the cause, and love as watering", so for the Five Aggregates, contemplate them as impermanent, and suffering, without self, stupid, motionless, like an illusion, like a ripple of sunlight, like the moon in water, like what is seen in a dream, empty, without possession, without form, without desire, without creation, without birth, without arising, without release, without form, Quiet, separate, not giving birth to anything. Observing the Five Aggregates like that, you can follow Emptiness Forbearance, follow the Formless Forbearance, follow the Vowsless Forbearance, because you want to follow the Five Hands Aggregates.

“Karma is the field, ignorance is the cause, love is the profit” (Karma is the good field, ignorance is the cause, love is the water): This is growth again. You wish to dry up the Karma Stream. Sometimes this word Hac is read as Co, sometimes it is read as Hac. “Dry” means “dry”. That stream has dried up; Because it has dried up, it will not be able to water and grow. First of all, you cut off Ignorance, contemplate that all things are impermanent, there will be no more Craving, and the mind of craving will not arise. Therefore, the Buddha said "Karma is a good field, ignorance is the cause, love is the water" then [Karma Save] can grow, what kind of growth? The Five Aggregates of Attachment, also known as Attachment, are also called Attachment. In the Heart Sutra, the Five Aggregates are Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness, [which can be said to be combined into] two dharmas, that is, Form and Mind. Feelings, Thoughts, Actions, Consciousness belong to the Mind Dharma, Form belongs to the Form Dharma. Those are two types, both of which are impermanent.

Therefore, you want to practice Concentration; First of all, we must contemplate these things as impermanent, as suffering, as not sweet, as not-self, and as the root of ignorance. You must contemplate these things as "like an illusion, like a flame, like water in the middle of the moon, like a dream with a view, empty, non-existent, formless, wishless, uncreated, unborn, non-arising" (like an illusion, like ripples of sunlight, like the moon in water, like things seen in a dream, empty, without possession, without form, without wish, without creation, without birth, without arising). If you want to practice this Karma, there are six types. First of all, we must observe from No Hand (no grasping), enter the three doors of liberation of Emptiness, No Form and No Wish first; Then enter again. After we study Buddhism, hope to practice, hope to truly enter, hope for liberation, this is the most basic dharma. All Vipassana subjects must practice like this.

So, I introduce a little to everyone. If you want to enter Concentration, you must observe the twelve types of stream of birth and death, you must cut off that karma, you must cut off the stream of Karma, the stream of afflictions, and the stream of suffering. If you want to practice Concentration, up to “reflection, dependence, concentration, contemplation, transformation, tranquility”; that is exactly what is said in this sutra. Great Master Tri Gia composed Thien Thai Tong Luc Dieu Mon, and changed one word in it to “book, depend, only, contemplate, complete, pure”. This sutra talks about Transfer, Transfer and Complete which have interrelated meanings. Change once, “revert, revert” (return to the origin), the meaning is the same. But [to practice Chi-Contemplation one must] have money and means; If you don't have predestined conditions and want to practice, you won't be able to enter. Therefore, Great Master Tri Gia proposed: If you want to practice Chi Quan, you need to fulfill all the causes and conditions. If you don't have that condition, you will not practice successfully. If you have enough causes and conditions, you will develop a desire to practice, hope to attain Concentration, hope to open up wisdom, and attain Concentration of Wisdom and you will be able to eliminate suffering. If you want to practice, you must have enough conditions. If there is no predestined relationship, one cannot practice successfully. What fate is that? You have received the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, you must maintain the precepts. At least maintain the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts in purity. The first thing is to maintain pure precepts to stop afflictions. By maintaining the precepts, meditation can be born, and suffering can also be eliminated, and wisdom can be born.

The first thing is to maintain precepts as a condition, but maintaining precepts has different situations. Great Master Tri Gia said: People who practice precepts have different [three types of situations] maintaining precepts. What are the three different types of precepts? I say simply:

- I have maintained, regarding the precepts I have received, basically I have never broken them. The first type is the best.

- The second type is that we commit very small, very light, not heavy crimes, and as soon as we repent, we can repent.

- The third type is violating the basic precepts. You have received the Five Precepts, but killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying are all transgressions. Having taken refuge in the Three Jewels, you then take refuge in other sects. That is destroying Tam Quy; This is the third type. But if you are sincere in following the Mahayana teachings, you can still repent, but it will require pain, crying, and daily repentance twenty-four hours day and night. Repenting like that, repentance is pure, purity has been achieved, it has been proven, [that is] seeing the appearance is good. Once pure, that cause and condition can still be established, and practicing Contemplation can still enter. But it is necessary that in the present life, one must not commit the five negative crimes. If in the present life we commit the Five Disadvantages and hope to achieve Samantabhadra, it will be very difficult!

Pure repentance has been accomplished. People who practice Zhiquan have one thing: they have never done evil things, and two, they have done evil things and can regret it, they can still repent. But repentance has three methods:

- The first is to believe in cause and effect.

- Second, fear arises, that is, fear of falling into hell, fear of reincarnation.

- Third is to be deeply ashamed.

After that, you can learn the method of eliminating sins, or bow according to a certain method of repentance such as Ksitigarbha Repentance, Contemplation Repentance, Thien Buddha Repentance, or Great Compassion Repentance. It all depends on which method is suitable for you.

Finally, if when you practice Contemplation, contemplate "the nature of sin is inherently empty, only created by the mind. If when the mind is lost, sin is also lost", that is, meditate on No Birth. If a person with severe karma meditates on No Birth, it is basically impossible to meditate. If in this life you really have very deep good roots in the previous life, practice [repentance] for seven days or twenty-one days or one month. We bow to Chiem Sat Sam, in the Contemplative Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: “Bow for seven days, fourteen days, twenty-one days”. If you bow for a month or two and still don't succeed, then bow for three years. It's not like we bow once a day. If you can still recite the holy name, you will be pure.

According to the repentance dharma of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, when practicing, it is like that. The first thing is that you have all those predestined conditions. I only mentioned the matter of reprimanding the five desires. The five desires are greed and desire. Life shouldn't be too comfortable. Life is too comfortable, if you want to enter Chi Quan, you will not be able to enter! Delusional thoughts are scattered, cloudy, and not pure. How can desires be forbidden? If you want to meditate, you must rebuke [the five desires]. The five desires are [craving for] Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch. Foolish people are confused in Forms, Sounds, Scents, Tastes, Touches, infatuated with Forms, Sounds, Smells, Tastes, Touches, and become greedy, unaware of their faults and harms. Wise people know that they are calamities and do not dare to be close to those five types; That's called “rebuking the five desires”. There are many things in there, if people want to learn, they must read a lot!

The second type is to eliminate the Five Things[29]. Among the Five Things, desire is Desire. Because of the realm of the five senses of Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, and Touch, you have desires. Even so, in your internal Mind Base, desire also arises. When you practice Zen, your mind gives rise to desire and cannot sit still. Therefore, it obscures your good intentions. When it's normal, it doesn't seem like you're angry at all. All troubles can be suppressed and endured. But when you meditate, you will not be able to endure it, everything that was suppressed in the past will surface, and it will be very strong and fierce. Therefore, if you want to stop the obstacles that arise from practicing Samatha or contemplation, you must practice Contemplation. During the process of counting numbers [according to the in and out breath], it may suddenly come to mind that at some point, someone treated us badly, made us miserable, and we must take revenge. The more you think in your mind, the more angry you become, making you forget everything you have been practicing! Even if you can't sit down and have to stand up, karma urges you to retaliate. If you want to rebuke the Five Desires, if you want to get rid of the Five Things, the first condition is to have enough external conditions. This includes all ten things.

There is also a fourth type[30] which is conditioning. Walking, standing, sitting, lying down, you can all practice, but sitting is more appropriate. When practicing Samantabhadra, you must definitely regulate your body and mind so that they adapt. First, regulate the body (regulate the body) then regulate the mind (regulate the mind). Having finished, then regulate the breath (regulate the breath), [that is, in order]: Regulate the body, regulate the breath, regulate the mind, must be in harmony. This is the fourth type.

I only mentioned the names of those ten conditions. If people really want to practice, they must study. The fifth condition is to have skillful means, to practice must have skillful means. Great Master Tri Jia taught skillful means.

The seventh type is making a vow, skillfully making a great vow.

The eighth type is that you yourself must recognize demonic obstacles. When you have not practiced, demonic obstacles do not appear. When practicing, evil obstacles will occur.

The ninth type is the treatment of Zen illness. When you practice Concentration, there will be many illnesses, that is called “Zen illness”. It is not our body that is sick. You must know thoroughly what Zen sickness is.

The tenth type is the ability to enter, that is, attain Meditation.

In general, “evil people act, good people serve, self-purify your mind, Buddhists” (don't do evil things, do good things, quiet your mind, the Buddha taught): If your other methods of practice do not have that, then when you practice visualization, recite these four sentences: “All the evil acts, all the good ones serve, purify one's mind, all Buddhas”. That is the Buddha's teachings when studying Meditation. If you know how to meditate and practice, you must first have all those conditions. Once all external conditions are pure, it is easy to enter the three doors of liberation.

The three doors of liberation are:

1) Khong Mon: Khong Mon is not [emptiness] as we say, because sometimes we use nothingness as an example. “Emptiness” is not [empty] like space; If you understand [Emptiness] as "emptiness", then you are wrong. “Emptiness” implies the meaning “everything is born of conditions, all dharmas have no self”. Their essence is Emptiness, because they are composed of many conditions and are also born from causes and conditions. Suppose we realize that all dharmas are born from causes and conditions and are without self-nature. On any day when I specifically talk about “Dependent Origination of Emptiness”, I will talk for a long time. Saying "all dharmas have no self-nature. Without self-nature, it is Emptiness", and also saying "its essence is Emptiness", is not destroying it, [don't understand it as] having to destroy it is to call it Emptiness. That's not what it means at all. But if “destiny dissolves”, that means the fate is no longer there, the fate is not complete, it will be empty (no longer exists). If you can understand this meaning, it will be very easy to achieve freedom. If you know, you will not have attachments to all things, and you can even cut off your Ego Attachment. The Omniscience attained by Arhat is Emptiness, [because He has] attained that level of meaning, He is liberated. Having entered Emptiness is liberation.

2) Formlessness is also called No Thought, everything is without thought. You already know that everything is Emptiness, for the physical appearance of men and women, reality is unattainable. If you recognize "all dharmas are formless", you will leave the distinct appearance of all dharmas and attain freedom. Because you have no attachment to all dharmas, knowing that they do not exist, that they are illusory appearances, false appearances, like shadows, like images. Formless means like that.

3) “Wishless, actionless” is also called Desirelessness. You already know all the formless dharmas, so you stay in the three worlds and don't expect anything. If you don't pray, you won't create karma. If you do not create the karma of birth and death, of course you will not experience the suffering that is the retribution of birth and death. Due to formlessness, you achieve freedom, one form, different forms, same signs, all signs, different signs, not wishing for all kinds of signs, because they are all Emptiness, all like illusions.

If you can enter those three doors of liberation, have wisdom, can truly enter, then it will be “in the world, but out of the world”. Even though you are in the world, you are separated from the world because you are not constrained by worldly dharmas.

Considering “book, depending, only, contemplation, transfer, net”, for Book, we often say “count numbers”, that is, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, count like that. What are you counting? Count your breaths in and out. This is cultivating Concentration, the mind needs to concentrate on one scene. From one to ten, then count from the beginning, from one to ten. Whenever you have a bad thought, you will count wrongly. You must concentrate on one scene, based on those numbers, making your mind fix on the number, and will no longer look for other delusions.

This type has many ways to practice. There was a period of time when I used the practice like this: I used the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, counting each word. When inhaling is Nam, exhaling is Mo, then inhaling again is Earth, then exhaling again is Tang. Then, inhaling is Bo, exhaling is Sat. Every word is visualized like that. You exhale and inhale like that, then exhale and inhale again, that's called Exit and Inhale (exhalation and inhalation). The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra aims to teach you to meditate on Exit, Entry, and Exit. It does not mention numbers to count; but generally speaking, the counting method [in the Book] is from one to ten. Luc Dieu Mon talks about the word Book even more clearly. That is the first step in practicing Samatha Contemplation.

The Ten Rings Sutra teaches in a simplified way, for each type, it says two types of appearances, that is, the appearance of being able to inhale and exhale, achieving Concentration in the form of exhalation and inhalation. So now while exhaling and inhaling, at first the breath is very coarse, until after you have meditated for a long time, the breath will become more subtle. After becoming subtle, [the stage will be reached] where there is no more breath. Like when I chant Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, after reciting it for a long time, I don't see any more thoughts, I don't breathe out, it seems like my breath has stabilized. From gross to subtle, so subtle that you can barely feel it anymore, it feels like you've stopped breathing. That is the form of Import, Export, and Importance.

Because you have entered the practice of Exit, Enter, and Breathe, you will be able to concentrate and follow the breath in and out to stop “delusional thoughts, false thoughts, seeking, investigating”. If you leave false thoughts, false thoughts will stop. There is no more searching, no more false thoughts, you have achieved the practice of Exit, Incarnation. Achieving kung fu, to put it a little more colloquially, will mean moving from the coarse form to entering the subtle form. Just like when we first started counting our breaths, the mind was very rough, very fluttering, chaotic, very agitated, the count was running all over the place. The more you count, the more your thoughts wander. When karma can stand firmly, that is, on the exhalation and inhalation, all other thoughts will no longer exist! Such a thought, contemplation at the tip of the nose, or contemplation of a certain appearance, will focus on one scene, with such a meaning. Concentrating on one scene, you can stop distracting thoughts, and the pattern of exhaling and inhaling has become very light and subtle. Skillfully hold the appearance of exhaling and inhaling. That appearance seems to be present or non-existent, but it still does not stop, it is necessary to reach the realm of Samadhi.

“Dependent, book, only, contemplation, transfer, purity”, these six things are related to each other. At that time, you feel that the exhalation and inhalation have disappeared, there is no more breathing, but you can also stay in Concentration, or as we say, Khinh An, also called Tam-ma-di. At that time, the sign of breathing has ended. When you can know whether you are exhaling or inhaling completely, that is Contemplation. When exhalation and inhalation have ended, it is Chi. Know whether the breath is exhalation or inhalation, observe exhalation and inhalation. When it stops, the mind is at peace. At that time, you must observe yourself, your mind must not stir up any other thoughts, you must observe. That is called “Due to Concentration, Minh is born”. Minh is wisdom. Wisdom means Illumination, reaching the fourth step of practice. Then, with regard to Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness as mentioned in the previous section, you have already let go of Form. That is the method of transforming the mind. You can abandon the Five Aggregates and gradually reach Concentration. You can truly enter Concentration, gradually you can enter the holy land (the status of a saint), you can be pure. When you are pure, you will let go of the Sutras of greed, anger, and ignorance. Removing all those Conjunctions will be able to give birth to pure view (pure seeing and knowing). Thus, wisdom has been revealed. It seems very easy to say, but very difficult to do; In it there are all kinds of subtle actions (subtle actions).

Furthermore, while you practice, the teacher will know which realm you have reached. If you ask your teacher: "What realm are you in now?" Especially when demons arise, you will be able to recognize them yourself. Even though we are aware of it, we cannot fix it! For example, say: "Every day we must meditate three times, or meditate five times." When you have Concentration, or at first you can overcome all the difficulties and then you will be pure, but as soon as you enter the door, obstacles will immediately arise. Or a lot of attachments and disturbances in the world will happen, making your mind unstable and disturbed. If you are sitting, walking, meditating, or reciting Buddha's name, even though your mind is in one scene, your mind is disturbed, naturally the outside world will disturb you. Even if no one bothers you, [inside] you will still search. That's Tam Tu. You search for it yourself, but you still retreat. If that happens, it will be very difficult to practice again to achieve the same level as before. Through this subject, we will be able to enter, be able to follow (Depending), let go of Thoughts and Thoughts, and not pursue any more. If you don't search, your thoughts will not be entangled, which also means that your deluded mind will no longer grasp the scene.

Especially for people who practice, this type of obstacle will arise: Or troubles arise in the mind, they don't want to do it anymore, they don't want to practice anymore, they don't think about practicing anymore. That [obstacle] arises from within oneself. Or friends or relatives [causing obstacles]. In general, whatever fate brings you. When you are about to enter, obstacles immediately arise. Why? Because in the past, we did not have good roots. Therefore, Great Master Tri Gia said: When you practice Contemplation, if you want to practice Concentration and Wisdom, you must first achieve all external conditions! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to repent, not to mention cultivating Concentration, because if you want to enter, want to learn, you must repent first. Otherwise, you won't even have the opportunity to study. Even if you have the opportunity to study, you will absolutely not be able to enter, because obstacles will block you!

If the Dharma friends want to cultivate Concentration to become saints, they vow: "I will listen to the entire Ten Chakra Sutra". This sutra is preached from beginning to end, without interruption to the listener, fearing that not many will be heard. I didn't dare say "no", or I would miss a session or two. When teaching the Contemplation Sutra, I experimented, and as far as I could see, there were very few people who studied it completely from beginning to end! What is the cause? Karma Luu! Especially in the Dharma Ending period, fate is not prosperous. In particular, one's own internal obstacles are more intense than external obstacles. Once there is karma, it will arise Or, Or will it cause insecurity, restlessness, and even troubles and troubles for whom? Annoyed with yourself. Can't sit patiently. Cultivation is like that, no matter which discipline you practice! Is there any obstacle to repentance? Very difficult! Create your own mind, make your own determination. At first it was fixed three times, then it turned into two times. Then two times turned into one time, very difficult! There are always things that disturb, who disturbs? One's own Karma and Afflictions. Suffering afflicts you. You hope to escape, it's very difficult!

Therefore, we hope to become religious practitioners, we hope not to create the karma of birth and death, we hope to cut off the stream of birth and death, but if we do not have the mind to make that vow, how can we fulfill it? Even if you have that mind and want to do it, there are too many obstacles in the middle, how should you overcome them? Except for your own strength, pray to Buddha and Bodhisattva for blessings. Therefore, we worship, pray for the power of others, use our own mind power to combine with the compassion power of Buddha and Bodhisattva, only then can you cut off the three streams. Having broken the third stream, you will attain enlightenment and be able to enter sainthood.

When we first started studying Avatamsaka, due to our Second Vehicle base, regarding being born in the Pure Land, we thought, thinking that nothing was necessary, even thinking that there was no need to study, thinking it was making a great vow. Currently, the more I learn, the more scared I become, the more I feel like I was wrong. The Arhatship of the Second Vehicle has cut off birth and death. The saints who have attained the First Fruition have cut off Views or Misunderstandings, but everything we see gives rise to discrimination, everything we see gives rise to craving, we are too far from the holy. Easy to say, difficult to do. [So] is it easy to “know”? Or is “doing” easier? Confucianists say “knowing the difficulty of doing things”, meaning: Knowing is very difficult, doing is easier! There are things that are very easy to know, but very difficult to do. I see: For those who study Buddhism, knowing and practicing are both difficult, but in comparison, you must really know first, then you can practice! This is the first step. You don't know how to practice? That knowledge requires wisdom. You must have many types of causes and conditions before you can begin to know!

If you encounter a master who is not very good, and cannot meet the dharma lecture, we think it is very simple, but in fact it is very difficult! As far as I know, based on my experience, it's not easy at all! Even if you know but you don't know, how can you practice? Right? The first step is to know, this is the basis. You must believe! If you don't even believe it, how can you know? Because you can only learn if you enter. I don't even have faith, so how can I practice religion? Let's not say anything else, just look at Te Cong, we all admire him very much. He is so leisurely, yet so talented, he can easily take on anything and achieve it. I see that for great Bodhisattvas, there is nothing that is not Buddha Dharma, but if you want to reach that realm, it is not easy!

At the beginning of learning, you should not be attached to all dharmas. Now I understand, I don't have the dharma, [so] there's no need to be attached to the dharma, how can I get rid of it? I must rely on the dharma to be able to eliminate Ego Clinging. Until I no longer have Ego Clinging, I no longer follow the Dharma. Right now, the Self is still there, every day the realm of the five desires is complete, I hope there is no need for dharma, how can you enter it? You are still drifting in the realm of the five desires. Is that so or not? Therefore, it can be said that it is difficult, but it can also be said that it is "very easy", which means that with a sincere heart of faith and understanding [it will be possible].

After believing, you will naturally know what is good and what is bad, of course you will follow the good and avoid the bad. It's obviously a fire pit, who will jump in? Buddha clearly taught “it is a pit of fire”. The Three Realms are a fiery pit, you must leave. Those who deeply understand will pray [for renunciation] earnestly. If you pray earnestly, you will be able to do it. You often think about impermanence, think about suffering, and every day you encounter the results of suffering. If this thing is not pressing, it will be that thing that is pressing. Just a little bit of goodness, then suffering immediately comes!

A lot of friends who do business and trade are like that, but also go to work, there are no problems with the house, everything is fine, [suddenly] the wife is unemployed, has no income, do you say it's troublesome or not? Just when things were going well, there was someone sick in the house, medical examination had to cost money, and it was very urgent. Now what we learn and need to practice is "keeping the idea of ​​coming and going", which also means we raise the idea, breathing is the thought of coming and going. Whenever a thought arises, it is not easy to grasp that thought firmly! We learn gradually, just like when we preach the Ten Rings Sutra, I'm afraid we won't be able to finish it in a day or two! What is the purpose of studying scriptures? If you can use it, use it immediately. For the beginning, we say it more than once. This Dharma is the most convenient for us, everyone can enter it, everyone can know it. Today, we're talking about "keeping the coming thoughts", but "satisfying, following, meditating, contemplation, turning, and tranquility" haven't finished talking yet! Everyone can read the book Six Wonderful Mons, for each thing, that book explains very thoroughly, but is only a starting place to practice all Concentration subjects.

Currently, Dharma Master Hoang Giac is teaching the Samatha Dharma in Bodhidharma [Second Treatise], which is according to Tibetan teachings, which is also very convenient, very simple, and clear. If everyone comes in, it's very easy. If you combine both of these methods, it will be even better!

(Sutra) Practice the means of cultivating Enterprising Contemplation, that is, practicing reciting past thoughts. Is the cloud river observed as it really is, entering and exiting the breath? The right person contemplates, records, depends on, only tries, contemplates, transfers, and purifies. In the middle of tri tri tri, the book of ability to create two types of career: First, ability to dress the Tam and Tu. Second, the energy of the hand enters and leaves the form. Depending on one's ability to create two types of career: First, renunciation, letting go of Samsara and Tu. Second, skillful hands enter and exit the form. Only the ability to create two types of careers: First, the ability to manifest, enter, exit, and destroy. Second, the ability to stay calmly overcomes samāma-ground. Contemplation of the ability to create two types of career: First, the ability to manifest, enter and exit, and end. Second, the ability to calm the mind and focus on the mind, observing differently. Transferring the energy to create two types of career: One, the ability to let go of the Aggregates. Second, use animal means to enter the holy land. Pure energy creates two types of career: One, the ability to let go. Nof understanding, the ability to see.
(Sutra: There is also a means to practice Entering and Exiting Contemplation (contemplation of the breath in and out), that is, practicing and maintaining the thought comes. How is it possible to observe the exhalation and inhalation by mindfulness? That is, the right observation, by the magic of Book, Sui, Contemplation, Transfer, and Tranquility. You should know that in it, the Book can create two types of actions: One can use it to subdue Samadhi and Sutra HWho can hold the form of inhalation and exhalation You can create two types of actions: One is to rely on renunciation to abandon the Thoughts and Thoughts. The other is to be able to skillfully hold the form of inhalation and exhalation. "Just" can create two types of actions: One is to be able to manifest inhalation and exhalation end. Hone is able to calm the mind and different mental dharmas to observe. "Transfer" can create two types of career: One is the means to let go of the Aggregates. Hone is able to enter the sainthood. "Pureness" can create two types of actions: One is existence can let go. Hwho can purify knowledge).

The ultimate means to practice the Samadhi of the Karma Wheel is to practice Entering and Exiting Contemplation. If you want to practice this method of expediency, there are six types, that is, “recording, depending, concentration, contemplation, transfer, purity”. This method of contemplation of Entering and Exiting Immediate is also called the practice of “retaining past thoughts” (mastering coming and going thoughts). Reciting coming and reciting away [is the object of contemplation of] the Book That Is Contemplation magic. Book means counting words or numbers; Use the counting method to capture your mind and distract your thoughts. We have just heard or learned it and feel that [this method] is very simple. If you really practice, [you will realize] it's not very simple. If you [only focus on] counting numbers, you're wrong. There are two ways to count:

- One type is inhale for a count of one, exhale for a count of two. Just inhale, count one, exhale, count two, inhale again, count three, exhale, count four. This is a way of counting.

- Another way to count is that you can combine inhalation and exhalation to count as one, [next] inhale and exhale to count two. Count to ten and you're done (count from one again). One is the starting number, ten is the ending number. The first ten rounds are completed, you count again from one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, and meditate on the number again.

At first, you feel that counting numbers like that is very simple, just worry

counting numbers is wrong. If the mind doesn't pay a little attention, one will count wrong numbers, two, the breathing in and out will be chaotic. Inhalation and exhalation are chaotic, you must balance your breathing. It has kept you from drowsiness, but it has also kept you from being distracted. Because this is the practice of Concentration, the first place to enter, you must calmly observe. Only when you are not dull or distracted, you can count correctly!

If you don't use this technique, at first you'll think it's too simple! Once you use it, you'll see that it's actually very difficult. In an instant, you'll lose count. If you only count single numbers, that means inhale for one, exhale for two, inhale again for three, exhale for four. Ten times like that, each turn counts as one round. If inhalation and exhalation are counted as one, then ten turns means ten inhalations and exhalations. Some people feel that when they inhale and exhale, they count to a number. They are afraid they will make a mistake, so they inhale and count as one, exhale and count as two. It just depends on what is best for you to attain Concentration. You can apply this tool yourself. But when you count to ten, count again from the beginning. At first, when I first used [this way of Quan], as soon as I sat down, my breathing was very heavy, very panting. You keep inhaling, exhaling, counting like that, your breathing will gradually become softer, until finally, both exhalation and inhalation will stop. In this way, you will gradually enter Concentration.

I'll summarize a bit. “Depending” means first of all depending on the breathing in and out, first of all following the way of counting. Next is "depending" on the Sutra. “Depending” can have two effects. Depending on how you count the number of breaths in and out, you can observe the appearance of exhalation and inhalation. While counting numbers, counting back and forth like that, regulate your breathing very subtly. Gradually, you will stop wishing and desiring thoughts. You can see it yourself, you can visualize the pattern of inhalation and exhalation, you can see the pattern of inhalation and exhalation. This belongs to Form Dharma, to form. Therefore, your Contemplation magic has physical form, you can use it to subdue the scattered mind. When you count the numbers, depending on the pattern of inhaling and exhaling, you can observe for yourself. That way can give rise to two effects: One is to stop the seeking mind, the other is to subdue the Samadhi mind.

By counting numbers, you can subdue the wandering mind. Until Sui [as mentioned above], will be able to renounce and abandon the mind of Samantabhadra. At that time, that person can skillfully maintain the pattern of inhalation and exhalation, [that is] while practicing, he can gradually observe. That is the effect of Sui. The effect of Chi is that when you are depending on the already existing signs of inhalation and exhalation, you will be able to eliminate the signs of inhalation and exhalation. At that time, you can gradually enter Concentration, stay in Concentration. When you feel that you can gradually enter Concentration, that is contemplation, it can inform you that the inhaled and exhaled breath has ended, is completely motionless, has been extinguished, and can rest your mind.

“Transform” means to subdue that form, to be able to let go of Form Dharma and Form Aggregate. The form of breathing in and out belongs to the Aggregate of Form. That person gradually eliminates afflictions and can enter the saintly state, which means he has eliminated afflictions. When he feels calm, he can let go of all kinds of Conjunctions, get rid of greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, Body View, Boundary View, Precepts of Precepts, Holding Views, Wrong Views, those ten afflictions. Complete renunciation is not cessation, we have not yet reached that realm. When we can stop, we can give birth to right knowledge and right view. These are called “six types of means”. These six types of means come from the magic of Book, Dependence, Meditation, Contemplation, Transference, and Purity. Great Master Tri Gia wrote Luc Dieu Mon, edited [Changed] to Hoan, [with the meaning] “revert” (return) to purity.

Each type of means has two symbols: One is coarse, the other is subtle. When you first practice, when counting numbers, it's up to you which way you choose. When I use it, I chant the holy name Ksitigarbha: For each word, inhale on Nam, exhale on Mo. When finished, inhale again to say the word Earth, and then exhale to say the word Tibet. Breathing in again is the word Bo. Breathing out again is the word Slap. I divided the six words into three turns. Inhale, exhale, inhale, exhale, inhale, exhale; If I recite Buddha's name ten times, I recite all sixty words. It's very rough at first, you have to concentrate your energy; If you are a little lax or lazy, you will immediately make mistakes. When used quite proficiently, counting forward, counting back, gradually the breathing is subdued, the mind immediately calms down. You can't raise false thoughts, but you also shouldn't be lethargic. If your mind doesn't pay a little attention, you won't be able to contemplate and will be mistaken. At first, you feel like it's too complicated. You can shorten it to make it simpler. First of all, count from the moment you inhale, inhale for a count of one, exhale for a count of two, then inhale again for three, then exhale for four. Therefore, in five rounds of breathing, there will be ten numbers.

According to my experience, if you can count five hundred times, no matter how you walk or sit, sometimes sitting there counting numbers, you will feel like an idiot, sitting there bewildered. Because you concentrate on one scene, the sutras teach "concentrate on one scene, you will be able to capture the mind", having subdued the gross feeling, you will enter the subtle [feeling]. When you are good, you have to pay even more attention. What will Te easily become? Easy to get depressed! You must definitely contemplate your breathing in and out, but you must pay attention: If you concentrate on one scene, you will not count wrongly. In this way, all delusional thoughts and observing minds will stop. When the breath stops, they will be subdued. You consider that appearance of compliance as the appearance of breathing in and out. When you are satisfied, you will be able to let go, you will be able to leave all the signs of breathing in and out, "leaving" is letting go. That is the meaning of “It depends”. “Depending” means “when you can let go, it will be according to your will”. It also means “having left behind the form of inhalation and exhalation”, leaving behind the gross form of Samsara and Sutra. But at that moment, only the very subtle appearance of inhaling and exhaling remains. That form must reach Silence, that is, in the situation of Dependence, it is necessary to reach Silence before you can enter Concentration. Once you have entered Concentration, the appearance of inhaling and exhaling will not exist. If there is none, then it is already in Concentration; However, that Concentration is still not Great Concentration.

When you just, the appearance of inhalation and exhalation has disappeared. Samadhi is Concentration. When you first attain Concentration, you feel extremely happy. This must be done step by step, you can't skip it, you can't skip ahead, you must do it step by step. We often say "Concentration can give birth to Hue", Hue here means Illumination, no more discrimination, no more searching. Whenever you search, you will fall back into Tam and Tu in the previous section. That's not what it means! It is projection, illumination, observation, then observation again. Once illuminated, the form of inhalation and exhalation no longer exists. Thus, there is no exhalation or inhalation, until that form [exhalation, inhalation] does not exist. First is to subdue Tam and Tu; After that, exhale and inhale to destroy the form. Until Sui, until the form of exhalation and inhalation gradually become very subtle, until there is no more, then it is time to reach Only, [exhalation, inhalation] is completely gone, has left. When it's completely gone, then you know your mind has settled down in the scene of Concentration, focusing on one scene, that's settling down. Mind, mental factor, especially the mind of observation, mind is the mental factor of dharma. We study the Hundred Dharmas, knowing that the Form Dharma has eleven items, the Mind Dharma has eight[32], the Mind Dharma includes fifty-one items.

“Observe” does not mean to discriminate or explore. Whenever you search, you will fall into Tam Tu, which [observation] is Illumination, illuminating your afflictions to subdue lethargy and distraction. [Drowsy and chaotic] ​​all belong to the Dharma of the Mind. Depending on your consciousness, you start to differentiate and become Six Imports, which means the ears hear sounds, the eyes see colors, the tongue knows tastes... When you illuminate the six senses, the above phenomena will no longer exist. That is not being stupid, nor is it being asleep, you have to observe. Because you are in Concentration, wisdom arises, that is the first step.

(Sutra) Like the six methods of practice, practice Entering and Exiting Contemplation, conveniently and conveniently contemplate the Five Aggregates. The reason why it's fake? Such as entering into the instant, emerging from the self-nature, the aggregate of name and form. Such as entering the breath, receiving the breath out, the name Tho Thu Uan. As the body enters the body, the prime minister emerges, the name Tuong Thu Uan. Such as entering the moment, creating creation, named Aggregate of Attachment. Just as it enters the breath, exits the breath and separates, the name is the Aggregate of Consciousness. Like the theory of the Five Aggregates of Grasping, the different, mutually incompatible, new and non-constant, non-existing, indestructible, indescribable. Such as observing the five aggregates of Hands and eliminating the three actions. Weakness is like the ultimate goal, depending on contemplating the three types of conduct, the ability to test the conscious body, the six realms, the ultimate goal depends on contemplating the Self, the Self, Acceptance of karma, ignorance, love, the field of human wealth, and the ultimate stage to the end.
(Sutra: Six such means, practicing Entering and Exiting Contemplation (contemplation of inhaling and exhaling), will You can freely contemplate the Five Aggregates. Why is that? The nature of inhaling and exhaling like that is called the Aggregate of Inhaling and Exhaling like that. Holding the form of inhaling and exhaling like that is called the Aggregate of Inhaling and Exhaling like that Thus, is called the Aggregates of Consciousness as mentioned, each type is different, not similar to each other, always new, not old, not permanent, not accumulated, cannot be described in words like that, if one can thoroughly observe the cessation of those three types of conduct, one will be able to deal with the consciousnesses, bodies, and six realms of existence. depending on the Self and the things attached to the Self, like a field covered, watered, and watered by ignorance and love, all will be exhausted.)

These six types of means are all the initial means to enter Samadhi. Don't think that Samadhi [in Book, Sui, Samadhi, Contemplation, Transfer, Purity] is the superior samadhi, that is not great samadhi. However, it is only in the one hundred and eight samadhis that one enters the First Hy Tinh stage, which is also the first time one enters practice. Until the Transformation, starting again, releasing the Aggregates again. Aggregates are contained. Having mastered the Aggregates, one has entered the holy land (the status of a saint). That's roughly how the saint Chu Qua cut off Views or Orcs. At that time, when it is already deep, you can let go of the Sutra, without pursuing it, but it is not yet an end, like the word Letting Go in the Dependent stage in the previous section. That person has achieved right knowledge and right view. The pure dharma eye is pure, that is, the six methods used to practice contemplating the situation of exhaling and inhaling breath. At that time, you can proceed to practice further. So the scriptures explain that: Taking practice one step further, contemplating the Body of the exhalation and inhalation is also the self-nature of the exhalation and inhalation. That Body belongs to the Dharma of Form, so it is called the Aggregate of Form. So all the forms that are stored up here have ceased. Breathing in, breathing out, one in, one out, has the meaning of receiving, that is called “receiving”, also called the Aggregate of Feeling.

The prime minister (holding the form) inhales, exhales, “prime minister” is the thought in the thought (thought), so it is called the Thought Aggregate. The artifact caused by inhaling and exhaling like that has the meaning of “transportation”. Due to the movement of that creation, it is called the Aggregate of Attachment. Distinguish (see, understand and clearly distinguish) the inhalation and exhalation like that. Inhale, exhale, [then] inhale, exhale. That separation is called the Aggregate of Consciousness.

Those five things are called the Five Aggregates. The Five Aggregates are Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, and Consciousness. “Thu” means “you are already complete”. The Five Aggregates of Grasping are complete. Each of us is complete. As long as you are a sentient being, you have all five Aggregates of Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness. In those five Aggregates, each item is different. This dish is not similar to that dish; then, they are not similar. Going one step further, if the above things are all eliminated, it is called Hau. There is the gross Five Aggregates and the subtle Five Aggregates. Because those things don't last, it's said to be "new and non-constant" ( always new, never old), [implying]: It's not something that already exists, but it's always replacing and innovating each other. Because they don't stay, is it just accumulating in one place? That's not true! If you want to use language to clearly explain the Five Aggregates, you cannot use language to explain it. Only when you contemplate, you can illuminate it.

You can reach such a situation, you will achieve “three virtues”. What is “Three Virtues”? It is merit, sin, and inaction. “No action” means inaction, it also means that neither the idea of ​​merit arises nor the idea of ​​sin arises. Regarding the “three virtues”, you can eliminate “merit, sin, inaction”, also known as indeterminate, [that is] without sin, without merit, with an indeterminate nature. If you can follow suit and contemplate that all three actions have ended, in the present, your body and mind will be pure. [In the sentence “Convenient ability to test the six realms of consciousness”], “consciousness” is the mind, “body” is the body. The body belongs to the Form Dharma, the mind is the Mind Dharma. For those two dharmas of Form and Mind, the six senses are pure. At that time, you can enter Ego Clinging to gradually penetrate the Contemplation of No-Ego. By eliminating egolessness, you will be able to enter the dharmas attached to the Self. The Clinging Energy (the subject of attachment) is the Self, the Ego So Clinging (that which is attached to the Self) is all the signs of the realm. What realms are you attached to? There is ignorance and love as the cause, [that is, as in the main sutra, comparing the false mind to] “a field with love and ignorance as the cause, covered by all sins”. The sins and blessings [from that field] have all ended. That's the first step.

(Sutra) Such as practicing the four stages of Reciting the Pillars to reach perfection, I will practice the Noble Eightfold Path to attain perfection. Perfection, like Thi Nhai's determination to practice the Eighteen Immortals plus the Buddha Dharma stage to attain perfection. Just like this lady who diligently practiced the One Immortal Dharma of Forbearance, Thu Lang Gia Ma sama-dia level reached perfection. Such as practicing the practice of reciting past thoughts, entering the Tathagata, the name of the Dharma surpasses sentient beings, the true name of cultivating the Tathagata, the true name of making offerings to the Buddhas of the three worlds, World-Honored Ones, the name of the Buddha's mind in the heart of the child, the birth of the Buddha's mouth, the realization of the Dharma, the transformation of the Dharma.
(Sutra: Practicing the four types of Mindfulness Pills like this leads to perfection, up to cultivating the eight noble paths All are perfected, like that until the practice of the eighteen Buddha Dharmas that are not combined are all perfected, like that until cultivating the All Kinds of Unborn Dharma of Forbearance (All Kinds of Wisdom), Shurangama Samāma-ground (Shurangama right concentration) etc. All are perfected. Practicing to keep the mindfulness until going like that, entering the Tranquility, is called living in the supreme meaning of the Dharma, is called practicing true Tranquility, is called true worship. It seems that the Buddhas of the three worlds, World-Honored Ones, are called the children in the hearts of all Buddhas, born from the Buddha's mouth, accomplished by the Dharma, and transformed by the Dharma).

After you have completed practicing these dharmas, you can begin to practice the four types of Mindfulness. Start contemplating the four types of Mindfulness: "Contemplating the impurity of the body, contemplating the feeling of suffering, contemplating the impermanence of the mind, contemplating the non-self of the dharma". Performed from the practice of Book, Depend, Only, Contemplate, Transfer, and Purify. After that, start contemplating the Four Foundations of Mindfulness again, you can enter very quickly and succeed very quickly. “Perfection” means “achievement”. At first, it all starts from the Book, that is, you need to start from Concentration. You take the next step to practice Thinking. After such four types of Mindfulness have been completed, the Noble Eightfold Path has been completed, until cultivating the Eighteen Non-Combined Buddha Dharmas has been completed, until cultivating the All-Sign of Non-Sentence Dharma of Forbearance, which is also the One-Kind Wisdom. Non-Birth Dharma Forbearance is accepting the non-born dharmas. The unborn Dharma has only one type of wisdom, achieving Shurangama samadhi. That's all in summary. If we talk about it in detail, it would be that each of the Samadhis must be complete. Above is a general explanation of the second Buddhist wheel.

Practicing “retaining past thoughts” (keeping each passing thought firmly) is cultivating your thoughts. Due to that thought, cultivating and reciting to enter Tranquility, “abiding in the Dharma surpasses the meaning of sentient beings” (being sentient beings abide in the superior meaning of the Dharma). What is “Dharma prevails” ? It is talking about the First Meaning, that is talking about the True Form, talking about the true and unchanging meaning. That sentient being has achieved success and can truly practice Tinh Lu and truly practice Concentration.

The Noble Eightfold Path is Right View, Right Thought, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration, and Right View. Regarding Buddha Dharma, there is no wrong knowledge or wrong views, the explanation is very accurate, far away from false views such as theism, materialism, and egoism. Although it is only two words, Right View is very difficult to arise. Many of us hope to have supernatural powers, long for inspiration, or have a very deep Self-Clinging or Self-View. As for yourself, always put the Self (your own view) in the first place. Ego View is not right view. In [types of views] theism, solipsism, and materialism, mind and environment are always separated into two. Mind and scene are split in two, only scene is materialism (only accepts the existence of matter), materialism only accepts matter. Don't classify material things as the first quality, or idealism as the first quality, [those attachments] are all wrong. [Not having such an attachment] is the only way to explain the Buddhadharma correctly. Outside the mind there is no dharma or scene. Outside of the scene there is no mind, and outside of dharma there is also no mind. That explanation is very profound. We just say [simply Right View] is to give birth to correct views and understanding, not to give birth to wrong knowledge, that's okay. [If you have right view], looking at the problem, you will be able to see the logic a little deeper. If I have to explain that reason, there are many reasons. Simply put, it is the true mind (ie the truth).

Our thoughts operate and cannot be separated from three types. Speaking from the human side, one is physical, the other is psychological, and the other is biological. Many people, based on the physics of life, when all matter is born, they reason like this: From a physical perspective, all matter changes, is born, remains, differs, and dies, they can find the law. For psychology, that is, for thinking in one's own mind, there are also certain changes, there are also certain rules. But unifying physiology with physics or psychology is not easy at all. Just as a country establishes laws, it is necessary to understand the situation in the country, the nature of people, the relationship between people and their families, the relationship between relatives, the relationship with the country, you cannot help but consider [those relationships]. Therefore, when making laws, we must pay attention to people's feelings. If the established law does not satisfy the people, that law will not be established and will not become law.

Therefore, we often talk about heavenly principles and human hearts, and also national laws, which are also “love, reason, law”. When it comes to morality, you can bring it up, but it must be in accordance with human feelings, in accordance with ethics, and in accordance with the laws of the country. Of those three types, if one goes against one, it cannot be established. Establishing a dharma that is completely contrary to human sentiments, in terms of morality, it may be okay, but in terms of human sentiments, it will not work. You will be opposed by the entire people, so that's no good. [If it's just] reasonable, according to reason, it's okay to do so, but from a legal perspective, it won't be acceptable. No matter what difficulties you face, the country must have unified laws. Heavenly principles, national laws, and humanity, you must understand those three things. Now that you understand, you can go back to studying biology, physics, and psychology.

As we just mentioned Right View, to teach living beings, the Buddha always has skillful means, hoping for you to reach the truth, reach the true realm. First of all, He spoke according to the situation. Everyone's personality is different, so why do we have to contemplate the basis (consider the basis) to preach the Dharma? Their ancestors (previous causes) are different. The ancestors were Ly, their thoughts and theories in the present are different. The Buddha observed each aspect and preached the Dharma to them, so they could become enlightened. When we talk about Right View, the first thing is to be selfless. Ego Clinging is too heavy, not discussing Dharma Clinging. When the Ego Clinging has not been cut off, is it possible to talk about the Dharma? Putting yourself first in everything is not Right View. Anything that has Ego Clinging will not be Right View. I only say one thing in detail, the other things cannot be said in detail.

Right Thinking: False thoughts, desires, and desires are all unjust. We hope to never get sick, this is impossible! As long as you have a physical body, [that physical body] is in harmony with Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind, due to the harmony of conditions, and you wish to be disease-free, no matter who you are, it is impossible. Śākyamuni Buddha also suffered from illness, [that is] He also appeared to be sick. If you think you will never get sick, that is incorrect thinking. There is also attachment and desire. That is also not Right Thought. Or we hope to listen to the Dharma more, increase our wisdom, expand our wisdom, and take wisdom as our life. That is correct, causing the karma of our religious practice to soon come to fruition. Such thinking is Right Thinking. We must have Right View to be able to give birth to Right Thought. Is your understanding wise or not? From your perspective on the problem, it will be revealed [whether you have Right View or not].

Right Speech is easy to understand: Don't speak indiscriminately, don't slander others, don't argue, don't speak harshly, don't provoke gossip. This mistake is very easy to make: Talking about other people's gossip, you yourself are creating gossip! Everyone, please think about it, is that true? This is correct, that is not correct. It's true Thi, it's not true Phi. [Discussion] "What Truong Tam did at that time was not right, Ly Tu was right at that time". You open your mouth to discuss a few words, discuss gossip, say right to wrong, twist right and wrong! What must be followed? According to non-self, according to the correct view. Because of correct thinking, correct words will be uttered. Just like there is a Chinese saying: “Non-ceremony, don't show, don't say, don't say, don't look, don't do.” How to understand the Ceremony? According to Buddhism, Ceremony is "in accordance with the law", if it is in accordance with Buddha's teachings, it will be a Ceremony. Right Speech is in accordance with the Dharma, in accordance with the Buddha's teachings. Don't lie, don't embellish, don't say double words, don't say bad words. That is the great premise, the four standards; But there are many [other standards] in there, you have to observe for yourself.

Right Action: Whatever is in accordance with the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and in accordance with the Buddha's teachings, will be Right Action. But the profession you are working in society, which profession you pursue, on the one hand is the precepts taught by Buddha, on the other hand is the law of the country. If the two sides conflict with each other, it means the national law and the precepts taught by the Buddha are in conflict, and the national law must be followed. Even though the Buddha taught like that, when you follow the national law, it is not considered a violation of the precepts. You follow the precepts, but the country may not approve. In the country you are in, you cannot do that. You should give up and follow the law of the country. That is just righteous behavior. At that time, as long as you do not break the law, do not hurt others, and do not calculate for your own benefit, we think doing so is noble! Each country, each race, each people's living habits, all noble sentiments are different. We give the relationship between the two natures as an example. There are many countries, many peoples with different perspectives, and different national laws.

According to the Buddha's teachings, if you commit sexual misconduct, you have committed a sexual violation. What you should not have, but obtain it in an illegal way, is a violation of the precept, that is, an offense of theft. Even killing people, breaking the precepts. According to the Bodhisattva precepts, killing animals is the same as killing humans. In the precepts of monks, precepts of bhikshunis, or the Eight Precepts, the precepts of upasakas and upasakas, the precept of killing is purely about killing people. If you commit it [killing living beings, but not killing people], you will not lose the precepts. The Noble Eightfold Path is said depending on the place, depending on each type of person, it is also the opposite (in accordance with the base). Speaking according to Bodhisattva will be completely different; According to ordinary people, it will be completely different. Must understand this principle! Since it is the Noble Eightfold Path, you must speak and speak in accordance with the Bodhi path. We explain it like that, one level deeper.

Right Livelihood: If you conform to the standards of precepts, be courageous, diligently cultivate the path, practice Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom, use that diligence to preserve your life. That is Right Livelihood. Right Livelihood is respecting oneself. Sometimes, in order to cultivate the Way, it is better to sacrifice one's life and life; Is it wrong livelihood or right livelihood? We see many ashrams, such as the Renunciation of the Body Nhai (the cliff of self-renunciation) at Nga Mi mountain, or in the Lotus Sutra, Phap Hy (The Joyful View of All Beings) Bodhisattva burns his body to worship the Buddha; Is that right livelihood or wrong livelihood? It depends on how brave and diligent you are, and also depends on how much you cultivate the path and what level of awareness you have reached? There are people who die because they keep the precepts, but for the sake of survival they break the precepts, it depends on how you interpret it! It's mainly due to your mind and concept at that moment, that's how I explain it. If it is for the sake of making the seeds of the Three Jewels uninterrupted, or temporarily making concessions for the benefit of the whole, you are a Bodhisattva who wants to protect the Three Jewels without interruption, but does not pay attention to all sacrifices. However, that single phenomenon of breaking the precepts cannot be used as a standard, nor can it be considered a commonly used dharma. The precepts established by the Buddha are the eternal dharma. Speaking of Right Livelihood means not living by wrong livelihood. For example, we talk about reading astronomy, reading geography, predicting horoscopes, and medical directions, but Bodhisattvas who are educated in the Five Insights must also do those things and do not consider them incorrect. He has skillful means to save sentient beings; However, if you are a Bhikkhu or Bhikkhuni. When doing those things, it will be a wrong life! If you take the Bodhisattva Precepts, and also take the Bhikkhu Precepts, you will not be able to do it. Saying it's Chanh means there are so many ways to choose!

Finally, Mindfulness means we must stay away from all crazy delusions. The person who is called “not losing mindfulness” is the person who recites without forgetting the Three Jewels. There are also Bodhisattvas who have participated in the positions of Faith (positions of the Ten Faiths), recognizing that bad thoughts have arisen from their pre-thoughts, will not let post-thoughts arise, and immediately correct them. There is a type of person who can repent even though he has broken the precepts. After repenting, he will be pure again. The other type is basically not breaking the precepts, maintaining the precepts very purely. Both types of people are pure. The word Right is the birth of true wisdom, from Concentration that makes one's own body and mind achieve perfect personality, like the personality of Buddha's disciples, obeying the regulations of the Three Jewels on the personality of all disciples. We have to explain it like that. I explain the Noble Eightfold Path in this simple way. There are many ways to explain the Noble Eightfold Path, depending on what status you have reached, so explain according to that status to speak appropriately. Normally speaking, that's the explanation.

Nhat Thiet Tinh Tri is all types. The Three Wisdoms are Omniscience, Path Wisdom, and Omniscience. “Seed” means “birth”. Omniscience is the total wisdom, all dharmas are held in the Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha dharmas. All-Wisdom is the section of Contemplative Views. Kien Tu's afflictions have been ended, but Tran Sa and Vo Minh have not been ended. Taoist Wisdom refers to Bodhisattva. He can know the different appearances of all dharmas. All Kinds of Wisdom is about Buddha. Among these three wisdoms, the Omniscience can know the causes of all sentient beings. If we name each living being, he can see from countless eons up to now, when has that person sown good roots and believed in Buddha. Omniscience is also known as Buddha's wisdom. Only by becoming a Buddha can one attain Omniscience. Once you become a Buddha, you will have all kinds of wisdom, which is called Omniscience, knowing all dharmas and all methods of attaining enlightenment, knowing the causes of all sentient beings. He also knows what dharma they should receive and tells them that dharma, and also knows the different wisdom of all sentient beings.

“Never-Being Dharma Forbearance” is the All-Wisdom. “Shurangama Samama-ma-ground” is Shurangama samadhi, one hundred and eight subjects of Concentration, which can be fully achieved. At the beginning, cultivating Concentration is cultivating “retaining past thoughts”. “Entering the Static Lu”: From the beginning, cultivating “retaining past thoughts”, entering Concentration, entering to the point of staying in the Tinh Lu. Next, explain all the Concentration subjects you have mastered. Regarding the supreme meaning of Dharma, these sentient beings truly practice Tinh Lu. If you truly practice Tinh Lu, you will attain [the subjects of Concentration]. From Omniscience, Path Wisdom, and Omniscience, those who attain these types of wisdom can truly make offerings to the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the three worlds. Saying so includes the Bodhisattva nature, that is, talking about the Path Nature. If one practices like that, and practices to that level, only then will a Buddhist be able to attain the path of the Buddhas. “Born from Buddha's mouth” (Born from Buddha's mouth): “Born from Buddha's mouth” is the dharma spoken by Buddha. Regarding the dharma taught by the Buddha, that person can attain enlightenment by following the dharma. Thus, that person's birth body has taken the dharma as its body, transformed by the dharmas.

(Sutra) Or a Bodhisattva like this practice, gradually recede, reach the end of Asrava, become an Arhat, magician. Or if there is a Bodhisattva who practices like this, gradually increases, his merit is perfect, he becomes a great Bodhisattva, reaches the Eighteen Non-Combined Buddha Dharma, and All-Signed Wisdom practices to perfection. Tthe eternal cause, attains Supreme Perfection Bo De. Good man! The self is like the karma of dharma, receiving the wisdom of cause and effect, observing the eyes of the Buddhas of the three worlds, establishing sentient beings, trying the ten strains of cultivating the wheel of karma, and practicing spiritually. Good man! The name Tathagata cultivates the wheel of karma.
Arhat, has all six supernatural powers. Or there is a Bodhisattva who practices like that, gradually increases, perfects his merit, and becomes a great Bodhisattva, until he fully practices the eighteen Buddha Dharmas and Omniscience. He will soon attain Supreme Bodhi. I will use wisdom to understand the karma, receive the causes and consequences like that, and use the Dharma eyes of the Buddhas of the three worlds to observe and establish sentient beings. Make them practice those ten karma wheels. This is called Tathagata cultivating the karma wheel.)

There are Bodhisattvas who, after attaining the Concentration of Extinction and Concentration, can no longer practice further. Saying “regressed” because he stopped here, also means that he has “regressed”. End of Gonorrhea: End of Gonorrhea is the end of what? Or that person's karma, i.e. Thoughts or Asrava, has ended. Gonorrhea has been eliminated, meaning there is no more leakage of [defilements], no more falling or falling into the three worlds, and the achievement of No Birth. Arhat also translates as No Birth, no birth, no death. Arhats believe that their own attainment is already birthless and deathless, no different from Buddha, and has no desire to advance further. As for the six types of supernatural power, i.e. Heavenly Ear, Heavenly Eye, Other Mind, Sufficient Life... he has achieved the Complete Accession of Asrava. As for the announcements (magical powers achieved by retribution) of gods, humans, or ghosts, there is no End of Asrava, because Kien Tu Or still exists. Developing the great mind, [that is] developing the Bodhi mind, cultivating according to the method of Samantabhadra is to progress to a higher level of practice, not reaching this point but stopping. He makes it possible for all living beings to reach that level.

The Beginner Bodhisattva is not at all on par with an Arhat. He must reach the Ten Bodhisattva Grounds to be on par with an Arahant, but because he has developed a great mind, he is superior to the Hinayana. Because the Bodhi mind has no limits, that Bodhisattva will not stop, but will definitely wish to become a Buddha.

For that reason, there are Bodhisattvas who gradually regress, feeling that Buddhism is long lasting, giving rise to the mind of withdrawal. Then he will attain Arhatship and enter Parinirvana. As for the great Bodhisattva, he gradually increases his own merit, growing into a Mahasattva, that is, a Great Bodhisattva. The content of the Eighteen Uncommunist Laws is very long. I have just talked about the Omniscience, practicing to perfection, practicing successfully, will attain Supreme Bodhi, [or more commonly said] “achieve Anuttara Sammyak Sambodhi”.

“Good man”: This is the Buddha's answer to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. "The ego is like the karma and dharmas that receive the knowledge of cause and effect." What artifact? This is the method of cultivating Concentration. The former is the cause, the latter is the effect. Until all the Path Wisdom fully repays the merits and has been completely perfected, “observe the eyes of the Buddhas of the three times and dharma, establishing sentient beings”, that is, use the Buddha eyes [of the Buddhas of the three times] to observe everything. The dharma eyes of the three worlds of Buddhas clearly see all the past, present, and future, causing all sentient beings, that is, all sentient beings who are cultivating Concentration, to practice those ten types of karma wheel of Concentration. [That is the meaning of the sentence] “spiritual practice” (makes them practice). But here, we must focus on “retaining past thoughts” (keeping the coming thoughts).

This passage of scripture focuses on the practice of “retaining past thoughts”. “Tathagata's name cultivates Concentration of the wheel of karma” (That is called cultivating the Concentration of the wheel of karma of Tathagata): Practicing Concentration of the wheel of karma, if penetrated a little deeper, will be penetrating Samantabhadra as the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma said. In the previous section, the Buddha pointed out the three wheels [in the second Buddha Wheel]. The first is cultivating the wheel of karma, the second type [will be discussed next] is practicing reciting the wheel of karma.

(Sutra) Good man! Cloud Ha Tathagata practices reciting the wheel of karma? The Śūsōs, or the Śśōni, the Oba-sach-ca, the O-ba-tu-ca, or the pure believers of the good men, or good women, have good roots with silver, follow the Worldly Truth, the base is mature, the self is positioned as a sentient being, spiritually reciting, early in life, late in life, diligently without treatment. If all sentient beings seek the Supreme Wisdom, the self is at peace with the pure Mahayana wisdom, the spiritual period is self-explanatory, or the teaching is other independent, the spiritual period is self-reciting, or the teaching is other reciting, the spiritual period is self-speaking, or the teaching is other teaching. In the middle of the Mahayana, the spiritual practitioner practices by himself, or teaches others to practice. The spirit itself, accessing other bodies in the Middle Ages, eliminates all attachments, the spirit attains the Supreme Wisdom, the one who eliminates the suffering of all sentient beings, the spirit beast enters fearlessness and becomes fixed.
(Sutra: Good man! What is the practice of reciting the karma wheel of the Tathagata? Bhikkhus, or bhiksunis, upasakas, upasakas, or good men and good women with pure faith, gentle good roots, relying on the Worldly Truth, whose roots are not yet ripe, I will arrange sentient beings like that, making them practice chanting. At the beginning of the night, at the end of the night, diligently, without laziness. If sentient beings seek the Supreme Wisdom, I will arrange pure Mahayana for them read it yourself, or teach others to read it, make them recite it themselves, or teach others to recite it themselves, or make them say it themselves, or make them practice the Mahayana themselves, or teach others to practice it, because they want to cause the great mass of afflictions in their own body and the bodies of others to be eliminated, to make them attain the Supreme Wisdom, to cause them to attain the Supreme Wisdom, to eliminate suffering for all sentient beings, and to make them enter the throne of fearlessness.

The second wheel of karma is learning to recite, learning how to recite, which also means reciting the Mahayana. If you practice Concentration without having this good root, you will not attain Concentration and will not practice successfully. You should read and recite the sutras a lot, either read and recite the Mahayana sutras, or read and recite the sutras of the Shravaka and Pratyekayana, or the sutras of the three vehicles. If you enter all three vehicles at the same time, it is also okay. I feel that the Buddha spoke from Mahayana to Middle Vehicle, then to Hinayana. After talking about the Bodhisattva Dharma, we then talk about the Pratyekabuddha Dharma. Having finished talking about Duyen Giac, he then talked about Thanh Van. Depending on the three vehicles, what kind of capacity you have, mainly makes you leave suffering, be happy, and eliminate afflictions. His purpose, which is his principle, is to speak to the four disciples, namely Bhikkhus, Bhiksunis, Male Disciples, and Female Disciples. Upāsaka (Upāsaka) translates as Male Closer, Upāsikā translates as Female Closer. Those are the four groups of disciples, [including] two groups of lay people and two groups of monks.
