There are also those who have not taken refuge or received the Dharma, or there are good men and good women with pure faith. Because their foundation for cultivating Concentration in the past life is a little thin, the good roots in the past are not thick, they will follow the Worldly Truth, not the meaning of the True Truth.

In the previous section, we said, in general, to practice according to Truth. Practicing Concentration is to rely on the truth, the first step is also worldly, gradually entering the truth. When they contemplate their mind, they will enter from reason. Comparing the two sides, Concentration is supposed to enter from reason, but they talk about this according to the Worldly Truth, which means the foundation is not yet ripe. The Buddha made those sentient beings learn “practice chanting”. Practicing recitation also has certain requirements. It is absolutely not the case that we recite a passage of sutras, or recite a set of sutras that is considered “practicing recitation”. We recite too little, too short. The Buddha taught them to practice reciting at the beginning of the night, at the end of the night, and in the middle of the night, [or in other words] the first four hours of the night, four hours in the middle of the night, and four hours at the end of the night, which is twelve hours. During those twelve hours, except for four hours in the middle of the night, you can rest a little and not recite. In addition, at the beginning and end of the night, you must be diligent, not lazy, and practice recitation.

Because that person's base is very shallow and thin, but his heart is very big and his vow is very big. In the past, that person sowed the seeds of Mahayana nature. Therefore, he invokes the Supreme Wisdom. Supreme Wisdom is the hope of achieving Buddhahood. The Buddha said: I will arrange for that person to stay in a pure Mahayana place, learn to read Mahayana dharma, recite Mahayana sutras, make him read it himself, and even teach others to read it. If you develop a great heart to read for yourself, but also teach others to read, learn for yourself, and also teach others to learn, you have the idea of ​​saving sentient beings. Either recite it yourself, or recite the Lotus Sutra, or recite the Prajnaparamita Sutra. If you cannot recite the entire Prajnaparamita, then recite the Diamond Sutra, or recite the Heart Sutra. Recite yourself and teach others to recite. Speak yourself, or teach others to speak. Or research and study the Mahayana scriptures yourself, and also teach others to study. Using such a method causes yourself and others to read and recite Mahayana sutras in order to end afflictions.

Regardless of whether the purpose of studying Buddhism is deep or shallow, to practice Concentration, or to practice Wisdom, to enter from the aspect of Hue, or to enter from the aspect of Concentration, one must practice Concentration. Reciting and reciting the Mahayana already contains the meaning of cultivating Concentration, is it not at that time that the order was placed like this: Whenever one cultivates Concentration, Concentration will be of the highest status. If we completely separate Concentration and Hue, we only study Concentration, not Hue, it will be impossible! Only practicing Hue, not practicing Concentration, is also not possible! It must be that Concentration and Hue are balanced. But speaking in order, Concentration can give birth to Hue, and through Hue it can also enter Concentration. When reciting a sutra, reading to the corresponding place, there is no one reading or the sutra being read, there is no sign of Self and Other, this is also a type of effort that belongs to the state of Concentration. However, cultivating Concentration is the same, cultivating Wisdom is the same, reading and reciting Mahayana is the same, "retaining past thoughts" is also the same, the purpose is to eliminate afflictions.

Due to afflictions, drowsiness or distractions occur. If it is not distractions, it will be drowsiness. As long as there is discrimination, nothing can happen. If the mind is not at peace, how can it be achieved? Our mind cannot be concentrated! If you don't have Concentration, even if you read and recite the Mahayana, you won't be able to concentrate. You sit there, chanting in front of the original sutra, [because your mind is wandering], not knowing where your recitation has gone. I kept reciting but I couldn't even find where I was reciting. I recited to the point of falling asleep. Ah! How far is the recitation? Don't know! Or raising false thoughts is also a mistake!

I feel like I'm not a hard worker at all. People who have really worked hard for several decades should also enter the land; Currently, I still can't! I mean it! Regardless of cultivating Concentration, as long as you are a disciple studying Buddhism, you must be free from afflictions. Are there many afflictions? Too much! I copied from the Bach Dhammapada Abhidharma to tell people about afflictions; This is also very useful.

“Great and middle afflictions” (Great and middle afflictions): “Great afflictions” are the basic afflictions. They follow your mind and accompany your mind and dharma. Just start thinking, troubles will immediately follow! You cannot leave it. The first thing is due to lack of wisdom, ignorance, and stupidity. Ignorance is often described by another name: Wrong View, or Ignorance, we all have a lot of it! Letting go includes many things, if we reflect, everyone will understand. Indulging and relaxing is in the middle of the night, and at the beginning and end of the night you recite the Mahayana, [so] what do you do during the day? Hesitant behavior? Impossible! Twenty-four hours a day, the Buddha teaches you to recite or meditate. You do not keep the precepts, [but because of such strict practice], you will naturally keep the precepts. We are stupid, lethargic, lazy, and unconfident, so why don't we develop a diligent mind? It's basically due to insufficient faith! Don't trust everyone's words, no matter who says it, they will refute it. If you don't believe it, why are you still sitting here? That faith is limited, and currently our faith is not steadfast. Because faith is not sharp, diligence cannot arise, relatively speaking.

Cau Xa Luan calls drowsiness and restlessness (excitement) the great afflictions. [Great afflictions] include six types, namely greed, anger, ignorance, pride, doubt, [and evil views]. From evil views, five things are born, i.e. Body View, Boundary View, Wrong View, Holding View, and Forbidden View. [Those five views combined with greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and doubt] form the Ten History of afflictions (ten articles of Conclusion), which is the basis of affliction. “Great affliction” can be understood as basic affliction.

What is “Middle affliction” again? It may be Dependent on afflictions (Upakleśa). “Middle afflictions” includes twenty afflictions. We divide the twenty afflictions into Great Sui, Middle Sui, and Minor Sui. Dai Sui's afflictions include eight items; That is also Dependent on Afflictions in the basic affliction. Unbelief (Aśrāddhya), Relaxation (Kausīdya), Movement (Auddhatya, excitement, turmoil, turmoil), Drowsiness (Styāna) are the Dependent mental factors. Basic afflictions depend on the mind. The mind dharma consists of eight objects, that is, the [consciousnesses] of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, Manas, and Alai Da. That is called “eight minds” (eight kings of mind). The Mind Dharma includes eight items, while the Mind Department Dharma includes fifty-one items.

Here, we only point out twenty items, that is, the Great Dependent afflictions including the eight items mentioned above, i.e. Unbelief, Laziness, Gestures, Drowsiness, Indolence (Pramāda, letting go), plus Seven Right Mindfulness (squandered mindfulness, Muṣitasmṛti), Distraction (Vikṣepa), and Unrighteous Knowledge (Asamprajanya), constitute the eight Great Dependent Afflictions. Unrighteous Knowledge is the Great Sui affliction, [call it] the Great Sui affliction to show that it is very heavy.

Central The afflictions are very simple, the first is Tam (shy), the second is Quy (tiger)[33]. We often say it together as Tam Quy. Actually, Tam is Tam, Quy is Quy, how to explain? Tam is feeling uncomfortable in your own mind, ashamed of yourself, embarrassed in your mind, feeling that you have done something wrong, not thinking "It's okay to break the precepts", or "It's still okay to do something", until you do something wrong, shame arises in your mind. Preciousness means that towards others, towards the Three Jewels, towards fellow monks, there is shame, there is shame towards oneself, there is shame towards others. Tam and Quy are Middle Dependent Afflictions. That is the Middle Dependent Afflictions. Eight Dai Sui dishes and two Trung Sui dishes, combined into ten dishes. There is also Tieu Sui's troubles, which includes ten items, combined into twenty items. The minor afflictions include Wrath (Krodha), Hatred (Pradāśa), Brain (Upanāha), Wealth (Mrakśa), Arrogance (Māyā), Shame (Asāṭhya), Pride (Mada), Harm (Vihiṃsā), Illness (Īrṣyā), and Xan (Mātsarya, stinginess), ten items.

What is anger? Discontent! We say "discontent makes us complain", we can't help it. Colloquially speaking, “can't help but get angry”. You cannot bear this, whether it happens to someone else, or you see a situation that makes you feel dissatisfied. However, that is the way of thinking in your mind. Hate is having resentment. If you think someone else harmed you, you immediately hate. The hatred became a little deeper. Brain means to upset you, to disturb you. Every noun contains a meaning. Phu means “obscure”, because it obscures you, making it impossible for wisdom to arise. Wealth is your behavior, or the obstacles in your mind that prevent wisdom from arising. The disease is jealousy. Being stingy, greedy, and unwilling to let go, when you see others giving alms, you become jealous: "That person always causes a stir, causing me to be obscured!" In my mind I always have that thought: when I see others doing good things, I won't be happy, and jealousy will arise. You just do it! That person doesn't do anything, such people are stingy with things!

Xan and Tac are considered a little lighter! Especially regarding the Dharma, he does not let others preach. If someone else preaches, that person will immediately be jealous. Because that person has a greedy mind. When you fall into greed and greed for the Dharma, you will fall into the path of hungry ghosts, which is very miserable. There are many stories like this! Regarding the Dharma, don't be greedy, don't be jealous. When you see others doing things, be happy and don't be greedy! Why be greedy? What are the reasons for being stingy and greedy? That person uses dharma to exchange conditions in the world! Whenever I get a price, I will treat you equally: "I preach the Dharma to you, you have to make offerings to me. We have to see if you pay the full price or not? If it's enough, then I'll say it, if it's not enough, I won't say anything!"

For those who study the Dharma, you must advise others to read and recite the Mahayana. [But] if that person doesn't advise others, that's fine. When he sees others advising others to read, he becomes jealous, "only I am good, only I am strong", spouting envious words, even uttering destructive words. “Xan” is that person who refuses to do it, “I teach you how to practice this dharma, you must make offerings to me properly!” There are masters who say it that way, but each person is different, so please consider depending on your mentality. There was a master who said something like that, "you have to bring a lot of money here", like what is said in Tibet: "You bring a good horse [to me], I will give you empowerment." I once asked my master: “What does that mean?” The teacher said: "That guy [disciple] is greedy and loves that horse like his life. How can he seek the Dharma? [Master] told him 'give me the horse and I will transmit the Dharma to you'. If he can let go, his practice will achieve success. I don't need his horse and give it to someone else." But you don't belong to that position, don't have the ability to forgive others, or don't have that virtue, don't make demands on others, or ask others to pay a certain price. What is the use of being offered a lot of gold, silver, and wealth?

Everyone, please read the story of Venerable Milarepa[34], his master is Marpa[35] asked him to offer all his possessions before transmitting the dharma to him. But [if we imitate doing so], what we say comes from greed, we do not have that ability, the other person will not be willing to let go, will not be willing to make offerings to the Dharma. Deceiving others is not trustworthy. Lying and flattery, you can easily see it. Anyone who is inferior to them, if they are arrogant, will definitely flatter their superiors. If you are arrogant towards your subordinates, you will definitely flatter your superiors. Seeing someone with power or money, that person will definitely bow their head, stoop, and that's what it means. He poured out all the flattering and sweet words. We can see this on TV. There are many people today who look like that. Those who study Buddhism should not flatter them!

Being complacent is not telling the truth. In that, it is divided into intentional and unintentional. You only seek profit and deceive people for the sake of your reputation. If you have a purpose, the crime of Cunning (deception) is a little bigger. Casually joking with others, or joking to tease, this crime will be much lighter. Cuong and Siam both belong to the category of false speech; But Cuong here is not like that, Cuong here is intentional, for fame and profit. Seduction (flattery, caressing) is also for fame and profit.

The harm is quite obvious, either harming others, but that person thinks of harming others, actually harming himself. Whatever harms others, it does not harm them, but on the contrary, it accomplishes them! You just harmed and stabbed people, causing them to lose their ears. Everyone who reads the Diamond Sutra [will know]: If anyone is despised by others, [that person's] sins in the previous life will also be destroyed. Or maybe you were harmed by someone else, you still can't pray! That person harms you, your sins in your previous life are destroyed. You originally deserved to fall into hell, because that person harmed you, you won't even fall into hell, that crime is gone!

Arrogance is arrogance. The word Kieu in “arrogance” has many interpretations. How many types of man are there? There are ten types of arrogance and ten types of arrogance. I'm just saying in general: That person has no ability, no soul, but still feels that he is better than others. There are many people of this type! That person's knowledge is not great, but he thinks he is very brilliant and better than anyone else. Everyone is despised by him. Even thought: "Śākyamuni Buddha is not real, I am the real Buddha." There are indeed people like that, there are also monks like that, there are also lay people like that. In the current era, everything is available! Anger, hatred, anger, wealth, anger, illness, anger, pride, harm, pride, how many things do we have now? The twenty items of affliction are all our afflictions. With these things, how can one be enlightened? Can you practice or not? Regardless of reading and reciting the Mahayana, or cultivating Concentration, they all block you, how can you enter it? Very difficult to enter! However, those are all our bad habits. The Buddha taught us that there are too many bad habits, everyone should check it out for themselves, don't come here to listen to pleasant words! The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra has very few pleasant words, and the later it becomes more complicated. Here we are talking roughly about our shortcomings. [Here mentioned] all kinds of great afflictions; In the following section, we will talk about each thing in detail, pointing out our mistakes that are arising at the present time.

If you eliminate those mistakes, it's good, you can practice Concentration and enter, reading and reciting the Mahayana can also give rise to wisdom. By reciting the Mahayana scriptures, you will read and recite the Mahayana sutras, enter Samadhi, and perhaps see a holy scene. Reading the chapter on Pure Conduct, you will see Manjushri Bodhisattva, there is not much difference! Reading Samantabhadra's Prayer, you will see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Reading the Ksitigarbha Sutra, you will see Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you read Pho Mon, you will see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, really? It's because your mind changes. Because your mind is determined, reading the sutra will arise. This is an illusory realm, don't think it's a holy realm. If you have a slight ego-view, you are attached to: "I'm so good, I can read the sutra and induce Bodhisattva to appear." That is pride and will immediately bring trouble. That's an illusory state. If you don't have any attachments, just read the same scriptures, it's okay if the [holy realm] appears, but it's okay if it doesn't appear! Like Van Hy Bodhisattva: “You are you, I am me”. When Manjushri Bodhisattva appeared before Van Hy, he showed the truth to the Master. The Master said: “Manjushri is Manjushri, Manjushri is Manjushri. You cannot do it for me”[36]. There is such spirit! Therefore, no matter what realm you are in, don't be attached to it. Whatever you should do, just do it. Whatever you should practice, just practice like that!

When you enter Samadhi, you can also see many realms. Especially when you first practice, Buddha and Bodhisattva are very spiritual, it seems like whatever you ask for is very compatible. Believing for a long time seems like Buddha and Bodhisattva are getting farther and farther away. It is not Buddha or Bodhisattva who are far away, but your mind that changes. Like us monks, if we become monks for one year, Buddha is before our eyes, if we become monks for ten years, Buddha moves to Tay Thien. After ten years, that person doesn't know anymore, Buddha is no more! For what reason? After studying Buddhism, many afflictions arise. Originally a holy matter, you turned it into a affliction. The place of Tuc De is not enough, add Khong Mon, it is certainly not empty. If there really is no emptiness, that means there is another emptiness, emptiness in the void. That Emptiness is very powerful, causing you to fall very quickly: "No problem! No!" Wipe out all cause and effect with one stroke of a pen. If that person doesn't study Buddhism, it's still a little better, he doesn't have such great courage. After studying Buddhism, I was very bold: "Buddha said No!" So that person dares to do anything. After doing it, it's definitely not for nothing! Wait until you feel pain, your stomach hurts, your head hurts, then you will know that Emptiness is not possible! Even a little bit is not considered a No! That person knows the benefits, so he will honestly learn.

In the previous section, we talked about the practice of reciting the wheel of karma, talking about "the accumulation of afflictions in the middle ages, the eradication of attachments, the witness of the Supreme Wisdom" (the huge blocks of afflictions in it are eliminated, because it causes the attainment of Supreme Wisdom). Let's repeat a bit. In the previous section, we talked about cultivating Concentration of karma, that is, cultivating Concentration; Here we teach about the practice of reciting karma. I'm afraid that people are afraid to practice chanting a lot, but to practice Concentration is a little. Because we read the Diamond Sutra, or read the Amitabha Sutra, “reciting practice” is reciting the Mahayana. Normally, people look at the words, recite them once, and they're done. Sometimes, because time is very rushed, it seems like I increase my reading speed faster. In such a situation, when reciting, it is not easy for you to enter. I say "cannot enter", because while practicing recitation, one cannot enter according to the principles in the scriptures and enter Contemplation, only reading according to the text. Practicing chanting like that, the potency is weaker. If you practice chanting like that, it will be difficult to cut off afflictions!

Practicing karma chanting and cultivating karma concentration are the same. If you can dedicate yourself to reading, such as reading the Pho Mon chapter, if you can hear it and have it explained, even better. Having not heard a lecture, or heard a master say "reading the Pho Mon chapter will be beneficial", you should request a copy of the Pho Mon sutra to read like that. Without a master teaching you, without anyone telling you how to read, the results you get will be a little less. Why? In reciting the wheel of karma, there is an additional word Practice. “Practice” is studying. After you have studied, then read. When you practice reciting the wheel of karma, that is, when we recite the Mahayana, you should not relax. At the beginning of the night and at the end of the night [must be recited].

Now we are in the End of Time, afraid that with the current situation, the bodies of living beings will not be able to endure! Everyone just reads, either the Universal Gate chapter, or the Samantabhadra Prayer chapter, or the Medicine Master Sutra, or the Amitabha Sutra, reading one set is enough. So you don't have to use it at the beginning of the night or at the end of the night, it doesn't become too much of a time-wasting problem.

When reading, you must follow etiquette. In general, an incense burner is required. At the same time, depending on how much you can handle, offer some flowers. If you can't offer many, one flower is fine. You use a small flower vase, pour in some water to offer flowers, light a stick of incense, that ritual is required. Laying out the original sutra, we must first bow three times. After the ceremony, open the prayer and calm down for a moment. After that, you must calm down for a moment and meditate for a moment. My mind was calm, so I opened the scriptures to recite. Reciting requires each word to be clear and distinct. When first reciting, it must be clear and distinct. If you want to penetrate a little, then follow the text and meditate.

If you read the Pho Mon chapter, the Pho Mon chapter praises the merits of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, praising Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as follows: Whenever you encounter any accident, just recite Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) can save you from suffering. The scriptures teach like that. You must know: Reciting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva must be focused; If you don't have the will, it won't be possible. If you know how to practice Avalokiteśvara, when reading the Universal Gate chapter, you contemplate why Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) made such a great vow? I also hope to learn from Him, read and recite the stories He did in the past, also the old stories, those are the stories Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva did in the past. You read [texts that teach about] Him, and you must also learn to follow Him and make your vows.

When chanting, if you add meditation, the effect will be great. Only then can afflictions be eliminated. Some Dharma friends once asked me like this: "I have recited the Samantabhadra Prayer for thousands of sets. Every day I have recited one set for more than ten years, but there is not even the slightest effect." I asked: "How do you chant?" That person replied: "I hold the original sutra and recite it." True or not? Correct! I said: "When you say effective, what effect are you praying for? In the first place, what vow are you making?" When you practice chanting, you make a vow. If you read a sutra, either the Ksitigarbha Sutra, or read the Universal Door chapter, or the Samantabhadra Vows chapter, then you will follow Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and make a vow to read the Ksitigarbha Sutra. If you read the Universal Gate chapter, you will make your vow according to Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara). Reading Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's Vows, you will follow Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to make his vows. If you chant like that, the effect will be great. If you can understand the meaning contained in that sutra, when reciting it, if you do not give rise to attachments, you will not see yourself as someone who can recite it, and there will be no sutras that can be recited. When chanting or reciting sutras, your mind and the sutra become one body, your mind and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva form one body. Whichever sutra you read, you will form one body with the Bodhisattva in that sutra. That is called an inconceivable realm. That is a method of reading scriptures.

After reading the prayer, you must dedicate it. When you start reading, you must make a vow, and after reading, you must dedicate it. Must follow a certain process, which is called “cultivation”. When you read the sutras, you practice the Bodhisattva path right here, you practice. [You wonder]: "I myself sit here reciting sutras, how can I practice the Bodhisattva path?" The merit of reading and reciting sutras is blessed and dedicated to all sentient beings, especially sentient beings in the three evil realms. You make a vow, hoping that Bodhisattva will bless them, save them, and eliminate disasters for them. The meaning of dedication is to use our mental energy, use the strength of the work we have done, and whatever reward we get, give it all to them. Just like when we work, we bring the salary we earn to make offerings to the Three Jewels. Afterwards, seeing living beings in poverty, he gave alms to them. His merit was very great. But you don't know that when reading and chanting sutras, it's the same. You have achieved the reward because the Bodhisattva family is blessed by you, the Three Jewels bless you, and you hope that the Three Jewels will bless all sentient beings, regardless of whether they are predestined or ungainly. That way, when you recite, you can end afflictions.

When practicing chanting, you can eliminate middle and great afflictions and achieve Supreme Wisdom. Otherwise, if you follow the scriptures and just recite the texts, you will not achieve [such an effect in eliminating afflictions]. When reading, when reciting, you must add the power of visualization, only then can you attain Supreme Wisdom. Because people rarely practice Concentration, chant the Medicine Sutra to eliminate disasters, reduce suffering, and make the body and mind healthy and disease-free. Even if you are sick, you will be cured, the Bodhisattva family will be cured. You must also know how to read the Medicine Buddha Sutra. At the same time, when you read, follow the meaning of the scriptures and enter Contemplation, Concentration and Hue together. When you read, if your mind is not confused, you will be able to enter Concentration after reading. This is not at all a deep sleep. If you read it and then become drowsy, [thinking] it is the same as entering Concentration, then you will be confused! Talking about the meaning of entering Concentration, it is like reading the Avatamsaka Sutra, you will enter the Avatamsaka realm.

In the past, there was an old monk like that. He read in Concentration, his reading speed was very fast, how fast? On his way from the Heavenly King Palace[37] to the main hall, he finished reading a set of Chinese Sutras

Serious! Everyone knows that the Avatamsaka Sutra has eighty volumes. He only walked one or two hundred steps like that and finished reading a set of the Avatamsaka Sutra. He read it in Concentration! If read commonly, “one is all”. Then, the attendant asked the question, not believing in Him, found eighty people, each holding a book. Eighty people listened to Him read the sutras. They took the first book and heard Him read one book, and took eighty books and heard Him read eighty books. He read it clearly.

Although we have not yet reached that concentration, we can do it from the initial, shallow level. You read the Ksitigarbha Sutra, and when you read a chapter, immediately visualize that chapter, know what that chapter means, understand the meaning and then read again, the effect will be a little better. Even when reciting prayers, don't let trivial matters accumulate in your mind. When reading the sutra, do not give rise to false thoughts. When your mind is confused, sit still and read the scriptures, and as soon as you read, you fall asleep. This situation also exists, if you read it, just read it, but you get confused, lethargic, and don't know where you are going. In cultivating concentration, one must not be confused or lethargic, and the same is true when reading sutras. Don't be moody (lao chao), but also don't be lethargic. If you behave, very little of that sutra will be seen. If you read for a very long time and still don't finish reading, you will get bored! If you encounter a long sutra, you will not be able to read it. Those are the mistakes you must prevent in order to reach Omniscience.

Reading sutras is cultivating wisdom, but also cultivating merit. The Diamond Sutra teaches about the Emptiness of Prajna. Reading the Diamond Sutra brings great blessings. [That sutra teaches reading and chanting the Diamond Sutra] the merit is greater than the merit of giving alms due to “using seven treasures to fill three thousand great thousand worlds to make offerings”. That is blessing, and it can also be used, that is, you can use [that blessing] to achieve Hue. That's Hue. Only by cultivating blessings and wisdom can one attain Prajna wisdom. In the scriptures [Vajrayana Sutra], it seems that nothing is said about how to practice, but in fact, each sutra teaches us the method. You practice, when you practice is when you learn, only then can you gain enjoyment. The Buddha made all sentient beings, if anyone has the Mahayana foundation and specializes in practicing the Mahayana, will make them learn to read and recite the Mahayana. Not only do you study and read yourself, but you also advise others to study and read. In this way, you will be able to attain unsurpassed wisdom, because reading the Mahayana sutras, dedicating them to all sentient beings, eliminating all suffering, can eliminate all the sufferings of sentient beings. You read it yourself, causing all sentient beings to read it too, causing them to enter the citadel of Fearlessness.

“Fearless City” means that after becoming a Buddha, there will be four fearless states. Fear is fear. Currently, the situation is very scary. There are many Dharma friends who read the Ksitigarbha Sutra and feel different emotions, or see ghosts and spirits, or feel cold. These are not all bad phenomena! At that time, we must ask: "Is that person afraid and does not dare to read the prayer anymore?" Originally reading the sutras was to eliminate fear, but that person had fear, and because of reading the sutras, he felt fear. There are many situations like this! Not only Ksitigarbha Sutra, reading other sutras will also be available. First of all, you must understand clearly: When reading and chanting Mahayana sutras, there will be dharma protectors to protect you. Why do you feel panic? Originally, when reading the sutra, you can enter without fear, enter without fear. The Buddha's Four Fearless Fears are All-Wisdom Fearless, fearless of obstacles to the path (not afraid of the dharmas that hinder the path). When you practice the Way, [Buddha] clearly explains these obstacles. When He was speaking, everyone was fearless. Only the Buddha can clearly explain all the dharma obstacles. If you want to cultivate the path, he will clearly tell you the obstacles to the path. When He spoke, He was not afraid.

There is also Fearless Gonorrhea. The End of Aspiration means not leaving behind the three worlds, not missing all sentient beings, allowing them to attain liberation forever. The fourth thing is the End of Suffering Path without Fear, which means saying “ending the path of suffering” without fear. When speaking, don't be afraid. Because of his wisdom, the Buddha was able to know [in detail]. That is the Mahayana Bridge. If you seek Mahayana, you must hope to enter Buddha's wisdom, reach the realm of Buddha, and eliminate suffering for all sentient beings. When you read and recite Mahayana sutras, you will be able to achieve those benefits. This is exactly the same as seeking benefits and attaining Concentration in the previous section.

(Sutra) Weak sentient beings seek Pratyekabuddha If all sentient beings seek the Shravakas Thea, I will attain peace and wisdom by reciting the Four A Level Demons for a hundred verses, a hundred verses by reciting the Vairocana Tripitaka, a hundred verses by reciting Abhidharma, up to Bhikāsha, and practice reciting them in a spiritual period. Good man! The name Tathagata practices reciting the wheel of karma.
(Sutra: If sentient beings seek Pratyekabuddha Thea, I will arrange the dharmas of dependent origination for them to recite. If sentient beings pray to the Shravakas, I will arrange hundreds of thousands of chants of the Four Aghasa, hundreds of thousands of chants of Vairocana, hundreds of thousands of chants of Abhidharma and Vaisya for them to practice and recite Hybrid).

If that person is not of Mahayana temperament, reading and chanting Mahayana will not be able to enter, Buddha immediately said Pratyekabuddha. The Pratyekabuddha Vehicle is the Dharma of the Twelve Causes and Conditions. Those twelve dharmas of dependent origination can also be said to be “dependent arising dharmas”. Seeing all things arising and passing away and changing, do you know why you have to suffer? Why will you enjoy? Of course, attaining nirvana is joy, reincarnation in samsara is suffering. Because of the transformation of all things, from his wisdom, enlightenment and wisdom can arise. He saw that the trees had turned green and yellow, the four seasons were Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter, until the length of human life was different. For those things, he devoted himself to research and found the cause. Two causes in the past give rise to suffering in the present, Ignorance is dependent on Actions, Actions are dependent on Name and Form, Name and Form are dependent on Six Entrances, and Six Entrances are dependent on Contact. When the Buddha preaches the Dharma, that is, when the Buddha appears in the world, Pratyekabuddhas will be enlightened based on the dharma of causes and conditions spoken by the Buddha. When there was no Buddha born, it was he who saw all birth and death and change and attained enlightenment, so he was called Single Enlightenment. There are also cases where, due to good roots in the past, for this type of living beings, one speaks the dharma of cause and effect, speaks of the dharma of dependent origination, and teaches them to recite this type of sutra.

A Ham School has a total of twenty-two volumes. There are four parts in it, including thirty sets of scriptures. The first book records things related to the Buddha's life. The second part is practice, the scriptures related to the teachings. The third part is that pagans question, debate with each other, and attack the wrong knowledge and wrong views of pagans. The fourth part talks about the morality of "birth, existence, difference, destruction, formation, existence, destruction, emptiness" of this world. In general, Tu A Ham all have those meanings.

Middle A Ham only teaches the Four Noble Truths (Catvāri Āryasatyāni), the twelve causes and conditions (Pratītya-samutpāda-aṅga), or gives examples, which are also the words when the Buddha and his disciples discussed, up to the things they did. Just like when we chant sutras, it's just language, but Trung A Ham teaches us how to practice, that is, the method of practice. Therefore, this sutra belongs to Action. Practicing according to language instructions, therefore belongs to Practice.

Tang Nhat A Ham means speaking in numbers. Because when practicing according to this sutra, every ten numbers are increased by one, resulting in eleven dharmas. For every ten dharmas increased by one, the word Increase Nhat has such a meaning. There are fifty volumes of the Sutra, and one more volume is added, so it becomes fifty-one volumes.

So originally Buddhism had four types of scriptures, the Four Agamas. According to the scriptures, I told everyone a little. “An arrangement of hundreds of verses to recite A Level Ma, a hundred thousand verses to recite Bhikkhuni Da Tang” (Arrange hundreds of thousands of texts to recite A Level Ma, hundreds of thousands of verses to recite Bhikkhu Da Tang): “Bhi Nai Da” (Vinaya) is the Vinaya Pitaka, specializing in precepts. Precepts are rules and laws that Buddhist disciples must follow. The reason it is called “precepts”, is not called law, because it has two types: Tri and Gia. “Treatment” is worth doing, there is Citadel and Tathagata. Only Tri is not allowed to do it. Tac Tri is something that must be done, must be done; If you don't do it, you will violate the precepts. Telling you not to do it, but if you still insist on doing it, you will also violate the precepts. It is necessary to divide it into two types of Instruction and Action, in which many things are said. As everyone is very familiar with Tam Quy. Does Tam Quy say precepts or not? The Three Refuges are also precepts. Taking refuge in Buddha is intended to prevent you from taking refuge in other sects. After taking refuge in Buddha, you can no longer take refuge in demons or pagans. After studying Buddhism, you must recite the Three Jewels, recite the Buddha's name, recite the Dharma, and recite the Sangha. That is Tac Tri. You can't take refuge in pagans, don't look at the classic books of pagans. When taking refuge in the Dharma, you should not look at the scriptures of pagans. That's Chi Tri. You must definitely read the Buddhist scriptures as Tathagata. Every thing is like that. When taking refuge in the Sangha, the Sangha is a monk, also all monastics, you cannot take refuge in an evil destinies, that is Chi Tri.

In general, in the precepts, for the precepts part of Thanh Van Thua, the monk precepts include two hundred and fifty articles. All two hundred and fifty precepts are not broken, if you keep them pure, you will definitely attain Arahantship. That is to say, from the day of receiving the precepts onwards, one must not violate them. If you commit a crime and follow the correct method of repentance, then you are a Tathagata. There is the Yet Ma Dharma, that is, [the ways] that teach you how to [repent, reveal], so do it like that. You have committed a sin, broken a small, very slight precept, repented, then been purified, restored to purity, that is Tathagata. [The method of revealing, presenting before the Sangha, sincerely repenting] is called the Yet Ma Dharma.

Abhidharma belongs to the Abhidharma Pitaka. [Abhāma, Bhikāṇa, and Abhidharma] are Sutras, Disciplines, and Treatises. In original Buddhism, the Agama Sutra is the Sutra, the Abhidharma Sutra is the Abhidharma. The Sutras, Laws, and Treatises are the Tripitaka. Vibhāṣā is a treatise that has received many criticisms and comments. For those who study Pratyekabuddha or Shravaka, we will teach them to practice chanting those things.

“The name Tathagata practices reciting the wheel of karma” (That is called the practice of reciting the wheel of karma of the Tathagata): How was it mentioned above to practice reciting? Recite those things. You feel which type is suitable for you. You read the Four Agamas Sutra and feel it is very good, then you read the Four Agama Sutras. You read the Mahayana sutras, Diamond Sutras, Amitabha Sutras, feel very good, read the Mahayana Sutras. After you take refuge with a certain master, very few people turn to the master to ask for Dharma: "Master! What is the best sutra I should recite?" Very few people ask about this issue. After taking the Three Refuges, you will leave. Not even reciting the Buddha's name, reciting the Dharma, or reciting the Sangha, and reading the sutras! They didn't ask for it! If there is a request, the master will explain it in more detail. Some teachers don't talk to you; You don't ask, the teacher doesn't say. You have received the Three Refuges, maybe you even want to receive the Five Precepts. If you accept the Five Precepts, [the master] will definitely have to explain them to you. Explaining the meaning of the Three Refuges to you, that is, from then on, you should not forget to recite the Buddha's name, the Dharma's name, and the Sangha's name. You must preach these things; that is the practice of chanting.

(Sutra) Good man! Van Ha Tathagata's business of blessings and karma? The sentient beings have dull base, the good roots, the wisdom is weak, lazy, absent-minded, infected with the previous species, receive private tools, far away from good friends, the self is at peace like the sentient beings, using good karma, the spiritual practice of Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, close to the body of teachers, and pedagogy. Good man! The Tathagata's name is a wheel of blessings and karma.
(Sutra: Good man! What is the Tathagata's wheel of merit and karma? That is, sentient beings Stupid inborn, not sown with good roots, with little wisdom, lazy, absent-minded, addicted to the enjoyment of things, separated from good friends, I will arrange for sentient beings like that, making them take care of cultivating good karma, that is, making them serve the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and serve the teachers and pedagogues. This is called the Tathagata's wheel of merit.

If you can't practice Concentration, you can't practice chanting, Tathagata still has the method of method. What methods and methods are there? Business blessings and karma. Karma is Action (doing). You do a little merit, that is, cultivate merit. This is talking about a type of sentient being whose nature is very dull, unable to read scriptures, much less able to cultivate Concentration, stupid, slow, and without wisdom. Because in the past, they did not sow good roots, their wisdom was very lacking, very poor, which also means "no wisdom". Then they manifest themselves as lazy and absent-minded. Everyone loses their thoughts easily! Sometimes we hold a rosary, and every time we pray it, we think of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. I put down the rosary and immediately forgot about it. Take the rosary and recite it. When it comes to “reciting”, any reciting does not forget the Three Jewels, or reciting Buddha, reciting Dharma, or reciting Sangha. You can also specialize in reciting Buddha's name. Because that person's wisdom is poor and his good roots are few, his moments of absent-mindedness will be even more frequent. They are attached to enjoyment, wanting to enjoy all the things in life. They would rather go play eight games of mahjong, tell them to come and listen to the sutra lecture here for just one and a half hours, they feel very miserable. Each person has different preferences. Just taking the teachings of the sutras as an example, those who don't believe in Buddha don't need to talk about it. For us Buddhist disciples, you tell them to have fun, their spirit is full of enthusiasm, tell them to recite the sutras, or practice concentration, they will be sluggish. As for the body or items necessary for life, they will keep it very carefully, not lazy, very diligent, completely opposite! That's because they are greedy and have desires for this world.

At the same time, it is also because there are no “good friends” (good friends) to help them. Being called “good friends” includes you, either as husband and wife, or as friends, or as relatives. Because we have a relative who believes in Buddha, he will advise you to believe in Buddha, hoping to lead you to believe in Buddha. Because of that person, you have the opportunity to believe in Buddha. If you don't have that predestined relationship, you won't meet that good friend. Among your friends, you will help each other, remind each other, and make you practice without slacking off. Laziness is the opposite of diligence, mindfulness is the opposite of mindfulness. If there is no good being, it will be like the kind of sentient beings [stupid, dull-minded beings are talking about here]. The Buddha taught: “I will make arrangements for them, making them take care of cultivating blessings”. “Business blessing” is to practice and accumulate some blessings. Reciting the Buddha's name, reciting the Dharma, or going to temples and shrines to do good deeds, or repairing temples, participating in practice, like many Dharma friends doing good deeds (doing charity, or doing meritorious deeds), depends on how you dedicate that merit. Even though you perform very small meritorious karma, you must dedicate and expand it to greatness. This story is related to ideas.

There are also masters whom you take refuge in, either as teachers themselves, or as pedagogues, when they exist, be their attendants, or take care of them. When they practice, you do a little work for them, all of which are “business blessings” (caring about cultivating blessings). If you take care of cultivating blessings, stay in the temple and help the monks. So, the lay followers, that is, the Upasakas, the Upasakas, are also the Servant Men and the Venerable Women. The Male Servant and the Female Servant are the business blessings. The first step is to deal with your own teacher. Generally speaking, the teacher is the monk, which also means the monk from whom you receive precepts, or the Buddhist monks, teachers, Buddhist monks, and monks who ordained you are all included. You do some work for them. If you don't succeed in cultivating Concentration and if you don't succeed in reading the sutras, then you should do some good deeds. If you work as an incense burner in front of the Buddha's table, or if you have a Buddha statue in your house, every day you clean the altar and burn incense, these are all blessings. There are many business stories and blessings; That is Tathagata's second Buddha Wheel achievement.

(Sutra) Good man! Self becomes like the second Buddha Wheel. Due to the trial of the wheel of karma, the supreme wisdom of the three worlds of karma, as it really is, fully understands all sentient beings, all karma and dharma receive their retributions, according to the dharma, establish the three wheels of karma, mature all sentient beings, attain peace and stability, attain no fear, attain no fear, bad devas, heretical heretics, turn the wheel of great brahma, become the great holy life, truly understand the retribution of sentient beings.
(Sutra: O good man! I achieved the second Buddha Wheel like that. Because of that wheel, use it without The wisdom of the upper three worlds of karma, as it really is, clearly knows the karmic dharma of receiving the causes and retributions of sentient beings. According to the nature of each sentient being, it has established three wheels of karma to mature all sentient beings to be saved, allowing them to live in peace, not to be frightened, not to be afraid, to dispel the evil talk of demons and pagans, to turn the wheel of great brahma, to achieve the great holy life, to truly know clearly the cause and retribution of sentient beings.

“Due to testing the wheel of karma, it is true that the supreme three-worldly karmic wisdom, as it really is, knows that all sentient beings receive their karma and receive their consequences” (Due to that wheel, using the supreme three-worldly karmic wisdom, it is true that the karmic dharmas receive the causes and retributions of sentient beings): “The three-worldly karma wisdom” refers to Buddha. For the past, future and present three lives, He can clearly know the karma of the three lives, knows exactly the karma of all sentient beings. All sentient beings in the past, present, and future have done what they have done, what they have sown, and what consequences they have now suffered, the Buddha knows exactly what it is. Therefore, “according to the occasion”, according to what should be, that is, adapting to their base, three types of karma wheels will be established. It can be said that the "three karma wheels" are the three karma wheels above, i.e. concentration karma, practice of reciting karma, and business of meritorious karma. According to their base, they see which type is suitable for them, that is, which karma wheel, then teach them to rely on that karma wheel to practice, so that all sentient beings who have been saved by the Buddha can be at peace. “Peaceful” means not suffering, not panicking, not afraid because of the three evil destiniess, making them fearless. Falling into the three evil realms is suffering, there is no need to even talk about falling into the three evil realms, even if we are human, as in the present time everyone is human, that is, humanely speaking, at present we are all Buddha's disciples, belonging to the four disciples, are you scared, sad or not? Every day we have to worry about winning, worrying about losing, and being afraid, why? You do not practice good Concentration karma. Even for the third wheel, merit is not enough, meritorious karma is not enough!

Buddha was not like that. He accomplished, for all sentient beings, knowing exactly whether the good roots of sentient beings are deep or shallow, as well as knowing whether they have created thick or thin karma. Is the karma created good karma or bad karma? Is the seed sown deep or not? Big or not? As for the retribution they are receiving, is there suffering or not? Are you afraid or not? Know you have fear. Because you have fear, the Buddha will teach you the method to eliminate fear, which is the three wheels of karma as just mentioned. Including how to practice Concentration, how many types of Concentration are there? As for reciting, reciting too much! It depends on what type of sutra you [prefer] to recite. Business blessings are very wide! Nowadays, everyone hopes for all kinds of good roots; As for reading and reciting Mahayana sutras, we also become cultivators of merit! Even though you don't gain wisdom, reading and reciting the sutras is still a blessing, even the blessing of hearing the name is not easy! Regarding the good roots in the past, the Buddha has all the Omnisciences, He can know everything, making you no longer afraid, making you finally become a Buddha, can also be exactly like Him, can also destroy the evil thoughts of all demons and pagans.

“Changing the great Brahma wheel”: “Pham” means purity. It is possible to achieve purity, so the karma you have done and practiced can all become pure virtue. “Pham Hanh” means purity. Speaking from the Buddha's side, the Buddha turned the great wheel of dharma, turned the pure wheel of dharma. He can truly know the causes and consequences of all living beings.

(Sutra) Thien Son! Nvoid Kshatriya empowered the great king to become skillful and wise, contemplated all the monks, Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Phietxa, Thudatta-class, types of merit, well-educated, brave, skillful,techniques. All sentient beings are endowed with merit, skillful, wise, diligent, courageous, steadfast and unwavering. Their merits and virtues are dignified.
(Sutra: Good man! As the great king of the Kshatriya nature has been contemplated. Achieve skillful wisdom, observe all kinds of merit, be well-versed, be brave, talented and skillful of all monks, Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Phiet-sama, Thu-datta, etc. If sentient beings are rich in merit, achieve wisdom of skillful means, be diligent, brave, steadfast and not shrinking, have all kinds of merit and virtue to adorn themselves.

Use this king wheel to illustrate the third Buddha Wheel. We have talked about the first and second Buddha Wheel, now we mention the third king wheel of King Sat-di-li. First is the simile, then the dharma. Dharma is about Buddha Wheel, that is dharma. Using Kshatriya in the world, that is also the nobility of the four types of Indian nature. After he received empowerment, received the royal throne, and achieved wisdom and skillful means. The king looks at the people in the country and observes everything. A monk (Śramaṇa) is a monk. Monks here include Brahmin monks, not just Buddhist monks. Brahmins also have monks. Other pagans also have monks. They use the word Samana to refer to them collectively. Samana translated means Can That, that is, “need to practice Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom, which means eliminating greed, anger, and ignorance” (diligently practice Precepts, Concentration, and Hue, to eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance). If we talk broadly about the meanings included in the word Samana, there will be many interpretations. In general, it has the same meaning.

India has four types of seed nature (Varṇa) outside the monks, what are the four types? These are Brahmana, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra. Brahmins are like readers in China, in India they are called “scholars”, that is, educated people. Sat-di-loi is an aristocrat, a descendant of kings. Phiet-xa includes industry and commerce, as well as scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants. Phiet-xa mostly talks about merchants. Thu-dala is a lowly race, that is, those who are butchers and servants. The four types of nature plus monks are all people in the country. The king has many different types of personalities for the people in the country. The king knows how to make them cultivate blessings, so that it is suitable for their career.

“Types of merit, multi-literature, bravery, skillful industry” (Types of merit, multi-literate, strong, brave, skillful): That is to say, depending on the type of person, so treat them properly like that. After that, the king will distribute and give them treasures, money, rice, land, houses, slaves, and servants. Therefore, the king also observed those people, which types of people had great merit and deserved to enjoy them, and which types of people were well-educated and wise. Multiliteracies are broad learning. Multiliteracies are about learning, not entirely about studying Buddhism. Like Thu-datta, basically they don't study Buddhism, there are people who don't believe in Buddha. “Technical skill” is Cong Xao Minh, Cong Xao (or skillful) is like a businessman. Phiet-xa includes workers, with technology, painting, decoration, and repair, all included in it. The word “industry” covers many things. Suppose we treat people with merit and wisdom (but here we are talking about people who behave very intelligently, not to be confused with wisdom in Buddhism).

“Accomplishment of skillful means” (Achievement of skillful means): The king gave this initiation to monks, brahmins, kshatriyas, bhikkhus, and Thudattala, the five types of people in the country, [judging] whether their merits were large or small, their abilities strong or weak, their skills Whether high or low, let's say a person has very abundant merit, that is, very great merit, that is one type, or has very skillful means, is very intelligent, that is, very agile, or has great contributions to the country, is diligent, brave, until whatever they do, they are steadfast and do not retreat, using their own merit to adorn themselves. Thus, the king will initiate the initiation based on their needs, wisdom, virtue and ability, whether large or small. Just like your current salary, whatever you can do, strong ability will earn you more money, poor ability will earn less!

(Sutra) Trying to initiate the great king's slayer-de-loi empowerment, according to the eagle, granting precious treasures, wealth, fields, slaves, servants. From the country's level, all sentient beings, virtuous and skillful, industry and silver, test the great king of Sat-de-loi to initiate, depending on the application, to support the family. In the absence of the country, all sentient beings are weak, their merit is weak, their diligence is small, they are lazy, lazy, they lose their mindfulness, they have no compassion, and they are not grateful. Because of the suffering of future generations, not seeing the chaplain, a layman, accumulating all evil deeds, trying to initiate the great king of Kshatriya, depending on the subject, the species will be punished. Hor the language of harsh teachings will be blamed, or we will take away the seed's precious treasures, wealth, or take advantage of the desired inheritance, or punish the gods. cane, or forbidden to go to prison, or exterminated, or beheaded. Such punishments are immeasurable.
(Sutra: The great king of the Kshatriya nature received that empowerment according to the merits Therefore, he gives away precious treasures, money, rice, land, houses, slaves, and servants. In his own land, if the living beings have poor virtue and talent, have little effort, and have a weak career, the king who has received the initiation of Kshatriya should provide some support and help them in his own land. thoughts, without compassion, without gratitude, without fear of suffering in the next life, immersed in the mire of inheritance, accumulating evil deeds, the king who initiates the Sat-samadhi will, as it should be, apply all kinds of punishments, or use harsh words of instruction, reprimand, or deprive him of treasures and wealth, or deprive him of wishes-fulfilling benefits and inheritance, or punish him with whips, canes, or imprisonment in prison, or beheadings. limbs, or beheading. There are countless punishments as such.)

“According to the person's preference, give away treasures, fields, slaves, and servants” (According to the right way, give away treasures, money, rice, land, houses, slaves, servants): In their own country, for all living beings, there is a distinction. Just like in ancient China, [officials] had nine ranks, from the position of Prime Minister to district governor, which was seven ranks, to office staff, to librarian[39], to village chief, village chief, a total of nine ranks. Depending on what they are suitable for, let them do it. As for the superiors, he gave them precious treasures, fields, houses, and servants. If you don't have any virtue, virtue is not very important and is given very little. Little merit is also corresponding to them. If their ability is such that they cannot even find food or clothing, the king will be compassionate, provide aid, and provide them with medical care. There are also people whose merit is even lower, who are not diligent, lazy, lazy, forget mindfulness, cannot do good deeds, and have no compassion for others. Even when giving them great favors, they still do not know how to repay the favor. Currently, they do not do good things, in the future, they will definitely suffer retribution. Regarding suffering and retribution in the next life, they are neither afraid nor panicked. Being an evil person has no fear at all.

“A layman, accumulating negative actions” (Immersed in the mud of family karma, accumulating negative actions): “Immersed in the mud of family karma” refers to a monk [not worrying about practicing, just worrying about making a profit, enjoying, just like a lay person], which is not renunciation. “Resident” is at home, at home is like a mud pit, submerged in a mud pit. Not only monks, but also others. “resident” can be explained in many ways, such as that person does not do good karma, specializes in evil karma, the country will have laws to punish that person. That is called “separate reward and punishment”. Above is talking about how big, small, many, few, and contributions to the country are. Great contributions will be greatly rewarded; small dedication, will be less. Even those who do not contribute at all and cannot maintain their lives, [the king] still has to diagnose, pity, and help them.

What about those who create evil? Those who accumulated evil deeds, King Sat-di-li punished them. There must also be “species of punishment” (types of punishment).. That is the law, or it will criticize them, if the evil karma is more severe, it will punish them, reprimand them, or confiscate their property, take away their treasures, property, or confiscate their inheritance. If that's not enough, either use a whip or stick to punish them, or give them a lot of whippings. Either put them in prison, cut off their limbs, or behead them, depending on whether they committed a big or small crime. These are just examples. We say these things mainly to show the Buddha Wheel. Because sentient beings create a lot of karma, they also commit a lot of evil deeds. When contradicting a country's laws, the penalties are many, there are countless penalties. Although there are many levels of rewards, there are also many levels of punishment.

(Sutra) Good man! The king of the Kshat-de-loi is empowered and accomplished like the third wheel of kings. Due to the test of rotation, the spirit of the country increases in peace and happiness, conquers all enemies and evil friends, good friends protect the body, and the spirit increases life span. Good man! Tathagata Tathagata achieved skillful knowledge of the basis of wisdom. Weak disciples, away from blessings, cunning and expedient means, reaching out for almsgiving, subduing tranquility, absent-mindedness, disordered mind, coming back to the self, taking refuge in the self, the good self knowing the base of ridicule, depending on hypnosis, winning the solution, depending on the situation, the theory of punishing the Vinaya Dharma.
(Sutra: O good man! Great Kingd Having received the empowerment of the third king wheel, because of that wheel, one can increase peace and joy in one's own land, be able to subdue all enemies and evil friends, and skillfully protect one's body, and make one's life span increase. If the disciples, who are wise and wise in their foundations, are able to practice almsgiving, and tame their tranquility, absent-mindedness, and disordered mind, they will take refuge in me. I, because I know well their basic thoughts, preferences, delusions, and winning solutions, will according to the right reasons tell them the dharma of punishment of Bhikkhunāda.

“Good man! Kshat-de-loi has initiated the great king, achieving the third king wheel” (Hey good man! The great king of the Kshat-de-li nature has been empowered to achieve the third king wheel like that): That is what the king of a country should do. Using this story as an example, because only by doing so can he make his country happy, can subdue all enemies and evil friends, make that country peaceful, everyone can live well.

“Good man! Tathagata has accomplished skill in knowing the basis of wisdom” (Good man! Tathagata has accomplished wisdom and knowledge of the basis or is so skillful): Knowing the basis of all living beings. This type of wisdom is not the skillful wisdom of the king who initiates the Sat-di-li, but is the wisdom of knowing the basic abilities of sentient beings. "If the disciples are far away from the wisdom of skillful expedient means, the wisdom of expedient means, the practice of giving alms, the control of tranquility, the loss of mindfulness, the disordered mind, the coming to the ego, the refuge of the self" (If the disciples separate themselves from the wisdom of skillful expedient means and blessings of wisdom, along with almsgiving, to control tranquility, forgetfulness, disordered mind, come to my place, take refuge in me): That Buddha's disciple initially believed in the Buddha, went to the Buddha, prayed for salvation from the Buddha, those people have wisdom. blessed with skillful means, to the point of being able to give alms, to subdue afflictions, to attain tranquility, attain Concentration, and to attain mindfulness. If you lose your thoughts, you will not be able to enter Concentration, your mind will be confused, and due to your lack of thoughts, your mind will become confused. “Come to me” is to turn to the Buddha to seek the Dharma and take refuge in the Buddha.

“I (the Buddha) know what that person's base is, what he likes, what his basic afflictions are, know that he has a lot of wisdom, a lot of good roots. That is winning the prize (understanding victory). The deepest prize is won when one reaches Buddha status and complete Buddha wisdom. “The sentient beings come to the Buddha” symbolizes all sentient beings, because in the past, they had wisdom and expediency, blessings, wisdom, and skill, giving alms, and controlling tranquility, but now they are absent-minded and confused, and the Buddha immediately observes and allows them to take refuge in the Buddha. Because He clearly understands their fundamentals, understands their ignorance, the basis of their afflictions, whether their wisdom is great or small, and the power to overcome, He will preach the Dharma to suit their fundamentals.

“Lai chi ca ca” (Come to me), they followed the Buddha to become a monk. [Buddha] preached the Vinaya Dharma for them. Vinaya is the precepts. Everyone who takes refuge in Buddha, at least takes the Three Refuges. Three Refuges, five precepts, or eight precepts, ten precepts, up to two hundred and fifty precepts [of Bhikkhus], three hundred and forty-eight precepts [of Bhikkhunis], four major precepts and twenty-eight minor precepts, or six major precepts and twenty-eight minor precepts [of the Bodhisattva Precepts in the Upasaka Precepts Sutra]. Bhikkhuni Da means “precepts”.

(Sutra) Weak sentient beings, with strange natures of hatred, those who study in the land, are incapable of serving, because The sacred teachings of the nine-headed self-abiding spirit, with many actions, are either based on memories and punishments, or the teachings of terror and blame, or temporarily suppressed, or subdued, reduced to worship, or without words, without communal benefits, or as grass-roots, or ascetic and obliterated.
My teachings exist for a long time [in the world], are practiced by many people, but either create ways of thinking, reprimanding, or using language of teachings to threaten, reprimand, or temporarily banish them to persuade them to sincerely worship, worship, or not talk to them, not share benefits with them, or [that person has committed a sin] then repent, or die again).

There is also the Tac Tri, which is also the law. If those sentient beings are stubborn, fierce, cruel, rough, and not well-versed in the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, and the eight precepts that they have received (“learning ground” refers to the precepts, it can also be understood as the law that they have learned), they cannot accept and obey them. These precepts protect the long-term existence of the holy religion.

If there were no precepts, Buddhism would not be able to exist for a long time. Why did the Buddha need to regulate precepts? Making the Dharma "permanent", that is, making the holy teachings able to exist for a long time in the world, making it possible for all sentient beings to gain benefits in the future. The Buddha Dharma lasts a long time in the world, and many people benefit from it. Therefore, I request everyone to come to my place to take refuge, and my disciples must all uphold the precepts. The purpose of maintaining the precepts is to make the holy teachings endure, to make the Buddha Dharma endure.

Precepts are intended to prevent and protect, like a wall to protect the people. The precepts are intended to protect your mind, your body will not be shaken, your mind will not be chaotic, protecting your body and mind. The prescribed precepts include the following types of dharma: Or if you make a mistake, when you remember it, repent. Or use scary language, saying "you have broken the precepts, you will receive retribution in the future, you will fall into hell". That is using scary language to reprimand. If it is more serious, breaking the basic precepts, the person will be immediately “exorcised” (expelled), expelled from Buddhism. Or force that person to repent, depending on what kind of crime that person committed. Either force that person to return and worship, or people won't talk to that person. Not talking means the Sangha doesn't care about that person anymore. It's not even “mutually beneficial” , [that is] if a lay donor offers material things, etc., it will not be shared with that person. That is called “non-communism”.

“Or like grass cover”: “Thao cover” (covered by grass) means that person commits too many sins, both big and small, like grass covers the ground. That person commits a crime like mud, so muddy that he cannot walk through it, he has to cover it with grass to get through. That is the way to repent for sins. The sins that person committed are both serious and not serious. There are so many violations, if we list each one, it will not be very convenient for everyone to let that person repent. That is a type of general repentance. Just like when we worship, we don't know about many things in our lives. In this life, we will not commit the Five Disadvantages and the Ten Evils, so when we worship, we can just dedicate ourselves like that. So it is possible that in the past, that is, in many other lives before, you have committed the Five Evils and Ten Evils, so you repent like that. These are things that can be repented of, because we do not know the past and have no wisdom. “Grass dad” is like grass covering the ground, using grass to cover the ground, that is, the method of repentance is equivalent to using grass to cover the ground, spreading it on the ground so you can walk through the mud. If you have made a lot of mistakes, you should repent. That is the meaning of total repentance.

Or in reality, there is no way, no cure can be prescribed, the Sangha cannot keep you, so “exterminate”, that is, kick you out. At temples on the Mainland, anyone who violates the basic precepts will be expelled from the temple or temple. Each region is different, in Mainland it is Mac Tan. Whenever someone breaks the precepts like this, he does not dare to return to the temple, he leaves; This is called the Mac Tan Dharma.

(Sutra) The wonderful wisdom of the Self, knowing all sentient beings, the Bodhisattva Jāla base, the mind mocking, hypnotizing, winning the prize, Like extracting punishment, the spiritual level destroys the vast and meaningless accumulation of darkness, dries up the afflictions of the servants, the spirit attains rebirth in heaven, Nirvana is lost, and those who practice evil destiniess Bo Da La attains to subdue them, according to the dharma of punishment, observe the black theory, the great theory of difference, according to the dharma of eagle, receive the data to punish and punish the dharma of evil deeds.
To punish those who follow the evil destinies, to make them all destroy the vast accumulation of meaningless darkness, to dry up the waterfalls of afflictions, to make them enjoy the joy of heavenly birth or Nirvana, to subdue the Buddha to follow the evil destinies, to speak the antidote and punishment dharma, to observe the black theory and other great theories, to teach the countermeasures and punish those who follow the evil destinies.)

“The ego is wonderfully wise, knowing sentient beings' base, taunting, following hypnosis, winning the prize, and apportioning punishment" (Due to my wonderful wisdom, knowing the base, liking, following the hypnosis, and winning the solution of sentient beings Bodhāraṇa, I punish properly): Pudgala (Pudgala) means "person", that is, sentient beings. Through life after life, the main thing that is transferred is the meaning contained in the word Bo Dat Gia La. The purpose of “treating and punishing according to the crimes you have committed” is to eliminate the darkness for you. In the past, you have accumulated meaningless things, with no meaning of victory, no meaning of pure conduct, these things are all dark, wanting to dry up those streams of afflictions, eliminating Ego Attachment and Ego View. That is the meaning of the precepts, the purpose of punishment, so that [the offender] after repenting, will enjoy the joy of rebirth and attain Nirvana. That's a broad statement, not necessarily just referring to monastics. [The purpose] is to subdue evil-doing sentient beings.

Many people who see temples or pagodas or hear the Buddha's teachings, they do not join the Buddhist community, do not believe in Buddha, nor are they an Upasaka, Upasika, Bhikkhu, or Bhikkhunī. As for this type of Bo Dat Gia La, they can hear the Buddha's teachings, or see temples and pagodas, and sow good roots for them, but when they see our precepts, they feel they cannot accept them, so they do not dare to join. I then told them about the good aspect, leaving aside the aspect of punishment and punishment, [telling them that in Buddhism] there is also the aspect of cultivating blessings, which are the three wheels mentioned in the above section (cultivating Concentration of karma, practicing recitation, and earning blessings). Observe whether their crimes are big or small, whether their crimes are different, to tell them about methods of treatment and punishment. For example, saying "will fall into hell" is telling them the method of treatment and punishment. They say they will receive retribution and will suffer from all kinds of diseases. For those evil retributions, whatever retribution you will have to suffer in the future is all black law. These things are called "dark theories, great theories", but we must consider to what extent these beings have poor nature!

(Sutra) The true wisdom of the ego, knowing all sentient beings, fully achieving the highest monks' faith and devotion, pure pure intention, Depending on the season, according to the theory of different types of good products, the spirit of cultivation, the spirit of the spirit must necessarily have good roots, the stage will reach perfection, and enter fearlessness. Good man! The ego becomes like the third Buddha Wheel, through the trial of the wheel, knowing all sentient beings' Bodhisattvas, the basic species, the mocking mind, the hypnosis, the data to win the prize, the Dharma of all karmas, the dharma of all karma, according to the dharma, the benefits of peace, the attainment of peace and stability, the attainment of fearlessness, the attainment of fearlessness, claiming the self as a great immortal, turning the Buddha Wheel, bad gods, evil sects, heretics, dealing with the masses, the right lion. roar.
pure, according to what should be said, different good qualities for them to practice, until all good roots are perfected, enter the citadel of fearlessness! This is how I achieve the third Buddha wheel, knowing the bases, preferences, and karma received by the Bodhisattva beings, according to what should be, to be beneficial, peaceful, to stay in peace, not to be afraid, not to be afraid. afraid, proclaiming myself to be in the position of a noble great immortal, turning the Buddha Wheel, dispelling the evil opinions of demons and pagans, performing the lion's roar among the masses).

This is what makes it possible for that person to increase his faith. This is a kind of wonderful wisdom of the Buddha, which makes sentient beings increase their devotion to the Three Jewels, makes their minds pure, their minds are not scattered, and tells them about different good products. Do the Ten Virtues, don't create bad karma, don't lie, don't tell lies, don't say embellished words, don't steal from others, don't kill. These two things are meant to be compared: One is the wheel of good dharma, the other is the wheel of evil dharma. The good dharma wheel can increase their faith, but it is not necessary that [those people actually] come to the Buddha. In the previous part, the scriptures said “come to my place” (to my place), but in the present era, whenever we go to the Three Jewels, it is also considered “to the place of Buddha”. You don't have to go there to seek ordination, but to seek the Three Refuges. There are people who are close to Buddhism, or come to the Buddha hall, we tell them about the two paths of good and evil. This also requires a cause and effect. Some people don't even see this kind of cause and effect. That type of living being has no way to grow good roots, because there is no such cause and condition.

Whenever there is this kind of cause and condition, the Buddha Wheel will be used to teach them, causing their good roots to reach perfection. Once completed, they will no longer be afraid. All sentient beings, born in this era, born in the Dharma Ending era, feel "nowhere to return, no place to take refuge", terrified, afraid. We see many people in a chaotic life, in the midst of chaos and war, let alone the swordsman, even during natural disasters such as locusts or floods, they have no food, it is very difficult to maintain their lives, and they even lose their lives! At that time, you tell them the ten good dharmas: "Why do you feel that result? It is because in the past, you did not sow good causes. Don't sow anymore causes, that is, in the present, you do not do evil anymore. To change the results will be very difficult. You can create causes for the future, sow new seeds, making other good roots complete." When the Buddha is not in the world, the Buddha's disciples represent the Buddha.

All four disciples should do the same, so that the good roots of all sentient beings are perfected. What the Buddha said was while he was still alive. The Buddha accomplished the good men: "I accomplished the third Buddha Wheel like that". But the Buddha is no longer in the world. Currently, there are very few kings of Kshatriya, even those of King Kshatriya. Therefore, when the Ming Dynasty comes into the world, the country will be very prosperous, the rain and wind will come at the right time, and there will be no disasters. If that king is very evil, the punishment is very heavy, the king wishes to commit evil, the teachers of the country must advise him: "Should reduce the punishment, grant amnesty. Reduce the crimes, [those who commit] minor crimes will be released." That is all the meaning of repentance. When the holy monarch is in this world, the country will be very peaceful, for several decades of peace. Like the Manchu Qing period in China, the Kangxi dynasty was prosperous. The Ming Dynasty occupied almost half of the reign of the Manchu Dynasty. During Qianlong's reign, for sixty years, there was no war, the people lived very peacefully, and the king himself was very happy. The king spent all day writing poetry and couplets, that is, having fun. There is no harm to the country, natural disasters and man-made disasters are very few. That time was when the holy king was on earth. The Chau family's life is also like that. In order to save the people, [Vuong Chau Vu] punished Tru, that is, punished the brutal ruler. At present, there is no King Sat-di-loi, there is no Buddha, nor Buddha in this world, but the dharma of the first emperor is still there, humanity, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, the old dharma of governing the country of the first king has been reintroduced. Buddha Dharma is usually like that, the Buddha Dharma of all Buddhas is like that.

Due to this cycle, it will cause the basis, sarcasm, attachment, affliction, and victory of all types of Bodhisattvas, as well as the karma they receive, to be “according to what is appropriate, beneficial and peaceful” (according to what should be beneficial and peaceful), that is, all people, all sentient beings, will be able to benefit. “Peace” means no fear. If they are not afraid, they will not be afraid.
