To be able to attain Formless Realm Concentration means to have overcome the bondages in the Form Realm and the Desire Realm, that is, to [treat] the bondages that have form. Entering this type of Samadhi, there will be no bondage. Thanks to that practice, you will be able to subdue your afflictions. Learning Buddhism is to overcome afflictions. Having attained those four types of Concentration, that person's mental realm and appearance will be completely different. That person is residing in Tranquility.

1) The first Gate of Samadhi is the Land of Boundless Space. Does nothingness exist? No! Boundless. [Named like that] is to imagine that the mind, when entering this Concentration, will not be bound by all the Concentration subjects of the Four Heavenly Meditations. That is, First Meditation, Second Meditation, Third Meditation, Fourth Meditation, those Concentration subjects have the form of bondage, while this Non-Place Concentration subject has no form, no appearance. We can imagine infinitely large space, with no limit in any way. Just how big is space? Boundless Land means “without limits, without land, without edges, without form”. This Concentration is superior to the Four Meditations and Eight Concentrations in the previous section. There are sutras that talk about the ninth type of Concentration, that is, the Nine Concentrations and the Four Eightfold Concentration. The Four Formless Samadhi here are the Four Formless Samadhi.

Currently, if you pay attention to the breath in and out, practice the practice of entering and exiting, [i.e., visualize] exhaling and inhaling. If you can hold on until the end, you will go higher. These types of Concentration all speak according to the mind, they eliminate your obstacles. There are no obstacles. In the air, are there obstacles? There are no obstacles! That is No Land. The Samadhi of Boundless Emptiness is the Samadhi of Emptiness, which can eliminate our obstacles. At that time, it is impossible to describe: Sometimes the ego energy enters Concentration, or the ego energy enters Concentration, Energy and So are both empty, the thoughts of that person (the person cultivating Concentration) still have intention. Intent is the Space of thought, boundless and formless. It only reaches the end of nothingness, there is no edge, so it is called the Land of Boundless Emptiness. According to us at present, if we want to practice this type of Concentration, we still have a very long way to go, we have to go step by step. However, we need to know that order first.

2) The second type is Samadhi Consciousness. Consciousness here is consciousness in the “conscious mind”. This Concentration is called Consciousness Concentration. That consciousness is infinitely large. Now we use the previous five consciousnesses: Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Snake Consciousness, Tongue Consciousness, and Body Consciousness. Those five consciousnesses have a local and limited nature. If there is nothing outside to help, no Great Space to help, no light from the sun, moon, or lamp to help, our eyes cannot see anything. In the dark, can you still see? If our ears are just a little obstructed, we won't hear clearly. Boundless Consciousness means that when you enter this Concentration, it will be completely different. Entering this Concentration, without relying on the light of the sun, moon, or stars for help, as soon as you pay attention, your eyesight can see everything. Great Brahma King can see three thousand great thousand worlds. Entering this Concentration, it is not empty. [Don't misunderstand]: If it is Emptiness, it is Emptiness, nothing exists. It is not the Cessation of Emptiness. “Entering this Concentration will be like being empty”, is not that meaning! This is Consciousness in Samadhi, Consciousness is also infinitely large, Emptiness is also infinitely large; But this Consciousness still has thinking. That thinking consciousness has no boundary.

3) The third Concentration is the Land of Nothingness, also known as the Wonderful Land of Concentration. This Concentration is higher than the Concentration of Boundless Consciousness, relying on all the signs of your thinking to abide. Wonderful Place of Concentration means that wherever you think, you will enter Concentration there. This is called the Wonderland. Wherever you think of, that place is where you enter Concentration, abide in accordance with all your signs.

4) Land of Neither Perception, Non-Perception: This Concentration is higher than the Samadhi of Nothingness. Thinking about that form, it is impossible to say that there is a form, but it is also impossible to say that there is no form! What do you think about, do you think or do you not think? Is it a good idea? The Land of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception is that non-perception that has also been eliminated, it is not illusory, nor is it empty. It is not perception, it is not non-perception, and it is also not non-non-perception; That's the inclusive meaning. Non-perception means that it cannot be considered to exist. It doesn't need your attachments, that is, it eliminates your attachments. That thinking is not thinking, it is not thinking, it is not like we use the six sense organs to think. Whatever we think about, thinking about this thing, thinking about that thing, it's not all like that. Non-Perception is not thought, nor is it non-thought. Non-Perception is not the corresponding Perception of Non-Perception. Phi Phi Perception means that this Concentration is different from the Concentration of Extinction. Destroying Concentration is the Arahant's Concentration, he has destroyed all afflictions. But when entering this Concentration (Neither Perception, Non-Perception), that person (the person who practices this Concentration) still has ignorance and afflictions. This Concentration still has afflictions. [The person who attains this Concentration] is not a saint at all, but it is not non-thought, different from non-thought. How should we explain the last two sentences, i.e. “not non-thought, different from non-thought”? Non-Perception means not thinking, not thinking. Not thinking is similar to Emptiness, which means it is different from Concentration of No Thought, not completely Emptiness.

The Four Boundless Lands of Concentration, those four types of realms are all achieved by thinking. What is the formless precept to treat? Treating bondage means treating the karma that binds us. In other words, we all have the same feeling towards the external realm. Those four subjects of Concentration are separate from perception, separate from perception of external realms. In other words, by attaining those Concentration subjects, our predestined mind will stop. Why is each of these four subjects of Concentration more advanced than the previous one? Collectively, they are called the Four Formless Concentrations, that is, the Concentrations belonging to the Formless Realm. In Only Thuc, it talks about them very clearly!

In there, there are three types of miracles. These three types of miraculous transformations are three types of teachings, three types of manifestations, three types of teachings. When Buddhas and Bodhisattvas teach and transform living beings, they demonstrate the “virtue, form, function” of body karma, speech karma, and mental karma:

1- The first thing is supernatural powers. Bodhisattva took pity on the sentient beings suffering in hell, and he showed supernatural powers. That's called "transfiguration miracles". Use His supernatural power to destroy mountains of knives, seas of fire, all kinds of execution tools, etc. in hell. When He uses his supernatural powers to subdue those phenomena, sentient beings suffering in hell can be reborn, can escape, and be born in heaven. That is the magical power of transformation.

2- The second thing is the appearance theory. The theory of transformation is also due to the Bodhisattva's compassion for sentient beings suffering in hell; What they thought and remembered (that is Ky), He then came and told them that dharma (that was Theory). Bodhisattvas have supernatural powers and preach Dharma to respond to opportunities. Whatever was in their minds, Buddha told them that Dharma, allowing sentient beings to rely on that Dharma power to escape hell. Thanks to the Bodhisattva's surrender and the power of preaching the Dharma, he escaped from hell and was born in the heavens and human realms, enjoying joy. That is the Bodhisattva's Universal Mind Insight. Sentient beings in hell may feel the Bodhisattva coming to preach the Dharma, but this opportunity is too remote! How can we feel? Unless in this life, before falling into hell, you have sincere faith in Ksitigarbha, Avalokiteshvara, Samantabhadra, Manjushri, or Amitābha Buddha, Śākyamuni Buddha. It is also due to the retribution of a type of karma. When you die, even if you do not maintain mindfulness, you will fall into hell as retribution, but because your good roots are very strong, you will inspire Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Those sentient beings have now fallen into hell. In the past, they had a certain predestined relationship with me and had a certain level of cultivation. Only then can the Bodhisattva sympathize with that person. Or through the prayers of six relatives, invite that Bodhisattva to save you. Just like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mother, because of his inspiration, she was able to be born in heaven. Like the mother of the Venerable Maudgalyayana who fell into a hungry ghost, he wanted to use his supernatural powers to save her, but he did not have enough strength. The food He gave to his mother turned into fire. He immediately prayed to Buddha to save his mother. The Buddha taught that on the Vu Lan Bon festival, the full moon day of the seventh month, you should make offerings to the mass of monks. Thanks to the power of making offerings to the masses, relying on that power to save his mother. By giving alms to the people, [His mother] will have food. This type of [appearance] is a miraculous transformation, that is, a miraculous teaching of the Dharma. If you were in hell and could still hear the Bodhisattva preach the Dharma, it wouldn't be easy! Compared to when we now come to Dharma conferences to study together, it is much more difficult!

3- The third type is the teachings that appear (transform teachings), which is also the Bodhisattva who develops compassion and preaches the Dharma to teach them. Thanks to that teaching, one can escape from hell and eliminate disasters, but only Bodhisattvas who attain the full penetration of the Sravakas can go to hell.

Bodhisattvas who have these three types of miraculous transformations, either teaching, showing, or educating, are all very rare. In the scriptures, the Buddha taught like that. That king, or the government, regarding the kingdom, any place that is dangerous, said that place could be turned into a place for entertainment, building a large city in that place. In those places, they prevent foreign enemies from entering, and also prevent robbers and robbers from taking over. Therefore, to keep foreign enemies from easily hiding and invading the king's kingdom, arrange all kinds of patrols, prevention, and arrange the country so that resentful enemies and evil friends cannot hide in the country. At the same time, make the people of that country live peacefully, away from persecution, away from suffering. That king achieved the king wheel like that; After that, the king's country grows peacefully and life is guaranteed. At the same time, resentful enemies and evil friends often do not come to invade or harass, and the people live peacefully.

People say “the mind is spacious”, meaning if the mind is more spacious, the body will be fatter. If the country is very stable, everyone doesn't have to worry, whether scholars, farmers, workers, or merchants, everything will be fine. No matter what you do, your mind is at peace, your blessings naturally increase, and there is no more sadness. The thing that causes the greatest damage to the body and life span is sadness. Why be sad? Life is not guaranteed, the body is abused and harassed. If you see a country with a slightly better life, it proves that the laws and politics of that country care about and protect its people better. If a country cannot protect its people, it is not a natural disaster, but a man-made disaster. Next, the scriptures talk about Buddha Wheel.

(Sutra) Good man! Such a Tathagata knows the Buddha's eye, as it really is, knowing all sentient beings, Bodhisattva Jāla, with greed, anger, and ignorance, and clearly knowing all sentient beings' different types of afflictions, illnesses, and behaviors. The Tathagata knows and knows, and quickly creates immeasurable diligence and mighty means and powers, depending on the doubt, receives the seed to cultivate the wonderful medicine of Concentration, the souls of sentient beings, diligently practice and practice, eliminating afflictions and diseases.
(Sutra: Good man! Tathagata uses the Buddha's eye like that, truly knowing all existence Bodhisattva Jāla has the minds of greed, anger, ignorance, etc., knowing clearly that sentient beings have different kinds of illnesses and afflictions. The Tathagata already knew that, so he raised up countless means and forces to be diligent and courageous, according to appropriate reasons, to give them wonderful medicines to cultivate Concentration, teach sentient beings to diligently and diligently practice to eliminate afflictions).

“ Good man! Nthe false vision of the Tathagata with the Buddha eye, as it really is, fully understands all sentient beings Bodāgāra” (Hey good man! The Tathagata uses the true Buddha eye to clearly know all sentient beings Bodāgāla like that): There are ten types Bo Dac Gia La. Pudgala is a noun used to refer to the cycle of birth.

The first type is that the Bodhisattva Gia La does not sow good roots. In the past life, or in the present life, that person did not have the good roots of Bodhi, nor did he develop the mind. If you don't sow good roots, you will do evil and will not create good causes.

The second type has never cultivated meritorious karma and does not give alms to others. In other words, never helping others, not even approaching Buddhism. We must approach the Buddhadharma to receive and maintain the precepts. Not cultivating meritorious karma is also creating many negative actions.

The third type is continuous impurity, which is also afflictions such as greed, anger, ignorance, Personal View, Boundary View, Precepts, Precepts, and Wrong Views. This is also called "not having good roots". Contaminated with greed, anger, and ignorance are very heavy, and continue without stopping, but they also create negative karma of greed, anger, and ignorance without interruption.

The fourth type is sentient beings who obey evil. Because with regard to good and bad karma, they seem to have an uncertain nature. When they meet good friends, they will learn good things. Meeting evil friends, they will do evil things. This is because their good roots in the past were few and they did not meet good friends. If they meet good friends, they cannot follow them to do good deeds. Currently, there are many people who believe in Buddha and also approach Buddha Dharma, even receiving the Three Refuges. Then they broke the precepts again. What precept is that? Pham Tam Quy, because he took refuge in an evil religion. They cannot penetrate the right path. Encountering evil friends, led by evil knowledge, he moved towards evil ways and followed evil friends.

The fifth type is one who is not afraid of suffering in the afterlife. Creating evil karma, that person does not believe in cause and effect, and is not afraid of cause and effect in the next life. This type of living beings does not believe in cause and effect. They say: "Death is the end, what is the afterlife, what is the afterlife!" Therefore, they are not afraid of suffering in the next life. This type of Bodhisattva Jāla has an insatiable desire for desire and is especially strong. As for wealth, [desire] has no limit forever. We see kings, government officials, big capitalists, large financial corporations, they all have no limits. There are ten billions, so I hope to have a hundred billions; having a hundred memories, then dreaming of a thousand memories! Give them the whole globe, they still hope to take over the sun, take over the moon in the air, forever unable to be satisfied! It's not enough to be a king, I still want to be a King of Zhuan Luan, I want the earth to be round and bigger. That is impossible. The desire is fierce and will never be satisfied. This type of Bodhisattva Gia La has strong anger and strong ignorance. There is no way to stop the afflictions that arise, especially the anger that arises very strongly. The three types of greed, anger, and ignorance are not inferior to each other, but ignorance is a bit stronger [than greed and anger]. Ignorance means being confused about all scenes, giving rise to wrong views, and destroying the Dharma.

There are Dharma friends who have believed in the Dharma, because they have believed for a long time, but due to some kind of benefit, or due to physical suffering, if they believe in cause and effect, they will know that it is the karma that we have left over, and then eliminate it completely. That is one type. Either the business fails, suffers a loss, meets someone who talks nonsense, or someone who boasts of having supernatural powers: "I will help you get rich" then believes it, forgetting that he has taken refuge in the Buddha, taken refuge in the Dharma, and taken refuge in the Sangha. Even [that liar] teaches them that they no longer need to believe in Buddha, no longer need to make offerings to the Sangha, and no need to be close to monks. That is the sin of stupidity. This phenomenon is very serious. This kind of Bodhisattva Gia La is also because in the past life the good roots were not accumulated deeply.

The tenth type is holding wrong views, not believing in the true teachings of Tathagata, holding wrong views of heretics.

These ten types of Bodhisattvas will naturally fall into the animal path, or into the hungry ghost path. We are Bodhisattvas with good roots, completely opposite to those types. But we also have greed, anger, and ignorance, but they are not greed, anger, and ignorance like those types of Bodhisattvas. They are [greed, anger, ignorance] continuously, without stopping. Understanding this meaning, [we realize] we are very lucky. Because Bo Dat Gia La's greed, anger, and ignorance are very heavy. The Buddha, in order to save this type of sentient beings, saw their illnesses, not just the sick bodies. Whenever there is affliction, it is a medical condition, there are all kinds of afflictions. Not only physical illness, but also mental illness, and all kinds of afflictions. Like a country with many dangers and dangers. Regardless of whether the Mainland is the same, Taiwan is the same, Canada is the same, the United States is the same, we look from here, [will see] that each great king who initiates Sat-di-li is still very far from the requirement of “pure country”! Because this era is completely different, greed, anger, and delusion are especially heavy, this era is absolutely different. What you encounter and see every day, as well as what you think about, all belong to different diseases of greed, anger, and ignorance. Tathagata understands clearly. If the Buddha and the great Bodhisattvas want to save those sentient beings, they cannot do it arbitrarily.

In the eighth chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, King Yama and the great demon king said: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has made such a great vow, why has he not yet completed his salvation? Why, after having saved him, do they then return? They just escaped from hell, almost immediately returned." The Buddha then told the great demon kings: “The living beings in Jambudvipa are stubborn, difficult to regulate, difficult to tame”. [Here, the Buddha taught] you must repair the country so that the enemy cannot penetrate; indeed [this] is very difficult to achieve. I'm afraid that the current king doesn't have this ability. Flying from the sky, crawling up from the ground. Cultivating meritorious karma can be exempted. If you don't cultivate good karma, as a human being you still can't say for sure, you can think of any countermeasures. Floods, storms, fires, is there any way? Buddhas and Bodhisattvas understand the suffering of sentient beings, they create countless means and powers of diligence and courage. This requires countless eons of diligent practice, just like the Dharma friends who have developed the great Bodhi mind to save sentient beings. If you're late and lazy, you can't even save yourself, so how can you save others? Must be diligent!

The truth is that we are not strong enough! It's not about being brave towards others, it's about being brave towards your own afflictions. You must be more courageous towards your own greed and anger! If you lose, your anger will forever grow bigger and bigger. We must courageously eliminate and overcome it. What strength must we use? Be patient. Forbearance is very difficult! [In Chinese characters, the word Forbearance] is above the word Heart, a knife is placed. How do you endure? Often when we are upset, we cannot be patient! The ancients said: “Anger is like a fierce tiger descending a mountain”. When a person gets angry, when anger arises, no one who advises him will listen, he must rely on his own wisdom to control it. Use patience and subjugation so you don't get angry. Always smile and be happy with others, learning from the compassion of Maitreya Bodhisattva. You make people cry, they cry in return. People curse you, but you still laugh with them. If they hit you, you still use a smiling face towards them, they will give up and won't be able to hit you anymore. That is the mind of anger. The same goes for greed. Greed, anger, ignorance are not much different!

The Buddha treated this type of living beings, using his own diligence and courage, using the power of wisdom, using skillful means, using that power. But we still need to know how to consider the underlying condition, see what kind of disease this being must have, and what kind of medicine must be taken. For those who have heavy anger and greed, you advise them: "Don't get angry!" Will they believe? They don't believe it at all! If your power is stronger than theirs, their anger will arise, wanting to fight. They want to fight, if you subdue them and defeat them, their anger will disappear, making them honest. “If the strong abuse the weak, they will be violent” (The strong oppress the weak, the east oppresses the few). The two words “force” contain this meaning. We know that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in the Han land has the appearance of compassion, mostly showing the appearance of a woman. In Tibet, he manifested the form of Dharma protector, that is, the fierce Yaksha form.

These things belong to the magical medicines for cultivating Concentration. Miraculous medicine gives birth to wonderful happiness, curing all kinds of diseases of greed, anger, and ignorance for you. Based on what? Rely on concentration. You say "not greedy", as if a Dharma friend turned to me to repent: When he was in a temple, when he left, he had to steal something to take away. If you don't take any item, you will feel very uncomfortable inside. No matter what temple or shrine he was in, no matter how poor that temple was, he still had to take something with him. Actually, it doesn't take anything. He took some offerings in front of the Buddha statue and took them away. As soon as he walked out, he gave them to others, completely without appropriating them as his own. Later, he asked me to repent, saying: "I don't understand why! In my heart, I knew clearly that it was a mistake, I knew that I had violated the Basic Precepts, I knew that it was stealing something from the Three Jewels, I couldn't help but fall into hell, and I also fell into the Unintermittent Hell. Even though I knew that, I still did it! Today, I told Him that was also considered repentance. If I say it, I'm sure I won't be able to do it again in the future!" I said: "It's not enough to tell just one person! Go to any temple, then tell [everyone in] that temple, I will steal things, you must pay attention to me, watch over me, make me stop stealing. Or you can repent for me. That courage is not easy to come by. When you steal someone's things, you must tell them frankly. Then, people will stop you. This is very difficult. towel!”

Everyone has greed. If you completely eliminate the root of afflictions, you will achieve success. Can't stop it! I don't have the heart to steal, but I do have the mind to take advantage, which I'm afraid many people have. There are also people who do not take advantage of others. Anything that belongs to someone else does not give rise to false thoughts. This type of person has very deep good roots in the past. When he sees things that belong to others, not only things that belong to people, but also all things, all material things, he will not be greedy, let alone possess them? I still want to let go of my own things, even contemplating my own body, knowing that it is fake, whoever wants it, I will give it to that person. However, I saw that in Taiwan, people donated their body parts and waited to die before taking them. I said: "If you truly develop Bodhi mind, you will give them to others without worrying. Whoever needs them can take them from my body and I will give them to them." I once asked a doctor, I said: "Suppose I was eighty years old, and if I wanted to give up my body parts to someone over thirty years old, would it be appropriate? Is that possible?" He said: "It won't last a few days. It's still okay to attach it, it depends on the teacher's physical strength, depending on how strong or weak the teacher's organs are. If the organ or body is sick, the teacher lets go and transplants it into someone else's body. Originally, there was no problem with that person's other organs. When transferring my organ to that person's body, it doesn't work, and the person gets hurt again." Doctors understand this very well. If you really donate your organs, then give them away immediately and give them to someone else. Regret, wait until after death, you die, no matter what, you will be burned, you have no control, whether you let go or not is the same! However, if you do not make that vow, if you do not let go, others will not dare to cut off your organs. Otherwise, it will be a crime!

Therefore, it is necessary to have the powerful miracle drug to cultivate this Concentration in order to eliminate it. Even for your own body, if you often practice Contemplation like that, you will have the power of Concentration. Having that kind of Concentration, is there anything you can't let go of? Do you still want to steal other people's things? Of course there is none! You must often meditate on patience, not getting angry with anyone. Whenever we encounter something against our will, something unsatisfactory, or being manipulated by others, we immediately warn ourselves: "This is a good opportunity for me to practice! This is a good opportunity for me to repent." If you often think like that, your existing greed, anger, and ignorance will be able to be treated like that. Is there still ignorance? That is having wisdom. Without wisdom, you won't be able to do it! Practice treating your own greed, anger, and ignorance. If you encounter this kind of situation, you will be able to overcome it! What kind of miraculous medicine did the Buddha respond to give us? Those are the dharmas! You learn according to the Buddha's method. When studying, you must be dedicated and diligent in your studies.

I think for everyone at that time, [for example] if I reprimand you, or a Dharma friend says a few words that offend you, or you fall asleep and someone else wakes you up immediately, you will often have anger. If I don't speak, [when awakened, that person will be irritated]: "If you listen, listen, what does it matter to you that [I sleep]?" I have indeed seen that. The two of them argued, I asked: "What are you two arguing about?" The other person said: "This person fell asleep, I asked him to cheer himself up a bit." At that time, I was preaching the Avatamsaka Sutra at Nam Putuo Temple, and I said: "In the future, pay a little attention, people will help you, you should repent of your ignorance [of falling asleep]." Then there is anger [when reminded], greed, anger, ignorance are all complete! I said [to the other person]: "You help that person, which is a good thing. If you quarrel with that person and your anger arises, it's like you didn't help that person at all." Very difficult! When we preach this sutra, you have a ray of light, greed, anger, and ignorance are all controlled and prevented.

Such a long period of learning; If you can concentrate and study diligently, your illness and suffering will be reduced. The greatest human suffering is the disease of affliction, not just the body getting cancer. Other things can be changed, but greed is very difficult to change. You want to change greed, anger, ignorance, it's very difficult! They have followed you for countless generations until now. How can you turn them around? Sickness in the present is only a disease in this life. When this life is gone, its appearance will change, I don't know what form it will become. We are here, male appearance, female appearance, old appearance, young appearance, always transforming. Before becoming Buddha, it was all like that. Everyone knows that Devadatta was the most opposed to the Buddha and fell into hell. But in the past, he was the teacher who taught Mahayana Dharma to the Buddha, we often only looked at the appearance of the realm in front of us.


(Sutra) For sentient beings who doubt and practice impurity, to eliminate afflictions and illnesses, it is convenient to receive the medicine of impure practice. For all sentient beings who suspect to practice transgression, it will eliminate afflictions and illnesses, which means it is convenient to receive the medicine of practicing transgression. For all sentient beings, doubts and cultivating dependent origination can eliminate afflictions and illnesses. That is, it is convenient to receive and practice dependent origination medicine. For all sentient beings, doubt and practice is recitation. To eliminate afflictions and illnesses, it is convenient to receive and cultivate, which is recitation medicine. For sentient beings who have doubts, they can practice the three doors of liberation to eliminate afflictions and illnesses. That is, it is convenient to practice the medicine of the three doors of liberation. If sentient beings should practice Tinh Lu to eliminate afflictions and illnesses, it is convenient to practice Tinh Lu medicine. If sentient beings should practice the Formless, to eliminate afflictions and illnesses, it is convenient to receive the Formless medicine. All sentient beings, with the intention of cultivating the Shurangama Samama-ground, eliminate afflictions and illnesses, that is, conveniently receive the Shurangama Samama-ground medicine.
(Sutra: If sentient beings should cultivate impurity to eliminate diseases and afflictions, immediately give them medicine to cultivate impurity. If sentient beings should cultivate the cessation of afflictions, then give the medicine to cultivate the cessation of afflictions. If the sentient beings should cultivate the cessation of afflictions, then give the medicament to cultivate the cessation of afflictions. If the sentient beings should cultivate the cessation of afflictions, then give the medicament to practice the 3 doors of emancipation To eliminate afflictions, immediately give the medicine to practice Tinh Lu. If sentient beings should practice Formlessness to eliminate afflictions, immediately give the medicine to cultivate Formlessness. If sentient beings should practice the samadhis such as Shu Langya Ma to eliminate afflictions, then give the medicine to Shulangāma samadhi.

All sentient beings should practice Impure Contemplation, I will let them practice Impure Contemplation to cure their afflictions, give them Impure Contemplation medicine, and tell them the Impure Contemplation method to cure them. If they accept to take that medicine, it means they listen to the Dharma and their illness will be cured. There are sentient beings who should practice Pham Tru. Pham Tru is purity, cultivating purity, either maintaining precepts, or being patient, is all holy conduct. Pham means “pure”, eliminating afflictions. I will give them medicine to practice Pham Tru. Cultivating the Four Foundations of Mindfulness, or cultivating the Five Faculties, or cultivating the Five Strengths is fine.

“If sentient beings are weak, practice dependent origination” (If sentient beings are worthy

should practice dependent origination): Understand that all dharmas arise from causes and conditions, and have no real reality. Those living beings practiced Emptiness Contemplation very well, so they immediately told them the dharma of dependent origination. All dharmas are dependently arisen, all dharmas have no self-nature, the essence of all dharmas is empty. That is called “dependent arising of emptiness”.

“For sentient beings, consider cultivating Right Mindfulness” (If sentient beings should practice Right Mindfulness): Right Mindfulness is stopping random thoughts, like “retaining past and present thoughts” (maintaining thoughts back and forth, i.e. Book of Instant Contemplation). That is the end of hope. Letting go of hope can eliminate your afflictions. “For sentient beings, doubtful that they can practice the three doors of liberation” (If sentient beings should practice the three doors of liberation): Also the three doors of liberation of Emptiness, Formless, and Wishless. That is cultivating Emptiness, cultivating Non-action, cultivating Formlessness. Those are the three doors of liberation, and will give them the medicine of the Three Doors of Liberation.

“If sentient beings should practice Tinh Lu” (If sentient beings should practice Tinh Lu): Tinh Lu is Concentration. Practicing samadhi means using Concentration to eliminate illness and afflictions. In this way, we will give them the medicine to practice Tinh Lu. “For all sentient beings, practice Formlessness” (If sentient beings should practice Formlessness): Formlessness is to eliminate afflictions. In the previous section, we talked about Formless Samadhi. Contemplating all dharmas without form is similar to cultivating Emptiness. Formlessness is possible with respect to the five aggregates of Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness, using form to represent. In the previous part, it was about cultivating the mind, but here it is cultivating the Form.

“For sentient beings, I am determined to practice the Shurangama Ma sama-grounds” (If sentient beings come to practice the samadhi subjects like the Samma-grounds): This is also great samadhi, that is, Shurangama Ma samadhi. Cultivating this Concentration is the ultimate Concentration, the very deepest and supreme Concentration among the one hundred and eight samadhis. So then I transmitted the medicine Thu Lang Gia Ma Sam-ma-dia.

(Sutra) The reason why the Tathagata receives sentient beings is like a dharma medicine, it is not necessary to transform sentient beings, it is free from the four evil spirits. The branch of the photography system, the non-spiritual must transform all sentient beings, the ancestors of the heavenly vehicle, towards the evil beasts, the non-spiritual Tathagata's unsurpassed dharma eye, the Three Jewels' nature and nature quickly destroy and destroy.
(Sutra: Because the Tathagata gave such dharma to sentient beings, it did not cause all sentient beings to be transformed Being bound by the four types of demons and resentments, accepting life, not allowing all sentient beings to be transformed into going against the natural vehicle of humanity, towards evil destiniess, not allowing the Tathagata's unsurpassed dharma eye and the Three Jewels' nature to be quickly destroyed).

“The Tathagata gives sentient beings the dharma medicine, the non-spiritual one must necessarily transform the sentient beings, because the four demons and resentments are in their possession” (Because the Tathagata gives the dharma medicine to sentient beings like that, it does not cause all sentient beings to be saved to be bound and received by the four demons): This is in general. Giving Thu Lang Gia Ma sama-dia medicine will be final. Regarding the dharma mentioned in those types of herbal medicine, if they are willing to accept it and accept it, it will be considered that they have taken the medicine. If you take the medicine, there will be no troubles. This is the seventh Buddha Wheel. This Buddha Wheel allows all sentient beings to not be bound by the four demons “system”, “system” is bound, “obsession” is maintained. The first of the Four Demons is the Five Aggregates. The Five Aggregates are Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness; it's a ghost thing. There is also the Demon of Affliction. Affliction includes the affliction of Jiansi. There is also Tu Ma. We are extremely afraid of Tu Ma, no one wants to die! If you can't help it, you can also commit suicide. Death is not comfortable. Anyone who commits suicide will suffer many times more than a normal death, going to hell as quickly as an arrow. You say you can't stand this trouble, you want to escape responsibility and commit suicide to get it over with. Once you die, it's over! That is an absolutely wrong way of thinking! In the precepts, suicide and murder are the same sin, you should not commit suicide!

When the Buddha was in the world, there were monks who obeyed the Buddha's teachings and practiced Impure Contemplation. They are extremely disgusted with the body. Having deeply practiced Impure Contemplation, they see that this body is truly maggots and unbearably impure! They are bored with their own bodies to the extreme. Having successfully practiced Impure Contemplation, there will be that phenomenon, but they do not develop Bodhi mind, do not recite and save sentient beings. Therefore, they simply practice Impure Contemplation, only thinking about how they can attain pure liberation! If they save sentient beings and have great Bodhi mind, they will not commit suicide. They realized that all sentient beings are like that. Unfortunately, sentient beings do not understand clearly, so they used their own actual phenomena to tell everyone. They say it, but others don't see it.

If they reflect on themselves and have successfully practiced Impure Contemplation, [because they do not have Bodhi mind], what will they do? Unable to commit suicide, they borrowed the hands of Indian pagans, brought clothes and supplies to those pagans, and asked them to kill them. The pagans wanted money, so they killed them. Later, the Buddha learned that suicide is not allowed, nor is killing by others. You can't kill yourself, and you can't borrow someone else to kill you! This is talking about old stories in the precepts. How should we contemplate that death? Death is an obstacle to our spiritual practice. If you are cultivating the path, death belongs to non-life. “No life” means not worthy of death, it is a cause and effect that hinders the path. This hindrance is considered a type of Demon, called Death Demon.

There is also Thien Ma. Thien Ma refers to ghosts and gods. When you cultivate the path to a certain level, when you are about to achieve it, heavenly demons will come and manifest all kinds of appearances. Like when Śākyamuni Buddha was about to become a Buddha, the demon king Ba Tuan immediately led a group of demon soldiers and demons to surround and harass the Buddha. Demons create obstacles for you. That's Thien Ma. You read the sutras, see a ghost, or a ghost comes, your body gets a fever, or you see something like that. That's not a bad thing. If it wasn't your relative, it wouldn't be possible to come before you. It's not like your parents from generations past, or your six relatives, won't be able to come before you! They come to you hoping for your salvation, not knowing that you are afraid. They just know that you are their family member, so they come to you. The person who comes to you depends on what kind of person it is. If it is a being with great power, your body will feel hot. If it is a deva or an angel who comes to listen to you recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, recite the Samantabhadra Vow, recite the Universal Gate, you will have a feeling, communicate with them, they will come to increase your blessings, you will feel hot on your body. If the ghost really comes, you will feel cold in your body, cold every moment, cold every moment. You just continue to recite the sutras as if nothing happened. By the time you finish reciting, nothing will happen! Some people [are afraid] and don't recite, saying: "If I don't recite anymore, [those scary things] won't happen." I said: "If you don't remember, of course you don't have it." That person said: "I will never recite again!" I said: "If you don't recite forever, you'll be lost! Just keep reciting, nothing will happen!" That's an obstacle, that's not a ghost, you have to distinguish clearly!

When the Buddha Wheel rotates, it will cause those people to not go against the natural vehicle of humanity, either to become humans or to be born in heaven. At least, do not go against human nature, do not move towards the three evil destiniess. At the same time, it causes Tathagata's dharma, Tathagata's dharma eye and the Three Jewels' nature not to be destroyed. Enable sentient beings to be saved and not go against the natural vehicle of humanity and not follow evil destiniess. As for the Tathagata's dharma eyes and the Three Jewels' nature, they will not be destroyed. “Rapid destruction” is like the Dharma of Sakyamuni Buddha that has been destroyed very quickly: the True Dharma five hundred years, the Immortal Dharma five hundred years, the Ending Dharma ten thousand years. Even though we say that, these things are not accurate. How do they depend on the karma of sentient beings? During the end of the Dharma, the Dharma still exists. As long as there are people reading and reciting the Mahayana, there are the Three Jewels present, there is a Buddha statue, there are Dharma Jewels, there is a Sangha, that is, there are the Three Jewels, there is a place for us to sow blessings, then [the end of the Dharma] can become the Dharma.

Now we are studying, that is the Dharma. If you leave this place to commit crimes, it will be the end of the Dharma. The meaning of the division into the moments of the Right Dharma, the Impression of the Dharma and the End of the Dharma is: The Dharma is speaking in the sense of the right path and attainment of enlightenment. As soon as you enter the Buddhadharma, listen to the teachings, become enlightened, and understand clearly, that will be the Dharma. Until the end of the Dharma, we study every day and our afflictions are not easily eliminated. Because our training power is not enough, we may only listen to the teachings once or twice in a few months, or we may only listen to them once every few years. Practice then practice, but how to practice? The Buddha asked us to listen to the Dharma and practice immediately. Once you have practiced, you will attain enlightenment. That is called “diligence, diligence and courage” to be able to eliminate afflictions.

(Sutra) Because of seeing the Tathagata, receiving sentient beings is like seeing the dharma medicine. Good man! Self becomes like the seventh Buddha wheel. Due to trial and error, the supreme wisdom of Changing Actions is achieved, receiving all sentient beings a variety of dharma medicine, cultivating spiritually, eliminating afflictions and diseases, attaining peace and stability, attaining no fear, attaining no fear, claiming to be a great immortal, turning the Buddha Wheel, bad heavenly demons, evil heretics, dealing with the masses, right lion's roar.
(Sutra: Therefore, the Tathagata gives such dharma medicine to sentient beings. Good man! I have achieved it. The seventh Buddha Wheel is like that. Because of that wheel, using the unsurpassed wisdom of Transformation and Action, I give all kinds of dharma medicine to sentient beings, making them diligently practice, eliminate diseases and afflictions, live in peace, not panic, not afraid, claiming that I belong to the position of great and noble immortals, turning the Buddha Wheel, dispelling the evil opinions of demons and pagans, performing the lion's roar in the crowd).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva asked like that, the Buddha answered like that up to the seventh Buddha Wheel. “Sarvatraga” (Sarvatraga) has five dishes, corresponding to the Special Scene [46]. The Five Elements [in the Dharma of Mind] are Intention (Manasi-kāra), Contact (Sparśa), Feeling (Vedanā), Perception (Saṃjñā), and Thought (Cetanā). The first dish is Tac Y. Intention is our mind thinking like that, using the concept of thinking. To receive is to receive. What forms do you receive? When people hit you, you will feel pain. People will massage you and you will feel comfortable, beyond the physical appearance. That is the meaning of “receiving”. For example, if someone else praises you, you also receive that sound. If you curse, you will receive it, it will give rise to trouble, or you will quarrel with that person. Other people praise you, and in your heart you are delighted. Feeling belongs to the mind and cannot be visualized with form. Perception is also “variable” (all-pervading). Changing Hanh is different from Special Scene. “Van” means “pervading everywhere”. Thinking is thinking, thinking. To think, you must Intention (arising ideas, using your mind). Tac Y is a little different from Tuong. Thinking is just Thinking, while Intention is thinking about how [to do things]. In the Mahayana Hundred Dharma Insights, this is explained very clearly. The fourth item is Tu, Tu and Tuong are often related to each other. Thinking is thinking, thinking for yourself. As for Chiang, sometimes he adds memories; Therefore, there are slight differences. Contact is contact. Contact and feeling seem to be the same, but in fact, they are not the same at all.

Those five Variables, due to the Supreme Variables, will lead to afflictions. For this, there must be wisdom. Without wisdom, it will be impossible to eliminate afflictions. If you are diligent and diligent, you will be able to eliminate diseases and afflictions, stay in peace, not panic, but also not afraid, not frightened. The Buddha claimed that he belonged to the position of a noble great immortal, to the status of a Buddha, and to turning the Buddha's wheel of Dharma. That wheel can dispel the evil thoughts of all demons and pagans. In the midst of the masses, lions roar.

(Sutra) Good man! As Kshatriya Empowers the Great King, the memory of self-forgiveness accumulates the original nature, the first-born, the pupil hopes for the same thing, the memory of the self-other is like the city, the first birth of wood, the ambition of the breast, the devil's detail, the mother-in-law, or the dirty soil, or the wild servant of the race, or practicing industry, or the restoration of business, the career, or the country, the night and the wife, or serving the king, or the king. service, or as Crown Prince. Or ascend to the throne, attain great freedom, enjoy all kinds of pleasures, be generous with names, and transform all directions. Reciting the truth, establishing the first king in accordance with the Dharma, protecting the people of the country, protecting the country, not invading foreign lands. Good man! The great king's seed of kshat-de-benefits empowerment,'s accomplishment is like the eighth wheel of kings. Due to trial and error, the spirit of the country increases in peace and happiness, conquers all enemies and evil friends, good friends protect the body, and the spirit increases life span.
(Sutra: O good man! As the great king Sat-de-loi has received empowerment, think of this. the origin and nature of ourselves and others, stories like when we were first born, having fun as children, etc. that is, we and others were in such a place, when we were born, we were bathed, held, breastfed, had our limbs massaged, to laughing, or playing with ash, soil, or traveling with servants, or learning a skillful profession, or establishing and taking care of all kinds of careers, or going to other countries, or staying at night to rest. Relax, or serve the king, or take care of the affairs of the country, or be crowned king, enjoy great joy and fame in all directions, then establish the Dharma that the previous king followed to calm and nurture all the people in his country, protect his country, and not invade other countries! Great king of the Sat-de-loi nature has attained the empowerment of the eighth king Because of that virtue, our country will grow in peace and happiness, we will be able to subdue all enemies and evil friends, we will be able to protect our body, and our life span will increase.

That king remembered the past, starting from the time he was a child, like everyone else, either playing with ashes and soil, or being served, playing around, or learning all kinds of skills, or cultivating all kinds of careers, recalling the stories of his time as a disciple, or as a disciple. What's the point of saying those things? Remembering the past, the king will know what to do in the present. The great king who received the initiation in the past, himself from childhood to adulthood, was brought up under the teachings of the previous king. He remembered how beautiful the previous king's Dharma was! We must develop. We will improve the areas that are not good, that is called “revolution”. Every revolution and reform means eliminating the bad parts, [but] history has developed completely in the opposite direction, eliminating the good things. They revolutionize according to evil things to carry out. I see history developing like that. Buddhists say they propagate Buddhism, but if they don't propagate it, it will be better. [Buddhism] will be destroyed a little more slowly. The more it spreads, the faster it is destroyed! The more Buddhist halls there are, the more fake Three Jewels disciples there are, everyone must have eyes for the Dharma.

Therefore, the king remembers the past and must use the dharma of his predecessors, using the dharmas applied by his predecessors to this country to calm the current people in the country and protect his country's good achievements. Such goodness will enable the people of the king's country to live peacefully. That is remembering the past, Śākyamuni Buddha also remembers the past!

(Sutra) Good man! The Tathagata in the assembly of the great assembly, the memories of self-absorbed worlds, sutras of immeasurable kinds of things, for a memory of one birth, or two, or three, even countless hundreds of thousands of births, or a memory of kalpas, or kalpas of karma, or a kalpa of countless kalpas, kalpas, sāgṇu of the past abides like the place of the past, like the name, like the nature of the seed, like the variety, like the food, like the cold receiving painful feelings, pleasant feelings, like the amount of feeling, like the nine abiding, such as the extreme world, feeling the limit, the world is one, the future is born in the world, obeying the world, reborn in the world. The thought of the whole world is like the world of immeasurable, boundless things, depending on the different natures of living beings, establishing the Dharma, creating many benefits. Good man! I become like the Buddha's eighth Buddha.
(Sutra: Good man! Tathagata in such great assemblies, think remember the countless things that you and others have experienced in previous lives, that is, things in one life, or two, or three, up to countless hundreds of thousands of lives, or remember the past lives, or remember the lives of destruction, or remember the countless lives of creation, destruction, in the past in such a place, with such a name, with such a nature, with such a species, with such food and drink, with such suffering and pleasure, with such a long life, such a long existence, extremely limitless and limitless life. Thus, from that place to death, to birth in this world, from this world to death, to birth in that place, thinking about the things of previous lives like that, immeasurable, boundless, depending on the different natures of living beings, to create benefits. This is how I achieve the eighth Buddha Wheel.

In the great assembly, what do you do for all the disciples taught by me, for hundreds of thousands of millions of sentient beings? Preach the Dharma according to the basis. Or in the karma of destruction, what are those disciples doing with me? In life, what do we all do? In a great kalpa, there are four kalpas: Creation, Persistence, Destruction, and Emptiness. The formation kalpa consists of twenty small kalpas, the permanent kalpa consists of twenty small kalpas, the destructive kalpa consists of twenty small kalpas, the emptiness kalpa consists of twenty small kalpas. The destructive kalpa is the stage between the successful kalpa and the empty kalpa, the world is about to be destroyed, the earth is completely gone. When the destruction reaches the extreme, the great three disasters [occur, the world] is no more, empty! Then, gradually condensing and condensing, the nebula gradually formed. The Formation stage consists of twenty small kalpas, the Dwelling stage consists of twenty small kalpas. Now we are in the Eternal kalpa, not the apocalyptic kalpa.

In the Eternal Life, think about the places in that life, having gone through that much time, and also going through so many places. In the scriptures, Śākyamuni Buddha once said this: In this Sa Ba world, that is, in this three thousand great worlds, there is no place as small as a mote that is not the place where he sacrificed his life. That is to say, He stayed in the Sa Ba world to save sentient beings for too long! Until [the time] as a sentient being in this world, there are many, sacrificing one's life and life to benefit sentient beings. In the past, I lived here, you also lived here. What is the name of the other person over there? What kind of nature and species are there, what foods do they eat, receive pain and pleasure, and have quite a long life span? They either live a long life in this world, or they live a very long life. “In the same land, born in different places” [meaning] born again in this place, from this place dies, then born again in another place. Thinking about such things in previous lives, immeasurable, boundless, too many! When everyone becomes a Buddha, looking back, you will know that the lives in the past were immeasurable and boundless.

While you recite sutras, dreaming is fake, not real; But when I dream, sometimes it's real! Again, if you dream, that dream is fake, but sometimes, your mind sees it as reality. Why say so? Indeed, I have that feeling. When I was in New York, I had a dream, which seemed to be a dream that began in the Yuan Dynasty. Tonight, the dream is still unfinished. When I wake up, tomorrow night I just need to put my head on the pillow and dream again, like writing a novel chapter by chapter, episode by episode. That dream will continue in the second act like this, like that! Then I woke up, no more dreams. That was originally fake, because I personally experienced my dream. It was because of a dream that he became a monk. He came to Cuu Hoa Son because of a dream. Coming to Co Son was also due to a dream. After arriving at Co Son, I didn't dream anymore. Once there, there are no more dreams. After that, I no longer dreamed. Until now, I still hope to be guided by the dream. When I'm not dreaming, that means when I'm not dreaming, I'm in a dream. Compared to when dreaming, the delusion is deeper. That's my bad habit.

Even though I said the dream was fake, it showed me the direction, so I thought it was real. At that time, I had never come into contact with Buddhism and did not know anything. Because of the dream, I became a monk, because of the dream, I became a monk. Master gave me the Dharma name Giac Awakening, meaning "whenever one is enlightened, one will awaken". After that, I thought that name was not very suitable. It seemed like I wasn't awake yet, so I said I was dreaming. Mong Tham is a name I gave myself, exactly the opposite of the word Giac Tinh. A few days ago, I suddenly remembered my teacher, the old monk Tu Lam. When I recite the sutra, I think of the worldly teacher who gave me my name. I thought: When will I be able to wake up? Now I'm about to die, I'm still not awake, I'm still in my dream, I'm still searching for help. Nowadays, even researching is not enough! Why? I've been so greedy for research that I've become old and frail, unlike when I was young, when I was just learning the Dharma and when I was just practicing. Therefore, cultivating the Way and hoping to get rid of afflictions is very difficult, I have experienced it myself. From my personal experience, having been a monk for more than sixty years, I am still very far apart, not able to grasp it at all! Don't think I'm talking nonsense, I'm not talking nonsense at all!

Therefore, when the Buddha taught all sentient beings, he based it on their past differences. Buddha preached the Dharma, we immediately became enlightened. If someone has not attained enlightenment, for example, we also want to truly develop Bodhicitta. We explain and preach for several months, fearing that neither the preacher nor the listener will be able to enter, just sowing good roots for the future. We affirm this: Although there is no great benefit, the benefit is still not small! What's the benefit? We recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, preach the Ksitigarbha Sutra, preach the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, and in general, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will pay a little attention to us.

Therefore, what we hear and recite, we all entrust ourselves to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Every time I chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, I think like that. My friends and I all entrust ourselves to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, hoping that Bodhisattva will quickly save us. Your mind has turned towards Him, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has turned towards us. Actually, it's you saving yourself, praying to others is not as good as praying to yourself! How can you pray for yourself? Recite, read, and see for yourself, and you will feel a sense of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you, the easier it is for you to become enlightened. Why observe the past? Because then we can know their nature, and also know the cause and effect between Buddha and us in the past. Even though we are Buddhist disciples in the Dharma-Ending Age, we can feel that the Mahayana Dharma Jewels still exist in the Dharma-Ending Age, the Sangha Treasures exist, the Buddha Treasures exist, these are also the Three Jewels of the Eternal World. The statue made of clay and carved wood is the Buddha Jewel, the Tripitaka is the Dharma Jewel, and the person with a shaved head and wearing colorful robes is the Sangha Jewel. You can see that the Sangha Jewels, if you regularly live together with the Buddha Dharma and the Three Jewels, will attain salvation very quickly. Sometimes we say: “Afflictions are very heavy, karma is very deep”, incredibly negative! Let's think from this perspective: Having planted many good roots, we can still live with the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. There are people who still recite at night, sometimes even in their dreams. There are friends who can still do that, so why are you afraid? Because you have studied the Dharma, you will not be afraid, and have already achieved the eighth Buddha Wheel!

(Sutra) Due to trial and error, benefiting the peace and happiness of countless sentient beings, attaining peace and stability, attaining fearlessness, attaining nothingness Lieutenant, claiming to be a great immortal, turning the Buddha Wheel, insulting heavenly demons, pagans and heretics, punishing the masses, right of lions.
panic, not be afraid, proclaim myself in the position of a noble great immortal, turn the Buddha wheel, dispel the evil talk of demons and pagans, in the public, perform the lion's roar).

Above is the eighth Buddha Wheel.

(Sutra) Good man! Like the Great King's empowerment, he meditated on the country of sentient beings, race, industry, up to date on career, trial of death and birth, cause and effect prevailed, differences were different. Knowing that sentient beings are born like the family, when the body is strong, or overcome the weakness, like the craftsmen, the learned, the learned, possessing good deeds, evil deeds, rich, mean, virtuous, dirty, like the class, the mother is fatal. Either the son of self-karma destroys the son, or the son of self-karma destroys the son, or the son of the sixth king violates the king's law, or the son of the brother harms the son, or the son of the immortal staff, or the son of the spiritual language, or the son of the learned industry, or the son of the enemy who kills him in battle, or the son of fight and avoidance of brawls, or the son of talent, or the son of lust, or the son of lust, or the son of anger, or the entanglement of labor. To cut off a bad son, or to take advantage of the opportunity to destroy a son, or to be past death, or not to be past death, or to be a young man, or to be a young man, or to be a young man, or to cause a son's seed of good karma, or to create a seed of evil karma. animal. Knowing that sentient beings practice evil deeds, their bodies will perish, they will die, and they will be in an evil destiny. Knowing the truth, self-reflection: "The self is rightly diligent, cultivates good body conduct, cultivates good speech, cultivates good mind. Nhe is practicing the method of giving, practicing almsgiving, controlling tranquility, body destruction and death, remaining in a good destiny, falling into an evil destiny." Try the great king Kshatriya's empowerment,'s clear thinking, courage, diligence, self-cultivation, speech, mind, three types of virtuous actions, constant practice of almsgiving, must possess food, clothes, statues, horses, taboos, excess, sleeping utensils, medicine, infirmary, lamp, extra personal tools, servants, servants, various kinds of treasures, head, eye, guard, self-sufficiency, Abstaining from one's own life, abstaining from any deceit, renouncing killing, renouncing non-attachment, renouncing evil desires, renouncing false speech, renouncing harsh and evil speech, renouncing false speech, renouncing impure speech, renouncing lust, renouncing anger, renouncing wrong views.
Thinking and observing the sentient beings in one's own country, their nature, skills, and careers, death here, birth there, causes and effects are better or worse, differences are different. Know that those sentient beings are born in families like that, their bodies are strong, strong, or weak, with regard to skillful professions learned or unlearned, all careers are doing good or evil, rich or poor, decent or ugly, rough, things like that until the end: Or some people die. nghiệp của chính họ chưa hết mà đã chết, hoặc có người nghiệp của chính họ đã hết mà chết, hoặc phạm phải phép vua, bị xử tử chết. Hoặc có khi tàn hại lẫn nhau mà chết. Hoặc do bị roi, gậy đánh đập mà chết. Hoặc do bị giam kín trong nhà tù mà chết. Hoặc do học tập tài khéo mà chết. Hoặc do chiến trận bị sát thương mà chết. Hoặc do tranh chấp, đánh lộn mà chết. Hoặc do tham lam, keo kiệt của cải mà chết. Hoặc do tham đắm sắc dục mà chết. Hoặc do phẫn Because of hatred, resentment, death. Or due to fatigue, depression, death. Or death due to fault.HOr death due to old age. Hor old age. HOr die in childhood. Or do all kinds of good karma and die. Or do all kinds of bad karma and die. Knowing that sentient beings do good deeds, their bodies will die, and they will enter the good path. Knowing that sentient beings will commit evil deeds, their lives will expire, and they will think to themselves: "I should diligently practice good deeds in my body, good deeds in my speech, and good deeds in my mind. Arrange all kinds of means, practice almsgiving, control tranquility. When the body is destroyed, when the end comes, you will enter the good path and not fall into the evil destinies." After receiving that empowerment, the great king Sat-di-li thought like that, then he was brave and diligent, practiced the three good virtues in body, speech, and mind, constantly practicing giving alms, all food, clothes, elephants, horses, mounts, vehicles, bedding, medicine, houses, lights, and other things. other living things, slaves, servants, all kinds of precious possessions, head, eyes, feet, hands, even the body, do not be stingy, and abstain from killing, abstain from giving and taking, abstain from evil desires, abstain from false and deceitful speech, abstain from harsh speech, dissociative speech, impure speech, abstain from desires, abstain from anger, abstain from wrong views).

In the previous section, I talked about the five Elements, I will explain again. Intention, Touch, Feeling, Thought, Thought, these are the five types. When those five types of Changes arise, they will arise simultaneously, without a before or after. Intention means “vigilance”, which means that when the mind has not yet raised [thoughts], Intention will cause the mind to raise thoughts. To start a thought is to raise the appearance of the realm. If the mind has just aroused thoughts, it will be able to initiate contemplation of the scene. “Contemplation” means facing the scene. Touching means facing the scene (receiving the scene). To feel is to receive, to receive the foreground. Thought means holding on to the realm. Thought is the beginning of the mind to create karma. These five types arise at the same time, so they are called Changes.

Ninth King Wheel of King Sat-de-li: That king has great wisdom, he himself first examines in that country, the nature, talent, dexterity, what career that country does, until the people in that country “die, be born” i.e. from this place die, be born in there. The wisdom of knowing that they "die in this place, are born in that place" is not Succesful Wisdom, the king completely does not know "when they die from this world, what world will they be born in", but based on the karma they have done, based on the things they have done while alive, they can judge. The things they have done in the present are causes; In the future, they will be born there as a result. [Specifically] where he was born, he could not judge; That king does not have the Wisdom of Life and the Forgiveness of Mind. Here it means that when he observes, he observes that the people in that country have sown good or bad causes, and now they are suffering the consequences. Why must we suffer such consequences? Because the past sowed bad seeds. Know whether their past karma is superior or inferior? Now, why is there such a difference? From the results of the past, one will be able to know the cause done in this life: Born in a good family, or born in a bad family. What is a good family? What is a bad family? This is absolutely not an argument based on wealth.

In India, being born in the Brahmin family is a good family, knowledgeable, and educated. To be born in the Sat-de-loi nature is to be in a wealthy family. If one is born in the nature of Ve-xa or Thu-dala, one is born in a butcher's house, or one is born in a worker's house, there will be differences in superiority and inferiority. Some people are born and always grow up, their bodies are very strong, very brave, very strong. Some people are born sick and debilitated, that is the meaning of the word “terrible” [in the main scriptures]. Some people are born very smart, very clever, and as soon as they learn a skillful profession, they immediately understand it. Some people learn very hard and are very stupid. Just like in the old days, workers followed the teacher for three years, some people studied for a year and understood, each person is different!

Therefore doing good, doing evil, being rich, poor, being born righteous, or being ugly, rough, of all kinds, up to the end of life, is also a different life span for each person. There are people who, because of their own profession, their lives are not worth dying for, but they die instead. That is, the life span is not yet ended, but the life span is short and death is imminent. When fate ends, death is a righteous death. The lay family has this view: If you die in your own home, it is called “living in the same bed”. If you die outside, it is because you have created karma, you cannot "live the same life", you die while wandering. If you violate the king's rules, you will be beheaded or hanged. That is “death by hexagram”. They died by killing each other, or by being beaten by whips and sticks. Being punished, or fighting with others, or being imprisoned, or dying in prison. Until a lifetime of darkness, death in prison. Or because of learning a skillful profession, no matter what profession you learn, you accidentally cause injury and death. There are also cases like that. Or the armies of both sides will fight and die. Or get into a fight with someone else and die. Or die because of greed for wealth.

For this story of greed for wealth, I tell a story: There was an old monk who spent his whole life scavenging a bar of silver, but was not careful and dropped it down the toilet. Because he regretted that gambler, he died. After his death, he turned into a frog in the septic tank, holding that silver bar. The master Tri Khach in that temple had supernatural powers and was very wise. Knowing that the old monk had died very unnaturally, he invited someone to dig up that bridge. The septic tank in the temple in Mainland China is very deep and it takes a lot of effort to dig it out. After digging up that vault, I took it out, recited the dedication sutras, prayed for him, used that silver coin to do Buddhist work for him, and helped him attain salvation. That old monk was lucky enough to meet that monk Tri Khach. If you don't meet it, you will forever fall there to regret it. People who die like that because of greed for money are usually those who fail in business, lose all their money, or regret the lost treasure. Because all one's attention is focused on it, if it is lost, that person's life will also end. It was because of greed for wealth and beauty that he died!

Or die because of lust. Some people fall in love and die sadly. Some people have fallen in love and die because of greed. Or when someone else harms you, your psychology is not balanced and you don't have the strength to fight that person, so you die in anger and depression. All kinds of deaths like that. Either he died from fatigue and exhaustion, or he died from hunger, thirst, deprivation, and exhaustion. Either make a mistake and die, or die without a mistake. Or die in old age, or die in youth, or die in childhood. Either someone has good karma and dies, or someone has bad karma and dies.

King Sat-de-loi based his judgment on various types of death situations. He said that sentient beings, by creating good karma, when their body breaks down and dies, they will definitely be born in a good place, born in the human world. If a person is very evil and commits a lot of evil, his body will perish and he will die, and he will definitely be reborn in the three evil destiniess. He saw the situation in society, saw it very clearly. However, it is only limited to the people of our country. According to Buddhism, we are not just a Kshatriya king, we look at the world, see the entire human world, this belongs to the Four Noble Truths. Again, it is a worldly dharma. All Buddha Dharma does not leave the world. The Buddha's teachings, as spoken by the Buddha, are for the sake of the world and establish laws beyond the world.

We have many people who live to the age of sixty or something, experiencing many things in the world. This sutra talks about different types of death, it talks about different lifespans, there are [different] types of death. At that time, there were no car accidents yet. If there is a car accident, there will definitely be a case of death from a car accident. There are all kinds of car accidents, and there are also cases of death by plane. At that time, there were only boats, there was a way to cross the river and drown, but the tools to cross the river were different. It's like we're on a big boat, the boat is powered by a motor, very good. Wooden boats used to be quite good. If you live in Tibet, when you cross the river in the Kangxi region[47] you have to sit on a boat, which will scare you to death! What boat is that? Boat made of cowhide. A layer of cowhide is peeled off, four wooden poles are used to stretch it, it is dried, and it is used [covered with a wooden frame to make a boat] to cross the river. They row like this: Each side has an oar. If you go this way, row on this side. If you go on the other side, row on the other side. Sitting in the boat will make you tremble with fear. When the waves come, the boat will be thrown very high. The waves receded and the boat sank again. If you encounter strong waves, water rushes in and you will be submerged. There is no way to submerge.

This is about all kinds of death, death in all ways and forms. This great king who was empowered with Sat-di-li, while cultivating blessings, observed all kinds of phenomena in the kingdom and then thought. He said: "Life is impermanent, we cannot do bad things, we should only do good things. We should follow the correct path, be diligent, and practice courageously." “I should be diligent and righteous” (I should be diligent and righteous): “Right” is correct, not evil spirits or pagans. Cultivate good deeds in your body. Good deeds in the body are body karma. Virtue is not killing, not stealing, not committing sexual misconduct. Cultivating good conduct in speech means cultivating the mouth, not lying, not saying embellishments, not saying harsh words, not saying double-minded things. That is cultivating good karma. Cultivating good conduct in the mind means not being greedy, not being angry, not being ignorant. In addition, we must practice all kinds of alms and arrange all kinds of facilities. Practicing almsgiving must also be a skillful means to tame one's own mind. The king can attain Concentration, regulate his breathing, and calm his mind. That way, when the body breaks down and dies, you will be able to be born in a good path and not fall into an evil destinies. King Sat-di-loi initiated thinking about this matter; After that, he was brave and diligent. Cultivate good deeds in the three karma of body, mind, and speech, and practice good conduct. Always practice almsgiving, what kind of alms? Food, clothes, all the means of transportation, elephants, horses, vehicles, even bedding for sleeping, even medicine for the sick, alms of houses, alms of lights, all the necessary items for life, whatever you can.

King of the Sat-di-li initiation has that power, but currently, he is not a king, at that time, he was a monk. Due to cultivating, thinking, giving, and not creating these karma, one should stay away from killing, stay away from not giving and take, stay away from sexual desires and evil deeds, which also means staying away from killing, stealing, and lust. Do not kill, steal or commit sexual misconduct in your body, and keep your mouth away from false words, harsh words, separatist words, and impure words. We call impure words false language (fabricated speech). Disparaging words are double talk, harsh words are evil speech, false words are false speech. Stay away from desires, stay away from anger, stay away from wrong views, also leave greed, anger, and ignorance.

(Sutra) Due to the fate of the visionary, try Sat-de-loi to initiate the great king, planning the ten merits of victory. Ha class vi ten? Most famous person, great name. The second one, the great fortune teller. Tam fake, wonderful form. Four people, many relatives. Five fakes, less illness, less brain. Scholars, friends, and relatives are knowledgeable and well-educated. Seven people, right will, right conduct, close offerings. The Eight Immortals, the vast beauty of the sound, and the ten directions' vibrations. The nine, majestic and virtuous angels, often protect them. The ten people, their body is broken, their life is over, they are born in heaven, they will always live in a good destiny, the Land of Peace. Good man! The contemplation of the Kshat-de-benefits empowers the great king, achieves the status of the ninth king wheel.
(Sutra: Due to that cause and effect, the great king Kshatriya who receives that empowerment will attain ten loại lợi ích công đức thù thắng. Những gì là mười? Một là trọn đủ danh xưng to lớn. Hai là trọn đủ của cải to lớn. Ba là trọn đủ sắc tướng mầu nhiệm. Bốn là có nhiều quyến thuộc. Năm là ít bệnh, ít phiền não. Sáu là bạn bè, quyến thuộc thông minh, trí huệ, đa văn. Bảy là chánh chí, chánh hạnh thân cận, cúng dường. Tám là thanh danh đẹp đẽ rộng lớn, vang rền mười phương. Chín là thiên thần có oai đức lớn thường theo bảo vệ. Mười là khi When the body breaks down and dies, one will be born in heaven, always in a good path, or in the world of Peace and Happiness! Great king of the Sat-de-loi nature has been empowered to achieve the ninth king wheel like that.

Due to the ten pure karma causes and conditions, the great king Sat-de-li's empowerment achieved ten types of outstanding merit. Not just him, any sentient being, if he practices the Ten Good Karmas, depends on how he practices the Ten Good Karmas, some are deep, some are shallow. As we receive the Five Precepts, regarding the precept of abstaining from sexual immorality, if that person maintains the precepts, even if he does not commit sexual misconduct, he will be able to be reborn in Brahma. That person does not lie, speaks the truth, does not say words that cause separation, tries his best to speak good words, making others gentle and good. That person has reversed [evil habits], that is his merit, everyone calls him “great good man”, beautiful reputation. Because that person gives alms, he will be able to gain great wealth. The reward of giving alms is to be rich. We think that after letting go, there will be nothing, but in contrast, in the future, you will gain great wealth. Having wealth comes from merit, or from cultivating. You have no blessings, all wealth does not belong to you!

Everyone knows that the last emperor of the Manchu Qing Dynasty was Tuyen Thong (Pho Nghi). Later, when he was in prison, only one nephew followed him. That nephew followed him to the end and was also in prison with him. His nephew had committed absolutely no crime. He had been by his side to take care of him since childhood, following him to prison so he could take care of the former emperor's life. He and his uncle hid many precious things, moved them from the palace, and kept them hidden.
