Above, the Ten Wheels of Buddha were used to compare the Ten Wheels of the world, that is, the Ten Wheels of King Sat-di-li, which are worldly dharmas, phenomena in the world. Buddha came from within the world, transcended the world, and reached beyond the world. This is only the second chapter spoken by the Buddha.

Starting from the third chapter, it will extensively explain the meaning of the Buddha Wheel, as well as the meaning of worldly dharma in King Sat-de-li, two situations coexist. However, in the current situation, in worldly dharma, sentient beings create the ten more serious evil karma, people who create the ten good karma are very few, not non-existent. Disciples who take refuge in the Three Jewels all practice Ten Wholesome Actions, but compared to fifty-seven billion people in the world, they are still a minority. As for Bodhisattvas who attain enlightenment and attain the dharani samadhi subjects, it is unlikely that there will be any. Even if we did, we wouldn't be able to see it because we don't have enough blessings and wisdom! Once you have developed Bodhi mind, you can believe, without doubting. Having believed in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of the Three Jewels, you will be able to practice, following the Buddha's teachings. Such sentient beings are very few!

III. Non Y Hanh - Pham De Tam

(The third item: Vo Y Hanh)

(Sutra) Ear-time, the middle-order of Maha Brahma, written in Thien Store, nine real good roots, dwelling in the Tenth Ground, specific Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas of virtue, i.e., the spring of the throne, joined hands to pay homage to the Buddha, and recited and recited: "The merit treasure of the wisdom treasure, the golden ego questions the doubts, may the wisdom of the sea of hearing, the ego eliminates doubts. The golden ego is thirsty for admiration, the virtue treasure surpasses the Dharma position, the ultimate meaning is updated, and the text of the teachings is sent to the assembly."
(Sutra: At that time, in the assembly there was a Great Brahma, named Thien Tang, who had planted good roots for a long time, abiding in the Tenth Ground, complete with all the virtues of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, immediately stood up from his seat, clasped his hands, bowed to the Buddha, and then recited verses and chanted: "Ocean of wisdom, storehouse of merit. I now ask about doubts. May the ocean of wisdom listen. For me to eliminate doubts. We now yearn to admire, conquer the dharma, the virtuous treasure, and the ultimate meaning. The great assembly all want to hear").

This verse praises the merits of the Buddha, “the wisdom ocean” refers to the Buddha's teachings. Buddha contains all merit, contains all wisdom, is as deep as the ocean, as wide as the sea. Brahma said "I have doubts", [meaning] now I have some doubts, can I ask? Is it possible to request?

“May the ocean of wisdom listen to you” (May the ocean of wisdom listen): Dear Buddha, please have mercy on me and allow me to speak, so that doubt can be eliminated for me. “Doubt” is an obstacle or obstacle. Whenever there are doubts or obstacles, it will be impossible to move forward. Only by eliminating doubts can you practice. We and the audience attending the Dharma Assembly all yearn for admiration, what is this thirst for? “The virtuous treasure trumps the dharma position” (The dharma taste prevails in the storehouse of merit). “The Treasury of Virtues” is a [word] praising Buddha, praising the World-Honored One, which contains all merits and has a superior Dharma flavor. “Taste of Dharma” is when the Buddha preaches the Dharma, there will be a kind of taste, just like when we eat and drink, we feel the wonderful taste arising. Here is the wonderful taste of the dharmas, such as when you have a mind of joy, a mind of joy, a mind of diligence, and a mind of repentance. This story contains many [meanings], depending on each person's power of wisdom when listening to the Dharma, as well as the strength of one's own good roots.

“The ultimate meaning” is the taste of the dharma due to hearing the dharma, listening to the First Supreme Noble Truth. That meaning is the First Meaning, everyone hopes to achieve that superior First Meaning, to have a position, and to be able to have enough. Listening to the taste of the Dharma is like eating food. Cultivate yourself, practice! Therefore, currently everyone is looking forward to hearing it.

First of all, we must know the meaning of the chapter on Non-Yanh Hanh to know the meaning of that dharma position. Ignorance means doing things that are not trustworthy. That means that when you practice a certain dharma, that dharma should be the basis for good roots and merit to depend on to arise, but the dharma you are practicing cannot be the basis [for good roots and merit] to rely on [to arise]! Non-yi means "not being able to rely on". Practicing dharma (the dharma performed) is inherently a refuge for generating merit and good roots; [Yet the dharma practices mentioned in this chapter] are Non-Year, that is, they cannot be used as a basis to arise [good roots, merit]! Why can't? Or it's because of your predestined thoughts, wrong knowledge, wrong views, creating all kinds of karma. Or due to evil conditions, you don't meet a wise master, but instead meet an evil friend who guides you, then when you practice the dharma, those dharmas cannot be a refuge for merit and good roots, that is, what you have done cannot give rise to good roots, cannot give rise to merit. Then what will be born? Giving birth to sins. Below, [the Buddha will list] there are ten types in total.

(Sutra) The Buddha reported to the Thien Store Maha Brahma: “The Tathagata, the alchemy of the four minds, asks, if asked and answered, the spirit happy mind". Great Brahma said: "Of course, World-Honored One!" Di recitation questions write: "The person who practices Samadhi, who abides without distraction, is the one who abides in the Noble Truth of the Noble Truth? The one who is guided only by birth and death? The one who abides in the Dharma, diligently reciting the practice, the one who attains the ocean of afflictions? The one who is regressing to the evil realm? The one who is brave and needs the blessings, the one who is concentrated in the realm of Nirvana? The one who deals with birth and death, regresses to the evil beast? The one who understands the Kshatriya, attains the ten seeds, the one who is in the midst of samsara and death? The one who is ascending to Buddhahood. The result? Contaminated mind is difficult to overcome, all afflictions are chaotic, how to purify the mind, cultivate Concentration, merit, and recite karma?
(Sutra: The Buddha told the Brahma Pitaka: “The Tathagata now allows you to do as you please. When asked, he will answer according to your question, making your heart happy." Great Brahma said: "Yes, World-Honored One!" Using verses, he asked: "The wise person who cultivates Concentration and abides without letting go, will he abide in the Noble Truth, or will he diligently practice the Dharma day and night, or will he overcome the ocean of troubles, or will he bravely and diligently practice merit, or will he surely attain Nirvana, or will he fall into the trap of birth and death? evil destinies? Through wisdom and attainment of the ten wheels, will one sink into birth and death, or ascend to Buddhahood? Contaminated minds are difficult to overcome, disturbing afflictions, what can be used to purify the mind, practice concentration, merit, and recite karma?”)

Buddha immediately praised the problems raised by Thien Pitaka

Thien asked. The Buddha told Thien Treasury Maha Brahma: “The Tathagata now allows you to ask as you please, and will answer according to the question, making your heart happy”. Great Brahma said: “Yes, World-Honored One!”, then used verses to recite to ask. First of all, he made a request. The verses recited in the previous section are to ask Buddha's advice: I have questions, can you answer them for me? Having answered the question, it will enable us all to enjoy the most sublime and miraculous taste of the Dharma by listening to the Dharma. “Dharma flavor, meaning”: In the dharma taste there is meaning, in the dharma there is meaning. Buddha replied: “As you wish”, meaning: You want to ask me, I will explain and answer for you. Great Brahma used this verse to ask questions. He said a total of five recitations, each recitation had four verses. He said: A person who has wisdom and advantages and cultivates Concentration, that is, cultivating Samadhi, can never let go. “Don't let loose” (Never let loose) means don't move around (chatter, be agitated), but also don't become lethargic. Will such beings reside in the Thang Nghia Emperor? Or do we still have to circulate in birth and death? Will it still refer to birth and death to circulate, or will it refer to Thang Nghia? That is to say, suppose there was a wise and sharp person cultivating Concentration, abiding in diligence and not being negligent to practice, would that person abide in the Thang Nghia Truth, or would he still rely on birth and death? That's a problem.

“Dwelling on the Dharma, diligently reciting it, will you save the ocean of afflictions? Regress to the evil realm?” (Diligence day and night, reciting the Dharma, will you overcome the sea of afflictions? Or regress to the evil destinies?): “Dharma” is the meaning contained in the sutras written by the Buddha. said. Every sutra has meaning, is supreme, is the First Noble Truth. Therefore, each dharma is called “True dharma” (true dharma).. As for the meaning of Buddha dharma, practice day and night, read and recite the Mahayana, and also be diligent, courageous, diligent, diligent, not lazy; Is it possible to cross the sea of ​​afflictions like that? By doing so, can he overcome the sea of ​​afflictions? Or will he fall into evil destiniess? This verse has the same meaning as the above verse: [The difference is] one side is to practice Concentration, the other side is to read and recite the Mahayana to cultivate Wisdom and cultivate blessings.

Next is to take care of cultivating merit. “Courage requires business blessings” (Courage, diligence in cultivating blessings): Do all Buddhist deeds, always be brave, diligent, and diligent in doing them. "The one who is determined to enjoy Nirvana? The one who experiences birth, death, and regress, or the evil one?", meaning: Can that type of being who specializes in cultivating meritorious karma use the force of merit and virtue to move towards Nirvana? Or is he still in samsara and falling into evil destiniess? Here's another thing!

The second problem, Kshatriya is intelligent, has wisdom, achieves ten types of wheel, "the one who is in the middle of birth and death? The one who is ascending to Buddhahood?" (will sink into birth and death? Or ascend to Buddhahood?): For kings of the Sat-de-loi nature as mentioned in the previous section, that is, Sat-de-loi is empowered to become a king, has achieved ten types of king wheels, ascends to the throne of Kim Luan King, or the throne of Dong Luan. There are four types of Sat-di-loi [being a Luan King], we always talk about the Kim Luan King being the king of all four continents. He has achieved ten types of king wheels, will he still be immersed in birth and death, or will he ascend to Buddhahood? That means is it possible to attain Buddhahood?

“The impure mind is difficult to overcome, the afflictions are chaotic, how to purify the mind, cultivate Concentration, merit, recite karma?” (The impure mind is difficult to subdue, disturbed by afflictions, how to purify the mind, cultivate Concentration, cultivate merit, or recite?): This is the part. The recitation aims to state these things in general. Living beings in the present time are the same, regardless of cultivating Concentration, cultivating and reciting karma (reciting and reciting Mahayana), it is the same for sentient beings who care about cultivating blessings, their minds are all impure minds. As for the Kshatriya who was empowered to become a king, why did he (Thivastavaṇa Maha Brahma) ask like that? If we focus on cultivating and creating merit, can we move towards Nirvana? Through the karma of reciting, can one attain Buddhahood? Can Tu Dinh achieve samadhi? Given that one side is the front, the other side is the contrast, why does he ask that? “Contaminated mind is difficult to overcome” (Contaminated mind is difficult to overcome).

The afflicted mind and impure mind of sentient beings are very difficult to tame. Often while practicing the Dharma, their mind cannot concentrate on one scene and will be disturbed by afflictions. What method can be used to keep the mind pure to cultivate Concentration, or cultivate blessings, to carry out such a wonderful career?

In the present era, at the end of the Dharma, there are many Dharma friends cultivating Concentration, even reading and reciting the Mahayana, setting daily routines, as well as morning and evening routines in pagodas and temples, which are all reciting the Mahayana, there are also some secret mantras, doing Buddhist work, or reciting sutras and worshiping. Or there are Dharma friends, requested by the owner, to arrange vegetarian offerings to create blessings. So can doing these meritorious deeds lead to enlightenment? Is it possible to achieve Buddhahood and achieve Buddhist karma? Why ask like that? Because when they do [those things], their mind is contaminated. Contaminated mind is the presence of both good and evil minds, their mind cannot concentrate on one scene.

When chanting sutras, everyone knows that it is not easy to focus on the meaning of the first stage, the meaning of the middle stage, and the meaning of the last stage in the text. Starting from the first sentence, reading the title of the sutra, until the end is dedicating. After reading, during that time, are there any mixed thoughts or not? Is the mind pure or not? We ourselves can judge. Sometimes the mind is pure, other times the reciting just keeps reciting, not knowing where the reciting goes! There are times when you recite and doze off! Sometimes, because we don't make any effort, we don't even realize it. If you make an effort, you will notice that both drowsiness and gestures appear in all directions! One moment I think about something else, the next moment I think about something else! Both sides are most easily disturbed.

While reciting the sutra, the mouth is still reciting, as if reciting slowly. I have been reciting the Pho Mon chapter for many years. I have recited it for more than ten years and know it by heart. Or like when we worship, it doesn't take long for everyone to memorize it. Once you know it, it's easier to get confused. The mouth recites it, the mind runs to another place and is lost! So is there a blessing or not? I think there still is. At least the verbal and physical karma have been determined, it's just that delusions cannot be purified yet! Brahma asked the question: How can we purify the mind? If you want to purify your mind, you must cultivate Concentration, cultivate blessings, and how you read and recite them, then the effect will be great. If you use an impure mind, it is because of afflictions and confusion, will you have merit or not? Does the Buddha have any skillful means to help those sentient beings get rid of their impure minds to cultivate concentration, cultivate blessings, or practice chanting? Brahma's question contains such meaning.

(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One told the Brahma Pitaka: “Good! You are skillful in eloquence and can ask about that dharma. You have practiced diligently about the virtues. In the past, you have lived with as many Buddhas as the sands of the Ganges River, diligently using the three karmas to continue the Three Jewels, and now, for the sake of benefiting countless sentient beings, you ask the Tathagata about such profound meanings! The World-Honored One in the past, because he wanted to mature sentient beings, because he wanted to make them weary of the dharma of birth and death, because he wanted to eliminate afflictions, and to make the three vehicles quickly reach completion, he proclaimed and maintained this great dharma of Non-Yāhāna

Buddha replied to Thien Pitaka Brahma: “You asked a very good question! You have unhindered argumentative talent and skillful argumentation, so you can ask about this principle." The word "Tu" refers to the issues that were raised before. "Thought" means "that meaning". "Nhuu tries the dharma of creating island" means: For this dharma, you have practiced for a long time. "Cu Lao" is to praise you. I have worked very hard, very diligently. Therefore, regarding the dharmas that you asked, you have completed them. Because your actions have been perfected, you have reached the Ten Bodhisattva Levels, that is, you have reached the Dharma Cloud Levels, and you have not only asked me in the present, but also asked about the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones in the past as many as the sands of the Ganges River.

He has practiced this type of deep meaning, has practiced it himself, has had experience, Brahma already knows. When cultivating Concentration, reading and reciting Mahayana teachings in order to cultivate wisdom karma, due to an impure mind, suffering from afflictions and chaos, can one attain birth and death? Is it possible to attain Buddhahood? He had experienced: Using a contaminated mind, you will not be able to attain enlightenment, you must achieve a pure mind. Is there any method that can make that person's mind not restless, can he attain a pure mind? Therefore, the Buddha praised: In countless past lives, in front of the World-Honored Buddhas as numerous as the grains of sand in the Ganges River, he used the three karma of body, mouth, and mind to diligently practice, protect the Dharma, flourish the Dharma, continue the nature of the Three Jewels, and also asked the Buddha-World-Honored Ones [the meanings] like that. For the benefit of countless sentient beings, he now asks me such a profound meaning. This morality is very deep! You say that if the mind is impure, there is no blessing, how can one achieve a pure mind? Good roots must be planted gradually, or karma gradually disappears. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas all practiced for countless lifetimes. Sakyamuni Buddha manifested his incarnation and practiced for three great Asanga kalpas. [Actually], is it possible that there are only three great Asanga kalpas? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva practiced for countless, countless kalpas, many three great Asanga kalpas. Therefore, Buddhism is difficult to achieve!

Hey good man! There is a great dharma called Vo Yanh Hanh, all Buddhas are like that. “Great Distinction” is a prediction, that is, the Buddha predicted that in the future it would be like this or that; That's called Ky Biet. Until the Buddha attested to a certain disciple, saying: "At some point, after many lifetimes, you will become a Buddha. When you become a Buddha, what name will you have, what is the name of that country, what is the name of that world?" That's called Tho Ky. [Dai Ky Biet] here is talking about preaching the Dharma. “Dai Ky” is about the dharma, not about people. Saying that in the future, all living beings will be like this and like that, that is also the Distinction. [Forecasting the situation in the stages] Dharma, Dharma Image, and Dharma Ending are also the meaning of the Distinction. In the Dharma-Ending Age, sentient beings will be like this, like that, even Buddha Dharma is sparse, creating many karma, Breaking Views, Permanent Views, many evil views.

(Sutra) At present, the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the ten directions, the mature herons, the sentient beings, the souls in denial The attempt of birth and death, the spirit of eliminating the affliction of karma, the spirit of the three vehicles speeding up the completion of perfection, preached, the abbot tried Vo Y Hanh to write great notes of the dharma. Regardless of the past, present, or future Buddhas, the Buddhas of the three worlds, in order to make all sentient beings cut off their karma, cut off their Views, and cut off their afflictions, make them mature, leave birth and death, attain Nirvana, achieve the state of the three vehicles, no longer reincarnating in the six paths, also proclaim the great Dharma. This Vo Y Hanh. The Buddhas of the three times all said so. “Nhu” (he) is to say to Thien Store Maha Brahma: You have been to the Buddhas of the past, and have heard this great Dharma inscription of No Yanh Hanh. You have already heard it, but for the benefit of sentient beings, you ask me to speak again. Now, in order to mature all sentient beings, to cause all sentient beings to end their afflictions, to attain Bodhi, to make them weary of birth and death, to make them attain Nirvana, to make them attain the status of Shravaka, Pratyekabuddha, Bodhisattva, and quickly achieve perfection, I will also proclaim this great Dharma of the Distinctive Practice of Non-Yāhāra!

“Nhu hap de listen!” means: Listen carefully, listen correctly. To everyone who requests the Dharma, the Buddha told “listen according to reason”, “listen carefully”. From Bodhisattvas of the Ten Levels to Manjushri Bodhisattva asking questions, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva asking questions, the Buddha all taught to “listen properly, listen according to reason” (listen, listen correctly), [speaking like that] to teach us [listen according to reason, listen truly]. We must think rationally. Speaking is Van means listening, listening is Van Hue. Literature, Thought, Practice, without listening, how can one think? Without thinking, how can you practice? Otherwise, it will be blind practice! You must know how to practice, how to practice? There will be a method to practice. Therefore, we teach you to “listen carefully”.

(Buddha taught: - Great Pham! There are ten dharmas of Non-Importance. If a practitioner of Concentration has any one practice, he cannot achieve the good roots in the Desire Realm. Moreover, will it be possible to achieve Samadhi of Form and Formless Realm, up to achieving one of the three vehicles?) That is to say there are ten types of dharma of Non-Yāhā. When that person practices according to the Dharma of No Clothing, does not rely on the Three Jewels, does not rely on the Buddha's teachings, then he will not be able to practice Concentration successfully!

Those ten types of Non-Conceptual Dharma, as long as there is one type, cannot be accomplished. Even the good roots in the Desire Realm cannot be achieved. If that person has achieved it before, when he practices according to those dharmas, that is, among the ten types of Non-Year, there is one type of Non-Year, what he has achieved before will be lost. Our good roots and blessings are not limitless. If you do not practice in this life, the previous blessings will be reduced and lost in this life. This life is all enjoyed, there will be no more! If a person who studies the Dharma is not diligent, if he becomes lazy, "studying the Dharma is like a boat swimming against the water, if he does not advance, he will inevitably fall back". If you are not courageous and diligent, until you have reached the Non-Regression position, you will still decline, unless you have become a Buddha! Once you become a Buddha, your body, mouth, and mind no longer need to be protected or thought about! There is no need to pay attention, it is natural, there is not the slightest bit of evil! Before reaching the Eighth Grounds, the Great Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas must protect and think [preserve the three pure karma]. Although Arhats have attained enlightenment and believe that Nirvana is immovable, they still have to protect their body, mouth, and mind. That is called “huu protector” (must protect). Buddha has reached the status of “unprotected” (no need to preserve or protect the three karma).

If among the ten types of Immoral Conduct, you have one type, if you hope to achieve good roots in the Desire Realm, it will not be possible! Previously it was accomplished, but now there is Vo Y Hanh. Whenever there is such a dharma, you will withdraw. If you want to practice Zen Concentration, you will not be able to attain Zen Concentration. Meditation subjects are all unattainable! Form Realm Meditation and Formless Realm Meditation are both unattainable. That is to say, the Four Meditations and the Four Emptiness Concentrations in the Eight Concentrations cannot be achieved at all, let alone the attainment of the fruition in the three vehicles, that is, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Bodhisattva, even one vehicle cannot be achieved! That's what it means. Below, list out ten Non-Yāhāhās.

Hdrinking the lake will be able to achieve Form Concentration and Formless Concentration, cso not achieving any of the three vehicles?)

“Ha class vi ten?” (What are ten): To ask the meaning, what kind of ten are they? "The one, the world is the same, although desire cultivates Concentration, the law of self-containment, prayers are disturbed" (Firstly, in the world there is a type of person who, although wanting to practice Concentration, lacks the conditions to help and is disturbed by the wishes): If you wish to practice Concentration, you must have self-respect; First of all, you must prepare your salary. Consciousness to practice Concentration is of two types:

1) You must have a quiet place.

2) Someone is protecting you. Dressing, living, everything is there, no worries, no thoughts.

These are all thoughts to practice religion. Even more important is thoughtfulness about the Dharma. If you want to practice Concentration, you must first practice family conduct. First of all, you repent to eliminate karma. We have received the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, first of all we must repent, that is because of this meaning. If you don't have any self-reflection and hope to practice concentration and tranquility, you won't be able to do it. If you can't do it, then false thoughts in your mind will definitely arise: If you eat this meal, there will be no next meal, what should you do? When sitting quietly there, you will think: "Is there still rice to put in the pot tomorrow?" Or the clothes you wear are not enough and cannot protect against the cold. Or maybe the place where you practice is full of mosquitoes. Mosquitoes bite you. When Concentration is not enough, you will not be able to concentrate. I hope to live in the mountains, find a quiet place, the mountains and forests are not an easy place to live. In Chinese terms, when you do not research thoroughly and cannot live in the mountains, it is because you cannot concentrate and do not have that power of concentration. The first type of Non-Importance is having no self-reliance to rely on. Practicing like that will not achieve anything. That's the first thing.

“Second people, who are of the same type, despite their desire to cultivate Concentration, violate the Thi La and practice evil actions” (Secondly, there is another type of person who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, violates the Precepts and commits evil deeds): Has violated the precepts, has broken the precepts. Thi La protects you. Thi La is the basis for being good, preventing mistakes, and ending evil. If you break the precepts, break the rules of ritual, and hope to practice Concentration, it will not be possible! Not keeping the precepts is breaking the precepts. Breaking the precepts is committing an evil act. If you practice evil deeds and want to practice Concentration, it will not be possible. This is the second Vo Y Hanh.

“The three false ones, the best of all, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, they are crazy in their views, falsely clinging to good and evil, and their body and mind are strong” (Thirdly, there is a type of person who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, has crazy views, is wrongly attached to good and evil, and their body and mind are stubborn): If they want to cultivate Concentration, they use crazy views, [attachment to] good, evil, misfortune, and blessing. Good, bad, bad, and blessed include many things! What is “Ant Crazy”? Seeing this house, or this house, as soon as you step in, take a quick look, then say: "This place is not good! That window is not in the right place. Opening that door is not good. Opening the door that way will bring danger, you have to make some changes. You have to do it in a good way." That's called "crazy ants". Good, bad, disaster, and good fortune come from your past karma, determined by past causes. Furthermore, when a good person is in an evil place, the evil place also turns into good. Evil people are in a good place, even a good place will turn into a bad place! It all depends on the person, not the place, nor the house!

When you have crazy views, are stubbornly attached to good, bad, bad, and blessed, your body and mind are very stubborn and will not receive right knowledge and right view. The Buddha did not say [sad, bad, misfortune, blessing] like that. Even those who boast of supernatural powers and tell big lies all belong to this category. Even considering good, bad, bad, blessed, astrological, changing other people's destiny, all are “crazy views”. What is the point of crazy reversal of views? Crazy cause and effect, not believing in good, evil, cause, effect.

“Four people, all are of the same type, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, their mind is agitated” (Fourth, there is another type of person, although they want to cultivate Concentration but their mind is agitated): The mind cannot be concentrated! Movement (excitement) is a lot of wandering thoughts, extremely chaotic, and is also the fluttering and popping of the senses. People who practice Concentration must at least absorb the six senses a little. Why do we have to open our eyes three parts and close our eyes seven parts when we practice Concentration? Let your eyes not look outward, explore, investigate, look everywhere! Be calm! When the eyes come into contact with the scene, it must be calm. When your ears hear sound, you must be still. Why must we find a quiet place? No disturbance! You stand on the main road, there is only the sound of cars passing by, how can you cultivate Concentration? I can't practice. These things all belong to the category of Gestures. The movement of the mind is due to not following the teachings of the sages, the senses are very troubled, restless, the body cannot sit still! The six senses of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are all fluttering and stirring!

“The five false ones are of the same type, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, they are not free from gossip” (Fifth, there is a type of person who, although wanting to cultivate Concentration, utters disparaging words): This is the phenomenon of breaking the precepts. The above paragraph talks about breaking the precepts, [this paragraph talks about] sparking schism. If you don't say words that stir up separation, that person won't be able to stand it. It's also when he sees someone else being good, his heart is jealous, he will intervene to fabricate things, make up stories, and open his mouth to sabotage both sides. We don't need to give an example of this, everyone understands this principle!

“The six people, the most obedient of all, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, have coarse and foul language” (Sixth, there is another type of person who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, speaks harsh words): Their mouths always spit out unclean words, always accompanied by very dirty words. That is “rough and evil speech”. Or “slander the saints and sages” (blaspheme, curse the saints), which includes slandering the Buddha, slandering the True Dharma, defaming the Sangha, up to and including the sages. Among fellow Dharma friends, when someone else cultivates the Dharma, obstacles arise for him. In it, there is always a fight for profit. Competition for fame is also included. However, saying harsh words does not mean scolding others for no reason, it always has that meaning. If you utter these kinds of words, you will be without clothes. If you practice without clothes, you will be evil clothes (relying on evil), not good clothes.

“There are seven false people, one of the best, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, they have mixed language” (Seventh, there is a type of person who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, utter impure words): Even though they wish to cultivate Concentration, impure language is just false language (fabricated speech). “Stupid language” is talking without any meaning, it is also gossip, or gossip. During chatting, here it is called “corpse pulse”, [which means] like a grain, if the husk is stripped away, the true bran layer will appear. The word Pulse is very meaningful. But speaking words that have no meaning, are impure, and also interject impure words, impure words, false voices, uttering false words to deceive people. That's false language!

“The eight falsehoods are of the same type, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, they are always greedy” (The eighth is that there is a type of person who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, embraces greed and jealousy): Stingy, greedy, jealous. From here on out are the three things of greed, anger, and ignorance. That person himself is greedy, he himself cannot achieve it, but when he sees others have it, he becomes jealous. Seeing others being respected, being offered alms, or doing business, trading, or whatever they do, whenever they gain benefits, not only does that person not rejoice or feel joy, but they also become jealous. Due to jealousy, that person immediately destroys it. Regarding the benefits achieved by others, he does not have a heart of respect, does not have a heart of joy, but gives rise to jealousy and obstacles!

“Nine people, who are of the first type, although they desire to cultivate Concentration, are filled with anger and anger” (Nine are there types of people who, although they want to cultivate Concentration, hold anger and indignation): The mind is angry towards other sentient beings. That person always finds other people unsatisfactory. Or seeing someone else's actions makes that person feel itchy. Seeing someone else talking, that person is also dissatisfied. In their hearts there is anger. If there is anger, there will be anger. Anger: Anger is in the heart, anger is in the form. That appearance is clear. Towards all sentient beings, they often give rise to resentment. This has nothing to do with harmful relationships. For all sentient beings, that person, as we often say, is a “resentful, worldly” person (hates life, hates the world). Regarding this world, that person is extremely jealous and extremely greedy! Because that person has achieved nothing, he is jealous of what others have. Therefore, that person often has anger!

“There are ten types of people, who are of the same type, although they desire to practice Concentration, they still have wrong views” (Ten means there is a type of people who, although they want to practice Concentration, often embrace wrong views): Wrong views are ignorance, that is, ignorance in “greed, anger, and ignorance”. Stupidity, wrong views, not believing in cause and effect. Not believing in cause and effect, immediately rejects "there is no cause and effect". Do not believe that "doing good will result in good, doing evil will result in evil". Not believing in cause and effect, is "no cause and effect" (refuting there is no cause and effect).

“ Great Pham is fully aware! Name the ten strains of Non-Year Dharma. If one cultivates Concentration, one only depends on one's virtue, the upper one cannot attain the good roots of Desire Realm. The first stone becomes complete, the samsara retreats. Hdrinking has the potential to become Form, Formless Concentration, even the three vehicles, Depending on one's attainment of one vehicle?" (Great Brahma should know: These are called the ten types of Non-Conceptual Practices. If a person cultivating Concentration has any practice, he will not be able to achieve good roots in the Desire Realm. Even if he has achieved it in the past, he will immediately recede and be lost. Moreover, he can achieve the Samadhi of Form and Formless Precepts, up to the point of being able to achieve one of the three vehicles?): The Buddha again said to the Great Brahma Bodhisattva: - Mr. You should know: What I just said above is called "the ten types of Non-Importance Dharma". When practicing dharma, not following good dharma, but creating all kinds of bad karma, doing all evil karma, "not wearing clothes" means there is no good dharma to rely on. If you are a practitioner of Concentration, among those ten types, if you have any one of them, you hope to achieve good roots in the Desire Realm, be born as a god or human, gain blessings, become rich, and when reborn in the next life, you will live a very peaceful, very happy life. That is impossible to achieve!

Therefore, we live a very happy life, we should be grateful for our past! Praying for others is not as good as praying for yourself. In the past, you created good roots, so you will naturally enjoy it in this life. In the past, you have hurt others a lot, and in this life you will also be hurt a lot by others. In the past, you unintentionally hurt others without even knowing it. In this life, you will also be unintentionally hurt by others. Like the racing gang in Taiwan, the police chased them and asked why they did what they did? Why do they want to kill people? Is there any grudge against the person who was killed? Do you know each other or not? Not familiar! They themselves don't know why they have to do that! This is due to the great feeling of collective karma. That is not the karma of an individual!

We want to cultivate good roots to change past karma, how is it possible? [But] in this life, all that has been cultivated is Non Yi Hanh! What is Huu Y Hanh? In the following section it will be said. I can say a little in advance, like when we take refuge in the Three Jewels, we have received the Three Refuges and Five Precepts. To accept the Three Refuges and Five Precepts is to rely on good deeds, to have the robe, what is that robe? Relying on the Three Jewels, relying on the teachings in the Dharma spoken by the Buddha, believing in cause and effect, of course “existence”. If you have Y, not only can you achieve good roots, but you can also achieve the status of the three vehicles, and you can definitely become a Buddha!

But in a day, there are many contaminated minds, we must be “repent once we do it”. While repenting, while worshiping, you dedicate. Dedicating the wrong things that have been done in this life, giving rise to wrong thoughts, giving rise to incorrect ideas, the body performing improper actions, even breaking the precepts. If you break the precepts, you will repent at any time. Repent and you will be pure again. That means having something to rely on, relying on the method of repentance taught by the Buddha, relying on the Three Jewels to practice.

The Buddha had certain instructions, such as this sutra, which is to practice “retaining past thoughts” (maintaining the idea of coming and going). That is Huu Y, that is, relying on the Dharma to cultivate Concentration and practice the Ten Good Karmas. That is called the Obedient Clothing, which can achieve the three vehicles of path and fruition. It's not just these ten types of non-clothing; Below, there are also [other types].

(Sutra) Restore the Great Pham! There are ten types of Non-Yāhāna Dharma. Those who do not cultivate Concentration, depending on one's conduct, will not be able to become samadhis. Thiet Su Tien Thanh, Tam Hoan retreated. Ha class vi ten? One person, mocking his career. The second person, mocked the conversation first. Tam fake, mock before hypnosis. The four spectators mocked the ball in front of the stadium. Five fake people, mocking beauty. Green fake, mocked the wonderful voice. That fake, mocked before dividing the incense. The bowl is fake, mocking the delicious food. Nine people, mocking before offering sacrifices. The ten people mocked Tam Tu.
hạnh, sẽ trọn chẳng thể thành các tam-ma-địa. Giả sử đã thành tựu từ trước, sẽ liền lui sụt, mất đi. Những gì là mười? Một là ưa đắm sự nghiệp. Hai là ưa đắm đàm luận. Ba là ưa đắm ngủ nghê. Bốn là ưa đắm lo toan, mong cầu. Năm là ưa đắm sắc đẹp. Sáu là ưa đắm tiếng mầu nhiệm. Bảy là ưa đắm mùi thơm. Tám là ưa đắm mỹ vị. Chín là ưa đắm sự đụng chạm vi tế. Mười là ưa đắm Tầm Tứ).

The ten dharmas in the previous section are Sister Hanh. There are also ten dharmas. If you complete those ten dharmas, you hope to practice and attain the subjects of Concentration, the subjects of Concentration are a little deeper. Samadhi is samādhi, achieved in the past, but in this life, any of the ten types of Dharma of Non-Yāhāna will be let go, will also decline, decline, be lost, no longer exist. These ten types of nouns will be explained one by one in the following section.

(Sutra) Great Pham Dang Tri! Tenumerate the ten strains of Non-Year Dharma. Those who do not cultivate Concentration, depending on one's conduct, will not be able to become samadhis. Thiet Su Tien Thanh, Tam Hoan retreated. Weakness cannot become the sam-ma-grounds, even though we accumulate the accumulation of good dharmas, we have the right to do things, we seek to receive and receive the credit and giving of causes and conditions, giving rise to evil thoughts, the mind possesses the dharma, kings and great ministers, committing too many sins, or being insulted, or being insulted, or having the details and attachments cut off. Due to the fate of seeing people, either one becomes seriously ill, has a long life of suffering, or has a life-ending disability, the three evil beasts, depending on one's birth, one's will, or one is born in the Infinite hell, such as Ot-Dat Lac Ca, A La Do De Sa, Cu Ba Ly Ca, Devadatta... If you are destined to fall into the Intermittent Hell, you will experience countless hardships and great sufferings”.
(Sutra: Dai Pham should know: These are the ten types of Dharma of Non-Importance. If a person cultivating Concentration has any practice, he will not be able to achieve the samadhis. If he has already achieved it, he will immediately retreat. If he cannot achieve the samadhis, even though he practices other wholesome dharmas, there is this thing, [that is] pursuing the enjoyment of [the offerings] from others. The condition of giving, giving rise to evil thoughts and the mind of possessing dharma, is that kings, ministers, etc. commit sins, or are scolded, scolded, or beaten, or have their limbs cut off. Due to that cause, they either become seriously ill, suffer for a long time, or quickly die in one of the three evil destiniess, and can even be born in the Unending Hell, like Ot Dat Lac Ca, A La Do De Sa, Cu Ba Ly Ca, Devadatta. Nsuch people retreat from Tinh Lu, until they fall into the Vu Gian hell, suffering immeasurable great and unbearable suffering”).

“The Great Brahma is present!” (The Great Brahma should know): The Buddha told that Great Brahma again, speaking to him, because he is the one who is in power. If you practice Concentration and practice any of those ten types of Non-Conceptual Practices, you will not be able to achieve the samadhis, and wishing to achieve deep Concentration in the samadhis will not be possible. Not only is it impossible in the present life, but [what was achieved] in the past life “returns and retreats” (will immediately decline and be lost). “If you are unable to attain the samāma-grounds, even though you accumulate a surplus of good dharmas, you will be able to do things, pursue the use of faith and give causes and conditions, give rise to evil thoughts, mind possessing the dharma, kings and great ministers, commit excessive sins” (If you are unable to attain samāma-grounds, even though you practice other blocks of good dharmas, but this happens, [i.e.] seek to enjoy [the offerings] through the causes and conditions of faith.” alms giving, giving rise to evil mind, mind possessing dharma, in kings and great ministers, committing sins). “Committing crimes is too sinful” means not being able to practice Concentration, what about good dharmas? That is, talking about other blocks of good dharma. What is “Residual of good dharmas” (Other good dharmas) talking about? If we do not attain Concentration, then we chant sutras and do Buddha's work, that is also a good thing, that is also a “good dharma gathering”. Having these things, relying on those good things to pursue enjoyment. “The pursuit of enjoyment” is enjoyment. Receiving the karma of others' faith and giving is because someone believes in the Three Jewels and so gives alms and makes offerings.

Because there is that predestined cause, that person pursues it. “Pursuing” is to encourage [believers to make offerings], that is the meaning of “turning conditions” . When transforming conditions, sometimes you can achieve it, sometimes you can't! In that person's mind, evil thoughts arose. “Evil thoughts, mind, mind possesses dharma”: Mind possesses dharma [are psychological effects] that correspond to the mind, and also arise at the same time. “Mind” is the eight consciousnesses (eye consciousness, ear consciousness...), the mind possesses dharma including fifty-one items (such as desire, greed, preciousness, greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance...). But the mind that gives rise to evil thoughts and the corresponding afflictions of the mind, Anger, will both be present, those afflictions correspond to the mind and arise at the same time.

In this kingdom, in the place of kings, ministers, etc., that person will commit many mistakes because of pursuing enjoyment, because the mind is conditioned to follow the pursuit. If you pursue it, you will make many mistakes. If you make mistakes, you will be reprimanded by the king or minister, or beaten, or have your limbs and arms cut off. “Details” are also limbs. Either he was beaten and later became seriously ill, or he suffered for a long time, or he died because of that. After death, he will fall into three evil destiniess, depending on what he has done throughout his life, he will even fall into the Unintermittent Hell.

Here, the Buddha raises a number of cases. Like Udraka Rāmaputra, A La Tu De Sa (Ārāḍakālāma), and Cu Ba Ly Ca (Gopālika), those are the three heretical sects. Devadatta was the Buddha's cousin and Ananda's older brother. He committed the Five Disadvantages, causing the Buddha's body to bleed, disrupting the Sangha's harmony, and wanting to become a Buddha[53]. People like that, all withdraw from Tinh Lu, also lose Concentration. In the past there was [Concentration], until we practiced Tinh Lu, when we practiced Concentration, we not only retreated, but also fell into the Hell of No Intermittent, suffering countless great and unbearable sufferings. There are many sufferings, so it is said to be “difficult to endure great suffering” (great suffering that is difficult to endure).

You see the sufferings written in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, if we use the physical body to endure, there will be no way to endure it. If you think about that suffering, it will be unbearable. But once you've fallen, you don't have the strength to resist, you still have to accept it. Our bodies and minds are tormented, everything we have suffered in the past is forgotten. From countless lifetimes up to now, all of us have suffered, but we've all lost our minds and forgotten everything! If that realm appears again, perhaps the mind of cultivating the path will be able to achieve it a little faster. Having known suffering, I will not dare to create karma anymore! These pagans all practice pagan Dharma. Devadatta practiced the Dharma for twelve years, and when he first became a monk, he did very well. Later, he did not attain enlightenment, so he became resentful and sought out pagans to learn magical powers. Having learned magical powers, he then did evil things. That is withdrawal.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One reported to A Nha Da Kieu Tran Na saying: “Ngo-hearing class A Practicing the Dharma Concentration on the top of the room, the top crouching equipment, the top food, necessarily Increases the level of liberation. Is it true that those who practice Concentration, weaken the predestined karma, that is, they necessarily give rise to evil thoughts, the mind possesses the dharma, and are unable to achieve the samādhis, and will fall to the Infinite Hell, and receive countless seeds. Difficult and enduring great suffering".
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One told A Nha Da Kieu Tran Na (Kieu Tran Nhu) that: "I allow you to give the best rooms, the best bedding, the best food, to those who practice Concentration in A Luyen Nha, all monks should be exempted. Why is that? Those who practice Concentration, if they lack the supporting conditions, will immediately give rise to all evil thoughts and evil thoughts of all dharmas, unable to achieve the samadhis, until they fall into the Hell of No Intermittent, suffering countless great and unbearable sufferings).

Because cultivating Concentration, it is necessary to have enough causes and conditions, to fulfill all the merits, so the Buddha reiterated. When the Buddha first attained enlightenment, he went to Deer Park to take care of five monks. Kieu Tran Nhu (Ājñātakauṇḍinya, A Nha Da Kieu Tran Na) was the Supreme Master, the first monk to become a monk, this was the chief disciple of the Master. Buddha. He was the first monk to receive the precepts. The group of five monks, also known as the "five monks" who had previously followed the Buddha, practiced asceticism, and later saw the Buddha receiving the butter and milk offered by the girl. his mind of asceticism, he immediately left the Buddha and went to practice at Deer Park (Mrigadava, Isipatana). Deer Park was not far from Bodh Gaya (Buddha-gayā, Bodh Gaya). After the Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodhi Gaya, he went to Deer Park first, and preached the Dharma to them first Nha Da Kieu Tran Nhu is the top disciple, he manages all distribution.

Why did the Buddha have to talk to Kieu Tran Nhu? Because the rooms, bedding, food, and drinks were all arranged by Mr. Kieu Tran Nhu. The Buddha immediately told Venerable Kieu Tran Nhu: "I allow you to give that monk cultivating Concentration the best room, the best bedding, the best food. All the labor that belongs to the Sangha of that person should be exempted, so that he can practice Concentration with peace of mind." Why do that? “What's the reason?” (For what reason?) That's a meaningful question. Why do I have to allow you to treat people who practice Concentration like that, to take such good care of them? The Buddha told Kieu Tran Nhu: If people who practice Concentration do not have a good conscience and do not have a very good environment, they will give rise to evil thoughts. Although their malice is not very serious, they can hold grudges in their hearts, and when they practice Concentration, they will not be able to feel secure. That's what it means! Everyone may have experienced this type of situation.

When I was in Phong Son, the friends lived in thatched tents. There were times when everyone met each other, went to the place where they usually lived to receive their food, and picked up a small paper bag containing salt, [grieving]: "Usual residents are so stingy, give us a little salt! What should we do after 30 days? Only a little salt is given out like that in a month!" They say they often live in misery, without making offerings. At that time, we were in the North and distributed millet. If we distributed corn, it would help a little, but it would take a long time to starve, but millet could not alleviate hunger very much. How is millet porridge? Thirty kilos of millet, usually keep three kilos, three kilos less from thirty kilos, a total of twenty-seven kilos given to you. With that little bit of salt, you can take it back to your thatched tent. You can only cook thin porridge. Dinh practitioners don't need much food! I mean they resent it. When they don't have enough self-esteem, how can they practice? Therefore, fate will prevail.

At that time, we had not long been monks, we were not long-time practitioners, and had no fate. The monk has thought for a long time: "Some benefactor should take care of me, should give me gifts." If that person's mind thinks about that, how can he cultivate Concentration? The Buddha clearly understood the minds of sentient beings, clearly understood all things. Therefore, exempt them from all particularly good labor and care. If a person is especially good, can he practice or not? Neither way is possible, nor is it possible to grow a greedy mind!

In Hebei province, there was a venerable monk who wanted to make offerings to Zen practitioners. Whatever the calm person wants, he gives it. There were people who came to the place where they usually stayed and asked for the best felt blankets, and he also bought them for them. Asked for the most luxurious watch, he bought it for me. Furthermore, in every house there was a thermos of hot water, which was a very high class at that time! He hoped that the people there would practice Concentration, put a thermos of hot water in each house, and buy one for each person. [Concentration practitioners] feel unwell and want to eat banh cuc. In the North, eating banh coc[54] is very luxurious. He then followed his instructions and cooked banh coc. After that, do people who practice Zen practice practice well or not? Not at all! In the end, his blessings were not enough, the Zen practitioners gradually left, leaving not a single person left! He also closed that ashram! At that time, it was the year one thousand nine hundred and thirty-something, about thirty-five, thirty-six, thirty-seven. Roughly less than three years have ended!

Too much suffering is not possible, nor is it possible to be too happy. Too happy, they get carried away. Suffering, they will resent. However, private conditions (conditions that help the practice of Concentration) are indispensable. Otherwise, it will lead to evil thoughts arising. However, if the fate is especially good, especially convenient, that person's evil intentions will also be established! Being greedy and predestined, that person cannot be determined, nor can he cultivate! Therefore, it is impossible to achieve samadhi, and even falls into the Hell of No Intermittent, suffering countless great and unbearable suffering!

(Sutra) Cultivation Practitioner, disadvantages predestined conditions, all samadhi positions can be achieved. If the weak immortals succeed, they will never retreat. Due to the trial of not arising necessarily evil dharma, spreading the thought of non-virtuous thinking, rebirth in heaven, attaining Nirvana. The practitioner of Concentration, the weak one, achieves all the samāma-grounds, the early night, the late night, while letting go of sleep and torpor, diligently cultivating, far from chaos, with few desires and contentment, without any attachment. It is necessary to be greedy, angry, angry, rich, angry, harmful, arrogant, arrogance, arrogance, deceitful, jealous, disloyal, cruel, vain, impure, necessarily hypocritical and promiscuous in the world, and must be far away. Such a practitioner who accepts Thich, Pham, the protector of the four kings, the Wheel-Turning King, praises, worships, respects, serves, and serves hundreds of na-du-da offerings, not to mention the Kshatriya, Brahman, Phiet-xa, and Thu-datta-la. The person who has attained Samadhi, the upper eagle receives praise, worships, respectfully acknowledges, serves, makes offerings, not to mention the attainment of sam-ma-ground (samadhi)!" At that time, the World-Honored One recited and wrote: "Practicing the power of Concentration to cut off Obstacles, the residual karma is ineffective, try to practice Concentration to become a respected person, the wise person accepts offerings."
(Sutra: If a practitioner practices Concentration, if there are enough supporting conditions, the samadhi subjects that have not yet been achieved will be able to be achieved. If the subjects of Concentration have been achieved before, they will not completely retreat. Therefore, all evil dharmas will not arise. In general, there will be no Samadhi, the four unwholesome thoughts, will be born in the heavens, attain Nirvana. A practitioner who practices Concentration has not yet achieved the qualities. Samadhi, at the beginning of the night, at the end of the night, you should give up sleep and practice diligently, stay away from noise and bustle, have little desire, know enough, and have no regrets. All greed, anger, resentment, concealment, harm, arrogance, arrogance, arrogance, stinginess, jealousy, gossip, harsh speech, lies, impurity, all the frivolous fun of the world should all be far away from the Buddha. The King of Brahma, the four protecting heavenly kings, the Wheel-turning King, etc. praised, worshiped, respected, served, and offered hundreds of thousands of offerings, not to mention the Kshatriyas, Brahmins, Bodhisattvas, Thudattas, etc. People who have not yet attained Samadhi are worthy of their praise, worship, respect, and service, not to mention people who have attained Samadhi! Then he spoke verses and chanted: "Practicing Concentration to eliminate Or, other karmas are impossible. You should practice noble Concentration. Wise people should make offerings").

A practitioner of Concentration must definitely fulfill all supporting conditions. At that time, it is possible to achieve the unaccomplished samadhi. If [the samāma-grounds] have been established before, that is, if they have been accomplished, they will increase further and will not retreat. Then, thanks to the power of Concentration, the mind can be subdued and all evil will not arise. “Advertisement on the unwholesome Samsara, Tu” (Broadly speaking, up to the unwholesome Samsara and Tua): Samsara means “pursuing”, [here, the text means] “no longer pursuing”. In this way, you can be born in heaven, attain Nirvana, and even more successfully practice. Either practice the Four Meditations, Four Concentrations, or the Four Emptiness and Four Concentrations, you will be able to be born in heaven, even penetrate and practice the samadhis, until finally attaining Nirvana, until attaining and achieving the fruits of the three vehicles.

This is the Buddha praising the practice of Concentration. In the world, when practicing, there are three types: The first type is practicing Concentration, the second type is practicing reading and reciting, the third type is cultivating blessings. A practitioner of Concentration is a practitioner, a practitioner of religion. Concentration is “Tinh Lu, tranquility”. When cultivating cause, it is cultivating tranquility, cultivating Tranquility, cultivating Contemplation. Later, when accomplished, one reaches samadhi. Sanma-dia in the previous section said a lot. Dang Tri translates as Tinh Tinh. People who practice Concentration should do the work of preparing their thoughts so that when they practice, it will be easy for them to attain enlightenment. There are things you need to pay attention to, which means you should pay attention to external circumstances and objective situations.

If you have not yet achieved samadhi, that is, before you have attained Concentration, you will have to work a little hard. At the beginning of the night, at the end of the night, when you have not yet succeeded, you should endure a little bit. If you calculate at the beginning of the night, using the current twelve hours to calculate, you can rest for four hours in the middle of the night. During the eight hours at the beginning and end of the night, you must always practice diligently, and don't be too greedy for sleep. “Let go of sleep” (You should stop sleeping), four hours is not enough. Here we are talking about people who are truly determined to end life and death, hoping to end afflictions. Such people who practice will truly believe and admire the Buddha's teachings. I must emphasize: That faith is absolutely not our ordinary faith, but truly deep, unchanging faith. If you believe in the Buddha's teachings, what the Buddha taught us to do, we will do exactly that. Only then can one enter the Dharma. Currently, we all claim to believe in Buddha, but I personally feel it's still not enough! We absolutely cannot spend twenty-four hours every day, only sleep for four hours, and practice the Dharma in the remaining twenty hours, right? Like us monastics, that is, monks and nuns, we are "professionals", professional but we can't do it, but like everyone who studies Buddhism, practicing is a side job, not a professional at all [what else can be said]!

Everyone knows: After we became monks, there were morning and evening sessions. We had to wake up at half past two in the morning. Every temple wakes up at two and a half hours. According to this regulation, you must wake up at 2:30 a.m. when you come to apply for a petition (join the permanent order) at any temple or pagoda. It contains a lot of meaning. In the past, in Mainland China, there was no dinner in temples. They called [eating to relieve hunger in the evening] “medicine stone” , which also means “taking medicine”. Currently, the body in the Mat era is not as healthy as the ancients in the past, so they have to take medicine. Consider dinner as medicine, but the usual rule in pagodas and temples [in the past], that medicine was porridge eaten with melon. If you want to eat then eat, if you don't want to eat then don't!

Currently, of course that is not the case. If everyone goes to the temple to have dinner, the food will still be delicious. There are young monks who even go to the snack shops outside, just like the ones outside our temple, which are all small shops! So how can we practice religion? Only sow good roots! If you really practice, you should not be too greedy for sleep, sleep is a thing. Let's calculate how much time we spend sleeping during our lifetime? Takes up a lot of time! But there are people who have to work overtime because of business or work, sometimes to make money, and also sleep very little. So it's not relevant, here, we're talking about practitioners. If you want to practice Concentration, be diligent, don't be lazy! Sleeping is relaxing. Don't waste the good times!

There are Dharma friends who have made a wish to live in the mountains, or there are many

Dharma friends or lay people who want to learn from ancient virtues, without sleeping, there are many people like that. There are even people who do not eat, take one or two meals, and focus their time on cultivating the Way, with the goal of attaining Concentration. What are the benefits of Dac Dinh? Everyone knows: Once you attain Concentration, you will be able to unlock wisdom. When you are in Concentration, you understand everything. Like the Arhats, if you invite them to dedicate, when they have not yet entered Samadhi, it will not be much different from us. Only when they enter Concentration, start contemplation, and wisdom is present, they can know. They gave up their retribution, then entered samāma-ground, realizing the Non-reason.

Therefore, when you have not successfully cultivated Concentration, you must give up sleep and rest, and must practice diligently. What are you studying? To learn Meditation, you must practice Concentration, but if you live in the city you won't be able to practice! Traffic disturbs you, making it difficult for you to enter Concentration. Noisy people's voices can't enter Concentration. Noisy place will not be possible! “Less desires and contentment” (Less desires, knowing enough): Satisfied people are often happy, don't want too much! Because our mind is too greedy, we do not realize that our body is illusory, do not recognize that the body is impermanent, always let the body be comfortable, [only thinking] about how to regulate the body, how to be leisurely and satisfied. Many desires are not enough, many people cannot be satisfied! There are times when poor people see rich people and feel very strange: "They have so much money, can they eat it all in their lifetime?" The rich see the poor and say: "You don't cultivate merit, you deserve to suffer. You are poor, that's what you deserve!"

This is teaching us to have few desires and be content, like the great monks who live in the mountains with great blessings, but they all let go, only then can they be happy. Knowing enough will often be fun. People with few desires are at peace. If you have few desires, then you can be at peace. Without asking, you won't hurt anyone. Therefore, it is necessary to have few desires and be content, and not to be attached. Attachment means attachment. Regarding all things in the world, speaking from our side, eating, wearing, living, traveling, as long as "eating, wearing, living" can be replaced, we should not be attached to it. Regarding greed, anger, anger, wealth, depravity, pride, arrogance, arrogance, stinginess, jealousy, separation, cruelty, deceit, impurity, you must have enough love, compassion, joy, and equanimity to counteract greed, anger, ignorance, and love. Attachment means greed and anger, and when you are not satisfied, troubles arise. Anger is an angry mind.

Those are the three basic sins, that is, greed, anger, and ignorance. Ignorance means there is no wisdom. Arrogance: Everyone thinks like this: "I am an ordinary person, what is there to be arrogant about?" But actually, that's not the case. Each person, when thinking about their peers or colleagues, always feels that they are better than them. Arrogance, simply put, is arrogance and complacency, but more broadly, it is arrogance and arrogance. Too many arrogant things to show off: Not understanding but pretending to understand, not knowing but pretending to know it all. Obviously it's not that good, but I still feel like I'm terrible! Why do we combine pride and arrogance? “Man” here means arrogant.

Are poor people arrogant? The poor are more arrogant! They feel very noble, especially the educated ones. In the past, it was “the same baccalaureate” (the miserable poor baccalaureate), now they are those who have graduated from university. Currently, graduating from university is still inferior, one must have a PhD or Master's degree! I remember twenty years ago, when I was in Shanghai, Dr. In Beijing, there are not many Doctors. I met two PhD students returning from America. A person studying Agriculture from Khang Nai Nhi School (Cornell), he is a university professor, so arrogant! He was arrested and thrown into prison, always thinking he was superior to others: "I am a Doctor in prison." I said: "I am a monk in prison!" He asked me to keep him company, always feeling arrogant. No matter where he went, he always showed his arrogance. At any time, he always [thought himself] better than others. Afraid of falling into hell, he still felt that only he was qualified to fall into hell! If you don't have that karma, you won't be able to get there! Like when I was in prison, I spent too long in prison and had contact with a lot of prisoners. There, among the prisoners, they also think that I am stronger than you criminals! Everyone has that expression. That is the Sentence of Self Attachment (inborn ego attachment). This is very intense, because we always think we are better than others. No matter how ugly a female friend is, she thinks she is very beautiful, always looking in the mirror and always applying makeup. Why? Arrogant, arrogant!

“Xan” means greedy, very stingy, the mind of letting go is not heavy! What do we mean by Equanimity? It is almsgiving and giving in “love, compassion, joy, letting go”. To let go, you have to let go from within your own mind, not just material things. Except for external material, first of all, we must let go of the mind. If your mind is pure and equanimous, you will succeed. Without greed and greed, it will change into almsgiving, compassion, and forgiveness. What about jealousy? This has even more meaning. Jealous of other people's good things! If it is related to good and harm, then jealousy can be explained, but this has nothing to do with that person! As long as there are a few people, whenever they talk about the good things of others, people praise that person, then that person immediately spits destructive words: "What the hell is he? What's so terrible about him?" That's jealousy. There are a lot of things like this, at any time, anywhere, you can encounter them!

Of the ten great vows of Samantabhadra's Vows, the fifth great vow is “rejoicing in merit”: Seeing others do good things, you must praise them. Compliment and rejoice, and half of that person's good deeds will be shared with you! We must always rejoice in the merits of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, everyone knows that he has great vows to go to hell to save sentient beings. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's vow power is also very great. He has twelve great vows. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva has ten great vows, Manjushri Bodhisattva has ten great vows, we all rejoice. If you are happy, you will receive a portion. When we see others doing good things, we don't have the strength to do the same, so we just rejoice. Depending on the person's happiness, when they meet, they will be divided in half. Chinese people [like to say] "when we meet, I share half", but Buddhism does not focus on material things, I rejoice as I please, nor do I harm what is available to others, that is rejoicing according to merit. That way you can eliminate jealousy.

“Separation from cockroaches, cruelty”, “separation from cockroaches” are the sparks of separation from cockroaches. If you see someone else succeeding, the [dissociative] person will sabotage you. There are also double-tongued words (two-way talk), insults and philandering. As mentioned in the above section, greed, anger, anger, wealth, anger, arrogance, arrogance, and all kinds of cruelty are all false, impure, and impure. Not only are those things thrown away, but even the fun and indulgent things in the human world are all far away. Like watching TV at home, does it count as fun? Depends on how you view it. If you are a person who develops the mind, a person cultivating the path, when in that situation, it depends on how you use your mind? Can you maintain concentration or not? If you can concentrate, even if you have fun, it will turn into diligence; Having fun and letting go all turn into diligence. “Na Gia is always in Concentration” (The World-Honored One is always in Concentration). Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas do all things according to sentient beings, they are always in Concentration. These things all turn into diligence. If we can't do it, if we don't have that concentration, it's best to stay away and reflect on ourselves.

There are people who often make excuses: "I'm not being promiscuous! I'm cultivating my religion!" That's fooling yourself! If we cannot practice for twenty-four hours, then is ten hours possible? Can't do it! Is five o'clock possible? Can't do it at all! Is two hours okay? Still can't do it! Is an hour okay? Still can't do it! So in the morning and evening, when you are about to sleep, when you are about to wake up, recite ten times “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, I am afraid this still cannot be done! Or a little more, reciting "the one, paying homage to the Buddhas. The two, praising the Tathagata" up to "the ten, universal dedication", reciting the ten great vows of Samantabhadra Great Vow King, is that okay? If you can't remember those vows, recite the holy name Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, but we still have the habit of reciting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva more. If you recite a few dozen sentences, you'll probably be able to do it! Whatever you do, just recite a dozen sentences and you will be able to do it!

Doing so will be able to cure many afflictions, little by little, although the time is very little, the benefits are extremely great. Normally, good roots are shallow, like your Dharma friends who often come to listen to sutras, listen for an hour or two, listen to the writing, or listen to the language of a certain magician, can it reach your mind or not? Use the Ear Organ to listen, listen and then turn back to the Hearing to hear your own nature, combining it with your mind nature. It seems that we violate all the things the Buddha said, so we do not attain Concentration. How to do this? After we know, we should gradually distance ourselves!

On the other hand, if there is greed, anger, anger, wealth, even deceit, impurity, all playing around and letting go, is not good. If it's not good, you have to leave. If it's good, you have to be diligent and do it. “Such a practitioner” (Such a practitioner), is also a practitioner of the Dharma, a person cultivating Concentration, of course not necessarily a monk, [but can be] Dharma friends, Upasakas, Upasikas, all lay people, whenever you practice Concentration you must do like this: In a quiet place to practice the Dharma, be diligent, reduce sleep and rest, you are not greedy, not angry, not ignorant, not stingy, Be greedy, not jealous, not self-indulgent, what should you achieve? May the Great Brahma King protect you. There are also the Four Heavenly Kings, or the Wheel-Turning Kings in the human world. As well as the king, they will all praise, respect, worship, and serve you. Even for that person who cultivates Concentration, that is, the person who practices that path, he will give away hundreds of thousands of alms and offerings of that much, which also means making a lot of offerings.

A person of the Kshatriya nature, or the Brahmin nature, up to Phiet-xa, Thu-datta-la, i.e. a person of those four types of nature, when they are practicing Concentration, even though they have not yet attained Concentration, they are still practitioners, they can all accept the praise of the King of Brahma, Indra, and the Four Heavenly Kings. to praise, worship, respect, acknowledge, and make offerings. If one has attained Samadhi, one has achieved Concentration practice, one has attained Samadhi, one has attained Samadhi, one will receive offerings that are even more inconceivable. It must be said in two aspects, related to the good roots in many lives in the past of that person.

For example, in India, there are Arhats who have attained the Four Fruits of Arhat, not only cultivating Concentration, but also attaining samadhi, attaining Emptiness, and achieving freedom. Why do they hold alms bowls but still cannot ask? At that time, someone asked the World-Honored One that way. The Buddha said it was because in many past lives, that person had rarely given alms. Although we have achieved success in the Hue aspect, we have very little in the Phuoc aspect. There is a saying in India: “Cultivating wisdom, not cultivating blessings, Arhats are empty of bowls” (Cultivating wisdom, not cultivating blessings, Arhats holding empty bowls), cannot beg for alms. “Cultivate blessings, don't cultivate wisdom, the fragrance will bring you happiness” (Practice blessings, don't cultivate wisdom, the fragrant elephant will bring you happiness). The king rides that big elephant, [the servant] wears jewels and pearls to adorn [the elephant's body]. It is cultivating merit, not cultivating wisdom, falling into the animal path of birth. Arhat cultivates wisdom, does not cultivate merit, holds an empty bowl, nor will he forever hold an empty bowl. Sometimes there are times when there is nothing to beg for alms. Therefore, know that in all things, whether in the internal religion or in the external realm, do not worry about trivial matters. There are people who like to ask these things, like to spin empty words: "I don't practice Concentration, I still get offerings." Or so you say! [Not knowing] the offering is due to your blessings, not due to the growth of wisdom. Here, the Buddha encourages and encourages people to practice Concentration.

The Buddha's teachings were all about giving sentient beings a little sweetness, so when Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha blessed us, [making it] possible for us to gain a lot of benefits, only then did they accept it. Pham Pho Mon says: Reciting the holy name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will be greatly blessed. Avoiding many accidents is like being blessed! Nowadays, if you say No to sentient beings, [they will be surprised]: "No? Then why should I believe?" They did not believe it, because they had interpreted it wrongly. You must have reached a certain level to speak at that level, that's what it means! Therefore, the World-Honored One used verses to express the above meanings. Why say so? Because people who practice Concentration can cut off Or. Or it means “deluded”, not understanding clearly, not having right knowledge, right view. Arousing greed, anger, ignorance, arousing anger, wealth, and harm, there is no power of Concentration. Once a person becomes greedy, he will not be able to concentrate and will be turned around. Because the mind is changed, it falls down. If there is concentration, the mind can change situations. The mind can change states, which means it is similar to the Tathagata.

Although the Buddha spoke of three methods, namely cultivating Concentration, reading and reciting the Mahayana, and cultivating blessings, among those three methods, only cultivating Concentration is the best. “Practicing Concentration can stop Or, other karmas cannot”. If you practice other dharmas, do not practice Concentration, but hope to eliminate Ordain, it will be very difficult. Therefore, “trying to cultivate Concentration is noble” (so cultivating Concentration is noble), most worthy of respect, most worthy of respect. Therefore, cultivating Concentration is the best. “Wise people are willing to make offerings” [meaning] people with wisdom should do that, make offerings, serve!

(Sutra) Ear time, Thien Store Maha Brahma words:
(Sutra: At that time, the Brahma Pitaka said: “World-Honored One, for those who have become monks in Buddhism, if Kshatriya, a minister, a prime minister, uses whips, sticks, etc. to beat them, torture them, or detain them in prison, or reprimands, curses, or cuts off their limbs, or ends their lives, is it appropriate or not? Or not appropriate?”)

This is specifically about monks. The Great Brahma King praised the Buddha as “Venerable World-Honored One”. For those who are ordained in Buddhism, “ordained” refers to monks and bhikshunis. To become a monk is to leave the secular world and enter the Buddhist world. For a monk who has become a monk, if the king Sat-de-li, or the king's minister, or prime minister are powerful and powerful people, use a whip or stick to beat the body of the monk, punishing the monk. Either put that person in prison, or scold and reprimand him. Or cutting off the limbs, "detailed explanation" means cutting off the limbs, that is, cutting off the hands, feet, arms, calves, or cutting off that person's life, up to death. To put it in the current way it would be

shoot to kill!

Is that correct or not? Is it appropriate or not? Or is it not true? There is such a question. In this question, many meanings are involved.
