It was extremely difficult for a monk during the Dharma Ending period to become a monk, and to practice the Dharma was even more difficult. During the Dharma-Ending Age, it was very difficult for people to believe in Buddha, and they did not even have faith. There are many people who don't believe, or believe, then move forward and back down. One time, I returned to Nam Pho Da Pagoda. Everyone knows that in Taiwan there is a Bhikkhunī who first assumed the title of Bhikkhunī, then returned to the lay life. She went to Mainland, advertised and solicited everywhere. People who became monks in temples naturally studied with her and thought she was very outstanding. After that, the religious department chased her away, an action that scared the monastics who studied with her and fled back to their hometown to hide. There is nothing left now. [Those monastics] are about to graduate from the Buddhist Institute, have studied Buddhism for several years, why are they still fascinated like that? If you are someone who rarely listens to Buddhism, encounter this type of heresy, encounter the so-called “magical powers”, often boasted as “opening the heavenly eye”, or “opening the third eye”, seeing this, seeing that, immediately consider it trustworthy. Currently, this situation is very common in Taiwan.

Regarding the Three Jewels, that is, Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, you must rather sacrifice your life and life than blaspheme the Three Jewels. Only by having that kind of faith can you maintain your faith. Your faith must "take root", must have strength. When you believe, you must believe to the point where Remembrance does not retreat, until you must practice Concentration so that Concentration does not retreat, and you must practice Hue so that Hue does not retreat. That is talking about the first step, that faith is not something you cultivate, but what can [help practitioners] reach the goal is that faith. Have such faith. With wisdom, you will be able to clearly distinguish between right and wrong. If you have the power of concentration, you will not be moved. Whatever others say, you will consider based on teachings. [Compare between] that person's Concentration and the Concentration taught by the Buddha, which is the Four Meditations and Eight Concentrations, even like “retention of thoughts of coming and going” (holding firmly to the idea of ​​coming and going) mentioned in this sutra, does it have that kind of power or not? As for seeing ghosts and spirits, the Ksitigarbha Sutra says it very clearly!

If you have any questions, use Ksitigarbha's Contemplation of the Wheel to ask about your own karma, to contemplate your own karma. That person is either a reincarnated fox, or a reincarnated weasel or civet, or [someone] who has supernatural powers due to retribution. In every country, there are people like that who control it. Their eyes can see thousands of meters underground, can see good and bad things in the future, and can make all kinds of predictions. They still belong to life and death, there is nothing wrong with them! You should not believe them, you must have full right knowledge and right view. When it comes to "right knowledge, right view", you can test it: Does that person say "all dharmas are selfless" or not? Is it possible to contemplate “all dharmas are impermanent”, to contemplate “all dharmas are suffering”, to contemplate “all dharmas are empty”? Is it possible to meditate like that? Is it possible to contemplate the body as impure, to contemplate feelings as suffering, to contemplate the impermanence of the mind, and to contemplate the non-self of dharmas? You use the dharma seal, use the dharma teachings taught by the Buddha to confirm once, and you will clearly distinguish! You must fully understand whether that person is right or not, you must have all that wisdom. Otherwise, it will be difficult to practice the Dharma in the last life, and it will be even more difficult to become a monk.

Dharma Ending Period, at the time when the five desires were burning hot, human desires were seething. What do you see in this world, what shape is society in today? If at this time, you can practice for a year, I think it will be much better than practicing for one lifetime in the Pure Land. In the Pure Land, no one bothers you, you are not so wrong. Who do you give alms to? Pure gold? Everywhere are precious gems, agates, and jewels. Trees are also made of precious substances, everything is made of precious substances. No one is greedy, too much, no more greed! When I chat with someone, that person says: "In this world, gold is the most precious." I say: "Not sure!" That person asked: "What did you say is the most precious thing?" I replied: “It's still the most precious plain rice or first grain That person laughed and said: "How much rice can one or two coins buy!" I said: "In normal times, if rice is available, it's not worth the money. If it's during a flood, you give them ten taels of gold for your head, and they won't sell it to you." When the country is in chaos, there will be chaos if there is no food, and there will be chaos if there is no clothing. Having gold or not, it doesn't matter at all.

There is a story like this: When the Yellow River caused a big flood, two people sought refuge. A refugee carries a bag of gold. There was a person carrying a bunch of heads. The person carrying the head is light, so he climbs the tree. The man carrying gold also climbed the tree. They are on that tree. Later, both of them were hungry. The one who brought the gold said: "I will give you a piece of gold in exchange for a head, is that okay?" The bold person thinks: "This kind of trading is really profitable, okay, let me sell you one." Giving him a tip, he immediately gave him a piece of gold. The water did not recede, so he used gold to buy the top at any time. The water still hasn't receded. The person carrying the other side sold all the other side to the person carrying the gold. He thought the water would recede very quickly, but the water still did not recede. The person who puts his head on the line thinks to himself: "When the water recedes, I will make a fortune." The one who brought the head said to the one carrying the gold: "Take this gold back so I can exchange it for the head." The person carrying the gold replied: "I have eaten all my first food, there is no more!" In fact, he still had eight or nine heads left, which he kept himself. Those who put their heads on the line will starve to death. The one who carries the gold survives because he has a head. The one who carried the money had already starved to death, but the one who carried the gold would exchange it for such gold! This story sounds like a joke at first. You say: What is the most precious thing? I say, the most precious thing is wisdom. When he escaped, it was right that he took his head with him, because there was nothing else in the house, nor any gold. But at that time, he didn't think what he needed money for? Can money be used? The greedy mind will not arise!

At that time, the king and his ministers did not trust the Three Jewels. You probably think that King Sat-di-li and his ministers and prime ministers all have blessings, so why do they not respect the Three Jewels and have no faith? Why do you still treat monks that way? Cursing, beating, cutting limbs? If you don't believe it, everyone should open your eyes and look, whether in Taiwan, or in Mainland China, even in America, people simply don't understand that you are a monk, and simply don't care! Do they understand those things? Coming to India, there are currently almost no Buddhist monks! Although it is said that India still has monks, but when they come to Mahabodhi Temple, those monks are probably from Tu Ly Lam Kha (Ceylon, Sri Lanka), but there are no Indians themselves. There are also temples, currently there are Tibetan lamas coming to practice there, but the Indian Buddhist temples have all been destroyed. This type of situation was common during the Dharma Ending period. Therefore, I often say: The Mahabodhi Sutra of the Ten Wheels is truly a photograph of the Dharma-Ending Age, photographed for us. Everyone, let's see if this is the current situation or not? There are still religious believers, although they are not monks, they believe in the teachings, always do good deeds, and do good things for others. So is it possible or not, true or not?

(Sutra) Buddha's report to the Thien Store Maha Brahma said: - Good man! Weak sentient beings, in the middle of the Dharma of the ego, have become a monk, except for the development of the world, have broken the ca-sa, weakly maintained the precepts, weakly broken the precepts, the lower will has no precepts, necessarily heaven, human, A To Lac class, following the traditional Dharma, due to the above unsuitable immortals, truong class daggers to examine the body, or close the prison, or serve the curse, or explain in detail, or cut off the life, not to mention the illegal practice! Why try? Except for the time when he strictly observes the precepts, is well-educated, is a monk in the middle of the Dharma, is weak and breaks the precepts, practices evil dharmas, is internally corrupted, is like a dirty oa loa, is truly not a monk, claims to be a monk, is truly not a virtuous person, claims to be a virtuous person, always claiming that the race of afflictions prevails, destruction leads to happiness. Such as breaking the precepts of all evil beings, due to their ability to show the path of all heavens, dragons, Duoc Xoa, Kien Dat Phuoc, A To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, humans and non-humans, immeasurable merits are treasured treasures.
(Sutra: The Buddha told the Maha Brahma Pitaka: - Good man! If sentient beings become monks, In my Dharma, even if you shave off your beard and hair, wear a kasaya, or keep the precepts, or break the precepts, even without the precepts, all gods, humans, A To Lac, etc., should rely on the secular Dharma, you should not use whips, sticks, etc. to beat them, torture them, or put them in prison, or reprimand them, curse them, or cut off their limbs, or cut off their lives, let alone those who follow the Dharma illegally Those who uphold the precepts, are well-educated, and become monks in my dharma, if there are those who break the precepts, practice evil dharmas, and are corrupt in their hearts, like dirty snails, are really not monks but claim to be monks, are really not virtuous, claim to be virtuous, and are always controlled, corrupted, and overthrown by all kinds of afflictions.

Such evil virtuous beings who break the precepts can still teach countless treasures of merit and virtue to all gods, dragons, Yak Xoa, Kien Dat Phuoc, A To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, non-human beings, etc.)

This Great Brahma Storehouse has wisdom, so ask the truth

like that. Therefore, the Buddha told Thien Treasury Maha Brahma: "Good man! If sentient beings leave the Dharma in the middle of the Dharma and become a monk, except for the development of the world, they will be banished by ca-sa" (Hey good man! If there are sentient beings who become monks in my Dharma, even if they shave off their beard and hair, and wear a piece of ka-sa): Very few! There is only one small piece, which means attaching a piece of ca-sa on the outfit. “Weakness in keeping the precepts, weak in breaking the precepts” [means] after becoming a monk, keeping the precepts very strictly, keeping the precepts without violating them, keeping the precepts pure; or after becoming a monk, he breaks the precepts. “Summer solstice without precepts”: There are people who destroy all the precepts they have taken.

“All gods and humans, A To Lac level, following the conventional Dharma, due to the above unconformable immortals, staff level daggers to examine the body, or shut up prison, or subdue insults, or explain details, or end life. In any case, it is illegal!” (All gods, humans, A To Lac, etc. Obeying the secular Dharma, you should not even use whips, sticks, etc. to beat them, torture them, or put them in prison, or reprimand them, curse them, or cut off their limbs, or cut off their lives, let alone those who follow the illegal law!): This is obeying the secular Dharma, that is, if you kill someone, you have to pay for your life, if you owe a debt, you have to pay, and if you steal from others, you will be in prison. If you are imprisoned or punished, it is also according to the laws of the world and must be punished. Before the law, everyone is equal, and monastics are no exceptions!

From the Tang - Song dynasties until now, every dynasty has one. Even great men like old man Tu Bach[56] died in prison, Master Ham Son was drafted into the army (exiled as a soldier), and also served time in prison. During the Ming Dynasty, the Queen Mother believed in Buddhism very much [but King Minh Than Tong believed in Taoism, listened to slander and harmed monks], this type of phenomenon often happened. Emperor Thai Tong was an emperor during his reign but also killed many monks. Therefore, the emperor cannot avoid creating this karma. If he follows the secular Dharma, he will make mistakes. He should not use whips or sticks to beat the body of Bhikkhus, or imprison them in prison, or curse them, or cut off their limbs, or end their lives. “Ha co co?”: Why say that? “Except for those who absolutely maintain the precepts, are well-educated, and are monks in the middle dharma” (Except for all those who maintain the precepts, are well-educated, and become monks in my dharma): Those who maintain the precepts, are well-educated, and have morality do not need to be said. If there are people who break the precepts, practice evil dharma, and have a rotten heart, even though they appear to be monks, they do not really practice, do not practice, and do not practice. Breaking the precepts means practicing evil, greed, anger, and ignorance as mentioned above, all of which are complete.

“Noi Noi corrupt” (Rotten heart): Dirty, like a loaa, that is, a snail. This species is sometimes called “oa tuu”. Snail withdraws into its shell. “Loa tu” (stuffed snail) has a shell to protect its body, but inside it is very dirty, it eats and excretes right there, very dirty. Those who create karma fall into that species. Therefore, someone who breaks the precepts and practices evil deeds is like a stuffed snail, or a snail. Although they wear kasa and have become monks, they are not monks. They say they are monks, they call themselves monks, they call themselves monks. “It's really not holy” (It's really not holy), what they did was not pure. That person himself says it is pure conduct, but is always overcome by all kinds of afflictions. Defilements prevail over good karma, evil karma trumps that person's good karma. “Destroying the tendency to happiness” (Corrupted, reversed): Both the Brahma conduct and the pure conduct of that person are corrupted. All Buddhist sects were corrupted by that person. An evil Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts like that can still create merit for gods and humans.

“Due to the ability to teach the path of almighty heaven, dragon, Duoc Xoa, Kien Dat Phuoc, A To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, people and non-human beings, immeasurable merits are treasured and preserved” (Still able to teach countless treasures of precious merit to all heaven, dragon, Yoc Xa, Kien Dat Phuoc, A To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, non-human beings, etc.): As long as that person is a disciple of Buddha, as long as that person still wears a piece of ka-sa, he will be able to teach the eight classes of ghosts and gods.

In India, there was a man who lived in the grave. He saw an evil dragon. He was originally a beggar who begged along the road. In that grave, there was [the body] of a monk who had passed away. After that, the ca-sa was torn and a piece fell out. The beggar quickly covered his head with that piece of clothing, but the evil dragon did not eat him and passed by. This story shows that, even though he is an evil Bhikkhu, wearing a ka-sa can still teach the eight classes of ghosts and spirits, because the piece of ka-sa contains countless precious treasures of merit and virtue. It's not because of that person at all, but because of that person's piece of clothing. That is called the Three Jewels of Nature.

(Sutra) Good man! In the middle of the dharma, the monk who has become a monk, even though he breaks the precepts, sentient beings fall into strange forms, but gives birth to the ten sublime thoughts, gathering countless merits and treasures. Ha class vi ten? In the middle of the dharma,a person who has become a monk, even though he breaks the precepts, even if he is a sentient being, or a sentient being has the right to view it, he will be born with recitation of the Buddha's name with great respect, faith and respect will prevail in his thoughts. Because of the predestined relationship, everyone can not trust the external teachers, commentaries, disciples, and even enter the great Nirvana.
(Sutra: Again, good man! People who become monks in my dharma break the precepts, but sentient beings see Their appearance will give rise to ten types of superior thoughts, and they will gain countless treasures of merit. What are the ten? That is, although people who become monks in my Dharma break the precepts, sentient beings, if they have seen them, will have superior thoughts and think of the Buddha, and because of that cause, they will not turn to and believe in non-Buddhist teachers, books, treatises, and their followers, until they can enter the city of Nirvana, away from the teachings. scared).

Seeing that ca-sa, the thought of superiority will arise. Even though that person broke the precepts, he was a Buddhist and still showed signs of being a Buddhist. What are the ten types of merit? "The person who is a monk in the middle dharma, even though he breaks the precepts, even though he breaks the precepts, sentient beings, or sentient beings, will be born with reciting the Buddha's name with respect and reverence for superior thoughts" (It is the person who has become a monk in my dharma, even though he breaks the precepts, but the sentient beings who are seen will give rise to the superior thought of thinking of the Buddha, respectfully and respectfully believing): Although that person breaks the precepts, sentient beings see him and do not think of him as a precept-breaker at all. Sentient beings only see from his body that he is a monk, only seeing one form. Because sentient beings only see that you are a monk, the idea of ​​superiority arises. Because of seeing that monk, they recited the Buddha's name, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Due to reciting the Buddha's name, the thought of supreme reverence arises. They will think like this: "This monk is a disciple of Buddha." Therefore, we will think of Buddha's merits.

“Due to the predestined cause and effect, they do not rely on pagan teachers, commentaries, or followers at all” (Due to that cause, they completely do not rely on and believe in pagan teachers, books, treatises, and their followers): That person, seeing the monk breaking the precepts, will think of the Buddha, think of the Dharma. Because of this cause and effect, that person takes refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and does not respect or trust pagan teachers. “Paganism” is a book, but also the dharma of pagans. “Followers” are non-Buddhist monks. “Do not take refuge in external teachers, texts, followers, or nuns, and even enter separation from the monks the city of great Nirvana” (Do not take refuge in pagan teachers, books, sutras, and disciples, until you can enter the city of great Nirvana, free from fears), meaning: Seeing the bhikkhu breaking that precept, that person gives rise to a superior cause and effect, thinking of Buddha, thinking of the Dharma, even respected that monk. Because of that cause and effect, that person can leave all fears, attain Nirvana, can enter Concentration, can attain "no birth and death".

(Sutra) Or having the right view, being born in the holy world surpasses thinking. Due to the cause and effect, one can renounce killing, renounce non-attachment, abandon evil desires, abandon speech, abandon dampness, drink, and lethargy, and enter the great Nirvana. Or if there is a view, the thought of giving surpasses the thought of giving birth. Due to the predestined relationship, one attains a great position of wealth, becomes close, makes offerings to the right will, right conduct, and is able to enter the great Nirvana of the elders.
With that condition, one can abstain from killing, abstain from giving and take, abstain from evil desires, abstain from false speech, abstain from drinking all kinds of alcohol, and avoid places that give rise to distractions, until one can enter the city of Great Nirvana, and be free from fear. Or, having seen it, the thought of alms will arise, and because of that cause and effect, one can attain great status and wealth, be close to, and make offerings to those who are righteous and virtuous, until one can enter the city. Great Nirvana, free from fears).

Some people saw that monk, saw his dignity, thought that he kept the precepts, was a monk, and thought that "the idea of renunciation" was very difficult to come by. Because of that cause and effect, because he believes that a monk is free from greed, anger, ignorance, does not kill, does not steal, does not commit sexual misconduct, is far from false speech, is far from drinking alcohol, is far from all kinds of alcohol because they are the place where hesitancy arises, [so] he does not drink alcohol. It is also because of seeing a monk breaking the precepts that gives rise to so many wonderful feelings! That person may, because of seeing a monk breaking that precept, sow good roots, eventually attain enlightenment, and attain Nirvana. When he saw a monk, a feeling of superiority arose and he made offerings to him, giving rise to the thought of giving alms. Because of that fate, great wealth and status were achieved. Seeing a monk and considering him as a holy monk will give rise to the idea of ​​superiority. Because of that person's appearance, [that person will] “be close to, make offerings to, have the right intention, right conduct, and even enter the great Nirvana city of great Nirvana” (close to, make offerings to those with the right intention, right conduct, until you can enter the city of Great Nirvana, free from fears).

Gentleness and directness prevail over thinking. Due to the predestined relationship, it is convenient to be far away from cockroaches, evil, impurities, anger, resentment, and anger, and even enter the Great Nirvana. Or if you have the right view, become mindful and become a monk, diligently practice superior thinking. Due to the predestined relationship, if one is able to renounce the Dharma, be brave and diligent, cultivate the sublime virtues, and be able to enter the great Nirvana with separation from the elders. Or with the existence of views, the thought of birth is far away from all scattered and chaotic minds, Tranquility, superior thinking. Because of the predestined relationship between people and people, the mind departs from the mountains and forests, the place of A Luyen Nha, resides diligently, cultivates the Dharma of Dharma, and has the ability to enter the great Nirvana. Or with the existence of views, the birth of wisdom and thought overcomes thinking. Because of the predestined relationship, she happily listened to literature, recited the Dharma, and even entered the great Nirvana. Or if you have the right view, give birth to thoughts of food, escape from the good roots of superior thinking, soften your speech, and be content with your rituals. Due to the predestined relationship, when being born noble, powerful, and countless sentient beings admire it together, they can enter the great Nirvana city of the elders. Good man! The person who has become a monk in the middle of the Dharma, even though he broke the precepts, sentient beings fell into strange forms, giving birth to the ten sublime thoughts, gathering countless merits and treasures. The king, the king, the minister, and the prime minister, must decide whether the immortal, the staff, or the body will be interrogated, or shut up in prison, or serve the mother, or explain the details, or end the life.
(Kinh: Or someone has seen, Then one can give birth to the superior thinking, thinking about patience, gentleness, and uprightness. Because of that cause and effect, one will be able to stay away from cockroaches, evil, impurities, anger, and resentment, until one can enter into great Nirvana, abandon all fears, and then give birth to superior thoughts, thinking about becoming a monk and practicing diligently. until one can enter the city of great Nirvana, leaving behind fears. Or there are people who have seen it, and then have the thought of transcendence, thinking of leaving behind the scattered minds, [toward] Tranquility, level-mindedness. Because of that cause, the mind loves the mountains, forests, and places of A Luyen Nha (Alan Nha), diligently cultivating the Dharma practices day and night, until one can enter the city of great Nirvana, leaving behind fears They will be born with superior thoughts and think about wisdom. Because of that cause and effect, they will love to listen, read, and recite the Dharma until they can enter into great Nirvana, and be free from fear. Or someone who has seen it will give birth to superior thoughts and think about the good roots of renunciation that have been sown before, and use soft words to comfort and greet them, until they will be born in a noble family with great power and immeasurable sentient beings threshold, until he can enter the city of great Nirvana, free from fear. Good man, even if he breaks his precepts, sentient beings who see his appearance will give rise to these ten types of sublime thoughts, and will gain countless amounts of precious merit. Therefore, all Kshatriya kings, ministers, and prime ministers should not use whips, sticks, etc. to beat him, torture him, or put him in prison. prison, or scolding again, or cutting off limbs, or having that person's life cut off).

“Or having a view, the thought of patience, gentleness, directness overcomes superior thinking” (Or maybe someone has seen, then gives birth to superior thinking, thinking of patience, gentleness, directness): This is the Paramita of Forbearance. “Due to this cause and effect, it is convenient to be far away from cockroaches, harshness, impurities, anger, anger” (Due to that cause and effect, it is possible to stay away from cockroaches, harshness, impurities, anger, and resentment): Get rid of anger, get rid of impurities. “Unclean” is a harsh word, but it is not an evil speech. Because they saw the appearance of that monk who broke the precepts, they were able to think like that, until they were able to enter the great city of Nirvana, leaving behind all fears. “Or if you have the right view, you have thoughts of renunciation, diligently practice the superior thinking” (Or maybe someone has seen it, so they have the superior thought thinking about renunciation, practicing diligently): The person who has become a monk is desireless, without attachments (no entanglements), pure, carefree[57]. Bhikkhus who break the precepts [on the outside] are also very carefree. Everyone saw Zen Master Dao Te displaying misdeeds. Although it was a misdeed, in fact, he practiced the Bodhisattva path. Who knows that he was a holy monk? Don't know! Seeing the Master drinking alcohol, going to restaurants, even going to brothels to save others. Hearing me say that He went to a brothel like that, people are probably skeptical, [thinking] that's not the case! I remember when I watched the Tale of Te Gong, at that time I also had the thought of victory, How do you save people?

One ​​day, he went to a disciple's house. At the west gate of To Chau citadel, there was a foreign minister named To Bac Son. The monk went there to find To Bac Son and asked: "Are you busy with anything today?" The disciple replied: "No!" Zen Master Dao Te said: "If you're not busy, come with me to this place." The disciple asked: "Master, where are you going? I'm going with you." Zen Master Dao Te said: “Bring a little more money!” [The student replied]: "Master drank wine, I offered it to you, it's okay." Zen Master Dao Te said: "Today I don't drink alcohol, I want to come to this place." The student asked: "Where to?" Zen Master Dao Te said: "I went to the street to sell flowers." "Master! Why did you come there?" "Don't worry, just come with me." That disciple shook his head, okay, let's go to the brothel! When we arrived, there was a new prostitute there, a famous prostitute (famous prostitute). Zen Master Dao Te said: "I want that prostitute, Ms. Dong Xuan Huong." Dong Xuan Huong saw a monk who was both dirty and unkempt, and his appearance was very unsightly! But the foreigner looks completely different, he has both a title and is rich. She was extremely courteous towards her grandmother. Zen Master Dao Te said: "If you come here, he cannot save you. To save you, you still have to rely on me." She asked: "What do you want to do, Master?" Zen Master Dao Te said: "Come here, I'll tell you. Being idle and comfortable, the monk also wants to have some fun. If you call Xuan Huong, come here, come to me, don't go to him." Dong Xuan Huong immediately asked: "Master! What do you want to do?" Zen Master Dao Te said: "Quickly take off your belt!" Xuan Huong was stunned! Zen Master Dao Te said again: "Give me a belt to tie my torn shoes. My grass shoes are broken, you give me a belt to tie my shoes, nothing else!" What does Zen Master Dao Te want to do? Ms. Dong Xuan Huong was harmed by someone else and sold to a brothel. Zen Master Dao Te came there to save her and told To Bac Son to ransom money for her and take her home. What the girl didn't know was that her mother and she were no longer in contact with each other. Zen Master Dao Te had supernatural powers, so he told her to find To Bac Son's housekeeper and give her some money. Zen Master Dao Te came to save people!

There was also an old monk who was the same. The monk took in a four or five year old child and took him to live in the mountains. In the mountains, that child, in addition to seeing trees, mountains, streams, and ravines, saw wild animals or tigers, and did not see anything else. Waiting until the child was eighteen years old, the master took him out to walk around the streets. Wow! The child's eyes were so dazzled, he couldn't take it! Finally, arriving at a brothel, the girls were wearing lipstick and makeup, and the master took him to see the prostitutes. The disciple asked: "Master! What is that?" The master replied: “Tiger!” In the mountains, tigers eat people! After returning to the mountain, the master asked him: "What was the best thing you saw today?" It replied: "Nothing is good, tiger is the best".

That's called Or. “Or” is delusion, also a karma brought from birth. Desire is difficult to cut off, each of us should experience it for ourselves! Bhikkhus who break the precepts can also cause you to cut off desire, because you only look at phenomena. The saints and Arhats display misdeeds, like the Zen master Dao Te going in and out of taverns and tea houses. Every day, the Master does the same, you see that the Master does not practice, nor does anything, holding a gourd to drink wine, with dog meat in the bag. Zen Master Dao Te can pull logs from the well in Tinh Tu Pagoda, can you pull them up or not? [He did so] to repair Tinh Tu pagoda. Currently, if you go to Hangzhou on the Mainland, go to Tinh Tu Pagoda[58] and look, in the well there is also a log guarded in it. Finally [the temple said] "that's enough", he didn't pull anymore, just left that log there!

Do you believe it or not? It's true! Zen Master Dao Te is indeed the truth. But there are things that are not true, but are created by fiction. He became a monk and was crazy and crazy. You thought he was a monk who broke the precepts. Actually, he secretly practices Bodhisattva conduct, you are completely unaware. Therefore, you should only respect the Three Jewels, do not consider whether he or she has broken any precepts, [that matter] has nothing to do with you, the person receiving the retribution is that person. Consider him a holy monk, consider all sentient beings as Buddhas, consider them as Bodhisattvas. The story of To Dongpo and Zen master Phat An[59] is also the same. If you use Buddha Nature, you will see that all sentient beings are Buddhas. But very few people can see like that. When contemplating, they still cannot visualize like that.

(Sutra) Restore the Great Pham! If you are not a monk, you are a false monk, you break the precepts, you commit evil deeds, you are corrupted internally, you are like a dirty oa loa, you are truly not a monk, you claim to be a monk, you truly are not a virtuous person, you claim to be a virtuous person, you will always be aware that all kinds of afflictions prevail, and your happiness will be corrupted. Like the Buddha, even though he broke the forbidden precepts and practiced all evil deeds, he was one of the Thien Thien, Dragon, Duoc Xoa, Kien Dat Phuoc, At To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, the level of non-human beings, good knowledge, and immeasurable merits and virtues. Like the Buddha, even though he has no dharma weapon, he cultivates and develops, is subdued by ca-sa, maintains his majesty, and is the same as the sages and saints. Human views are persistent, countless sentient species have good roots, they attain birth and growth, have the potential to reveal countless sentient beings and good animals, and are born in heaven, the true path to Nirvana.
rotten, like a dirty snail, really not a monk, claiming to be a monk, really not a holy person, claiming to be a holy person, always controlled, corrupted, and overthrown by all kinds of afflictions. Even though he breaks the forbidden precepts and does evil deeds, he is a good knowledge for all gods, dragons, Yak Xoa, Kān Tathagata, Asura, Yet Lo Do (Ca Lau La), Khan Nai Lac (Khan Na La), Mo Ho Lac Gia (Ma Hau La Gia), non-human beings, etc. teach countless treasures of merit. Although this is not a Dharma weapon, he shaves his beard and hair, puts on a kasa, and walks around majestically like a sage. Because of seeing that person, all the good roots of countless sentient beings are born, and can also show countless sentient beings the right path to advance to the path. good, born in heaven, attain Nirvana).

If there are those who follow me to become a monk, breaking the precepts, doing bad deeds, what is the crime? Like snails, even though they create such karma, you should not underestimate them. They can teach the treasure of immeasurable merit. Although those monks are not dharma objects, they are not a very good tool to hold the dharma. A good bowl will hold food, hold food best. All monastics or the four disciples are all dharma containers, containing all the dharmas taught by the Buddha.

Even though the people [mentioned in the main sutra passage above] are not very good Dharma weapons, they shave off their hair and beard, wear kasayas, and carry majestic gestures still like saints, "companions of saints". Because all countless sentient beings see them, they will be able to develop good karma. Moreover, those who have been ordained for a few days, at worst, still know how to say a few Buddhist sentences. It can also reveal to countless sentient beings, "a good destination, birth in heaven, the right path to Nirvana" (the right path to the good path, being born in heaven, attaining Nirvana).

Even though they themselves do not practice, they tell you how to believe in the Three Jewels, how to practice, how to be respectful, how to give alms? Therefore, people do not feel fear towards pagans and evil masters. If you are afraid, worship before the Buddha, Bodhisattva, and scriptures, and you will be able to avoid evil. As long as you have the right mind, right understanding, right view, wrong views will not be able to penetrate!

(Kinh) Thi Co, y ego Nhi became a monk false, weak maintain precepts, weakly destroyed worlds, summer will without precepts, the unpromised self of the Chakravartin Holy King, the king of du du, the great gods, follow the Dharma, the immortals, the superiors, the main examination of the body, or the closure of prison, or the recovery of ha ma, Either explain it in detail, or cut it off, let alone it's illegal! Dai Pham! If you break the precepts and commit evil deeds, even though you are in the middle of the dharma of Vinaya, the name of a corpse, you will become a monk and follow the precepts of the world, like an ox, a musk, your life will end, but even if you unconsciously give birth to a corpse, the ox will have the yellow color, the musk will have the fragrance, the energy will be immeasurable and boundless, the sentient beings will create great benefits. Breaking the precepts of up-sō-yi, dressed like this, even though I fell into the dharma of Bhikkhu-Da in the middle of the Buddha's name and death, I became a monk with the virtue of the world, and the power of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings brings great benefits.
(Sutra: Therefore, those who follow me to become a monk, whether they keep the precepts or break the precepts, do not even have world, I do not even approve of the Holy King Zhuan Luan and other kings, ministers, etc., relying on the secular Dharma, using whips, sticks, etc., to beat them, torture their bodies, or imprison them in prison, or reprimand them, scold them, or cut off their limbs, or cut off their lives, let alone those who obey the Dharma! Great Pham! Such an evil act is called a "dead body" in Vinaya in my Dharma, but The remaining virtuous power of monastics, such as cows and musk deer, after the death of their bodies, although the corpses of eagles are no longer aware of anything, but cows have yellow bulls and musk deers have musk, which can bring great benefits to countless, boundless sentient beings. The same is true of the Buddha who breaks the precepts, although it is called a "corpse" in Pi Nai Da in my dharma, due to the remaining virtuous power of monastics. can create great benefits for countless, boundless sentient beings).

For this reason, whoever follows me to become a monk, regardless of whether they keep the precepts or break the precepts, even those who do not have any precepts, I do not accept the Holy King Chakravarti and other kings, ministers, etc. “following the Dharma” means using worldly laws to beat, torture, and punish. come and use whips and sticks to whip them. “Either put them in prison, or serve their insults, or explain in detail, or end their lives, let alone be illegal” (Or put them in prison, or reprimand, scold, or cut off their limbs, or end their lives, let alone rely on illegality): Illegal is even worse, it's even more of a crime! "Great Pham! Such a person who breaks the precepts and commits an evil act, even though it falls within the dharma of Bhikkhu, is known as a corpse" (Dai Pham! A Bhiksu who breaks the precepts and commits such an evil action, even though in my dharma of Bhikkhu, it is called a "dead body"): In our Buddhism, if we break the four basic precepts, "killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying" are the four basic precepts, breaking the four basic precepts is called “corpse” (dead body). The Bhikkhu precepts have seven collections of dharma. In the dictionary, the names of the seven clusters are not translated, but from the content we can know a little bit. The seven dharmas that call the four basic precepts are the Four Paramitas, that is, the Guilt of Sin (the crime that causes the person to commit it, will be worthy of being thrown out of the Sangha), worthy of being kicked out of the sea of ​​Buddha, expelled from Buddhism, are called Paramitas (Pārājikuddeso). In the world of monks. This sin does not allow repentance.

Following the Mahayana dharma, like we bow to Ksitigarbha, or bow to Great Compassion, Contemplate Good and Evil Karma, we can still repent, but after repenting, we must see a good appearance. If you worship and see Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, worship Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, or worship Great Compassion and see Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), your sins will be purified. But in the precepts, the monks cannot repent [by personally bowing to the Dharma and praying for a good appearance]. When you want to repent, you still have to face a large assembly of monks, [must have] twenty pure monks tell you: "You have finished repenting." [After that], I stayed alone, bowed my head, and followed the Buddha's teachings. This is also speaking according to the precepts, specifically talking about bhikshus and bhikshunis. The second type is the Sangha Dharma. Sang Tan (Saṃghā-vaśeṣa) means there is still one breath left, not yet dead. Regarding handling issues, I only say nouns, everyone knows that's okay!

That Tu Tinh Gioi specializes in talking about monks. That person does not completely violate all of those precepts, but if he only violates the four basic principles, Luat Tong calls that person a “corpse”. “Corpse” means like a dead body, which also means having committed a sin. “There is a remaining force of monastic virtue and precepts” (There is the remaining power of the monastic virtue): Even though one breaks the precepts, at first when that person becomes a monk, he still keeps the precepts pure. The power of pure precepts has not yet been completely lost. That force is like a cow with a Bull. If a cow eats Ganoderma grass, its stomach cannot digest it, like it has cancer and a tumor develops. What's in that hump? That's called Niu Hoang. If a horse eats lingzhi grass, it will be called Ma Bao. If a dog eats Ganoderma lucidum grass, it is called Cau Bao, all of these things are called Bao.

What is the function of this thing called Treasure? Eliminate illness and suffering. Niu Hoang cures incurable diseases. Cut a little bit of Ox Hoang to make medicine and give it to you to drink to cure your illness. Musk is musk, after the musk deer dies, even though it has sacrificed its life and died, musk still has value, is still a treasure. Even though the cow is dead, the Ox Hoang is still a treasure, not every cow has it. But when the musk deer is about to die, its belly swells and rubs on the ground until it breaks, causing the musk to flow away, making the hunter unable to get it even if he wanted to take it!

The deer have velvet buds. If you hunt it, injure it, or kill it, the hunter must hold its head first. Otherwise, it will headbutt the trees. Antlers are blood, if the blood is lost, it will no longer be effective. People hunt deer because it has antlers. Deer hunting is because it has musk. Niu Hoang is not certain, sometimes the cow gets sick and dies, the doctor judges and says the cow is dead. Even though it has a Ox Hoang, the owner is completely unaware, burying it, or cutting it up to eat, is wrong! This needs to be concluded by a veterinarian.

After the body's life ends, even though the corpse of an animal has no sentience, even though it is an animal, has no sentience, no knowledge, but the corpse of that animal, like a cow with a bull, a musk deer with musk, can bring great benefits to countless, boundless sentient beings, can be used to make medicine, and can cure many diseases. disability for humans. The same is true of Bizō who breaks the precepts. Although in the Buddha's teachings, Bhikshu is called “corpse”, due to the remaining power of the precepts, it can create great benefits for countless, boundless sentient beings.

(Sutra) Dai Pham! Like the ancients, entering the great ocean, killing the most countless sentient beings, taunting the strange eyes, fierce Mat Dat Na fruit, harmonizing and reversing, becoming the precious eye medicine. All sentient beings are bright and clear, with no eyes, even the fetus is born strong, holding on to the precious medicine, keeping the eyes open, dispelling all the troubles, attaining clear and pure eyes. Breaking the precepts of up-sō-yi, dressed like this, even though the Buddha-dharma of Bhikkhu-Da is in the middle, his name is "corpse", he has become a monk in majestic form, immeasurable spiritual energy, boundless sentient beings temporarily attaining a seer, cultivating a pure wisdom eye of the dharma, not to mention the ability to altruistically proclaim the Dharma!
(Sutra: Hey Great Pham! Just like a merchant entering the ocean, killing countless living beings of one species, gouge out their eyes, combine it with the Mahādāna fruit, mix it and create a precious medicine for the eyes. If sentient beings who are blind, have no eyes, even those who have been blind since they were still in the womb, apply this precious medicine to their eyes, all diseases will be eliminated, and their eyes will be clear and clear Therefore, although it is called a "dead body" in Bhikkhuni Da in my dharma, it has the appearance and majesty of a monk, able to temporarily see limitless, boundless sentient beings, and can also attain pure wisdom and dharma vision, not to mention being able to proclaim the Dharma for them).

In the sea there was a type of living being, a fish, that merchant killed that living thing to get their eyes. Mahdāna fruit, also known as Drunk Cause and Effect, but it is poisonous. Use the eyes of that fish, that is, use the eyeballs, grind them together with that fruit, and make medicine to treat eye diseases. There are sentient beings who are blind, or have no eyes, and have been blind since childhood, can use [that medicine]. Even those who are blind, that is, blind from birth, apply that precious medicine to them, they will see, and their eyes will immediately recover.

Bhikkhus who break the precepts are the same. Although in my Vinaya practice it is called a “corpse”, that person has the majesty and appearance of renunciation, which can cause countless, boundless sentient beings, even if they only temporarily see that person for a moment, to be able to attain the pure wisdom eye of the dharma! That's you sowing good roots. If there were no such cause and condition, we would not even see the appearance of the monk who broke the precepts, nor could we see the person wearing the kasa robe. Even the merit that comes from seeing it like that is inconceivable. Really! In Mainland China, during the period from 1950 to 1980, if you wanted to see a monk wearing monk clothes, you would not see it at all!

I remember the magician Dai Quang, who wrote the book Tran Hoi Luc Luc, told me: "When I arrived in Shanghai, I immediately acted strangely." I asked: "What the hell is wrong with you, teacher?" He said: "I wore a yellow robe, a red robe, in my hand holding a staff, also the staff of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and went to Nanjing Road on the outer port of Shanghai. When I got there, I walked around. The people there were surrounded by black and red people. Everyone said this was a monster, I didn't know what it was?" So the police rushed in and dragged him away. As soon as they saw that he was an overseas Chinese from Hong Kong, they immediately expelled him. At that time, if anyone wore monk's clothes, it was illegal. That's already breaking the law, let alone proclaiming the Dharma for others? This monk who breaks the precepts can still preach the Dharma, which is even more wonderful!

(Sutra) Dai Pham! It's like burning incense, but the quality is ruined, the energy is mixed, and the incense is scattered. Break the precepts and turn on the heron to serve as thi. Because of breaking the precepts and not having good fortune, even though he always resides in faith and sacrifices, his body is burned, his body is destroyed, he dies, he falls into the three evil realms, his children are immeasurable, boundless, sentient beings create great benefits, the spiritual person who attains enlightenment is born in heaven, Nirvana is fragrant.
(Sutra: Hey Dai Pham! For example, burning incense, although the material is bad, but the scent is fragrant, incense Other things make them also fragrant. The same is true of Bosho breaking the precepts, because breaking the precepts is not a field of good blessings, although day and night he will always be burned by faith, his body will be destroyed, he will die, he will fall into the three evil destiniess, but it will bring great benefits to countless and boundless sentient beings, that is, it will make them smell the fragrance of heaven and Nirvana).

Even though burned incense is of bad quality, the scent is still fragrant, and the person who is imbued with the scent also smells good. Bhikkhus breaking the precepts are the same. Because he broke the precepts, he was not a field of good blessings, but was always burned day and night by the offerings of believers. When his body broke down and his life ended, he would fall into the three evil realms. He himself, due to receiving offerings from believers, after death, will fall into the three evil realms, fall into hell, fall into the three evil realms, but [while alive] can still create great benefits for countless, boundless sentient beings. In other words, if he himself breaks the precepts, he still has to receive retribution, but he can do good things for all sentient beings. As for all sentient beings, they can still hear the scent of heaven and Nirvana. There is a scent on his body, which means he still has the scent because he had previously received precepts and kept the precepts pure.

(Kinh) Thi Co, Dai Pham! If you break the precepts and commit evil deeds, you must be protected by a white robe and respectfully make offerings. I do not promise that the laity, Di Immortal, and Truong Dao will examine their body, or close the prison, or restore the mother, or explain the details, or end the life. The ego only promises to purify the Sangha, the Buddha-sattva time, or from the four times, the spirit is released, must be given to the four directions by monks, food, tools, and not heard. Immortal, staff, system of blessings, end of life." At that time, the World-Honored One recited and wrote: "Even though the Bo Ca flower is weak in the pancreas, the superior child surpasses the remaining flowers. Breaking the evil precepts of the Buddhas, by overcoming all heretics."
(Sutra: Therefore, Dai Pham! Such a Bo-sho breaks the precepts and commits such evil deeds, all white-clothed people should protect, respect, and make offerings to him. I absolutely do not approve of lay people using whips, sticks, etc. to beat him, torture his body, or detain him in prison, or reprimand, curse, or cut off his limbs, or kill him. I only allow the Sangha to beat him, torture his body, or detain him in prison, or reprimand him, curse him, or cut off his limbs, or kill him. I only allow the Sangha to beat him, torture his body, or detain him in prison, or reprimand him, curse him, or cut off his limbs, or kill him. Purity at the time of Bodhisattva, or at the time of fourth, expel [him] from the Sangha, not allowing him to receive all the provisions, food, and utensils offered to the Sangha of the four directions. For all matters related to Bhikkhuni Da of monks, [he] is expelled [not allowed to participate], not allowed to be in the community, but I do not approve of treating him with whips, sticks, chains, or death." At that time, The World-Honored One then recited verses: "Even though the Champa Flower withers and fades, it is still better than other flowers. Those who break the precepts of evil conduct are still better than all non-Buddhists."

It's not okay to just let him rage like that. The monks will hold a pāsattva ceremony to punish him. The so-called “bodhisattva” (Upoṣadha, Upavasatha) is the person who leaves home on the first and full moon days, which means he must preach the precepts once every fortnight. Bodhisattva is the doctrine of precepts. You hang notice signs at pagodas and temples, sometimes it says “bodhisattva”, sometimes it says “reciting the precepts”, that is, take the original precepts and read them all at once. Then, call him out and kick him out of the Sangha. Whoever makes offerings to the Sangha, in harmony with the Sangha to enjoy food, things needed for life, clothes, single[61], he will forever have no share. If everyone comes to recite the precepts every fortnight, he will not be allowed there. Whenever he acts on Ket Ma, as long as he does things that belong to the Law, he will be kicked out. He is not allowed to be in the assembly, but the Buddha does not allow the use of whips, canes, binding, or cutting off his life.

Even though it is breaking the precepts, like the Campaka flower (Campaka, Chiem Bac flower, Golden Sac Hoa) in India, it withers and the fragrance fades, but it is still superior to other types of flowers. Even though he is a monk who breaks the precepts and has an evil nature, he is still better than all the heretical cliques and all the evil people. This means that lay people are not allowed to defame monks. Previously, I told my Dharma friends: "No matter how bad a monk is, you should not say the fault of the four monks!" There are great virtues and monks, you don't need to worry about them personally! Especially those who wear white clothes (at home), you should not comment. Can a monk say the monk's fault? A person cannot say anything, we must ask the public to expel that person, or even condemn him, depending on which law he has committed in the Seven Dharma Gatherings, what crime he deserves, and what punishment he deserves, then punish him like that! But when it comes to the Sangha, you are lay friends, consider them as Buddhist disciples, consider them as Sangha Jewels, consider all Bhikkhus as holy monks. In your mind, they are holy monks, your merit will not be lost at all! Just because that person broke the precepts doesn't affect you! Buddha taught very clearly. Therefore, everyone should not say that it is the Three Jewels' fault. If you despise monks, defame them, beat them, curse them, cut off your limbs, what retribution you deserve will be discussed in the next section.

Please, friends, pay attention to this point: This story can only be told to Buddhist disciples. Those who do not believe in Buddha, of course they do not believe! Even good monks, they can't believe it, no need to know what kind of monk you are! They don't believe you anyway. Just like in the past in Hong Kong, if they saw a monk shaving his head early in the morning, the Cantonese people would curse them, saying they would have bad luck, and there was no need to do business today! "Monk! Don't go out so early in the morning!" Nowadays it is better, because there are many monks. Nowadays, they also do a lot of Buddhist work, gradually they have learned about it. If they don't know, you have no choice!

The next part of the scriptures is very long, teaching to respect monks. This is absolutely not Buddha covering up shortcomings. It absolutely does not mean that no matter how bad a disciple of Buddha is, you all have to be respectful, no matter how bad you are, you still have to be respectful! That's not the meaning. Because the Buddha sees so far away, he can see countless lives in our past, and also see countless lives in the future. He saw many people who, because of defaming the Three Jewels, fell into the three realms. By respecting the Three Jewels, they achieved boundless happiness. Bhikkhus we consider good, of course we respect them. Regarding monks who break the precepts, do not defame them, and do not take action against them.

In the previous section, it was said that if you see monks, your mind immediately desires to escape the world and wants to practice peacefully in the mountains and forests. Bhikkhus stay in a pure place and practice Concentration. If you meet them, you can grow in wisdom. How do you explain that meaning? Why will seeing them be able to develop wisdom? Seeing that they will be able to attain Samadhi? Everyone who meets me every day, do they have Concentration or not? Does wisdom arise or not? This is not an overnight thing. You see that person, if he gives rise to a mind of reverence for the Three Jewels, will be able to gradually grow the good roots sown previously in his past life. Because we plant rice and flowers on the land, and are nourished by the land and water, just like we see the Sangha Jewel, see the Dharma Jewel, see the Buddha Jewel, it will cultivate your [good roots] once again, develop it once again. Planting like this, over time, the good roots grow; over time, you will naturally achieve it. From studying Buddhism to attaining enlightenment, it is not achieved immediately after contact, but from countless eons until now. Doing evil, committing crimes, is not created immediately, but is accumulated over many lives, countless lives. Now you want to eliminate the sins of countless lifetimes, you have to go through a very long period of practice!

Therefore, reading this passage, you will understand why we still have to respect Bhikkhus who break the precepts, or even Bhikkhus who have no virtue? That's what we often say: "If you don't look at the Sangha's face, you have to look at the Buddha's face", that's the meaning. We see that they are Buddha's disciples, [respecting them is] because we respect the Three Jewels, respect Buddha, has such a meaning. If you think: "Obviously we know that guy is very bad. We see him wearing a ka-sa and still respect him very much, that's not very reasonable!" That's not the meaning, it's absolutely not about valuing that individual! That person is already a disciple of Buddha, while he does not have Dharma clothes or hair, if he violates the precepts, the Sangha will expel him. That person has no Dharma clothes; At that time, he was not a Buddhist disciple. As long as that person still wears the ka-sa, he will still belong to the Sangha Jewels. Even though he breaks many precepts or breaks the precepts, that monk who breaks the precepts will not tell you "I am a monk who breaks the precepts". Will he bang drums, bang gongs, and propagate ["I am a monk who breaks the precepts"]? You basically don't know if he broke the precepts or not! Therefore, as long as he appears as a monk, just respect him!

Why does the Vinaya Pitaka teach to reveal repentance? If you have committed a sin, you must repent; If it is hidden, it will be a deception. In addition to the crimes committed by that person himself, that person also commits the crimes of concealment and deception. That is more sin than sin, many more. When repenting, it is very difficult to repent purely. In the past we have made mistakes, committed many, but we were not enlightened, even in life, when we got sick, we encountered many unsatisfactory things, others had smooth sailing, but you had troubles and difficulties, what is the cause? From countless lifetimes until now, I have done so many things. Even if you repent at once, it is still not easy to repent purely. You must repent for a very long time!

(Sutra) Restore the Great Pham! There are five great evil karma. Ha class vi five? The first person, Co Tu Thanh Tu. The second author, Co Tu killed his mother. Tam fake, tried to kill Arhat. Four people, island and ants destroyed Thanh Van Tang. Five false, evil minds emerge from the Buddha's body and blood. Such as the five races, the reputation of Vo Giac is a great crime. Weak people try the Five Immortals, create one race, are not eligible to become a monk, or receive the Precepts. If a weak spirit becomes a monk or receives the precepts, the monk will commit a crime. When the Belgian eagle is exhausted, the spirit emerges from the dharma. Like a person who has become a monk, has a majestic appearance, the fall of the heron does not promise to be a fairy, cane, or closes the prison, or restores the mother, or explains the details, or cuts off the life span.
Five is to intentionally kill one's father, three is to intentionally kill an Arhat, four is to destroy the Thanh Van Sangha due to evil intentions, five types of such are called "The Great Sin of Non-Continuity". If anyone commits any of these five types, it is not appropriate for him to become a monk or to receive the Precepts If such a person has the dignity and appearance of becoming a monk, I will not allow him to be beaten with a whip or stick, or locked up in prison, or reprimanded, cursed, or cut off his limbs, or end his life.)

Called the Five Immortals are five such types, collectively known as “The great evil karma of Incontinence”. If, among those five types of sins, a person commits any of them, he is not suitable to become a monk, that is, he cannot be accepted to become a monk, and even more so, he cannot receive the Full Precepts. When you are about to become a monk, the teacher will ask: "Before you became a monk, what things did you do? Did you commit those things?" If you commit this crime, the teacher will not dare to accept you. There are also people whose six senses are not complete. Currently, in Buddhism there are also blind people, lame people, lame people, people with mental illnesses, all of these cases are impossible. There are also five types of Non-Man, which are also neither male nor female. This type of person is not allowed to become a monk, you must tell the truth. You don't say anything, the teacher can't check, you have to speak frankly. If you deceive and do not tell, you will commit the crime of deception. If you mix in here, the Dharma protector Dragon Heaven will cause all kinds of obstacles to harm you. This cannot be deceived!

When you receive the precepts, when you enter the precept platform, [the teachers giving the precepts] will ask about “tribulation” (obstacles), such as the Five Non-Intermittents being “tribulation”. There are still many obstacles that prevent you from taking the precepts. Like the five types of Non-Man, neither male nor female, when living with men, that person is female, when living with women, that person is male. Or half male, half female, the top is yang, the bottom is yin. Such people all belong to the five types of Non-Men. Like a eunuch, he will not be able to become a monk, nor will he be accepted. Therefore, being a monk is very difficult.

At first, if in the past you committed the crime of Five Immortals, you must pay attention to the word Co. “Intentional murder of father” (Intentionally killing father): “Tu” is preparation, which includes murder, killing method, murder, murder karma (the cause (cause) of killing, method of killing, person performing the act of killing, and karma of killing), which must destroy one's life. Only after death is counted, that crime has been established. If it is not intentional or mindless, then it is not violating the basic precepts, it is a similar crime (manslaughter), it is a similar crime. Therefore, in front of the crimes of killing one's father, killing one's mother, or killing an Arhat, there is the word Co. Those three types of crimes all have the word Co, meaning intentional. Being intentional, even scheming, those three types [of charges] are like that. “Inverted views destroy the Thanh Van Sangha” (Inverted views destroy the Thanh Van Sangha): Inverted views are not right knowledge, right views, wrong knowledge, crazy wrong views, destroying the harmony of the Sangha, dividing the Sangha, which was originally one, into two groups. For example, in our temple there are thirty monks, you tease and separate them, tear them into groups of three or more, that is destroying their harmony. Sparking a quarrel with someone doesn't count. If you cause seven or eight people to separate, it will destroy the harmony of the Sangha. When everyone is together in harmony and cultivating the Way, you destroy it, it is called “disrupting Sangha harmony”. This story is limited to the Thanh Van community. Malice causes the Buddha's body to bleed. Malice means having a mind of slander, even anger, and anger. These thoughts are all considered evil. Making the Buddha's body bleed is only when the Buddha is still alive.

A friend asked me: A Buddha statue drawn on paper, because we didn't pay attention, caused it to be torn, destroyed, or hung there, when you took it down, it was torn, does that count as "making the Buddha's body bleed"? That doesn't count, it can only be counted as a minor mistake. It can only be counted as not very respectful, it can only be counted like that. It cannot be counted as making the Buddha's body bleed, because paper statues cannot bleed. Do clay or carved wooden statues bleed? There is no blood, that is talking about the present scene, the real scene. Only then can it be counted as the Ngu Nghi crime. That's called the Five Great Sins. Endless suffering means suffering without interruption, suffering without stopping. When you are about to die, when you enter hell there is no interruption at all, it is very fast.

For those five types, whoever violates any one type is not allowed to become a monk. Even a lay person cannot, much less, be allowed to receive precepts. Receiving the Complete Precepts, also means two hundred and fifty precepts for a Bhikkhu. Suppose any master allows that person to become a monk, or allows that person to receive the Full Precepts, that teacher has committed a sin. If by accepting that person, the master himself commits a sin, then what about the disciples he has accepted? People who have all kinds of hardships must be expelled from the Sangha. They cannot be kept in the Sangha. They must be expelled from Buddhism and not accepted into Buddhism. To use an example, it is like a dead body drowning in the sea, the ocean waves will definitely push it to shore. The ocean does not tolerate corpses, the ocean of Buddhism does not tolerate those who break the precepts.

As for those who commit the Five Immortals, the master still accepts that person and allows him to receive Full Ordination. He has not yet been expelled and still blends in among the monks. That person has the dignity and appearance of becoming a monk, has received the Full Precepts, and still wears the robe, but the rear robe (hai qing robe) does not count as anything. Ao Dai is the costume of the Han people. [Throughout generations] Han, Tang, Song, and Ming were all like that. However, the pockets of the shirt are unfortunately not that big, and the sleeves are not that wide, [when sewn into vestments for monks and lay people] they are slightly increased. At that time (when the Buddha preached the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra), he talked about the robe (ca-sa); Now, he has also been modified! There are people who say: "Society has changed, it must change." Currently, [robes] with rings and hooks come from China. That style originally came from India as well. Currently, Indians wear the same clothes. Here, we have a lot of Indians, you see men and women [wearing traditional clothes] will overlap the hem of their shirt like that.

That person has all the majesty of a monk. How much dignity does a monk have? Three thousand! Since ancient times, the dignity of renunciation has been visualized: If you go to the main hall, or when walking on the road, do not look forward more than five meters[62]. If you turn your head to look East and West, like shaking a drum[63] then it is not okay, it is a violation of dignity! Traveling on the road has certain limitations, these things must be learned. Even while eating, it's not like us. How to dig into a bowl of rice, how to hold chopsticks, how to eat when eating, especially while eating, if you chew the tip, it's not okay!

When I was in Co Son, there were more than a thousand people on the street (having lunch). Entering from the street door, you don't hear any sound inside. There were no sounds of chopsticks or bowls, not even the sound of chewing rice, it was not like eighteen hundred people were eating there. You don't even know there are so many people in there! At that time, I had just arrived at Co Son, I said this temple is so big, why is it so deserted, as soon as I entered, I still felt a little scared. Walking down the hallway, I didn't see anyone. When I heard the bang[64], when I got to the main hall, at every small door, which at first glance was very narrow, there were monks standing. At that time, there were more than eight hundred and seventy monks there, and more than a thousand pure people. Pure people are people who serve in temples and pagodas, take care of gardening, and take care of fruit gardens. It seems that everyone fulfills the dignity of a monk.

If you become a pure person in the temple, you will be fully majestic. Just entering the temple will not be the same as the secular world. However, progress has been made now! [Current people think] those things are no longer needed, they feel too cumbersome. Three thousand majesty and eighty thousand virtues bind each individual to become like that.

At that time, the monks living in the temple did not feel [bound], it had become a habit. Since receiving the precepts, he has always lived in the forest until the big pagoda. If you become a monk, you must live in the forest to know the majestic appearance. As long as that person has a majestic appearance, no matter if he has committed the Five Disadvantages in the past, or even if he has mixed in with the Sangha, as long as he has not been expelled, he should not be punished, beaten, or imprisoned in prison, or scolded, or cut off his limbs, or killed, none of these things are possible! Even if sentient beings in the past committed the crime of the Five Immortals and infiltrated Buddhism, they would not be able to!

Today, a Dharma friend asked me: "If I knew that that person was a person who committed the Five Disadvantages, I wouldn't be able to have the heart to respect him!" You should not give birth to [that mind], you should repent. Because your mind is not the Buddha mind, it is not the Three Jewels mind. When you meet the Three Jewels, why can't your faith arise? You think that person is breaking the precepts, as long as that person has the Sangha, we see that this master is very good, that master himself also feels very good. But that person who violates the precepts of the subtle realms, dragons, heavenly beings, ghosts, and gods all knows it, [that person] doesn't even know that he or she has violated the precepts! Never having studied the precepts before, how do you know that you are breaking the precepts? Even so, dragons, heavens, ghosts and gods still respect that person.

(Sutra) The Four Kinds of Resurrection, close to the Five Immaculate Continents, the basic sin of evil karma. Ha level vi four? One person, having an unkind mind, killing Doc Giac, killing living beings, commits the fundamental crime of evil karma. Second, adulterous Arhat,on-soni Tang, lustful and evil conduct are the fundamental sins of evil karma. The third person, infringing on the property of the Three Jewels, committing an evil act is the fundamental crime of evil karma. The four wrongdoers, opposing views, destroying the harmony of the Sangha, corrupting words and sayings are the fundamental sins of evil karma.
(Sutra: Again, there are four things that are fundamental sins belonging to the great evil karma, close to the Five Immortals. What are the four? One is to arouse an unwholesome mind, killing Practitioner, which is the basic sin of the great evil karma of "killing living beings". Two, the impurity of Arhat, the great evil karma of "sexual immorality". "Fourth, crazy views that destroy the harmony of the Sangha. That is the basic sin of the great evil karma of "speaking falsely".

This is talking about the Near Five Non-Indirect Crimes, which are absolutely not as serious crimes as the Non-Indirect Crime. There are four things in the Five Infinite Sins:

1) The first type, giving rise to an unwholesome mind, kills the Single Enlightenment. An unwholesome mind gives rise to evil thoughts. Aroused the evil intention of killing Doc Giac. Single Enlightenment is when there is no Buddha in the world, he lives in the quiet mountains and forests practicing, attaining Single Enlightenment, that is, attaining Single Enlightenment status in the Second Vehicle. Because there was no Buddha in this world, he enlightened himself and attained enlightenment, so he was called Pacceka. If a Buddha appears in this world, he is called Pratyekabuddha. He is enlightened by relying on the twelve dharmas of causes and conditions. Killing [Poly Horned] is a crime of Near Five Non-Interruptions, not counted as five crimes of Non-Interruption! However, this is the sin of killing, a fundamental sin of great evil karma, and is not considered the sin of Indifference.

2) The second is the impurity of the Arhat, the monk, regardless of whether he knows it or not. This is the crime of Near Vo Interruption, also a great crime.

3) Third, violating or damaging objects belonging to the Three Jewels, or objects given to the Three Jewels. This is the great sin of "not giving but taking".

4) Fourth is crazy views that destroy the harmony of the Sangha. Inverting knowledge and destroying the harmony of the Sangha is just creating a crime through that person's language. For both sides, it stirs up gossip and gossip, only included in evil speech and false speech (deceptive speech), involving the precepts of lying.
