It will definitely fall down, and it will fall very fast! The two types of man-made sins, Five Infinite and Near Five, up to the four basic sins, as well as defamation of the Dharma, doubting the Three Jewels, and the two types of sinners Near Four Infinite and Near Four Basic Sins will be the same, falling into hell very quickly!

“Try the top ten sins of faith, create one type, destroy the body, end life, no remaining separation” (Of those eleven crimes, if you create one type, when the body and life die, there will be no gap): The five sins of Non-Interruption above are five types, called the Five Non-Interruptive Crimes. [In addition to] the four basic sins are four more types, forming nine types. There are two more types: Basic access and Immediate access; therefore, into eleven types. If you commit any kind of offense, your body will be destroyed and your life will be over, there will be no loopholes! In the common network, there is not the slightest gap. “Determining to be born in the great Intermittent Hell, experiencing all kinds of suffering” (Definitely being born in the Great Intermittent Hell, suffering extreme suffering): This type of suffering is extremely intense, so it is called “extremely serious evil karma”. Bo Dat Gia La violated the Dharma of Non-Yāhāhā, committed an extremely serious crime and evil karma. In this life, that kind of sentient beings certainly cannot end their afflictions!

In this life, if you want to eliminate all afflictions and attain Buddhahood, it will not be possible! Can't even attain Concentration. Still unable to achieve samadhi, let alone able to enter the true nature of separation from birth? “Rebirth and true nature” refers to Nirvana. The right nature of separation from birth of those who see the path has left the afflictions of birth and death, that is called "entering the right nature of separation from birth, entering Nirvana, leaving birth and death". When that person dies, he will certainly be born in hell. Not only will he not be able to attain fruition, he will also be unable to be born in heaven, and he will also be unable to be reborn as a human being. “Suffering all kinds of suffering” (Suffering all kinds of suffering): From the Unintermittent hell, the time is extremely long. Even though it is possible to be reborn in the human world, due to past karma, that person will become blind, deaf, mute, speechless, and have disabled limbs.

Such people escape from the three evil realms, or from hell, roughly the type of people who escape from the Five Immaculate Continents. They are reincarnated into families where they are still evildoers. “Methods gather into types, things are grouped together” (Methods gather into types, things are divided into groups). Don't commit this kind of crime! Through repentance, claiming names, Great Compassion Repentance is also possible, Ksitigarbha Repentance is also possible. We worship Contemplation and Repentance and worship Thien Buddha and Name Sam to eliminate this type of karma. That is called Mahayana dharma. If you recite the holy name Ksitigarbha, recite the holy name Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, recite several great Bodhisattvas, or recite the Buddha's name, all of your sins can be destroyed. However, it is impossible to expect achievement in this life!

We say the opposite, the person who is accomplished in the present life means that in the past he has accumulated very good, very great karma, cultivating the path to completion, but has not yet achieved it, so in this life he completes it. That's the meaning. When you see someone else being offered offerings, you must rejoice and praise them, because that person has merit and blessings. Even though you won't get it, by rejoicing and praising it, you will get half of it. You must definitely rejoice in the merits. The fifth of the ten great vows is “rejoicing in merit”, which means we sow good roots to cultivate blessings. That is the best method. You see on the street, whether you are a disciple of the Three Jewels, or an ordinary person, randomly doing good deeds, seeing people liberating animals, even though you don't spend money, but praise and rejoice a little, you will have the same merit as that person. When you see good things, you should rejoice. When you see an evil thing, you must repent and help that person dedicate it, then you yourself are practicing the Bodhisattva path. The fourth great vow is “repentance”, having repented, then rejoicing. This must be done at any time. That is private salary. Preparing this kind of self-reflection will have a great relationship with achieving enlightenment in the future!

(Sutra) Restore the Great Pham! Weak good men, weak good women, with pure faith, take refuge in the Dharma, or accept the Shravaka Vehicle, or accept the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, or embrace the Mahayana, stick to the Dharma, have pure faith and become a monk, receive the Complete Precepts. Try to be brave and diligent in protecting. Like the people of the world, there are always people and non-human beings, depending on the axis to support them, and receive offerings from people and heaven.
(Sutra: Come, Great Pham! If good men or good women use a pure mind and believe, take refuge in the Dharma of me, or moving towards the Shravaka Vehicle, or moving towards the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, or moving towards the Mahayana, staying in my dharma, being pure in faith, becoming a monk, receiving the Complete Precepts. For the places of study, with deep respect, for the precepts of the four basic sinful natures, being steadfast, brave, diligently maintaining, such a person is often closely followed and supported and protected by all human beings, etc. It's a waste to receive offerings from heaven and people."

In the previous section, it talks about people who do evil and break the precepts; Here, talking about maintaining precepts, comparing the two sides. If there are men and women, that means men who are very kind and good, women who are very good and have pure faith. We all have faith, but “purity” is very difficult. In general, not for fame, not for profit, looking for the holy path, not looking for a comfortable, parasitic life. Seeing a monk, I thought that being a monk is very easy to live. In the past, there was a poem admiring the monk's life: "The armored general went to the mandarin, the courtiers served five cold hours, the day appeared in the three cans Tang started, the audience of fame and fortune was not as leisurely" (The armored general crossed the border at night, the official went to pay his respects early in the cold, it was almost noon, the Sangha had not yet woken up, it seems that fame and fortune are not as good as leisure). After I became a monk, I felt that the poem was not correct. Why? “ Nhat exported three cans Tang vi arise” (The sun rises three meters high, the Sangha has not yet risen). They saw the monk sleeping, not knowing that at 2:30 a.m. the monk had to wake up, go to the main hall to chant, drink porridge, finish the journey, and return to rest a bit. When they saw it, they thought the monk had not yet woken up. Some people sleep a little, some people meditate, they only see then. The monk woke up at 2:30 a.m., you go to the temple to see. As soon as the bells and drums are rung, everyone in the temple wakes up. You cannot avoid your duty. Use such a mindset to become a monk, admire the peaceful life of a monk, or avoid debt, or take refuge and blend in as a monk. A person like that cannot be a good monk, but you should not despise him either, with this meaning. That is having a pure mind.

After taking refuge in Buddhism, that person seeks to cultivate the path, either cultivating the Four Noble Truths, i.e. Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path, cultivating the twelve causes and conditions, or cultivating the Six Noble Truths. We speak in general, taking those dharmas as representatives, that is "three vehicles". That person, using pure faith and faith, left home like that and received the Full Precepts. “Where you study” (Where you study): “Study” is precepts. Once you have received the precepts, you must study them. You must receive the precepts before you can study. The Bodhisattva precepts are the opposite. Before that, you must study them carefully before receiving them. The Three Refuges and Five Precepts are easy. You can study first and then receive, or you can receive and then study. That is a skillful means to guide (receive, receive, receive), but the precepts of bhiksunis and bhiksunis are completely different. After receiving the precepts, the first five years of a monk's renunciation must definitely study the precepts. Only after mastering the precepts can you study sutras and treatises. Precepts come first. At the same time, when studying, you must have a deep, kind, and pure mind. Deep heart includes many things; Here it is said to be deep in the heart, meaning to have a sincere and urgent mind. Mahayana Awakening of Faith teaches that the heart must fulfill all good dharmas. What the Great Bodhisattva did was only from the depth of his heart, but also with sincerity and earnestness. Only then can we be steadfast, courageous, and diligent in keeping the four basic precepts of "killing, stealing, sexual immorality, lying". Taking the precepts is easy, keeping the four basic precepts is very difficult. Therefore, it must be sturdy. “Steadfast” means being extremely resilient, not being discouraged when faced with any challenge, only then can you keep the four basic precepts. Otherwise, it won't be easy to keep it! Because there is habit energy in countless past lives, but it is only limited to the Bhikkhu precepts, you can maintain it.

In the Bodhisattva world, it also refers to the mind. Like the four basic precepts, anger does not arise. Without the mind to kill, one cannot kill. When you hate others, any mind will arise. First of all, let's not talk about murder. You see a cockroach or mouse, biting something, or destroying your food, anger immediately arises. You want to catch it and make it die, that is murder. Therefore, you must have deep faith; That is the meaning “steadfast, brave”. You should not retreat from those four basic precepts. If you retreat a little, it's over! Even though you haven't committed a fundamental violation, you haven't committed an ultimate violation, but in one aspect, you've committed a violation. You have to be diligent in maintaining it, don't let it go even a little bit!

“Preventing the mind is like protecting a citadel” (Preventing the mind is like protecting a stronghold): Maintaining the precepts is like white, clean, unblemished wish-fulfilling jade, unable to have the slightest dent, how to do it? Whenever you make a mistake, immediately repent. Every half month of Bodhisattva is to point out the mistakes that one has committed, making the Sangha aware of them. You are pure and fulfilled again. This is like dirty clothes, wash them. After washing, it's still not completely clean like before. If clothes are torn, mending them is more difficult than washing them. Even though it says patched, there are still patch marks. Having broken the precepts, even though you have repented, in general you still have shortcomings. Therefore, you should diligently preserve it. If you keep it like that, then you can receive offerings from heaven and people. “Human non-human”, “non-human” refers to ghosts and gods. They will support you and receive offerings from God and people.

(Sutra) In the center of the Samyana, depending on the joy, the speed of the animal enters, the ultimate salvation. Thi tries, truly seeks fake Nirvana, sacrifices his life and life, and never destroys it like the four dharmas. The reason why it's fake? All sentient beings of all kinds, are weak because of the three causes to attain Nirvana: Nare only the Tathagata as the cause. All sentient beings should try the three people, practice diligently, and attain Nirvana. Weak people destroy the law like the four dharmas, the ego is not the master, the disciple is not the disciple.
(Sutra: In the three vehicles, according to your liking, quickly enter, complete practice, and ultimate achievement Therefore, a person who truly seeks Nirvana would rather sacrifice his life and not violate these four dharmas. Why is it that sentient beings must attain the joy of Nirvana by following three causes? Second, relying on my disciples as a cause. All sentient beings must practice diligently to attain the joy of Nirvana is not his teacher, he is not [my] disciple).

In the dharma of the three vehicles of Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Bodhisattva, depending on your preference, due to the cause in the previous life and external support in the present, the cause and effect have ripened [so learn a dharma]. That way you will study the Four Noble Truths, or study the Dharma of cause and effect, the Six Dharmas, without violating the four basic precepts. If you violate other rituals and virtues, as soon as you repent, they will be pure, will not hinder you from cultivating the path, will not hinder you from achieving them. Breaking the four basic precepts will hinder you from successfully cultivating the path. When you cultivate the path, there will be no way to enter! Why say so? If you practice until the end, then you will seek Nirvana, seek the principle "no birth, no death, no birth, no death". Therefore, to what extent should you keep this precept firmly? “Ninh sacrifices his life” (I'd rather sacrifice my life)! In the precepts of Buddhist scriptures, to what extent is it forbidden to kill living beings? Tied with grass. When the robber captured that person, there was nothing to tie him up with, so he used a rope to tie him to the grass. He knew that the Bhikkhu did not dare to move. Whenever you move, the grass will be uprooted; That's breaking the precepts. That's how Indian bandits believe in monastics. That's called "bhikkhu grass" (bhikkhu tied to the grass). If so, he will attain enlightenment. That is called “courageous diligence”.

We all have skillful means. Why must he be tied to the grass? You tie him to a tree, he will think of a way to untie himself and run away on his own, is that true or not? This is talking about firmly maintaining the precepts, he would rather sacrifice his life and life, not breaking the four dharmas like that, not breaking the four precepts of lust, killing, stealing, and lying. Why say so? “The reason why it is false?” (Why?): To say that all sentient beings must achieve the joy of Nirvana due to three causes. The first three causes are the Tathagata's teachings. "Y refers to Tathagata as the cause" (Relying on Tathagata as the cause). Expanding a little further, it would mean that y refers to good knowledge, relying on Buddha, having to rely on holy teachings, having to rely on the Dharma. The Tathagata is the cause, the holy teachings are the cause, that is, using the dharma as the cause. I also have to rely on my disciples, which means I rely on the Sangha. That is called relying on the Three Jewels as a cause. After that, we will receive the teachings, which is to say that the Tripitaka, the rules, and the treatises are all included in it. It is not just about the precepts, but the Sutras and Treatises are also included in it. All sentient beings, all sentient beings, relying on those three causes, that is, relying on Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to practice diligently, will be able to attain the joy of Nirvana.

I have preached these things at the Thanh Tuyen Assembly Hall in Taipei four times, teaching about taking refuge in the Three Jewels, which is also saying that relying on the Three Jewels to practice is enough. Relying on “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, day and night reciting “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, the merit is immeasurable. Therefore, consider this as the cause. There is also support. Having these three causes, practicing diligently, practicing diligently and courageously, without slacking off. The Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra teaches how to practice by “retaining past thoughts”, that is, observing the breath in and out. These are all methods of practice. Therefore, the Three Jewels act as a cause, which means you do not distinguish between people who violate the precepts or do not violate the precepts, do not care, only care about keeping your own mind good. That cause is planted in your mind. Buddha taught: For all my disciples, you do not need to differentiate between them. You treat all Sangha equally, the same goes for our holy monks, and we also treat ordinary monks as holy monks. There is no distinction between holy monks and ordinary monks. Don't say, "This monk cultivates the Way and practices very well. If I make offerings to him, my blessings will be a little bigger. That monk is a monk who broke the precepts. I make offerings to him, but I'm afraid my blessings will be reduced." Don't differentiate like that! If you don't have a discriminating mind, you will all become offerings to saints and monks. That way, you will sow blessings and receive blessings. That's the way to practice.

If you see that this is a clay statue, a carved wooden statue, saying it is a paper statue, [distinguishing] a statue drawn on paper, a statue made of clay, a statue made of carved wood, of course it will not be sacred. What's so special about paper? If you consider it a real Buddha, you will be spiritual. That is the mind of your spirit. That is the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Three Jewels right in your heart, acting as the cause for cultivating the path for you. Only if you have pure faith, that is, if you have pure faith, can you enter and reach non-discrimination. If you don't have pure faith, how can you be indifferent? Our two eyes use consciousness and visual consciousness to differentiate. According to habit, without even having to taste it, you already know bitter, spicy, sour, and sweet. Bitter melon is definitely bitter! We must always guard this kind of morality. That is to say, all sentient beings must adhere to these three causes and practice diligently in order to achieve the joy of Nirvana. If you violate the four dharmas like that, committing "sex, killing, stealing, lying", I will not acknowledge that person as my disciple. “I am not a teacher, I am not a disciple” (I am not that person's teacher, that person is not a disciple), must be expelled from Buddhism!

(Sutra) The destruction of weak causes is like the four dharmas, the principle of micro vi vi vi viet ego, the profound and vast theory of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self, corresponding to the benefits and peace of all sentient beings and liberation teachings. Weakness is like the teaching of liberation, it is necessary to be still, stable, to become strong, unable to enter, because of all afflictions and evil karma. Absorbing the three vehicle dharmas, the heron is non-energy, falling into an evil realm, experiencing great suffering. The weak good man, the weak good woman, the self-centered teaching of liberation, has the four basic types of serious sins, pure and innocent, the self is the teacher, the disciple is, according to the self, good in the self, must act, the stage is fulfilled. Try the good cause that abides in the Thi La Aggregate, the good name that abides necessarily in the good dharma. Either the name of the person who abides in the Thanh Van Vehicle, or the name of the person who abides in the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, or the name of the person who abides in the Mahayana. The reason why it's fake? Weak ability to protect the four basic dharmas of sinful nature, with knowledge and principles to establish necessarily existent and non-storm, good dharma wins the cause. Preserving and protecting like the four dharmas, the name and reputation are necessarily basic good dharmas.
permanent, suffering, emptiness, non-self", corresponding to the benefits and peace of all sentient beings, which are very profound and vast, as I have declared. If you go beyond the Dharma of Particular Liberation like that, then all of you will become blind, unable to enter, bound by evil karma and afflictions, and will not have the right temperament to practice the three vehicle dharma, will fall into the evil destinies, and suffer heavy suffering. If a good man, or a good woman, towards the four basic types It is a serious sin that I have established in the Dharma of Particular Liberation to keep pure, not to violate, I am that person's teacher, that person is my disciple, according to my words, well abiding in my Dharma, all his deeds will be accomplished to perfection. Because of this, he is called well abiding in all good dharmas Why? If you can protect the four basic dharmas that belong to the nature of sin like that, you should know that it is establishing the superior cause for all good dharmas with outflows and non-outflows. Therefore, protecting the four dharmas like that is called the basis of all good dharmas.

If anyone violates the four dharmas like that, it is contrary to the Dharma of Particular Liberation “impermanence, suffering, emptiness, no-self” which is vast and profound, corresponding to the benefit and peace for all sentient beings as I have said. Because you have gone against or exceeded it, you have also committed a crime. What is beyond? It is all the dharmas I have mentioned, in general they are impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self, those four dharmas correspond to Nirvana. These dharmas correspond to immortality, immortality, and correspond to the achievement of moral karma. If you do not violate those four dharmas, corresponding to the Four Noble Truths of Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, and Non-Self, you can bring benefits to all sentient beings, up to the point of allowing all sentient beings to be liberated.

“Particular liberation”: If you keep one precept, you will be freed from bondage. “Upholding one precept will free you from bondage”, that is liberation. Two hundred and fifty pure precepts without breaking, achieving Arhatship, distinguishing the precepts of liberation like that. If left over, it will be a violation.

“It is absolutely necessary that Static Lu, equal maintenance, stage becomes manh minh” (That is, for all Tinh Lu, equal maintenance, it becomes dark): Equal Tri is to maintain all dharmas, equally maintain the "Dharma meaning" of all dharmas. “Manh minh” is blind, “minh” is dark. While you cultivate Concentration, practice the Dharma, and even learn the teachings, you cannot enter, it is a dark atmosphere. “Manh” is something that cannot be seen. We have eyes, we are not blind, but in a dark place where there is no light, no sunlight, no moon light, when there are no three lights (lamp light, sun light, moon light), you are also blind, you cannot see anything. Therefore, cannot enter. How do you enter Nirvana? Bound by negative karma and afflictions.

“U three vehicles of dharma, herons are not dharma weapons” (As for the three vehicles of dharma, they are also not dharma weapons): Such afflictive evil karmas, the evil karmas created are not in accordance with the dharma nature, and do not correspond to liberation. That is evil karma.

Or say we have a lot of afflictions; That's because the things we have done are all giving rise to afflictions and not giving rise to merit. Merit has no place to rely on, what you have done is not trustworthy, it gives birth to afflictions, cannot give birth to merit, cannot give birth to good dharma. Because evil forces bind you and keep you in trouble all day long, can you still cultivate the Dharma? Whether you practice good or bad religion, after believing in Buddha, regardless of whether you recite sutras or practice concentration; This is the best way to check and feel how your own afflictions are. Whatever you see, your mind is not happy. After you have believed in Buddha, taken refuge in the Three Jewels, received the Three Refuges, and reached the Five Precepts, the reason you do not gain benefits is because you are still in afflictions. Affliction corresponds to the evil destinies, corresponds to unwholesome karma, corresponds to evil karma. Not having afflictions corresponds to good dharma, corresponds to good karma.

If we can protect the four basic precepts well, as the Buddha said, we should do so. “Depending on my words, staying well in my dharma” (Depending on my words, staying well in my dharma): Medical teachings practice. No matter what the Buddha said, that person immediately did so, always remaining in the Buddha Dharma. What is that dharma? Buddha Dharma is your mind Dharma. Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us “Good use of the mind”. “Good use of the mind” (Skillful use of the mind) is the end of afflictions. Anytime, anywhere, use your mind very well, to a wonderful extent. We see many people who are skillful in using evil, claiming that they have many advantages, have many intentions, seem to have very methods, but their ideas are evil thoughts, not very useful for good! How can he achieve the things that person has accomplished?

If “according to one's words, the good person abides in the self-dharma” (depending on my words, abides in my dharma), then everything that person has done will be “satisfied”, that is, completely accomplished, without any shortcomings. “Testing good people to abide in Thi La Aggregates” (He skillfully abides in Thi La Aggregates): Thi La (Śīla) is the Law. Thi La means you are skillful in avoiding mistakes and ending evil. Ceasing evil will give birth to good dharma. That is the meaning of Thi La. “Aggregates” is hidden. In Thi La, there are hidden immeasurable good dharmas and immeasurable merits. That is called “good abiding in all good dharmas” (joyfully abiding skillfully in all wholesome dharmas), “or a name-instrument fully abiding in the Sravakayana” (or called abiding fully in the Sravakayana), “or a name-instrument fully abiding in the Single Enlightenment Vehicle” (or called abiding fully in the Single-Enlightened Vehicle), “or a name-instrument fully abiding in the Mahayana” (or called abiding fully in the Mahayana). Thus, one abides in the three vehicles!

Everyone, think about it, these four precepts “lust, kill, steal, lie”, in the past, although not committed in such a serious way, but in our mind we cannot control it, we cannot stop it. When we see someone else's good things, we wish to have them and take them as our own, which is a violation of the precept of theft. Excessive expectations arise, just like a flower has a owner, without a owner it doesn't count, a mountain doesn't count. Flowers "have an owner" [here in the sense of] flowers to worship Buddha, you go there and smell a little, that is "stealing incense". Incense is for worshiping Buddha. When buying incense or flowers, don't smell it first. If you don't buy it, don't use it to worship Buddha, or have no intention of using it to worship Buddha, you can smell it a little.

If you have determined that I bought this flower to worship Buddha, if I smell it a little, it is "stealing incense". You didn't have Buddha's permission, so you picked it up and smelled it, that is "stealing incense", that's not okay! Thieves are extremely difficult to keep. If I don't steal anything from someone, is it still a violation of the precept of stealing? Many people, when I tell them they have committed the precept of stealing, do not admit: "Did I steal someone else's things?" Throughout the day, you all have the mind of stealing, the karma of stealing, the ways of stealing, the fate of stealing, so many! Therefore, shaman Hoang Nhat wrote a separate book about the world of thieves. The precepts of thieves are very difficult to keep. But for us, moving [something] from its original place is a violation. Like this flower, you take it out of its original place. After that, I regretted it and put it back in its original place, having violated the precepts! Still have to repent. Just moving it from its original place is already a violation! Once the first thought is completed, it becomes reality. Then regret, the second thought is to keep the precepts, how could we commit that crime? That is a violation of the Five Precepts. sexual misconduct, killing, stealing, lying, the four basics are complete. Run quickly and put it back in the old place. If you have committed a crime, put it back and you will repent. However, that is a very small error.

Truly speaking, if one does not violate the four basic dharmas, one has established the superior cause of all good dharmas with both outflows and outflows. In the dharma of existence, that is also the superior cause. If you wish to gain blessings from humans and heaven, wish to gain glory and wealth, you must also rely on these four types of dharma, which are also worldly and extra-worldly dharmas. Anasrava refers to the worldly dharma, anasrava is the attainment of enlightenment in Buddha Dharma. The Buddha Dharma is anasrava, one can attain that state. That is the supreme cause of all good dharmas, the most sublime. Cause is the cause that can arise, that is, can give rise to all good dharmas, is the most sublime cause. Therefore, protecting these four dharmas is called the basis of all good dharmas. Therefore, you must maintain those four dharmas. Those four dharmas are the basis of all good dharmas, because good dharmas will arise from those four dharmas, from there.

Let's review, here, the nature of sin. In daily life, in communication between people, think about it, how much money can a person who does not commit those four types of sins have? Everyone from Taipei, look back and see how many people in Taipei have not committed those four types of crimes? So many. Killing unjustly, harming others, making up stories about harming others, I'm afraid is very common. Those who truly want to uphold the four dharmas without violating them become a minority, those who violate them become the majority! Therefore, the Mahabodhi Sutra is very relevant to our daily lives. We should meditate at any time, these four types are very easy to remember. When you start thinking and contemplating, it is also very easy. Suppose we are not pure and do not have solid faith; In it, so many afflictions arise, thousands of them, with all kinds of methods, all kinds of different things. Everyone knows that studying precepts is very difficult! After old magician Hoang Nhat became a monk, he advised to review the three major collections of Nam Son[66], the three major collections are three treatises. He did not criticize or comment at all, just advised on a few points, punctuation, and punctuation, which took many years of effort. If we open it, even if we have literary knowledge, it is not easy to read and understand. When he (the founder of Dao Tuyen) wrote, [the original] didn't even have punctuation! The precepts are very difficult to learn, so when we receive the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, we must adhere to the Three Refuges and Five Precepts. The Five Precepts are the four basics. If you can keep the Five Precepts carefully, the basis of all good dharmas will be complete, and you can even gradually become a Buddha.

(Sutra) Like the great earth, necessarily medicine, cup, destruction, wood, wood, forest, and the stage of growth. Just as the physician is extremely good in upholding the four fundamental precepts, the wholesome dharma stage must be able to attain birth and growth. Like the great earth, all the mountains, Tieu Luan Vi mountain, Dai Luan Vi mountain, Dieu Cao mountain king, will be able to stay in peace. Just as she is extremely good in protecting the four basic precepts, the Shravaka Vehicles, attaining the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, the unsurpassed Mahayana, attain attainment of peace. Like the great earth, seek to obtain all the world's delicacies. Just like this robe, he is extremely good at protecting the four fundamental precepts, seeking to attain the complete mindfulness, concentration, total retention, peace and patience of the holy path, and the aspiration to Supreme Bodhi.
(Sutra: As if depending on the great earth, all herbs, grains, trees, forests are okay He only protects the four extremely good basic precepts, all good dharmas are born and grown on the great earth, all the mountains, Tieu Luan Vi mountain, Lord Dieu Cao mountain, all stay in peace. He only protects the four basic precepts like that, the Thanh Van Vehicle, and the Supreme Mahayana all rest in the great earth. He only protects the four precepts Such an extremely good basis, wishing to achieve all Mindfulness, Concentration, Total Abiding, peace and patience in the holy path, up to the Supreme Bodhi.

The four basic precepts are “lust, kill, steal, lie”. The precept "forbidden to drink alcohol" in the Five Precepts is not included. The precept “not drinking alcohol” is considered very small. Those four basic precepts, whether one takes refuge in the Three Jewels, or a disciple who takes the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, or a disciple of the Eight Precepts, up to the novices, novices, nuns, nuns, monks, nuns, and the seven disciples all follow. Why is it called the basic precepts? Because basic precepts can give birth to basic wisdom. If you violate these precepts, you will not be able to gain wisdom, and your blessings will also be lost. If you break the four basic precepts, all your good dharmas cannot abide.

Buddha said for example, because there is great earth, all types of food, medicines, flowers, and even trees can grow. We know: Without trees, we cannot survive, trees produce oxygen (Oxygen, oxygène). If the city lacks trees, it will be impossible to regulate oxygen. Without the great earth, all things could not exist, with this meaning. Likewise, using the great earth as an example, we must uphold the four basic precepts for the purpose of growing all our good dharmas. Like the earth, all mountains must rely on the earth to rest. All good dharmas must rely on the protection of the four basic precepts. If, after receiving the Three Refuges, one does not receive the Five Precepts, basically that person has not committed a violation. If that person violates these four basic precepts, he will be punished by national law. Violating these four basic precepts, from ancient times to the present, will be punished by national laws. Thus, that person will not commit a crime, but the merit and good dharma that that person has achieved will not be able to grow, and will grow very slowly!

If, after entering Buddhism, you hope to attain Meditation and attain Samadhi. “General maintenance” is samadhi, attaining dharani, up to attaining the Six Paramitas of all virtues, and even becoming a Buddha, but if you do not uphold these four basic precepts, you hope to achieve pure mindfulness, attain pure concentration, attain samadhi, it will be impossible, much less can you hope to become a Buddha! Just like the great earth does not choose, it is equal. Therefore, regardless of whether you have something clean or unclean, it does not discriminate, is equally preserved, there is no choice, it is impossible to say "if it is pure, we will maintain it, if it is not pure, we will not maintain it". The Buddha used this to compare a monk breaking the precepts. If you have broken the four basic precepts, what will happen again? As we said in the previous section, the king Kshatriya, or Brahmin, down to the two lay disciples, everyone must respect the monk, should not destroy, should not proclaim his faults!

(Sutra) Huu is like the great earth, pure, impure, the accepted stage. Extremely good and upholding the four basic precepts, good men and good women will be dressed like this. Trying to use the dharma air to access the dharma air, the mind is equal, there is no opportunity, there is no abuse, there is no self-cultivation, there is no hesitation, and the place of birth of necessarily good dharma is necessary. As good as the earth, all sentient beings can live together and enjoy life. Extremely good in upholding the four fundamental precepts,good men improve good women,reverence the horse as it is. pure faith. All sentient beings have no different thoughts, so the Four Dharmas are equally received, all sentient beings share the same dharma, receive the blissful Dharma, and naturally exist.".
(Sutra: Again, like the great earth, both the pure and the impure are maintained equally. The good men and good women who uphold the four basic precepts extremely well, are also like that: With regard to dharma objects and non-dharma objects, their minds are equal, do not criticize, do not ridicule, are not arrogant, do not carelessly rebuke or blame, can be the birthplace of all things. Good dharma. Again, like the great earth, all sentient beings take advantage of it in order to survive. The good men and good women who uphold the four basic precepts are just like that. Regarding the Dharma spoken by the Tathagata, they give rise to the purest faith and joy. For all sentient beings, there is no difference in thinking. Using the Four Dharmas to receive equality, all sentient beings follow the same principles and enjoy the Dharma to live on their own. also”).

Next, talk about [the relationship between] monks and monks, monks and monks. For a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts, what should be done? This Sangha is like the great earth, regarding the pure and impure, whether they maintain pure precepts or do not maintain pure precepts, they are still treated equally. However, if you keep the precepts pure, you will easily attain the holy path, easily escape afflictions, and easily leave suffering. In the past, you broke the four basic precepts, and even though you went through countless lives, you still suffered. Even if you can become a human again, you will either have crippled limbs, or an abnormal spirit, or you will have no merit or wisdom. Then [those people] will have nothing to do with concentration, recitation, or even taking care of doing meritorious deeds as mentioned in the previous section! If in the past the basic precepts were broken; At present, it will be very difficult to hear the Dharma again, we will have to go through countless countless kalpas, and it will be very difficult to meet the Three Jewels. Therefore, it is said that all good men and good women who uphold the precepts should be like the great earth. Sometimes it is a Dharma weapon, when you hear the Dharma you can receive and maintain it, and it is also a container that holds the Dharma. Sometimes, even though they hear the Dharma, it is not a container for the Dharma, it will leak out. Like a cup or bowl of water, there cannot be a hole as big as the eye of a needle. If there is a leak, the water will not be able to be contained, it will always flow away. But we can do a little mending, find things to mend the bowl. Currently, there is another way: use tape to cover the bottom, seal the hole, it won't leak; but still defective! The great earth can treat everything impure or pure equally.

Therefore, the Sangha in the Sangha, treating those who have become monks, or those who are lay people who receive the Five Precepts, are also receiving the four basic precepts, even though they have broken the precepts, your mind still treats them equally. Don't be sarcastic, don't laugh at them, don't act like: "I keep the precepts pure, you're a precept-breaker." Among our Dharma friends, there are many problems like that. The Buddha pointed out these issues bluntly, and everyone must pay special attention. We must use a mind of equality to treat them, do not be careless in blaming them, or even denouncing them or spreading their mistakes. Like our Dharma friends, even though we both receive the Three Refuges and Five Precepts from the same master, we still criticize each other. If it's not the same master, then there's no need to talk anymore! Those are all mistakes.

If maintained like that, it will cause all good dharmas to grow, and those who have done wrong things and broken the precepts will pray for repentance. After repentance, you will be pure; But the person who cannot repent, as long as that person has a shameful mind, has a remorseful mind, does not continue to do anything, for everything that has been committed, that person knows it was wrong. Even if he has not repented completely, that person will never continue to do it. Committing crimes is the same, but doing good is also the same, it's like being used to it, getting used to it, not doing it, their hearts are very restless! When I was in prison, I asked a petty thief: "Why do you steal other people's things? After stealing, you don't enjoy it." That person replied: "I see something that belongs to someone but I don't steal it. My heart is itchy, I can't sleep, and I can't swallow rice!" When he has finished stealing, he will not use it himself, take it and then throw it away, or give it to someone else, he will feel secure.

Furthermore, if you ask a butcher, [you will know] that person does not do (does not slaughter animals), and will not have peace of mind. Someone who commits a certain type of karma, that type of karma causes that person to continue doing evil, that person cannot repent. The Sea of ​​Sangha in Buddhism is the same, like the earth, all sentient beings on the earth enjoy it together and can live together. These four basic precepts make the Sangha good, make Buddhism flourish, and can exist for a long time in the world. Then if you keep the four basic precepts, the Buddha Dharma can last a long time in this world.

What is the greatest joy and pure faith? For all sentient beings, all sentient beings do not give rise to discrimination, do not think there is any difference. But there is a problem, since there is no difference, why are monks and nuns the same, but the precepts of the female community are so strict? There are three hundred and forty-eight precepts; Why do men only have two hundred and fifty precepts? That is not the difference! Why do monastics who receive the Bodhisattva precepts must receive ten major precepts and forty-eight minor precepts, while lay people can receive six major and twenty-eight minor precepts? It's not a difference in dharma, it's a matter of inborn ability, some people can accept it, some people can't! But [even though the number of precepts is different], they all require you to have pure faith, don't give birth to different ideas, the dharmas in the three vehicles are all equal!

For this base, that person can receive to this level, then tell them Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path. For people of different abilities, due to different levels, immediately tell them about almsgiving, morality, patience, meditation, wisdom, and tell them about the Six Dharma. That is not difference, but true equality. Tell him as much as he can receive! The Buddha had the Four Dharmas to receive equally and give alms without choosing the object. If we say that person is a Buddha or Bodhisattva, we will make offerings to him. That person is a suffering being, we will give it to him. Giving alms does not necessarily mean giving a little money, but also includes Dharma Giving: You preach the Dharma to that person, the first thing is giving alms. Like Ai Ngu means telling others the words they like to hear, not uttering cruel words, and not arbitrarily scolding others. For anyone, it's the same. Even if a child is only a few years old, he has self-esteem, so you are used to scolding him. If something goes wrong as a parent, they can give their child a quick slap, or hit them a few times. If he makes a few mistakes, he curses and shouts, don't do it!

And doing beneficial things for others is Loi Hanh. Regardless of language or action, or in terms of financial gain, whatever benefits others, do many things to benefit others. Colleagues are you who want to save others. Whatever they do, you do the same, only then can you easily approach them, making their hearts feel friendly and accepting. The Buddha taught us to use the Four Dharmas of Reception to receive all sentient beings. That way they will easily accept it. Because when Buddha Dharma existed in the world, all sentient beings were in the same direction. If they only obey, they will be able to attain joy in the Dharma, they will be able to gain joy in the Dharma. So “survival” includes two types: One type is survival according to worldly dharma, not competing with life, life with very few afflictions. Another type of survival is to stay in the teachings, that is, in the Buddha Dharma, regularly practicing the religion like that, nurturing one's own Dharma Body.

After the Buddha said this passage, Venerable Upa Ly felt puzzled and asked the Buddha: "How should I deal with the evil actions of monks?" The next paragraph will talk about that.

Sufficient, heaven and earth one firm, all things before the ground, united palm, respectfully, said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! As the Buddha said, extremely good in upholding the four basic precepts, good men and good women, all dharma air and non-dharma weapons, no mind equality, no chance, no blasphemy, no self-cultivation, no self-deception. Such as the attendants, the future monks, the good men, breaking the precepts, evil deeds, are truly non-monks, self-proclaimed. Monks, it's really not virtuous, claiming to be virtuous, are monks and monks of the same class, and so on, are you using such expedient means?
(Sutra: At that time, the Venerable Uba Ly heard the Buddha's teachings, stood up from his seat, and corrected Cut off your clothes, bow at the feet of the Buddha, untuck one shoulder of your robe, put your right knee close to the ground, clasp your hands, and respectfully say to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! As the Buddha said, good men and good women uphold the four basic precepts extremely well. They are equal in their minds towards dharma objects and non-dharma objects, they do not criticize, do not laugh at, are not proud of themselves, and do not carelessly rebuke or blame. If that is the case, then in the future life, there will be On-sho breaks the precepts and conducts evil deeds. He is not really a monk. He calls himself a monk. It is not really a holy life, but he claims to be a holy person. How will the Buddhist monks reprimand, punish, and expel those people?")

The Venerable Upāli is the foremost dharma-holder among the Buddha's disciples. The Vinaya Pitaka was compiled by the Venerable Uba Ly, who presides over the compilation. He protects the precepts. He heard the Buddha say that everyone must be equal like that, but still did not reprimand the monks for breaking the precepts or doing evil deeds. If so, what should the Sangha do? He immediately asked the Buddha. The first part of this passage talks about the rituals when He made inquiries. He asked, according to the Buddha's teachings, good men and good women uphold the four basic precepts, that is the Dharma weapon. If someone who is not a Dharma weapon breaks the precepts, [specifically] breaks the four basic precepts, how should we treat them equally? It's not even allowed to criticize or satirize them, nor is it allowed to tease them.

A Bhikkhu who maintains the precepts must not be arrogant or conceited, and cannot arbitrarily scold or condemn a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts. If that's the case, in the future, those who break the precepts and commit evil deeds are basically not monks, claiming to be monks, what they do is polluted. That person claims to be a virtuous person, a pure person, [then] in the great assembly, how should we punish that person?

(Sutra) The Buddha denounced the Venerable Upa Ly saying: "The end of the world does not promise pagans, the common cause is the sin, The upper self does not promise that the monks do not follow the dharma, if they violate the precepts, what if they do not comply with the dharma? If they do not follow the dharma, if they do not follow the dharma, or if they obey, it is a great sin.
(Sutra: The Buddha told Venerable Upa Ly: - I absolutely do not allow pagans and worldly people to be punished for breaking the precepts, and I also do not allow Buddhist monks who do not follow the Dharma, to carelessly rebuke, to condemn them for breaking the precepts, let alone expel them? If they do not follow the Dharma and arbitrarily reprimand or condemn them for breaking the precepts, border-radius: 4px;"> Turn on the number, or chase it away again, you will commit a big sin).

In Buddhism, “non-Buddhist” means not belonging to Buddhism. There are also lay people, lay people, even kings and ministers, [Buddha] does not allow them to punish monastics for their sins, does not allow them to punish monks for their misconduct. If it is necessary to rebuke or condemn them, they must obey the dharma. What dharma is it to obey? The Buddha has seven types of precepts for Bhikkhus who break the precepts. What are the seven types of sanctions? The first is the practice of dharma, the second is the dharma of reciting alms, the fourth is the dharma of natural punishment, the fifth is the dharma of disobeying sins, the sixth is the dharma of many people (whether or not many people approve of whether the person is allowed to repent), the seventh is the dharma of repentance (allowing the offender to self-repent and repent of his sins)[67]. Must rely on these things to do the Yet Ma method.

In order to count the sins of a Bhikkhu, one must obey the Dharma, which also means to reprimand or condemn the Bhikkhu for breaking the precepts, it must be [done] by the monks. One person cannot, at least there must be three or more monks to be allowed to offend a monk. You don't like him, see him breaking the precepts, internal troubles arise, then arbitrarily scold, blame, blame the monk for breaking that precept, or kick him out, [or more formally] “retired” .

“Scheming is a great sin” (Instantly committing a great sin). That is your own sin, you must accept punishment. That crime is of course not a Bodhisattva Sangha crime, nor is it a Paramita crime, but the crime of cursing the Sangha, the crime of disregarding the Three Jewels, the crime of destroying the Three Jewels. Your sin is very great. Therefore, after finishing speaking, the Buddha immediately told Upali...

(Sutra) Uba Ly! Like the golden wisdom, the ten are illegal, the ear ha is breaking the precepts, taking advantage of the great sin, the wise men of the false stage do not accept it. Ha class vi ten? One person, discord with the Sangha, the king's money, the ear-ha sent to break the precepts. The two monks, discord with the Sangha, the Pham-chi assembly, the hurrah-ha-ji breaking the precepts. Tam fake, disharmonious monks, officials of the money, the ear ha sent to break the precepts. Four false, discordant monks, wealthy people, lay people, all of them, they break the precepts and break the precepts. Five fake people, women in front of them, hat hur ha ji broke the precepts and turned on the number. Luc fake, the men in front of the crowd, the ear-ha-gi broke the precepts-so. Seven people, pure people, all over the world, they break the precepts and break the precepts. The eight fake ones, the multi-bich-sho, the b-soni money, the rat-h-ha-e breaking the precepts-b-sō. The nine people, full of resentment and money, will break the precepts and break the precepts. Ten people, filled with anger and resentment, rushed to break the precepts. Such as the ten strains, illegal reputation, ear ha, breaking the precepts, and committing a serious crime. Is it really true that the audience will not accept it, let alone not really? Dear friends, you have committed a great sin!
(Sutra: Hey Uba Ly! You should know that there are ten illegal types of reckless reprimands and condemnation. If you break the precepts, you are guilty of a great sin, which should not be accepted by wise people. One is discord with the Sangha, recklessly scolding you, and condemning you for breaking the precepts. Second, discord with the Sangha, recklessly scolding you. Third, discord with the Sangha, recklessly reprimanding you, and disobeying the Sangha for breaking the precepts In front of wealthy people and lay people, one should scold them lightly and commit the crime of breaking the precepts. Fifth, in front of women, one should scold them lightly and commit the crime of breaking the precepts. Sixth, in front of men, one should scold them lightly and commit the crime of breaking the precepts. Seventh, in front of pure people, one should scold them recklessly. Eighth, in front of many monks and nuns, one should scold them lightly Ninth is the sin of scolding and rashly scolding someone who has pre-existing resentment, and the sin of scolding and breaking the precepts. Ten is the sin of scolding and breaking the precepts in the heart. Ten types of such actions are called illegitimate and reckless scolding. If you scold or commit a sin based on the truth, you should not do it, let alone if it is not true [That crime] is also a big sin!)

You now know that “there are ten types of illegal acts of breaking the precepts of the up-sō, plotting a great sin” (there are ten types of illegal acts of recklessly scolding and condemning the crime of breaking the precepts of the turn-sō, you will be guilty of a great crime). Whenever it is consistent with those ten types of scolding of a monk, [the crime] will be established. People with wisdom should not do that. What are ten? I said ten types of illegality, what are the ten types? “Monks are not in harmony”, you must pay close attention to this! All the Sangha [are not in harmony], that is, their opinions are not in harmony, or their interests are not in harmony. Everyone knows if opinions are not in harmony, you have your view, I have mine, there are a lot of disputes! Disharmony of interests means distribution of permanent objects, unreasonable distribution, of course there will be no harmony.

In the Mainland, it's the same, [when dividing money for donations and donations], the Duong Tutor, Tri Guest, old monk in the temple, they take twenty coins, you [not holding a position] only get one coin. During Buddha's time, this was not possible! Buddha also only accepted one coin! I just give an example, in fact, when the Buddha was alive, no one offered money, nor did the Buddha accept money. He forbade Bhikkhus to hold gold and silver. Offering robes, monks' robes, if you want to offer robes, each person has one set. After the Venerable Ca Luu Da Di (Kālodayin) passed away, the property he owned was worth sixty thousand.

Sixty thousand back then, I don't know how much money it was. When the Buddha was in the world, the Venerable Ca Luu Da Di appeared greedy and deliberately made that appearance. He attained Arhatship, achieving selflessness. Why does He still have to do that? It appears that in this way [Buddha] can conveniently control the precepts! I give that example.

Therefore, there are ten types of things that are not allowed to reprimand a monk who breaks the precepts like that. The first condition is “The Sangha is not in harmony”, you cannot do Buddhist work, which is inherently inharmonious. Or in front of the king, “shat-rha-ha-cai-breaking the precepts-so” (recklessly reprimanding, condemning the Bhikkhu for breaking the precepts). The king came to the temple, of course the monk who broke the precepts could not accept [being reprimanded or condemned], he also looked down on the king. A monk who breaks the precepts is very arrogant. He doesn't even receive the precepts. What is he afraid of? Second, the Sangha is not in harmony, in that Pham-chi[68] practices pure conduct, [“Pham-chi” in India] like a rich man or Confucian scholar in China. Right in front of them, one cannot blame the monks for their mistakes. Third, the Sangha is not in harmony. In front of a superior, a local official, or a high-ranking official, you cannot blame the Bhikkhu's faults or blame him for any wrongdoing. This should not be the case! Fourth, the Sangha is not in harmony. In front of the elders, elders, and lay people, in front of the elders and lay people of lay people, we cannot easily blame the Bhikkhu for breaking the precepts. Fifth, when dealing with women, you should not blame a monk for breaking the precepts. Sixth, in front of lay men, do not lightly blame the monks for their mistakes. Seventh, in front of pure people, do not lightly blame the monks for their mistakes. Those pure people live in temples and pagodas and are not monks. For example, if we have someone who comes to do a little work, or to do meritorious deeds, they are called “pure people”. But because they have been in the temple for a long time, you should not blame the monks for their mistakes in front of them. Eighth, in front of a large number of monks and nuns, everyone is gathering, [that is] in front of many monks and bhikshunis, do not blame the monks for fear that the monk [being talked about here] is a monk who breaks the precepts! Ninth, due to facing someone who already has a grudge from before, that Bhikkhu has a grudge against others. You should not confront a person who has a grudge against him, then scold him and blame him for his sins, you should not! Tenth, holding resentment in your heart, resentment has arisen in your heart, you immediately blame the monks, you should not! Even though that person breaks the precepts, you cannot be careless. If you have not adopted the correct method to point out his faults, you will not be able to reprimand or blame him for his sins!

“As shown in the ten categories, illegitimate names and names of the ear ha send breaking the precepts and breaking the precepts” (Ten types like that are called illegal and recklessly reprimanding and condemning the sins of monks who break the precepts): Here there is a problem, everyone should reflect a bit: Bhikkhus have broken the precepts and the Buddha still protects them. What's the point of that? Why not allow others to reprimand them? Don't even allow others to report their crimes? All Buddhas in the past were like that! Even though those monks have broken the precepts, the pure seeds still remain. When that person has a thought of receiving the precepts, in that one thought, until the process of becoming a monk, in the future, he will definitely be able to become a Buddha. For that reason, we think that all sentient beings who hear the Buddha Dharma, the Bodhisattvas who can be close to the Buddha Dharma, will definitely be able to become Buddhas. When did you become a Buddha? Not sure, it will take a long time! They have sown the seeds, they will definitely take root, sprout, grow, and can definitely become Buddhas.

“The set of robes is really like that of the audience, it is not acceptable to accept it, not to mention it is not true” (If based on the truth to reprimand or blame, it should not be accepted, let alone not true): That person made a mistake; Breaking the precepts is a fact, also a real situation. It should be [done] in the Sangha, according to the Dharma of the Sangha to punish that person's sins. There are twenty monks, ten monks, or [at least] three monks, relying on the Yet Ma method like that to punish that person. In the next section of the text, an example will be given. If you do not do so, it will be illegal. Furthermore, whether that story [breaking the precepts] that you heard is true or not still needs to be investigated. But if [just hearing about] that makes you commit a crime, then it's not right! Any monk who rebukes or commits a crime in that way is also guilty of a great sin. "If you receive [complaints], if you rely on the truth to rebuke or condemn, you should not accept it [immediately before investigating clearly], let alone [hastily reprimand or condemn based on accusations] that are not based on the truth). What does this word Tho refer to? If someone makes a complaint, when it comes time for the Sangha to act, we should not immediately accept [the accusation to reprimand or condemn the accused person], first of all, we should investigate. Investigate clearly and then accept [guilty conviction]. If it is true, you must be careful, because [not being careful like that] can easily destroy the Sangha.

For example, the Bhikkhu Dai Thien (Mahadeva) in India was reprimanded and condemned, so he single-handedly divided into a separate community, consisting of five hundred people, to establish his own dharma, that is, with the addition of Dai Thien's dharma, [often called] “The five dharmas of Dai Thien”. This is the case with the famous generals of the precepts, because of disagreement in opinions, the [Sangha] is divided. After the Buddha entered Nirvana and compiled the precepts, he divided into twenty groups, that is, at that time divided into twenty sects[69]. That's because of disagreement. You agree that this Bhikkhu breaks the precepts and wants to commit the Dharma of the Buddha, I do not agree. If your group agrees, then you can practice the Dharma. If we don't agree, I will separate into separate groups. At that time, it was divided into twenty sects. You have to study the precepts to know this. This is specifically about Bhikkhus harmonizing them. Regarding this issue, the Buddha was extremely cautious and said a lot.

(Sutra) Resurrection of the ten illegal races is recommended to break the precepts, commit a sin, intellectuals Heron does not like life. Ha class vi ten? First of all, the rest of the pagans ha sent a pop-so. The second person does not maintain the precepts and stays at home in white clothes. Tam fake, creating Vo Intermittent crime of ha ha bo-so. Four fake people, slandering the Dharma. The five hypocrites, destroying the sages and saints, Ha Ki Bu So. Six people, crazy and crazy, have a crazy heart. Seven people, suffering from depression and anxiety. The eight monks and monks of the four directions have pure people. Jiu fake, guard forest man ha ki pop-so. The 10 wrongdoers will be punished. Such as the illegal act of breaking the precepts, committing a serious crime. If the iron robe is truly accepted, the heron will not accept it, not to mention it is not true! Those who accept it, the heron will commit a great sin.
adults, wise people should not follow. What are the ten? One is that other non-Buddhist people rebuke and condemn. Second, those who do not uphold the precepts rebuke and condemn and condemn Crazy, confused, reprimanded, punished, punished, rebuked by monks of the four directions incur a great sin. If based on the truth, you should not accept it, let alone accept it. Those who accept it will also commit a great sin.)

Don't accept, don't take on this type of problem. What are ten? Do not [allow] non-Buddhists to reprimand or blame a Bhikkhu. A layman's white robe does not maintain the precepts of reprimanding or reprimanding a monk. “forbidden precepts” [mentioned here] is a lay precept. You receive the Five Precepts or the Eight Precepts. The Buddha forbids, according to the Law, white-robed lay people cannot reprimand or punish monks. The third person who committed the crime, Vo Giap, reprimanded and condemned the crime. You have committed the crime of Non-Infringement, and you cannot even reprimand or condemn the Bhikkhu. Even though you have repented, you still cannot reprimand or punish a monk. Fourthly, those who slander the Dharma cannot be reprimanded or punished by monks. Fifth is the person who slanders, slanders, and rebukes the saints and saints. This type of person cannot reprimand or punish a monk.

Therefore, the lay robe reprimands and condemns the pure monks, you have committed a crime, committing the crime of Non-Infringement. For a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts, you cannot reprimand or condemn that person. First of all, you should check whether you are pure or not. In the above part is the harmony of the Sangha. If the Sangha does not get along, it will not be possible to condemn the Bhikkhu's sins.

“Six is ​​a fool, a crazy person with a crazy mind, he is a crazy person, his mind is crazy, he reprimands him, he blames him for his anger): Your insides are abnormal, your words are not trustworthy. Ninth is the one who takes care of gardens and forests. Take care of the forest garden of the Sangha, and also be the guardian of the monks' property. They cannot reprimand or punish a monk. "Ten are punished by being punished by a monk who is punished and reprimanded by being punished by being punished by a monk.

Ten types as above, “like the illegal thirties ha e breaking the precepts, plotting a great crime. If they really accept the wrong person, the heron will not accept it” (The ten types of reprimanding and condemning illegal crimes like that will commit a great sin. If they rely on the truth to rebuke and condemn the crime, they will also commit a great sin. should not be accepted): The Sangha should not be accepted, even though the above types of people speak the truth, they should not be accepted, because [their accusations] are "illegal". Moreover, they are not telling the truth! If anyone accepts [those accusations] and then reprimands the monk, he will commit a great sin. Having said that, can a monk who breaks the precepts live with the Sangha?

(Sutra) Restore the Upasam Ly! Weak people turn on the number, break the forbidden precepts, harm the Sangha together.
