If you commit a light crime, accept light punishment, be respectful and repent of the crime”.
(Sutra: Hey Up Ba Ly! If there is a monk who violates the precepts in the company of the Sangha. Among the Sangha, there are other monks who follow the rules and all are complete, all five virtues are not perfect, you should stand up from your seat, straighten your clothes, respectfully bow at the feet of the Sangha, come first and break the evil precepts, please. Then listen to the sin, say this: ‘Elder, think about it! I now want to point out the things that the elder has committed, state the truth, not falsely, at the right time, not at the wrong time, speak softly, not rudely, harshly, kindly, not angry, beneficial, not harmful, because the Dharma eyes and Dharma lamp of the Tathagata will shine brightly for a long time. I will point out the elder's sins according to the Dharma Elder'. If that person is willing to listen, it will be stated according to the dharma and the truth. If that person does not listen, he should bow at the feet of the Venerable monk and respectfully say: 'If such a person commits such a thing, I will state it according to the five dharmas and according to the truth. At that time, the Venerable will speak up in the Sangha You should consider and observe the person committing the crime and the person being committed, as well as the things committed that are false, real, light, or serious, based on the Vinaya and Sutra Pitaka (Sutta Pitaka) for the means of questioning, verifying, consoling, and reprimanding, and using seven types of dharma to properly eliminate them. If you commit a serious crime, you should punish it severely punish minor crimes, make the person ashamed, repent of the crimes).

That person breaks the forbidden precepts, that is, he has violated the Buddha's prohibitions, but is still in the Sangha, living with the Sangha. Thus, the other Bhikkhu is someone who obeys the rules, does not violate the precepts, is pure, practices the pure precepts, all are complete, all five virtues are not perfect. I am afraid that those five virtues are not the same as the five virtues often said. The five virtues are on the day of summer retreat, can be settled. “Tu Tu”. What does “Tu Tu” mean? Then you will point out each other's mistakes. That is, when you enter the retreat from the full moon of April to the full moon of the seventh lunar month, you will repent of the sins you have committed in the past. That is, in this short period of time, you will commit any wrongdoings in that year? You yourself can point out your mistakes "seeing, hearing, doubting". Even doubts can be expressed, but if they are not true, there will be no repentance!

A monk has an angry mind and says another monk commits impure conduct, but in reality, what crime does he say? Because he saw that the male goat and the female goat were doing impure things, [the monk had an angry mind] so he said that the other monk was also practicing impure deeds. Does this kind of thing count as truth? That is called "unreal views, unreal views" (what is seen is not real, what is stated is also not real). That's called "doubt", this crime doesn't count! Although he publicly repented in front of other monks, he had to consider whether the crime was big or small. For a big crime, three Bhikkhus, for a bigger crime, ten Bhikkhus. After repenting purely, practice skillfully. That is Tu Tu. Tu Tu has five virtues: Speak for yourself, have no obstacles for yourself, no shame, no embarrassment, no doubts. “From the four words to the letter, the four tri tri chi” [meaning] I think to myself that I am guilty of that crime, is that really a sin or not? I still don't know, so I say it so everyone can confirm it for me. Everyone says: "You did not commit that crime", then you will not commit it. If you say you committed a sin, you immediately repent. That is called “five virtues” (one's own five virtues).

Second is “the five virtues of guilt” (five virtues when counting sins), also known as Forgiving the Five Virtues. “Knowing the time” (Knowing the time): You must know when to be able to commit the sin of a Bhikkhu. Knowing that this is the right time to confess in front of the Sangha to repent. It's the right time. Normally, when a mass of Sangha gathers, first of all, you come out and ask permission. If that person (the accused person) accepts, [that is] "you just state the crime". Once that person accepts, you can commit the crime. If it is true, it is beneficial for that person, beneficial for yourself, beneficial for the Sangha, you must be gentle, kind, and have a compassionate heart. Those are the Five Virtues, collectively known as the Five Virtues of Self-Forgiveness. With such five virtues, the five virtues of oneself and others are complete. Such a monk stood up from his seat, neatly arranged his clothes, “respectfully bowed to the monks” (respectfully bowed at the feet of the assembly of monks), and bowed to the assembly. Next, he faced the monk who broke the precepts and said: "I will punish you, do you allow it or not?" “Say it like this” (Say it like this): How to talk to that person? Say "elder remembers": Teacher, think, think, remember a little, now I want to tell you about the crime you committed.

“The elder has committed the crime of the elder's ego” (I now want to point out what the elder has committed): I speak the truth, not an illusion. Now is the right time, not the wrong time. Now I am gentle, kind, and soft-spoken, not harsh or cruel. I don't have any anger, I want to make the Sangha pure, to make the teacher practice pure. I do this out of kindness, not out of anger. I want to benefit you, not harm or reduce your morality. Because it causes the Dharma eye treasury and the Tathagata's Dharma lamp to shine brightly in the human world forever. For that reason, I ask the elder to allow me to tell you about your mistake.

“Listener” (Listen, allow): If the monk above hears the monk who wants to condemn the crime say it correctly, allowing him to tell it, then he can condemn that crime according to the Dharma. If the other person, that is, the accused person, does not accept or pay attention to the person asking for remission of sins, saying: "What you said is not true, I did not make a mistake", then what should that person [asking for remission of guilt] do? He will pay homage to the Venerable.

“Venerable” or Venerable Upali, or those who have been ordained for a long time, are also Venerable monks who have become monks[70] high, master maintain that dharma assembly. Immediately bowing to that Venerable, he would also respectfully say the same, saying that such a Bhikkhu had committed such a crime. "The five dharmas, as they really are" (I will point out the five dharmas as they really are): Those five dharmas refer to the first five types of precepts [in the Seven Pure Precepts of the Bhikkhu], which are the Paramitas (Pārājika), the Sangha (Saṃghāvaśeṣa), the ninety precepts of the Badiṣikas (Pāyattika, Single Fall), up to thirty-three. The precepts of Ni Sa Ba Di De (Naiḥsargika-pāyattika), are also four dharmas, plus two precepts of the Undetermined type, but the two Undetermined precepts (Aniyata) will not be counted and can be ignored. There are also one hundred things in the Dharma Learning Assembly (Saṃbahulāh Śaiksa-dharmāh), all according to the precepts in the precepts, they must be stated in the truth.

In addition, there are five dharmas called Yet Ma Dharma, which is the story of monastics. These five dharmas should only be spoken to monastics, not to lay people. In addition, there are five dharmas that need to be chanted when the Sangha has gathered. “Elector” (holding up a card) is like a vote, [indicating] whether you agree to charge that person or not? If there is one person who does not agree, it will not be possible to commit a crime. There are many more dharmas, just to talk to monks. For such Sangha, the Venerable Bhikkhu should observe. "Nong, no": The person who commits the crime and the person who is blamed, the story of the person telling the crime and the crime committed is fake, real, made up, or real, serious, or light. Then, based on Vinaya, that is, obeying the Vinaya Pitaka, Sutra is the Sutra Pitaka, obeying the sutras spoken by the Buddha, obeying the precepts taught by the Buddha, “means” is the skillful means to test it once. At that time, both comfort and reprimand that person.

“Of course seven types of dharma, such as to destroy” (Use seven types of dharma, according to the right reason to eliminate): It is also the seven types of dharma as we just said, that is, reciting the dharma (the dharma of thinking and remembering), the four dharmas, the dharma itself (the dharma speaking on its own, stating the sin itself), until finally that person has committed a great sin. too small, like grass covering the ground, to repent like that in front of the crowd. But [the crimes committed] are not the four fundamentals (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying). Breaking the four basics is not possible! For serious crimes, use the method of treating serious crimes; for minor crimes, use the method of treating light crimes. “Repenting of the sinful spirit, repenting of the crime” (Making that person ashamed, repenting of the crime he committed), achieves what purpose? Causing a monk to break the precepts will definitely show repentance; From now on, don't do it again! The Sangha punished that person, told him to worship, and forced him to “face the wall” (look at the wall to repent). Detention means not allowing that person to go out. These are all sanctions methods. Depending on the situation at that time, decide. Currently, this dharma is almost impossible to implement, and the Sangha itself is not so harmonious! Nowadays it's "you charge me, I charge you", the Sangha is even more chaotic, the only thing to do is obey the sutras and repent! Is it possible to do so? For this reason, the Venerable Upali again asked the Buddha.

(Sūtra) At that time, Upa Ly spoke to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! Weakness is too real, evil deeds are upsetting, The power of the white robe, or the power of talent, or the power of literature, or the power of eloquence, or the power of disciples, are like the power of all the great powers, the great monks of the Venerable Bo-sō, the monks of To Dat Lam, the Bhikkhus, and the Mahatma Ly Ca, like the teachings of the Dharma, the stages are not acceptable. Buddha's words: "Uu Ba Ly! The Venerable upheld the Tripitaka, in harmony with the Sangha, commanded the envoy to report to the king, ministers, and powerful spiritual assistants. In the future, the punishment will be followed in accordance with the law." At that time, Uba Ly said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! If you are too weak, evil deeds will turn into numbers, if you are rich in wealth, or if you have great knowledge, or if you have the power of eloquence, or if you have the ability to be cunning and expedient, then you will be happy with the king, the great minister, if you break the precepts and violate the law with integrity, you will tolerate such crimes as evil, if you do not listen, you will be punished according to the real law. At this time, are the Sangha satisfied and so on?" Buddha's words: "Upa Ly! In the middle of the Sangha, if you are a serious sinner with the appearance of a false path, then the Sangha will let go of the wisdom. If you are in the Sangha, if you are a serious sinner with the appearance of a false person, then the Sangha will harmonize with the Dharma and practice Buddha Dharma. Upa Ly! For example, like oats, in the middle of the veins, the roots, branches, limbs, leaves, The data vein is similar, the impure vein is pure, when the wisdom comes out, when the farmer accepts the right to let go of wisdom, when the farmer is terrible with impure pure veins, the pure roots are scattered, the air is filled with dirt, the precepts are turned on, the white clothes are similar to the force, the position is in the middle of the Sangha, the majesty, appearance, and data of the Sangha are similar. In the Sangha, the good will of the gods is enlightened. In the Sangha, the gross sin shows the false appearance, then the Sangha accepts the right to let go of the wisdom. In the Sangha, the gross sin shows the false appearance, then the Sangha accepts the Dharma, and the spirit emerges from the Buddha Dharma.
(Sutra: At that time, Upalya said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One, if the evil action of the Buddha is truly at fault, relying on the strength of the layman, or the strength of money, or the strength of literature, or the strength of eloquence, or the strength of disciples, due to such forces, oppresses and resists the Sangha and the Venerable who upholds the Sutras." The Vinaya Pitaka, the Abhidhamma Pitaka, and the Abhidhamma Pitaka, do not obey the teachings of the Buddha. How should the Buddha punish him? "Venerable Buddha, you should, along with the Sangha, send someone to report to the king and the great mandarins so that they can be punished according to the law." At that time, Upasaka said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! The guilty Busa used the power of money, or the power of rhetoric, or the power of skillful means, to make those kings and ministers happy, all staying in the group of cliques that broke the precepts, illegally, tolerated the crimes of such evil Busa, and did not accept the punishment according to the law. At that time, what should the Sangha do? If, in the Sangha, the gross and gross sins of that person are not yet clearly revealed, the Sangha should temporarily leave it there. If the monks' gross and gross sins are clearly revealed, then the Sangha, in harmony, will expel that person from the Dharma. For example, in a field of barley, [the weeds] have sprouts, stems, branches, and leaves that are similar to barley, making the barley unclean That type of grass has not yet bloomed, at that time, the farmer should temporarily leave it there. The rice has sprouted, at that time, the farmer is afraid that they will pollute the barley, so he uproots and throws it out into the field. Breaking the precepts of Vo Y Hanh is like that, relying on the powers of lay people, etc. in the Sangha, their majesty and appearance are similar to the Sangha, the impure Sangha is pure, not even a good deity. In the Sangha, the gross and gross sin [of the Bhikkhu who breaks that precept] has not yet been revealed. At that time, the Sangha temporarily leaves it there. If the good spirits have discovered that the gross and gross sin has been revealed in the Sangha, then the Sangha should harmonize and chase that person out of the Buddhadharma.)

“Ma Dat Ly Ca” (Mātŗkā) is the Abhidharma Pitaka. [Bhikkhus who break the precepts and conduct evil actions against] the correct teachings in the Tripitaka are not accepted. The Buddha immediately told the Venerable Upalya: "The Venerable Upasaka holds the Tripitaka" [meaning that the Venerable Upasū] is a person who is well-versed in the Tripitaka, Vinaya, Abhidhamma, "harmonizes with the Sangha" (should be with the Sangha), you should unite the entire assembly, the assembly in the assembly unanimously agreed, send a monk to tell the king and ministers, hoping that the king and ministers will not cooperate. With bad actions, Bhikkhus will increase the power of the Sangha. After that, exactly as it is, obey the law to punish and discipline that person!

The Venerable Uba Ly said again: "World-Honored One! If that Buddha is a person with evil faults, has evil deeds, has the power of money, bribes the king, bribes the great mandarins." Money can be magic! Everyone knows: When Buddha was alive, there was this situation! If not, how can we establish precepts? “Or possess multi-literate ability” (Or have multi-literate ability): That person listens to a lot of sutras, is very fluent in argument, and has unhindered ability to argue. That person is guilty, arguing that he is innocent, arguing that black is white; There are also people like that! Sometimes they can even quote sutras and arguments [to prove their innocence]. “Or maybe use all kinds of force and means” (Or use all kinds of force and means): Think of all kinds of methods to destroy the Sangha, making it impossible for you to punish that person's sins. Either that person makes the kings and ministers happy, uses all kinds of methods to bribe the kings and ministers, or turns black and white upside down. Those kings and ministers are all the gang of the monk who broke the precepts, they are friends of that person, belonging to that person's party. Tolerating the sins of the monks like that, the king and his ministers will not help the Sangha become pure. “At that time, what should the Sangha do?” (At that time, what should the Sangha do?): At that time, how should we handle it?

“Buddhist saying: - Upa Ly! If you practice Non-Yhaha, you do not follow the path taught by the Buddha.” That's called Vo Y Hanh. But “the middle Sangha” (in the Sangha), that person has committed a crime, no matter gross or serious, up to light crime, as long as it is not obvious, not public, not known to everyone, still not revealed. “If you turn on someone who practices Non-Yhaha, in the Sangha, the sign of a gross sin will be exposed to the wrong person” (If you turn that person on to commit Non-Yhaha, in the Sangha, the gross and serious sin will be revealed): In the Sangha, everyone knows; At that time, the Sangha should obey the Dharma, rely on my Dharma to expel that person, expel that person from the Sangha, causing that person to leave the Dharma.

Buddha again told Up Ba Ly: For example, oat. Oats grown in the field have not yet bloomed. In the barley fields, the things [wild rice or other weeds] have sprouts, stems, branches, and leaves exactly like good barley, you can't clearly identify them. Just because it has no seeds or hasn't set seeds yet! “Impure pure vein” means adulterated wild grass or rice mixed with pure barley; At that time, they were still young seedlings.

“Belgium grass” (Those grasses): Before they bloom and set seeds, you still cannot tell if they are oats. You handle it, others still won't accept it, wait until the rice has sprouted, then you will know what is not barley. Weeds of course do not bloom, do not become food, and do not form grains of rice. Only then will the farmer uproot and throw it away. But when it first sprouts, the farmer can't tell the difference. Waiting until the rice sprouts, it will be concluded that it cannot produce seeds, then the farmer will pull the weeds from the roots, throw them out of the field, and throw them out into the field. Bhikkhus practice non-clothing and break precepts in the same way. He relies on the powers of the lay people, resides in the Sangha, and has the same majesty and appearance as the Sangha.

“Impurity of the mass of people” [means] causing the pure mass of people to be tainted, unable to be pure. At the same time, the good gods have not yet discovered, the good gods have not denounced, the Dharma guardian gods have not denounced, the gross and serious sins in the Sangha have not yet been clearly revealed. At that time, the Sangha did not care about him and left it there. When the good god was discovered, the dharma protector was discovered, his gross and serious sins were clearly revealed to the Sangha. At that time, the Sangha should harmonize and expel that guy according to the Dharma.

(Sutra) Uba Ly! For example, like the great ocean, with no corpses, the Thanh Van Sangha's disciples obeyed like this, no evil, breaking the precepts, evil deeds turned the corpses together. Weaknesses break the precepts, evil actions turn on the number, the Sangha harmonizes with the community, the evil turns on, the force of talent, or multi-literate force, or from the force, or the kind of skill and means, the spirit of the king, the great minister rejoices, the order breaks the precepts, the illegality equals the middle, the majestic force persecutes the Sangha, the spirit is like breaking the precepts and turns the data on the Sangha. At that time, are the Sangha in submission?" Buddha said: “Upa Ly! At that time, the middle monks should always repent of you, upholding the precepts, protecting the precepts, and not accepting anger or insults breaking the precepts. On the occasion of giving notice to the king, a minister, or a terrorist, if you do not report it, please let go of the original residence and leave the land."
(Sutra: Hey Upa Ly! Just as the ocean does not contain dead bodies, my Thanh Van Sangha disciples are the same, not living together with dead bodies. Upasaka breaks the precepts and conducts evil deeds." At that time, Upasaka said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One, if the monks had broken the precepts and committed evil deeds, they would have been expelled by the Sangha in harmony, so he would use his wealth and resources. Or the power of eloquence, or the use of all kinds of skillful means, to make the king and his ministers happy, all stay in a gang that violates the precepts, violates the law, and uses powerful force to oppress the Sangha, and forces them to let the monks break the precepts to live with the monks? At that time, what should the monks do? "At that time, there was a monk in the Sangha who could repent, be ashamed, and protect them You should not be angry or curse at someone who breaks the precepts. You should only explain clearly to the king or minister. If you are afraid of being bullied or oppressed but do not explain clearly, you should leave the place you are staying and live somewhere else."

If you jump into the sea and die, the sea will definitely use its waves to push your body back to shore. The sea does not contain corpses. "I, the disciples of the Thanh Van Sangha, all of our disciples are dressed like this, not evil, breaking the precepts, and living together with the evil deeds of the corpses of the Thanh Van Sangha" (My disciples of the Thanh Van Sangha are also like that, they do not live with the "corpses" of the monks who break the precepts and commit evil deeds), absolutely do not live with that person! “At that time, Upasaya said to the Buddha: - World-Honored One! If you break the precepts, do evil deeds, the Sangha in harmony with the community of devotion, evilness, or talent, or multi-literate power, or from eloquence, or skillful means, the power of the king, the great minister will be happy.” Breaking the precepts, that evil action was already expelled by the Sangha in harmony, but he used the power of money, or the power of literature, or the power of rhetoric, or the power of all kinds of skillful means to make the king and his ministers happy): The king and his ministers both sided with the Bhikkhus who broke the precepts, gathered factions and formed parties, used their power and authority to bully and coerce the Sangha, forcing them to live with the Bhikkhus like that. In the past, Indian kings did this a lot. Therefore, the Sangha was divided into two groups. Bhikkhus who break the precepts still have people who agree with them. For example, bhikshus who indulge in distractions and live with them. Therefore, even during the Buddha's time in the world, there was this phenomenon of Sangha division!

So what should we do? Chasing them, they don't go, they stay in the Sangha. “Buddhist saying: - Upa Ly! At that time, a loyal monk who is able to repent, upholds the precepts of up-sū, is a strong protector, does not accept anger, breaks the precepts of up-sō, on his birthday reports to the king, a minister, or a great mandarin without reporting it, wishes to let go of the original residence, goes away to the land” (Buddha said: - Hey Up-sū! At that time, in the Sangha there was an up-sū who could repent, sorry If you are shy, keep the precepts, for the sake of protecting the precepts, do not get angry or scold the king or ministers for breaking the precepts. Or if you are afraid of being bullied or coerced and do not clearly tell the king and ministers, you should leave your current place and live somewhere else separately. That's schizophrenic, what to do? The solution is for the good monk to leave and find another place to live himself. You can't tease him, hide yourself! That's what it means. Still not allowed to control or punish that person. This clearly shows that the king's good faith was surrounded by evil forces at that time!

Devadhartha and King Ajatasatru wanted to usurp the throne, [Devadatta] sent Ajatasatru to usurp the throne of his father Ajatasatru. He said: "When you become emperor, I will become Buddha." During Buddha's time, this kind of thing happened. Besides, he is still very evil. Due to his influence, he was Anand's brother, also of the royal family. Therefore, he used all kinds of methods to harm Buddha. At the top of the mountain, he used a rock to crush the Buddha. Unable to press down on the Buddha, it stabbed and caused the Buddha's body to bleed. At that moment, the great earth cracked open, quickly sucking Devadatta in, trapping his body in hell. Destroying the harmony of the Sangha also [will incur sin] in the same way!

After Upabali finished asking, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately stood up from his seat, turned to the Buddha, and said: "World-Honored One! At that time, the beings in this world, the beings in the Buddha realm, will have unbearably heavy afflictions!

“Xi prosperous” (fierce): Very prosperous, like a big fire.

Not doing good things, doing bad things, everyone is used to doing it. In the realm of the five desires, everyone competes to practice killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying. That's how it is now. You can use Buddhist scriptures to compare it. Stupidity is also a very strong anger, very strong ignorance, and very violent. “Le” means fierce. For the word Han, you should use a pen to circle [to mark], [unlike] the word Ngan of the Dog family, Han means "not easy to teach, stubborn, difficult to tame".

Sometimes it is an evil king, Sat-di-li, that king is Chien-dala, an evil person. Caṇḍāla[71] denotes evil meaning. There is also the official Chien-do-la. “Evil officials”: If there is an evil king, there will be evil officials. Those lay people are not lay people who have received the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, but are lay people. Are not the layman of Chien-dala, the rich man of Chien-dala, the rich man [the person who practices] the Ten Virtues? Sometimes when rich people have wealth, wealth, and great power, they also turn into evil people. The evil people among the rich, that is, the evil rich people, Brahmins, etc. Such people have few good roots, have no faith, are delusional, and are stupid. “Khuc” is not straight. Their minds are not upright, deluded, and not upright. You see a person who is extremely flattering to his superiors and superiors! In the office of his superior, he will bow his back, bend his knees, and stand very respectfully. When he returns to his own office, he will definitely treat his subordinates arrogantly and arrogantly. If you flatter your superiors, you will definitely be arrogant towards your subordinates. That person has no wisdom and is stupid, but he relies on himself to be smart and knows how to flatter. The traitor and the traitor are both very intelligent people. They do bad things very smartly. Because they are very smart when doing bad things, they are arrogant and arrogant, seeing that no one is as good as them. But as for the suffering results in the future, they do not see them, nor are they afraid, nor do they believe. If we talk about good and evil karma with them, and tell them what the future will be like, they basically don't believe it, because they only see the living suffering their sins, not the dead carrying the burden!

I met a very evil man; Now, he is old. In the past, he worked as an executioner. Currently, changing to execution by gun, he no longer has a job. Currently, he is very old, very poor, and very miserable. He still hasn't changed that habit, and I chat with him all day. I advised him to believe in Buddha. I said: "You can change the evil consequences in the future." He said: "I don't believe what you said!" Even if I don't believe it, I still talk to him. He boasted to me: His sword is nothing like we imagined. We often think that to kill someone, we must use a very large knife. That's not true! His knife is very small, like a fruit knife, but very sharp and very thin. When he kills people, it's not like we are aggressively cutting people down, it's not like that at all. His knife was in a tube, hidden in his sleeve. When it's time to kill you, he slaps his shirt on your neck, presses hard, and your skull falls off! The knife is extremely sharp and very thin. He sees someone else, whether it's his mother, father, or relatives, he will look at their heads to see where he will strike! He specializes in seeing where the knife can be cut, which bones have empty spaces, except for a layer of skin! He will cut it right there, like slaughtering a cow. He killed a cow very quickly, finding a joint to cut into it very quickly. That kind of evil person always thinks about evil things in his mind, he only knows what is beneficial for him!

In this society, each of us has also been harmed, have you ever harmed others? It must have been harmful! In relationships of benefit, those who have not harmed others at all, I think are still in the minority. If there really is such a person, he is truly a Bodhisattva. In this world of five evils, we should not think that this time is not good! During this time when you can receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, with a mind oriented toward goodness, compared to when you were in a pure world, as well as when this world had Buddha, your merit is greater than theirs who practice good deeds for ten years, hundreds of years, thousands of years! Therefore, at a time when one cannot do good deeds, there is no strength to do good deeds, there is no strength to break through the real situation. Therefore, if you do not do evil, you will be attacked and oppressed by all kinds of evil people. Everywhere you are, you are limited and constrained. In other words, you are in trouble everywhere!

We say “the guardian angel protects you”, [however], sometimes the power of the guardian angel is not enough! Why? Demons and evil gods have greater power than guardian angels! The human world is not yet in chaos, the heavens are already in chaos. Asura and the gods fought first, but I was afraid that at that time, the gods would be busy fighting the enemy, and the power of the evil people would strengthen. Therefore, there will be such suffering in the next life, leaving the good knowledge and heading towards the Hell of No Interruption.

(Sutra) Like a person of good fortune, a bad person who violates the precepts, evil deeds turn on, supporting and harming non-virtue The Dharma is equal to the Party, the stage of determination is towards the Vo Cockroach Hell. In the place where existence exists, the self and self reside in the world. Therefore, the Buddha, World-Honored One, the Tathagata's Dharma King, benefits all sentient beings in peace and happiness. The supremely wonderful nectar of dharma, the means to transform the path, the spirit attains the practice, and exalts like the Kshatriya Chien-dala, the brahmin Chien-dala, the beastless spirit towards the Uninterrupted Hell”.
(Sutra: People like that, for financial gain, along with evil deeds, breaking the precepts, helping each other, and forming illegal gangs, are all sure to head towards the Hell of No Interruptions. If there is such a place, I will stay there, using the Dharma of the Buddha, the Tathagata Dharma King, to benefit and bring peace to all sentient beings, [allowing them to enjoy] the supreme wonderful nectar of nectar of Dharma, means of educating, guiding, making them accept, obey, and save Kshat-de-loi-Cham-d-la to Brahman-Chen-d-la like that, so that they do not go towards the Unintermittent Hell”).

This is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow, the focus of the Ten Rings Sutra. First of all, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva turned to the Buddha and said: In the world of the five evil defilements, at the end of the Dharma, when there is no Buddha, the afflictions of sentient beings are very strong. Among human beings, there are also evil people, but the king is also evil, the officials are also evil, the people are also evil, even those who set an example such as the rich man are also evil bourgeois, the Brahmin scholars are also evil, they are also Lamb-dala. Such people have no good roots, no faith, no ambition, and no fear of suffering in the next life. Teaching the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to them is not very effective, they do not believe, it is of no use!

“Giai Dinh is headed towards the Uninterrupted Hell” (They are all definitely headed towards the Uninterrupted Hell). Why? That person is out for profit, people like that person are not just out for fame, but are dedicated to profit. People who want to be famous are a little better, because they still have to care about their face and have to maintain a good reputation. Those who are greedy for wealth, everyone is ignored! Those evil people break the precepts together with monks, group together with evil deeds, and can also denounce lies. This type of people is everywhere! In the Buddhist world, in the monk world, there are also people who flatter, rely on gods, and rely on worldly things! When they first became monks, [those people's] thoughts were problematic, and they were not at all pure as monks. There are also masters who accept that person and establish relationships based on financial interests. There are temples that, in order to preserve themselves, wish to harm others, [thinking] "If you don't harm others, you won't be able to preserve yourself. Only by harming others will you preserve yourself." But in reality, you can also protect yourself by chanting sutras, reciting Buddha's name, worshiping Buddha, and reciting Buddha's name.

However, at present, even the good gods cannot protect us, there are too many evil gods! Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva made this vow: If there is such a place, I will definitely go there. “The Self abides forever” (I will abide there), I will use the Dharma of the Tathagata Dharma King in Buddhism to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, allowing them to attain the supreme wonderful nectar of nectar, a means of teaching and guiding, allowing them to receive and practice, and not enter the Hell of No Interruptions. We preach the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra for the purpose of clearly stating the great power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, who specializes in saving sentient beings who cannot be taught. When they fall into hell, He will come and educate them. Wait until they go in there to suffer, maybe they can change a little. However, this is also very difficult to talk about!

When I was in Beijing, there was an old monk who, on the street, saw an old woman taking her young grandchild and two grandchildren to beg for food. When the monk saw it, he felt pity and returned to the world. However, when mentioned, we still call him "old monk". He himself has a place to live, a very spacious one. The Master told the old woman: "Please let this child follow me to become a monk. You will also go there to become a pure person. We will live together. Why do we need to beg for food?" Isn't that a good intention? The old woman was angry: "We are beggars, we are already at our best, do we still have to be monks?" The Master told me: "Dharma Master! Currently, there is really no way!" I asked: "What's wrong?" “I want to help her settle down, wouldn't it be nice to live where I live?” She immediately said: She has gone to the extreme, and still has to be a monk? He even told me: "Being a monk is worse than being a beggar!" He told me: "You still shouldn't become a magician, you shouldn't return to the temple." I said: "I'm still a prisoner! I haven't fully recovered [my citizenship status] yet." He said: "Forget it! Tomorrow after recovery, don't be a monk anymore!" Oh! Really pitiful. If so, no one would preach Buddhism anymore! You say, is this society evil or not? It's so evil that you consider the monk to be like that!

(Sutra) At the ear, the Buddha reported to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva: - Good man! In the future, in the midst of the Buddha's salvation, all sentient beings are afflicted and prosperous, practicing evil deeds, ignorant and resentful, and are unable to transform the path. The Kshatriya-sastra of Chien-dala, the minister of Chon-dala, the layperson of Chon-du-la, the rich man of Chon-du-la, the monk of Chien-du-la, the Brahmin Chien-do-la. Nare vain, have few good roots, have no faith, are ignorant, foolish, lack intelligence and arrogance, abandon good knowledge, have untruthful speech, are unable to follow good knowledge, often practice slander, destroy death, and curse dysentery. Obeying the Dharma, hesitating to reverse views, not having any views, not fearing the consequences of suffering in the future, often mocking the evil laws and doubts, eager to kill living beings, even holding wrong views, when the world ends, one will be harmed. The killing of Chien-dala, the brahmin of Chien-dala, destroys the dharma. U fell into the Dharma, then became a monk, destroyed the forbidden precepts, and mocked the common business. Brahman-class brahmins, reverently making offerings, greedy for wealth and wealth, unkind words, transmitting letters, passing messages, ancient translations, reading foreign scriptures, cultivating farm food, storing treasures, guarding estates, wives, concubines, men and women, practicing talismans, spells to ward off ghosts, predicting auspiciousness, harmonizing and healing herbs, curing diseases to seek wealth, self-care for life, greed for food, clothes, Protect yourself, need to do business, destroy the Thi La, practice evil dharmas, practice bad conduct, truly not as a monk, calling yourself a monk, truly not as virtuous, claiming to be as virtuous. The Brahmin Chien-dala, the brahmin Chien-dala, cherished his close friends, respectfully made offerings, and listened to the teachings. Try to break the false precepts, the Sat-de-loi Chien-dala, the brahmin Chien-dala, close to him, respectfully make offerings, listen to the teachings. The weak view of the cause, the self in the dharma, attaining renunciation, the precepts, rich virtue, diligent practice, Learning, Unlearning, the desire to attain the ultimate fruition, the attainment of Kshatriya Chien-tà-la, the strong will of the Brahmin Chien-tà-la, reversing birth and disability, not mocking close friends, respectfully making offerings, listening to teachings.
(Sutra: At that time, the Buddha told Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva: - This is good. Men! In the future, in this Buddha world, there will be sentient beings who are illustrious, accustomed to evil deeds, foolish, cruel, and difficult to educate and guide, namely, the Kshatriya Chien-du-la, the official Chien-dala, the layman Chien-du-la, the monk Chien-du-la, and the brahmin Chien-du-la. Such people have few good roots poor, unfaithful, flattering, crooked, foolish, conceited in intelligence, separate from good knowledge, not truthful in speech, unable to follow the words of good knowledge, often slandering, disparaging, cursing about the Dharma, so he hesitates, has a crazy view, does not see, does not fear the consequences of suffering in the next life. Those Kshatriyas and Brahmins destroy and disrupt my Dharma. They are ordained within my Dharma, destroy the precepts, and like to worry about worldly affairs. Those Kshatriyas and Brahmins respectfully make offerings, are greedy for wealth, only talk nonsense, have no virtue, pass on letters, exchange information, trade, barter, and love to study sutras. reading non-Buddhist books, cultivating crops, farming, storing treasures, protecting gardens, houses, concubines, sons and daughters, practicing talismans, mudras, and magic spells to command demons, reading the appearance of good and bad things, preparing medicine, treating diseases to make money, to support themselves, being greedy for food, clothes, and precious jewelry, diligently taking care of worldly affairs, destroying Thi La, practicing evil dharmas, learning the behavior of dogs, are they really not monks who claim to be A monk is not truly a virtuous person but claims to be a virtuous person. That person who violates the precepts even likes to be close to him, makes offerings to him, respects him, and listens to his teachings. If he sees someone who is in my Dharma, he has become a monk. full of precepts, full of virtue, diligently cultivating, cultivating the conduct of both Learned and Unlearned, until attaining the ultimate ultimate fruition, the Kshatriyas of Chien-dala and Brahmins of Chien-dala were arrogant and jealous, did not like to be close to them, respectfully make offerings, or listen to the teachings).

The Dharma seems to be destroyed, the doubts of sentient beings are especially heavy, the confusion of views is especially serious. Even after entering Buddhism, they still develop crazy views and still believe in evil spirits and pagans. That's because that person in Buddhism, in Buddhism, does not gain any benefits. I think people are probably skeptical of this. That person believed in Buddha for a long time, but did not gain anything, because that person had the mind of seeking to achieve! What's the bridge? "Buddha and Bodhisattva bless you and make you rich. Buddha and Bodhisattva bless your family with peace. Buddha and Bodhisattva bless your family with peace, no illness, no accident will happen. So whatever you want to trade, whatever you want to do, you will be rich", even "if you want to harm others, you must also help yourself harm that person!"

I have encountered such things before. That person said: "Can you help me?" I asked: “Do what?” That person said: "My kid is especially naughty, I can't help but correct him!" I said: "I can't help you! If I help you, it will kill me. How can I help you?" Many people misunderstand Buddhism, Buddhism is a matter of understanding. You must clearly understand what Buddhism is? Buddhism is your mind. You must be enlightened, it is you, you are yourself. Know yourself, don't have crazy views. That is true right knowledge and right view. Speak with correct speech, work with correct conduct. Body, speech, and mind must be right view, right speech, right mind, all must be right, everything must be right, not crazy. You have to believe that if you do a little harm in this life, in the future, you will have to pay back ten times more, and you will also have to pay interest! Flowers, retribution, retribution! For example, you often get sick. That's because you killed too much, still owe your life, paying for your life is not enough, you still have to pay interest, and have to bear the consequences.

Your body is not healthy. That's the result. You can find any doctor at your convenience, find Amitābha Buddha, find Śākyamuni Buddha, find Medicine Master Buddha, almost all of those doctors can cure your illness. If you seek a worldly doctor, you won't be able to cure it. You must treat it according to your own karma and retribution. By deceiving the world like that, you harm yourself, both yourself and others are harmed. Therefore, Kshatriya Chien-dala to Brahman Chien-dala “destroy the ego” (destroy, disrupt my dharma), that is, destroy the Buddha dharma! Those Lambo-la guys are powerful, powerful, and wealthy people. How do they destroy them? They collude with monks [breaking precepts, doing bad deeds]. If you collude with a monk, you will destroy it. Therefore, in the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, it is written: When the Buddha was about to Nirvana, the demon king Ba Tuan came. At that time, the Buddha had not yet decided to enter Nirvana, and was still considering the fundamentals of sentient beings. If at that time, Ananda had come to the Buddha before Ba Week and asked the Buddha to stay in the world, nothing would have happened! Ananda came after Ba Tuan, that's no good! Three weeks ago, he said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! You should go. You have saved many ghosts and ghosts of mine. In the future, I will destroy you." Buddha asked: “How will you destroy me?” He said he would destroy Buddhism like this and like that, but the Buddha smiled and said: "You can't destroy it!" He added: "I still have the best method. I will send my children and grandchildren to become monks in His Dharma, to be monks and nuns, to eat His food, to wear His clothes, but not to do His things. That way, it will be destructive!"

Everything needs to rot first before it can give birth to maggots and worms. Starting from internal corruption first; After that, the worms are born. Everything is like that. Therefore, outsiders cannot destroy Buddhism! Then monks and bhikshunis wear monk's robes and do bad things. Other people look at them, see that they are monks, [then grab their chopsticks] "That's what Buddhism is like!" Do you see it or not? Who can believe it anymore! They have sabotaged it! You must know that those sabotaging monks and sabotaging Bhikkhunis are all brought by demons from children and grandchildren. This story has already been predicted! But the evil Kshatriyas, evil Brahmins, and all the evil lay people as mentioned in the above section respectfully and make offerings to those evil monks are not truly good believers, they are people with crazy views. They make offerings to those who are greedy for wealth and gain, only talk, do not practice, even send letters, exchange news, trade, do business, like to study pagan books, all kinds of business, grow crops, store treasures, protect gardens and houses.

It's okay to get married, not for profit, but dedicated to benefiting sentient beings, it can still be tolerated. All things can be communicated. Therefore, there are beneficial things that can be planned and tolerated. We can also communicate with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. So for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, reciting His name, studying the Ten Rings Sutra, reciting Ksitigarbha Sutra is also having communication with Him, but that is communication with good dharmas, not communication with evil dharmas! During that time, they exchanged information, studied pagan scriptures, traded, and did business. Nowadays, Japanese temples are all companies! Chinese temples and pagodas today also learn that style! I'm afraid that Mainland China has followed suit very well and has already started doing the same! Self-reliant, you do business, the government encourages and encourages you. Currently, you still have to buy tickets to enter. When you go to the temple to burn incense and worship Buddha, you have to buy incense and buy an entrance ticket!

I went to Nam Putuo Pagoda (in Xiamen, Phuoc Kien province), [the entrance ticket at that time was] one penny, now when we return it is one coin, in the future, it will increase to five coins! Need to sell admission tickets! Otherwise, how will more than five hundred people live? Must rely on admission ticket sales! When you go to court to worship Buddha, pay respects to Buddha, and burn incense, you also have to spend money and have to buy it. That's no way, that's the end of the Dharma! There are also people who practice magic spells to control ghosts and spirits, and to see signs of good and evil. There are also people who sell medicine and prepare medicine. Selling fake medicine is bad, selling real medicine is a little better. Currently, there is a lot of fake medicine being sold. Especially in the mountains, we brag that our medicine comes from Vu Di mountain in Phuoc Kien, created by some temple, or prepared by some old monk. Very good, that's very valuable! There are many such things, "to live for oneself, to be greedy for food, clothes, and jewelry, to need business and customs, to destroy Thi La" (to support oneself, to be greedy for food, clothes, precious jewelry, to diligently take care of worldly affairs, to destroy Thi La). Thi La is precept. They did all the things that Buddha prescribed not to do, and they violated them all. The most important are the Four Kinds of Purity and Repentance (four clear teachings on pure conduct), which are also the four basic precepts. All four basic precepts can be committed, but other mistakes are even more numerous. The body kills, steals, commits sexual misconduct, the mouth speaks double-mindedly, lies, embellishes, speaks evilly, until the mind is greedy, angry, and ignorant. If all of these things can be done, they are called “evil actions”.

“Boi yin cau hanh” means learning the methods of dogs. During the End of the Ages, Bhikkhus slandered each other, both sides were suspicious and jealous of each other, immersed in futility and unable to save themselves. Using a dog as an example, "bei yin conducts the dharma, the branch practices the dog dharma" (the person who practices the dharma is the dog's dharma), which also means "bei yin karma" means to practice according to the dog's method. In doing so, that person has lost the essence of a monk, violated the four basic precepts, and is not a monk. Regardless of meaning or essence, they have lost their status as monks; but that person himself did not repent. If that person himself cannot comply, he can “retreat”. If you feel that [those precepts] are not suitable for you, you can renounce them. But that person did not renounce the precepts and was still mixed in with the Sangha. “Retiring” means leaving the religion and returning to the world. Why did that person do that? If he renounces the precepts, he will have nowhere to find food! In temples and pagodas, the Sangha is very large, and in general there are great virtuous people. A virtuous person will feel the food, clothing, and shelter brought to him, and that person will still be able to enjoy it! Therefore, people like that practice the methods of dogs, so it is said to be “boi yin dog conduct”.

What that person himself does is not pure conduct. “Pham Hanh” means pure conduct. Although he himself commits impure actions, he still calls himself a virtuous person. That is the image of the type of monk who breaks the precepts. There are still people who believe and admire him! If the evil King of Sat-di-li is added to the word Chien-dà-la, it means “of the evil type”. Before that (before each category), the word Chien-dala was added, meaning evil kings, evil Brahmins, they were very close to those monks who broke the precepts. That is called “methods are grouped together, objects are clustered” (methods are divided according to each type, things are divided according to each similar characteristic). Evil spirits (stinky smells, bad people) attract each other, get close to each other, and form cliques. “Respectfully make offerings”: To say “Reverently make offerings” means to respect and make offerings to the monks who break those precepts.

The person who breaks that precept, from Kshat-de-loi Chien-dala to Brahmin Chien-dala, always likes to be close to, make offerings to, listen to, and receive the teachings of that person. If you see someone, “u ego dharma” (in my dharma), “u ego dharma” is in the Buddha dharma to become a monk and receive the Full Precepts. In the previous section, it was about “corrupt Bhikkhus” (bad Bhikkhus), while this subsection talks about good Bhikkhus. After becoming a monk, after receiving the Complete Precepts, you can follow and maintain the precepts. “Fu vic” is very rich in morality, abundant in virtue, full of precepts, and able to practice diligently. “Study” is practice. Studying is “studying the dharma”, which means the status of Being Learned. “No Learning” is to attain Arhatship. Counting from the First Fruition, the saints who have attained enlightenment do not study like us, their study is uneducated, until finally they attain Buddhahood. But it can be said that [Unlearned Conduct] is the Arhat fruit, from the First Fruit to the Four Fruits.

What does this mean? That is to say, Kshatriya Chien-dala, Brahmin Chien-dala, towards an evil-doing Bhikkhu, is close to him, makes offerings, listens to his teachings, but towards virtuous Bhikkhus, not only is he not close, but he is also arrogant. is that he does not like to be close, nor does he like to respectfully make offerings, nor listen to teachings or accept virtuous monks until he attains that fruition. They are not close to them and do not accept their teachings.

(Sutra) Good man! For example, if you are a person, you will enter the precious gemstone, the exhaust gas, the royal blue, the blue, the golden, the silver, the true pearl, the red lotus color Phiet Luu Ly, the great true price, the Ca Gia pearl. In the future, if the Buddha saves you, you will be the Kshatriya Chien-tà-la, the brahmin Chien-dà-la, and the heron will be like this. Entering the true dharma treasure of Chu Trung, the equanimity of the precepts, rich in virtue, mocking the Emperor of the Noble Truths, the self-centered and noble Learner, the unlearned person, attaining good and different births, diligently cultivating the Six Dao Bi Ngan, the meritorious true saint disciples, upholding all the precepts, eager to do evil, indifferent, unprincipled, harsh language, arrogant in body and mind, separated from all white dharmas, unkind, uncompassionate, evil deeds, unlucky. field, respectfully make offerings, and listen to teachings. Like an evil person, a disciple, destined to go to the Unbroken Hell.
(Sutra: Hey good man! For example, someone enters a treasure dump and throws away the treasures that actually exist high values such as royal blue[72], great green, gold, silver, pearls, pink lotus-colored Phat Lau Ly, etc. to get the Ca Gia pearl. In the future, in this Buddha world, there will be Kshatriya Chien-dala to Brahmin Chien-dà-la as well, in the same way. In the safe harbor of my Dharma, let go of those who are fully precepted, rich in virtue, who like the Supreme Emperor, who are Learned, Unlearned, full of shame, and other good beings, and the disciples of true saints who diligently practice the Six Paramitas, full of merits, to choose the evil deeds, break the precepts, like to do evil things, not ashamed, not ashamed, not harsh, vulgar language, arrogant in body and mind, away from Dharma, no mercy, no compassion, consider those guys as a field of blessings, respect, make offerings, and listen to the teachings of such evil people, teachers and disciples will definitely enter the Hell of No Interruption.

Ca Gia (Kāca) Chau is also a type of Mani Chau, but is far inferior to Phiet Luu Ly (Vaiḍūrya, Phat Luu Ly, Pi Lapis Lazuly, Lapis Lazuly), which means it is one step lower. That person does not take something that is good, but takes something that is inferior. This is the Buddha giving an example, to say that at the end of the Dharma, in this Buddha land of ours, sometimes the evil king Sat-de-li, sometimes the Brahmin Chien-t-la, that is, the evil Brahmin is the same. As for virtuous monks, they do not trust, do not get close to, and do not listen to and accept teachings. Regarding the Bhikkhu who broke the precepts and committed evil deeds, "an ox seeks an ox, a horse seeks a horse" (a horse seeks a horse, an ox seeks an ox), and also turns to that guy to seek the Dharma, listen to his teachings!

Having arrived at the treasure shore of my Dharma, I have abandoned the person who is full of precepts, has many virtues, and has abandoned the person who loves the Supreme Emperor. Thang Nghia De means True General. The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is the realm of the True Form, the Supreme Truth, that is, the supreme truth. They also throw away the shameful step, “Learner, Unlearner”. “Student” is not yet certified. “No Learner” is a person who has attained enlightenment. “Access to good and different births” (And all kinds of good and different births), that is, good Bodhisattva Jāla. Even if they abandon Upasaka, Upasaka is someone who truly practices, truly believes, admires the Dharma, and respects the Dharma. Even abandoning the disciples of the “true saints” who truly diligently practice the Six Paths of Compassion, that is, practice the Six Paramitas, with full merit. That is a true disciple of [Buddha]!

“True saint” refers to Buddha. They are true disciples of the Buddha, [towards them], those who [evil deeds of Kshatriyas, ministers, etc.] are not close to them, but arrogantly "follow all the precepts, are eager to do evil things, are heartless, unprincipled, have harsh words, are arrogant in body and mind, separate from all white dharmas, are unkind, indifferent, have evil deeds, turn to the Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra)" (choose evil deeds Up-so breaks the precepts, likes to do evil things, is not ashamed, is not ashamed, has rude language, is vulgar, is arrogant in body and mind, is far from the white dharma, is not kind, is not compassionate, considers it a field of blessings). So what results will you get? “If you are an evil person, a teacher and a disciple will definitely go to the Uninterrupted Hell” (If an evil person is like that, the teacher and disciple will definitely enter the Uninterrupted Hell). You accept that person's teachings, believe in him, admire him, and will follow him to hell. This is certainly beyond doubt. Therefore, a kind of wrong knowledge and wrong view will arise. In this Dharma Ending era, there are really not many people [like that]. If everyone follows the teachings, applies their own wisdom, uses right knowledge and right view, you will be able to discern.

For the present, this is very specific and very realistic, but you can use the way the Buddha taught to judge, not according to your own opinion, but using the Buddha's teachings, using the Buddha's teachings as a teacher, not taking your own mind as a teacher. You can see who leads you to hell. That person also does Buddha's work, but twists Buddha's work and uses crazy knowledge to do Buddha's work. Buddhism is inherently a good method to clear one's mind and realize one's nature. If that person uses Buddhism to create fame and profit or conduct business transactions, won't he go to hell? Therefore, the Buddha spoke of ten types of karma. Those ten types are not good wheels at all, but evil wheels.

(Sutra) Good man! The ten evils luan, uh taste hybrid like that, try Buddha

mid-level, right-killer Chien-du-la, official Chien-du-la, layperson Chien-du-la, rich man Chien-du-la, monk Chien-du-la, Brahmin Chien-dala, like-minded people, the ten evil wheels, or depending on the best, Or if you achieve it, the first step of cultivating all the good roots will be destroyed, destroyed, the stage will fade away, the body will not be damaged, the day and night will not be able to say anything, you will be subjected to all kinds of suffering and poison, painful and difficult to endure, and will eventually be reborn in the Uninterrupted Hell.

(Sutra: Good man! There are ten evil wheels, in the future life, in this Buddha land, there are If the kshatriya Chien-dala, the official Chien-dala, the layman Chien-dala, the rich man Chien-dala, the monk Chien-dala, the brahmin Chien-dala, such people, among the ten evil circles, if they accomplish any one of the evil circles, or fully achieve it, then all the good roots that have been cultivated before will be destroyed, burned, will all turn into ashes, and soon, the limbs will wither. Failure, defective, tongue-tied, unable to speak for many days and nights, suffering extreme suffering and pain that is difficult to endure. After death, one will certainly be born in the Hell of No Intermittent.

The monks who break the precepts, the monks who commit evil deeds, the Brahmans of the Lamb in the previous section, “such people” (such people), from the kings to the people, to the ordinary people, to the monks, to the scholars, are all included in it. There are such people who, because of the ten evil wheels as mentioned below, "either achieve the best, or achieve the specific" (if they achieve a certain type, or achieve it completely). Whenever one completes one wheel, or has two full wheels, or completes three uncertain wheels, or only has one wheel, the good roots that that person has cultivated and accumulated over many lifetimes will be destroyed or burned. If one accomplishes one thing in those ten cycles, all the good roots and good thoughts that that person has practiced over many lifetimes will turn into ashes! Therefore, we feel that only planting good roots, only studying Buddha Dharma, does not really eliminate afflictions at all; In the future, you may also fall into these Ten Evil Wheels! Because when you reincarnate, if you do not practice and attain Satisfactory Life, you will easily be entangled with fame, profit and desire and easily fall into the Ten Evil Wheels.

We study the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, study the Ksitigarbha Sutra, read and recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, until reading the Ten Wheels Mahasamadhi Sutra, until Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses us, allowing us to have such good roots and causes in this life. By marrying Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we will not fall into the Ten Evil Wheels, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has assured Śākyamuni Buddha. When we read the Ksitigarbha Sutra, we will be able to feel and understand those great Bodhisattvas. As for the Bodhisattvas appearing in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, as well as in the chapter about the names of Buddhas, the ninth chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, whatever name we recite will never fall into the three realms. If we build strong faith like that, we will not be involved in the Ten Evil Wheels and will not be fallen. For what reason? Due to the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, but also due to the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we do not fall into the evil realm. Even in the Dharma-Ending Age, if you are close to Buddhism, entering the Buddha's door is about the size of a grain of dust, so tiny, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will definitely bless you. But if you refuse His blessings and don't even bother to get involved with Him, it will be a different story!

“The limbs will be disabled and lacking” (Soon, the limbs will be disabled and lacking): That is in the present life. “Unable to speak, unable to speak” (For many days and nights, unable to speak with a tongue-tie): Unable to speak, the six senses have lost their effectiveness. “Suffering the poisons of suffering” (Suffering the poisons of suffering): This type of suffering cannot even be described! We see a lot of people get into car crashes and then turn into vegetative people. In the past, I thought there weren't many people living in a vegetative state, but in 1993, when I went to Taiwan and went to Yongmin General Hospital and Truong Canh Hospital in Lam Khau, I saw too many people living in a vegetative state in the hospital. Therefore, the above descriptions refer to those people. Suffering from suffering and poison, his body has ulcers, he cannot speak, everything is disabled, lacking, and extremely damaged. The mind is disabled, turning into a vegetable. Either because of one's karma in this life, or because of one's karma in a previous life, the pain is extremely unbearable. Not to mention the matter of after death, currently, that person is still alive, suffering extremely unbearably, suffering from crippled and missing limbs. A person who has all the Ten Evil Wheels will definitely be born in the Hell of No Interruptions.

(Sutra) One level and one level? Such as breaking the precepts, committing evil deeds, possessing the Kshatriya, having an evil view, blaspheming A Luyen Nha's purity, saying: "You false people! Such as this, are foolish, ordinary guavas, pretending to be strange, stalking or worldly, seeking food, clothing, nourishment, respect, honor, self-praising, destroying others, jealousy and chaos, greed for fame and profit, no self-sufficiency, contentment. Such is the practice of deceitful speech, the true truth, the true truth, the true enlightenment, the heron is free from desires, the eternal cessation of defilements, the position of nourishment, respect, honor, the self-existence of virtue. The kidneys make offerings, revere, and acknowledge, such as thi siam khuc, non-true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), non-practitioner. During, Kshatriya Chien-tà-la, the brahmin Chien-dà-la, the pure Alyna Nha, was unable to give birth to true faith, rare thoughts, mind without reverence, mind always slandering, not mocking close friends, taking care of things, making offerings, possessing words, not listening to feelings. Disdain destroys like the pure A Luyen Nha residence, that is, contempt destroys all dharma eyes of the Three Jewels of the nature.
Kshatriyas and ministers, etc., receiving [his] evil views, immediately blasphemed the pure Upsō in A Luyen Nha, saying: "O you people! Such a Būsō is foolish, ordinary, despicable, lies about strange appearances, deceives, deceives the world, seeks food, clothing, nourishment, reverence, honor, praises himself, criticizes others, is jealous, fights, causes trouble, is greedy for fame and profit for nothing. Not enough, he should be banished, chased away, don't believe his words. Such a Bodhisattva specializes in lying, leaving the Dharma is certain, for that Dharma, he does not attain enlightenment, nor does he leave all the defilements, just for the sake of gain, respect, honor, and pretends to be virtuous in A Luyen Nha must be a field of true blessings, not a person cultivating the path." At that time, Kshatriya Chien-tala to Brahmin Chien-dala, towards the pure up-so in A Luyen Nha, could not give birth to true faith, had no rare thoughts, had no reverence in their mind, embraced bullying, despised them, did not like to be close to them, to receive favors, to make offerings, and did not listen to all of his words. Contempt. To scorn and slander the pure Buddha who abides in A Luyen Nha like that means to scorn and slander all dharma eyes of the Three Jewels.

From here on, explain the Ten Evil Wheels. "Such as he breaks the precepts and conducts evil deeds, the Kshatriya and the Kshatriyas are up to the level of authority, and endures evil views" (Busho breaks the precepts and conducts such evil actions because there are Kshatriyas and officials, etc., who receive [his] evil views): For that evil-doing Bhikkhu, there are the Kshatriyas and the officials of the Chom-tala who receive and believe and listen to his words. he does evil. What evil are you doing? “Profane the pure sūtra of A Luyen Nha” (blaspheme the pure bhikkhu residing in A Lan Nha): Blaspheme that pure bhikkhu. A Luyen Nha (A Lan Nha, Araṇya) is a quiet place, in the mountains and forests, under the canopy of palm trees. In modern terms, it means cultivating in the mountains and forests, cultivating oneself. What words did that evil-doing Bhikkhu slander those people? The evil-doing Bhikkhu told King Sat-di-li and the chief minister: The people in those mountains and forests are very foolish. They appear strangely, deliberately pretending to practice, and are liars. “Deceptive to the world” (Deceiving, deceiving the world), “seeking food, clothing, nourishment, respect, honor, self-praising, destroying others, jealousy and fighting, greed for fame and profit, non-existence, self-satisfaction, pleasure in depravity, things receiving strange words” (seeking food, clothing, nourishment, respect, honor, praising oneself, criticizing others, jealousy, fighting, causing trouble, greed It's not enough to indulge in fame and fortune. You should expel them, chase them away, don't listen to them).

That is an evil monk criticizing a pure monk. The following is his slanderous words: "Like a Buddha who specializes in false speech, abandoning the truth of the truth. If he has no attainment of the true path and fruition, he is free from desire, eternally freed from defilements, is nourished, respectful, honorable, maintains A Luyen Nha" (Such a Buddha specializes in false speech, separates from the true dharma, neither attains enlightenment nor fruition therein, nor is he free from desire, not eternal. completely free from all defilements, only for the sake of gain, respect, and honor, they stay in A Luyen Nha): That is to say that in reality they do not attain enlightenment, nor are they separated from desire, nor are they free from the taints, only for the sake of gain, respect, and honor, because of those things, they stay in a pure, quiet place. “Existing virtue yourself, carefully making offerings, respecting, taking advantage of things, like a market of praise, non-true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), non-virtuous path” (Pretending to have virtue yourself, be careful, do not make offerings to, respect, and take advantage of those who flatter, manipulate, are not true fields of merit, are not such practitioners). Those are the words that defame the pure Bhikkhu of the evil Bhikkhu!

“At the time, Kshat-de-loi Chien-dà-la, even Brahmin Chien-dà-la, the pure Alyna Nha, could not give birth to true faith, rare thoughts” (At that time, Kshat-de-loi Chom-dala to Brahman Sheng-dala towards the pure up-so in A Luyen Nha could not give rise to true faith and rare thoughts): Regarding the good Bhikkhu, they did not give rise to true faith, did not give rise to the idea that he was a rare and hard-to-find good and knowledgeable person, so they did not have a heart of respect, but held a heart of oppression and contempt. “Lang” means to oppress, we say “mighty spirit” (a fiery aura that overwhelms others) has this meaning. Disparaging that person. To scorn and slander the pure Buddha who abides in A Luyen Nha like that is to scorn and slander all the species of the Dharma eye of the Three Jewels. After saying so, the evil Bhikkhu slandered the pure Bhikkhu, attracting evil people from Kshatriya to Brahmin to slander him together. How effective was that? Because they want to destroy the nature of the Three Jewels. “Dharma eye”: “Nhan” means observation. There is no dharma, destroying pure dharma. Those living beings have done all evil things and have no eyes for the Dharma, so they are crazy. Saying good becomes evil, arrogantly turning the evil you have done into good. So what results will you get?

(Kinh) Thời, bỉ quốc trung hữu chư thiên, long, Dược Xoa thần đẳng, tín kính Tam Bảo vô động hoại giả, ư Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, nãi chí sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, tâm sanh sân phẫn, hỗ tương vị ngôn: “Nhân đẳng! Đương quán thử Sát-đế-lợi, tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, giai tất khinh hủy nhất thiết pháp nhãn Tam Bảo chủng tánh, tổn giảm thiện căn, do ác hữu lực, nhiếp chư tội nghiệp, đương đọa ác thú. Ngã đẳng tùng kim vật phục ủng hộ thử Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la đẳng, tịnh kỳ sở cư quốc độ, thành, ấp”. Tác thị ngữ dĩ, nhất thiết thiên, long, Dược Xoa thần đẳng giai tất khí xả, bất phục ủng hộ bỉ Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la đẳng, tịnh bỉ sở cư quốc độ, thành, ấp. Ư bỉ quốc độ, nhất thiết pháp khí chân thật phước điền, giai xuất kỳ quốc. Thiết hữu trụ giả, diệc sanh xả tâm, bất phục hộ niệm. Do chư thiên, long, Dược Xoa thần đẳng, cập chư pháp khí chân thật phước điền, ư Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la đẳng, tịnh bỉ sở cư quốc độ, thành, ấp, giai xả thủ hộ, bất hộ niệm dĩ. Thời bỉ quốc độ, tự quân, tha quân, cạnh khởi xâm lăng, cánh tương tàn hại, tật dịch, cơ cẩn, nhân thử phục hưng. Bỉ Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, nãi chí sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, nhất thiết quốc dân, giai vô hoan lạc. Tiên sở ái nhạo, kim tất biệt ly. Bằng hữu, quyến thuộc cánh tương sân hận, tiềm mưu sai nhị, vô từ, vô bi, tật đố, xan tham, chúng ác giai khởi. Sở vị sát sanh, nãi chí tà kiến, vô tàm, vô quý, thực dụng nhất thiết Tốt-đổ-ba vật, cập Tăng Kỳ vật, tằng vô hối tâm. Bỉ Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, tăng tật trung hiền, ái nhạo siểm nịnh, linh kỷ quan thứ hỗ tương xâm lăng, phẫn khuể kết oán, hưng chư đấu tránh. Cộng dư lân quốc giao trận chiến thời, quân sĩ ly tâm, vô bất thoái bại. Bỉ Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, bất cửu tiện đương chi thể phế khuyết, ư đa nhật dạ, kết thiệt bất ngôn, thọ chư khổ độc, thống thiết nan nhẫn, mạng chung định sanh Vô Gián địa ngục.
(Kinh: Lúc bấy giờ, trong nước ấy có các trời, rồng, Dược Xoa thần v.v… tin kính Tam Bảo chẳng bị lay động, phá hoại, đối với vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la cho đến các sa-môn, Bà-la-môn v.v… toàn là hạng Chiên-đồ-la, tâm sanh sân hận, phẫn nộ, nói với nhau: “Các vị! Hãy xem bọn Chiên-đồ-la Sát-đế-lợi, tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn này thảy đều khinh miệt, hủy báng hết thảy chủng tánh Tam Bảo pháp nhãn, tổn giảm thiện căn, do sức của bạn ác mà thâu tóm các tội nghiệp, sẽ đọa vào đường ác. Từ nay, chúng ta chẳng còn ủng hộ bọn Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la v.v… ấy và quốc độ, thành, ấp nơi bọn chúng sống nữa”. Nói lời ấy xong, hết thảy trời, rồng, Dược Xoa thần v.v… thảy đều vứt bỏ, chẳng còn ủng hộ bọn Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la v.v… ấy nữa, và cõi nước, thành, ấp nơi bọn chúng sống. Trong quốc độ ấy, hết thảy các bậc pháp khí, phước điền chân thật đều ra khỏi nước ấy. Nếu có vị nào ở lại thì cũng sanh tâm lìa bỏ, chẳng còn hộ niệm nữa. Do chư thiên, rồng, Dược Xoa thần v.v… và các bậc pháp khí, chân thật phước điền đối với bọn Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la v.v… ấy và quốc độ, thành, ấp nơi bọn chúng sống đều buông bỏ sự thủ hộ, chẳng hộ niệm nữa, trong quốc độ đó, lúc ấy, quân của chính mình và quân nước khác đua nhau dấy lên xâm lăng, tàn hại lẫn nhau. Dịch bệnh, đói kém do vậy lại dấy lên. Vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la cho đến những gã Chiên-đồ-la thuộc loại sa-môn, Bà-la-môn… hết thảy quốc dân, đều chẳng được vui sướng. Những gì yêu thích trước kia, nay đều biệt ly. Bạn bè và quyến thuộc sân hận lẫn nhau, ngầm tính mưu kế, nghi ngờ, chẳng từ, chẳng bi, ghen ghét, keo tham. Các điều ác đều dấy lên, như là sát sanh, cho đến tà kiến, chẳng thẹn, chẳng hổ, ăn dùng hết thảy những vật thuộc về Tốt-đổ-ba (tháp thờ Phật) và vật thuộc về Tăng chúng, chưa từng có tâm hối hận. Vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương ghen ghét bậc trung hiền, ưa thích phường siểm nịnh, khiến cho quan và dân của chính mình xâm phạm lẫn nhau, phẫn, sân, kết oán, dấy lên các sự đấu tranh. Khi cùng các nước lân cận giao chiến, do lòng quân ly tán, không lúc nào chẳng thua chạy. Vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la, và bọn tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn Chiên-đồ-la ấy chẳng lâu sau sẽ bị tứ chi tàn phế, thiếu khuyết, trong nhiều ngày đêm bị đớ lưỡi chẳng thể nói, chịu các khổ độc, đau đớn cùng cực khó thể chịu đựng, mạng chung nhất định sanh vào địa ngục Vô Gián).

Các vị thiện thần hộ pháp nổi tâm sân hận. “Hỗ tương vị ngôn” nghĩa là các thần nói với nhau: “Nhân đẳng! Đương quán thử Sát-đế-lợi, tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn Chiên-đồ-la nhân” (Các vị! Hãy xem bọn Sát-đế-lợi, tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả, sa-môn, Bà-la-môn Chiên-đồ-la này). Họ nói hiện thời, trong quốc độ này, từ quốc vương, cho đến tể quan, cư sĩ, trưởng giả của ông ta, thậm chí còn có hàng xuất gia, Bà-la-môn đều là Chiên-đồ-la. Chiên-đồ-la là ác nhân. Ác nhân hành ác pháp. Chúng nó hủy báng Tam Bảo và hết thảy chủng tánh pháp nhãn Tam Bảo, tổn giảm căn lành. Người trong quốc độ ấy chẳng có thiện căn, do sức của bạn ác mà thâu nhiếp các tội nghiệp. Từ ác lực, tạo ra hết thảy ác nghiệp. “Đương đọa ác thú” (Sẽ đọa vào đường ác), nhất định đọa vào tam đồ!

“The ego is at the same level as the metal, the object of support is to try the Sat-de-loi Chien-do-la level, the pure state of residence in the country, city, hamlet. The language, necessarily heaven, dragon, Duoc Xa god-level, phase must discharge" ("We from now on will no longer support the Sat-de-loi" This sheep-dala and the country, city, and hamlet where they live." After saying that, all the heavens, dragons, Yak Xoa gods, etc. were all thrown away). The good gods left that kingdom, leaving only La Sat and evil Yaksha! From then on, that country was not auspicious, and the good protectors no longer supported it! “For those who stay, the heron gives rise to the mind of letting go” (If anyone stays, they also give rise to the mind of letting go): Or there are a few who still stay, haven't gone, but don't protect them, giving rise to the mind of letting go. Not only gods, but we monastics [also let go]! We can see this social phenomenon: After the good monks all let go, no longer protect, no longer protect the thoughts of the Ksattriyas of Chien-tu-la and the countries, cities, and hamlets where they live. After there was no more protection, "in the country's self-government, self-government, self-government, foreign power, invasion" (at that time, in that country, the army of one's own country and the army of another country raced to invade): "Self-government" was the army of one's own country fighting each other, just like in Mainland China, Mao Zedong's army and the Kuomintang's army fought for many years. Then, “spare army” (another country's army), the Japanese immediately invaded the country. “Extra army” (Other army) means that after someone else attacked, our country's army attacked and killed each other, leading to epidemics and famine. There are also water and fire disasters. “Renaissance” [here] means that those disasters arise again. “Kings of Sat-de-loi Chien-dala, the monks and brahmins of the Chon-dala level, all the people of the country, are happy” (Kings of Sat-de-loi Chien-dala to the monks and Brahmins of Chien-dala, all the people in the country are not happy): Cannot be happy! “The first love is ridiculed, the gold is gone forever” means that everything that was enjoyed and loved in the past, the pleasant scenes are no longer there, they have all left!

“Friends and relatives are angry at each other” (Friends and relatives are angry at each other): Your relatives are angry at each other, hurt each other. This needs no explanation! Not only Taiwan has a lot, but the Mainland has a lot too. Every day you can see, just like we see, even the selling gourds are fighting. “No shame, no preciousness” (No shame, no shame), then “envy, greed, all evil things arise” (jealousy, greed, all evil things arise). It's all about creating negative karma, up to killing karma, and wrong views. “No shame, no shame”, includes a lot of wrong views! We give the simplest example. While they eat other living beings, they say those living beings were born for them to eat! That's called wrong view. Pigs, goats, whatever, are all foods? Pigs and goats are born for humans to eat, so are chickens also born for humans to eat? That being said, are humans born to be fed to wolves and tigers? [Being questioned like that], they didn't think like that, and didn't say like that either. This is called wrong view! Wrong knowledge, wrong views, no shame, no shame! Even for money in pagodas and temples, they all came to rob it and spend it, not afraid of the Hell of No Interruption. They stole money from all temples and pagodas for their own use. “Monks of Strange Objects” are offerings in temples and shrines of the Sangha, they all take them for their own use, without even the slightest bit of repentance!

Those people, “slander King Kshat-de-loi Chien-dala to be loyal and kind” (King Kshat-de-loi Chien-dala is jealous of loyal officials and wise men): Jealous of good people, jealous of good people, favoring the slanderous and flattering people. “Flattery” is a traitor, a bad person.
