We say they become bad people. From being an official to being elected as a senator, they all violate each other. Sometimes it comes from self-interest, sometimes it comes from the party, never worrying about the people of the whole country, although they always proclaim "we consider the entire nation", using that trick to achieve fame and profit for themselves. “Mutual invasion”: At that time, that person's strength cannot withstand you, so you immediately kill him, or massacre his entire family. Their resentment is tightly formed into “resentment” in their hearts. “Anger” is the power of anger that cannot be released, and if it accumulates in the mind, it will give rise to anger. That's making enemies and accumulating resentment, and even when you die, you still say: "If I become a ghost, I have to repay you!" So it's forming hatred and resentment in your heart. In your next life, if you meet each other, will that person be able to treat you well? Why would someone who just saw another person, without any connection to that person, immediately pull out a gun and shoot? That is not this life, but the [wrongdoing] that was committed in the past life. As soon as that person saw him, he couldn't help but kill him, because in his previous life you killed me. Because that person does not see the previous life, that is “the end”.

“Hung chu fight avoid” (Raise fighting, dispute): Initiate fight, praise fight. Fighting to the point of children fighting fathers, husbands and wives fighting each other, families fighting each other. “When there is a war between neighboring countries” (When fighting with neighboring countries): In such a country, soldiers in the army cannot fight. When fighting with others, soldiers, that is, combat soldiers, their minds are exhausted, they do not think about protecting that country, do not think about sacrificing their lives to protect the country. Therefore, if you fight with the enemy, you will be defeated! “Bhat-de-loi Chien-dala kings, ministers, laymen, wealthy people, monks, Brahmins of the Sheng-dala level, are inconvenient in their crippled limbs” (The Kshat-de-loi Chien-dala kings and those Chom-dà-la officials, lay people, bourgeois, monks, and Brahmins will soon be crippled and lacking limbs): That is, those That person is either killed or devastated by others, or he or she falls ill himself. Regardless of the illness, it causes an incurable evil and lasts a long time. For many days and nights, my tongue was numb and I couldn't speak. I had a mouth but couldn't eat anything!

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! The Kshatriya Emperor, the king, the official, the layman, the rich man, the recluse, the Brahmin of the Chongdala level, is subject to evil actions, the roots of good are few, ignorant, ignorant, arrogant, ignorant of the Three Jewels, impure and pure in mind, without any view, without fear of the suffering of the consequences of the future. Trying to be of the best kind, the Shravaka Vehicle attains low faith, is truly foolish, is self-perceptive, self-centered teaches the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, updates the Mahayana Dharma, destroys, slanders, does not listen to sentient beings, accepts and upholds it, recites it alone, and chants it in the summer.
The Buddhists are officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, and brahmins who follow evil friends, have few good roots, are ignorant, are arrogant and intelligent, and when it comes to the Three Jewels, their minds are not pure, they do not see, and are not afraid of the sufferings of the next life. Such people believe a little in Thanh Van Thua. The Mahayana and the Mahayana dharma that I have spoken about are denigrated and slandered, not allowing sentient beings to receive, uphold, recite, recite even just one verse.)

This is another type of evil circle. There is a king who is an evil king, all his officials, subjects, lay people, wealthy people, monks, and Brahmins are all evil. “According to evil, you act” (According to evil friends). “Evil friends” (evil friends) are monks who break the precepts as we just said, even fake monks! Nowadays, there are many fake monks. A layman who also called himself a magician, also wore the yellow robe and red robe of a monk, also ascended the throne to preach, explaining Buddhism in a different way. I'm in Taiwan and heard that you can even broadcast on television. That guy bought a talk show for a few minutes. That's crazy. What kind of things does such a person do according to evil friends? “Dangerous, foolish”. He also thought he was very smart. Saying “smart”, because he thinks his own wrong view is very smart, to what extent? There is no faith in the Three Jewels, no pure mind, no respect, no belief in cause and effect. At that time, it can be clearly revealed that he is a person who does not believe in cause and effect. If he believed in cause and effect, he would never dare to do those things! That's someone who doesn't study Buddhism. There are times when his mind does not dare to do evil things, he cannot do them, because in our country, such as the Chinese people, Confucianism is the same, in the historical tradition of thousands of years, even though [at a time when] there was no Buddhism, they also knew this could not be done, they could not do things that would harm others or benefit themselves. Confucianism also teaches like that. “Immoral things thi” (Don't look at things that aren't ethical), don't look at things that aren't ethical, don't do anything that isn't ethical, don't listen to sounds that aren't ethical. “If you don't show an object, don't say something, don't hear an object” (Don't look at impolite things, don't say impolite words, don't listen to impolite things), these things are consistent with Buddhism. That is “focusing on cause and effect”.

“If you harm others, others will always harm you. If you kill others, others will always kill you” (Whoever harms others, others will always harm him. Whoever kills, others will always kill him). But he didn't believe it, thinking he was very smart. If you tell him the Shravaka Dharma, he will say: "I am Mahayana!" If you speak the Bodhisattva Dharma to him, tell him to practice the Bodhisattva way, he will say: "I am a Hinayana, I am self-interested." After all, who is he? Not even one surplus! He is the excess of hell, but also the three things of excess. He sat on that carriage, that carriage transported him into the three realms, and he was even satisfied!

Or about the dharma of cause and effect, that person understands a little, so he blasphemes the Thanh Van dharma, blasphemes the Mahayana dharma, and blasphemes the Luc Do dharma. Or that person studies the Sravaka dharma, studies Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Path, then blasphemes the Pratyekabuddha dharma, blasphemes the Mahayana dharma, and blasphemes the Six Paramitas dharma. He considered himself perfect, that he was studying the Mahayana dharma, and started to slander the Hinayana dharma. The Buddha also praised the Hinayana dharma. Studying the Mahayana dharma, I thought there was no need to study the Second Vehicle dharma, [but] the Buddha did not slander the Second Vehicle dharma at all. The Buddha told people of Mahayana background and taught them the Mahayana dharma. You have developed Bodhi mind and saved all sentient beings. All sentient beings can be saved, let alone saints of the Second Vehicle? Therefore, the three vehicle dharmas are correct. We must understand the Buddha's fundamental response to preach the Dharma, not specialize in any particular Dharma! If there were sentient beings with this type of capacity, he would tell them this type of dharma. For another type of basis, He will say a different type of method. There are eighty-four thousand methods of practice. There are many methods, it depends on who you are talking to! If you talk to that person if it's not appropriate, you won't be able to say it, that's the meaning!

Understanding this level of meaning, regarding the Three Vehicles, one must read and recite, not slander. Here again, for those who have become monks, as well as for lay followers, between lay people, between monastics, good men and women who are pure believers, treat the four assemblies of disciples, care for each other, and respect each other. How should a monk who breaks the above precepts be treated? That person has his own cause and effect, you should always consider that person as a saint. You use the mind of a saint and see that everyone is a saint. Accept, uphold, read and recite the Three Vehicles, at least one verse.

(Sūtra) Of the best kind, the Pratyekabuddha attains through little faith, is truly foolish, is clear-minded, If you fall into the trap of preaching the Sravakayana dharma, refer to the Mahayana dharma, destroy it, slander it, do not listen to sentient beings, accept it, recite it alone, and recite it one at a time. Of the best kind, the Mahayana Dharma is attained through little faith, is truly foolish, is self-perceptive, and self-centered speaks of the Sravaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, destroys death, slanders, does not listen to sentient beings, accepts and upholds it, recites it alone, and recites it in the same way. As for the people of the same class, those who slander the Buddha's Dharma are those who defy the three worlds of Buddhas, destroy the three worlds of all Buddhas, completely destroy the Buddha's part, destroy all the Buddhas in the third world, destroy all eight branches of the holy path, and destroy the Dharma eyes of countless sentient beings. Nazareth-de-loi Chien-tà-la-king, Ni Chi monk, Brahman-level Chien-dà-la, the Buddha preached the Sravaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, updated the Mahayana Dharma, rich treasures of obstacles, hidden miracles, one single chant.
intelligent, diligent, regarding the Sravakayana dharma and the Mahayana dharma that I have spoken about, slander and slander, do not allow sentient beings to receive, recite, recite, even one verse. There is a type of person who believes in the Mahayana dharma a little, is really stupid, considers himself intelligent, diligent, regarding the Sravakayana dharma and Pratyekayana dharma that I have mentioned, does not allow sentient beings to accept, recite, recite, even one verse This is called destroying the Buddha's Dharma, it is also contrary to the three worlds of Buddhas, destroying all the teachings of the three worlds of Buddhas, burning, destroying them all to ashes, eliminating and destroying all eight branches of the holy path, blinding the dharma eyes of countless sentient beings, if King Kshatriya Chien-tala as well as the monks and brahmins of Chien-tala are against the Sravakayana dharma, the Pratyekayana dharma, and the Mahayana dharma due to virtue. The Buddha said that it hinders, conceals, and causes it to be hidden, even if it's just a single verse.)

“The most virtuous being, the Pratyekabuddha attained with little faith” (There is also a type of people who believe a little in the Pratyekayana): Truly foolish people, they do not attain the Pratyekabuddha path, consider themselves intelligent, and then blaspheme the Shravaka Vehicle. This is called “destroying the Dharma”. Do you know what meaning “Auṃ, maṇi padme hūṃ” (Auṃ, maṇi padme hūṃ) contains? You must use the method of showing, using the language of showing to explain, then you can know. “An, mani ba di red”, all the sutras of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva can be included in those six words, even included in one word An. One word Sentence completes everything. There is no basis for the Existential Teachings, you don't understand, how can you enter? This is to teach us that when it comes to the Dharma of the Three Jewels, we should protect it and not slander it. If you slander, you have slandered the true dharma, which is the dharma collection of the Buddhas of the three times. Regardless of sects, sects, whether Explicit or Secret, if you think a certain dharma is not correct, it's okay to not study it. That Dharma is not suitable for your ability. You must find the dharma that is right for your ability. Despise is equivalent to “burning and destruction” (burning, destruction), blinding the dharma eyes of countless sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to become blind, without wisdom in the dharma.

“ Weakness of Kshat-de-loi Chien-dà-la, a monk, a Brahmin of the Chon-dà-la level, the Buddha preaches Shravaka Vehicle, Pratyekabuddha Dharma, access to Mahayana Dharma, obstacles, riches” (If King Kshat-de-i Chien-dà-la up to the monks and Brahmans of the Lambdala who hinder and conceal the Sravakayana dharma, the Pratyekabuddha dharma, and the Mahayana dharma spoken by the Buddha), making it impossible for those dharmas to propagate, "mysteriously hidden" (causing them to be hidden). If a sutra is not spoken, that sutra will gradually no longer exist in the world. Why do some people say "when the Dharma is destroyed, the Amitabha Sutra will still exist for one hundred years"? Because there are many people propagating the Pure Land. [Meanwhile, there are sutras] that have very deep teachings, but explain too little, no matter which sutra [encounters that situation, it will gradually be hidden]. Currently, in the Sutra Pitaka there are many good methods, but many of them are hidden!

If you browse the Canon (read the Tripitaka), you can feel that the Sutra is very suitable for you, but no one preaches it, no one propagates it, no one promotes it, and it is not published. Except for a few sutras such as the Diamond Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, and Medicine Master Sutra, many sutras will gradually no longer be mentioned, they will gradually disappear. There is no one to propagate it, it will be lost. The Amitabha Sutra is widely propagated because this dharma is suitable for our basic needs in the Dharma-Ending Age, it is truly the corresponding basic ability. If you don't understand what you're studying, just recite Amitābha Buddha and you'll be fine! Reciting Amitābha Buddha's verse can also achieve salvation. But if you have studied, you must study carefully. What does it mean to study carefully? There are many methods of reciting Amitābha Buddha. First of all, purify your mind, ask yourself what mind do you use to recite? Reciting the Buddha's name is not a matter of reciting the Buddha's name, reciting the Buddha's name must come from the mind. Every thought must be directed to the mind. This mind of yours is Buddha, this mind is Buddha. Amitabha is you. You yourself can release immeasurable light, but you must learn thoroughly. If you slander, that dharma will immediately be hindered and will gradually be destroyed!

(Sutra) The visionary, is disrespectful necessarily dharma eyes of the Three Jewels of the nature. Do see cause and effect, the spirit protects the country necessarily heaven, dragon, Yak Xa god level, believer in the Three Jewels without action, destroyer, U Kshat-de-loi Chien-tà-la-king, nuns, brahmin-class Chien-dà-la cause, the mind gives rise to anger indignantly, widely preached that the Kshatriyas, kings, officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, Brahmins, and Brahmins of the Chongdala level, were not inconvenient as their limbs were crippled, had lost their lives, and had not spoken, endured all kinds of sufferings and poisons, were painfully and painfully endured, and were destined to be reborn in the Great Hell of Uninterrupted Hell.
(Sutra: You should know that person is called not reverent to all the natures of the Three Jewels. Because That cause and effect caused all the gods, dragons, Yaksha gods, etc., who protect that country, those who believe in the Three Jewels, to be unmoved, not destroyed, to have anger and indignation towards King Ksattriya Chien-dala, to the people of Kshat-de-li Chien-dala, to the people of Kham-d-la-la-samon, Brahmins, in general, to the kings--Kat-d-rei Chien-dà-la, officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, That Brahman Lambu-la will soon have crippled and missing limbs, for many days and nights, will be speechless, suffer from toxic suffering, extreme pain that is difficult to endure, and will definitely be reborn in the Great Hell of No Intermittent.

Whoever slanders should know: Whoever slanders, who is “not respectful of all the dharma eyes of the Three Jewels of all kinds, due to the cause and effect, the spiritual guardians of the kingdom of all heavens, dragons, Yak Xas of the divine level, having faith in the Three Jewels of the inactive and destructive ones” (not respecting all of the dharma eyes of the Three Jewels. Due to that cause and effect, all are caused. All the heavens, dragons, Yak Xoa gods, etc. protecting that country are those who believe in the Three Jewels and are unmoved and undamaged): The faith of those ghosts and gods has a foundation and does not waver arbitrarily. “Unmoved and destroyed” [meaning] never wavers in their faith, cannot destroy their faith. Heaven, dragon, and Yak Xa god are like that, among the gods, dragons, and Yak Xa god is Yak Xoa, there is good and evil. Humans have good and evil, gods also have good and evil in the same way. The good protector of the dharma towards King Khamdala Sat-di-li, as well as the Chm-d-la people in the world of monks, Brahmins, etc., had anger and indignation, in general, even to the people including King Ksatt-la Ksatt-la, officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, and Brahmins, who were Chm-d-la, and soon their limbs would be crippled and lacking. The person who violates the Dharma “du da da da, ends up unable to speak, endures all kinds of sufferings and poisons, painful and difficult to endure, and is destined to be reborn in the Great Hell of No Intermittent” (for many days and nights, speechless, unable to speak, suffering poisons, extreme pain that is hard to bear, and destined to be born in the Great Hell of No Intermittent Hell): This is the same as in the previous part [said], determined to be born in the Great Hell of No Intermittent Hell, that is also is the Hell of No Interruptions.

(Kinh)

kings, officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, Brahmans of the Lamb-dala level, breaking the evil precepts and turning on them, spreading the word of the country's righteous dharma, the true field of blessings, the Sat-de-loi Chien-dà-la level, the equanimity of the world. mind, children do not protect thoughts. Even though he lives in the country and lives in the Dharma, he is often unhappy with the worldly affairs of the family. Thiet Linh is temporarily gone, Nhi protects language. Ignoring the words of friends, creating nothing but nothing, always not being able to rely on family money, destruction of property, and contempt for those who break the precepts. If you break the precepts and commit evil deeds, you will never be disdainful of the question, the heron will not appear, try to show off the evil, always be close to the field of blessings, and far from breaking the precepts. Those who break the precepts, commit evil deeds, keep the precepts, practice virtuous conduct, reborn anger, despise and destroy invaders, are the Kshat-de-li Chien-tà-la kings, nuns, brahmins of the K-d-d-la-class, laymen, men, women, big, small, pre-eminent, all kinds of reverence, vain talk, destruction, slandering the keepers of the precepts, the Kshat-de-li. Chomdara kings, Nizhi monks, Brahmins of the Shengdala level, self-centered disciples with few desires, contentment, precepts, multi-literate, wonderful eloquence, anger, harsh language, insults, urgency, mental anguish, body restlessness, or taking away robes, bowls, personal items, sacred dharma jars, or taking away the gifts of the monks of the four directions, not receiving or hearing anything, or shut up in prison, go to jail for torture, or explain in detail, or behead yourself.

Officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, and Brahmans are those who follow evil and break the precepts. In general, in that country, there are people who are true dharma objects and fields of blessings. For those Kshatriyas, they all have the mind to abandon them and do not support their thoughts. Even though they live in that country, they live according to the Dharma. They often do not like to live in the world, and they do not often visit the donors' houses When it comes, he keeps his words and speech, never lies, and never criticizes, defames, or ridicules those who break the precepts or violate the precepts in front of lay people. He never carelessly interrogates them, nor does he intentionally reveal their mistakes. He is always close to the meritorious field, far away from those who break the precepts and conduct evil deeds towards those who keep the precepts and do good deeds and arrogantly giving rise to anger, contempt, defamation, invasion, against King Sat-de-li Chien-tala, as well as the monks, Brahmins Chien-tala, lay men, women, big, small, all kinds of gossip, false talk, disparaging, slandering that precept-holder, causing King Sat-de-li Chien-tala to the Samanas of Samana, Brahmin towards his disciples who have few desires, are self-sufficient, keep the precepts, are well-versed, are full of my skillful eloquence, give rise to anger, use all kinds of rude words, reprimands, curses, and oppressors, causing their minds to be troubled, their bodies to be unstable, or robbing them of robes, bowls, and necessary utensils, causing them to be deprived, or taking things to give to the Sangha of the four directions, or imprisoning them in prison, shackles, torture, or cutting off their feet. hands, or beheading).

This passage of scripture says: From evil kings to evil people, all have been abandoned by the good gods who protect that country, and no longer protect their thoughts. Some are still in that country, some have left, some have not left yet. Even though I don't leave, I don't care, I don't protect the country, I don't protect those above! That type of person does not like to live in the world, but prefers to live in a quiet place, that is, as mentioned in the previous section, “abiding in a quiet place”, that place is called A Lan Nha (or A Luyen Nha). They also do not often go to the donor's house, which is also a faithful donor's house. “The spirit is temporarily gone” (Suppose it is temporary), or because something has to happen for a while, when it comes to their own speech, they carefully guard it, do not say false words, do not say words to deceive or deceive others. Nor in front of lay people "disparaging" (disparagement, slander, contempt, ridicule) of those who break the precepts, that is, absolutely do not say the fault of the monk who breaks the precepts, no matter to anyone, no matter to the king! Above, many cases have been mentioned, but none of them said the fault of the Bhikkhu's bad conduct. “Attempting to show the wrong thing” means intentionally revealing the mistakes of the Bhikkhu who broke the precepts and committed evil deeds. "Always close to the field of blessings, far from breaking the precepts" (Usually close to the field of blessings, far from those who break the precepts): They themselves do not live with monks who break the precepts, but when they break the precepts, their evil and arrogant actions give rise to anger towards those who observe the precepts. Because of the good person, the monk's good conduct comes from preserving his speech, there is no sentence that mentions his mistakes. But the evil Bhikkhu is different, he becomes "despise, destroy, invade" (despise, destroy, violate), violate that good Bhikkhu, in front of "Ksat-de-loi Chien-tà-la, matriarcha, Brahman-class Chien-dala" (king Kshat-de-loi Chien-tà-la to the guys Chien-dà-la in the world of monks, Brahmins), or in front of laymen, women, adults, small people, all kinds of insolent and false discussions, “destroying, slandering false precept-keepers” (destroying, disparaging, defaming the person who upholds that precepts), speaking ill of that pure person, that is, the pure Bhikkhu, causing King Kshat-de-loi Chien-dala to grant him To those monks and Brahmins, their minds were filled with anger, and they used all kinds of harsh words, scolding, cursing, and persecuting them, causing their minds to be troubled, causing monks like that, that is, monks who practice both body and mind, to not be peaceful and at peace! Or even worse, rob the monks of their robes, bowls, and living utensils, causing them to be deprived. Or win gifts for the Sangha of the four directions. The things offered to Bhikkhus by others are taken away by them and are not allowed to be enjoyed. Even worse is “either being locked up in prison, being tortured, or explaining the details, or being beheaded” (or being locked up in prison, tortured in shackles, or cut off limbs, or beheaded). All sorts of punishments and unreasonable torture!

(Kinh) Thiện nam tử! Đương quán như thị chư Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, nãi chí sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, thân cận phá giới, ác hạnh bật-sô, tạo tác như thị chủng chủng đại tội, nãi chí đương đọa Vô Gián địa ngục. Nhược chư chúng sanh tác Ngũ Vô Gián, hoặc phạm trọng giới, hoặc cận Vô Gián tánh tội, giá tội do khinh. Như thị chư Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la vương, nãi chí sa-môn, Bà-la-môn đẳng Chiên-đồ-la nhân, thân cận phá giới, việt pháp trọng tội. Thiện nam tử! Như thị phá giới, ác hạnh bật-sô, tuy tác như thị việt pháp trọng tội, nhi y ngã pháp, thế trừ tu phát, bị phục ca-sa, tấn chỉ oai nghi đồng chư hiền thánh, ngã thượng bất hứa quốc vương, đại thần, chư tại gia giả, y tục chánh pháp, dĩ tiên, trượng đẳng, chủy khảo kỳ thân, hoặc bế lao ngục, hoặc phục ha mạ, hoặc giải chi tiết, hoặc đoạn kỳ mạng, huống y phi pháp? Quốc vương, đại thần, chư tại gia giả, nhược tác thử sự, tiện hoạch đại tội, quyết định đương sanh Vô Gián địa ngục. Ư chư phá giới, ác hạnh bật-sô, do thượng bất ưng như thị trích phạt, hà huống trì giới chân thiện hạnh giả? Thiện nam tử! Nhược hữu bật-sô, ư chư căn bản tánh trọng tội trung, tùy phạm nhất tội, tuy danh phá giới ác hạnh bật-sô, nhi ư thân giáo hòa hợp Tăng trung, sở đắc luật nghi, do bất đoạn tuyệt, nãi chí khí xả sở học Thi La, do hữu bạch pháp hương khí tùy trục. Quốc vương, đại thần, chư tại gia giả, vô hữu luật nghi, bất ưng khinh mạn, cập gia trích phạt. Như thị bật-sô tuy phi pháp khí, thoái thất thánh pháp, uế tạp thanh chúng, phá hoại nhất thiết sa-môn pháp sự, bất đắc thọ dụng tứ phương Tăng vật, nhi ư thân giáo hòa hợp Tăng trung, sở đắc luật nghi bất khí xả cố, do thắng nhất thiết tại gia bạch y. Phạm tánh tội giả, thượng ưng như thị, huống phạm kỳ dư chư tiểu giá tội. Thị cố, bất hứa quốc vương, đại thần, chư tại gia giả, khinh mạn, trích phạt.
(Kinh: Này thiện nam tử! Hãy nên quán các vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la cho đến bọn sa-môn, Bà-la-môn Chiên-đồ-la như thế, thân cận bật-sô phá giới, ác hạnh, tạo tác đủ mọi tội to lớn như thế, cho đến sẽ đọa vào địa ngục Vô Gián. Nếu các chúng sanh tạo tội Ngũ Vô Gián, hoặc phạm trọng giới, hoặc tánh tội Cận Vô Gián, giá tội còn nhẹ. Các vua Sát-đế-lợi Chiên-đồ-la cho đến bọn người sa-môn, Bà-la-môn Chiên-đồ-la như thế thân cận kẻ phá giới, vượt pháp, phạm trọng tội. Này thiện nam tử! Bật-sô phá giới, ác hạnh như thế, tuy tạo trọng tội vượt pháp như thế, nhưng do nương theo pháp của ta, cạo bỏ râu tóc, mặc khoác ca-sa, oai nghi cư xử, giống như các vị hiền thánh, ta còn chẳng cho phép quốc vương, đại thần, những kẻ tại gia nương theo chánh pháp của thế tục dùng roi, gậy v.v… để đánh đập, tra khảo thân họ, hoặc giam trong lao ngục, hoặc lại quở trách, chửi mắng, hoặc chặt chân tay, hoặc đoạn mạng họ, huống hồ nương theo phi pháp! Quốc vương, đại thần, các kẻ tại gia, nếu làm chuyện ấy, sẽ mắc tội lớn, quyết định sẽ sanh vào địa ngục Vô Gián. Đối với các bật-sô ác hạnh, phá giới, còn chẳng nên trừng phạt như thế, hà huống [làm như thế đối với] bậc trì giới, thiện hạnh thật sự ư? Này thiện nam tử! Nếu có bật-sô đối với các trọng tội mang tánh chất căn bản, hễ phạm một tội, tuy gọi là “bật-sô phá giới, ác hạnh”, nhưng luật nghi đã được truyền thọ bởi Tăng chúng thân giáo hòa hợp vẫn chẳng đoạn tuyệt, thậm chí kẻ đó vứt bỏ Thi La đã học, vẫn còn có hương thơm bạch pháp đọng lại. Quốc vương, đại thần, những kẻ tại gia, do chẳng có luật nghi, chớ nên khinh mạn và ra tay trừng phạt. Bật-sô như thế, tuy chẳng phải là pháp khí, lui mất thánh pháp, uế tạp Tăng chúng thanh tịnh, phá hoại hết thảy các pháp sự của sa-môn, chẳng được thọ dụng vật dụng của tứ phương Tăng, nhưng chẳng vứt bỏ luật nghi đã đạt được từ thân giáo hòa hợp Tăng, vẫn hơn hẳn hết thảy kẻ bạch y tại gia. Kẻ phạm tánh tội còn nên như thế, huống hồ kẻ phạm những giá tội nhỏ khác. Vì thế, chẳng cho phép quốc vương, đại thần, và những kẻ tại gia khinh mạn, trừng phạt).

“Như thị chủng chủng đại tội” (Đủ loại tội lớn như thế) tức là vì dùng đủ mọi cách hãm hại bậc tỳ-kheo thiện lương, tỳ-kheo trì giới, tỳ-kheo tu hành, tức là phạm vào đủ loại tội lớn, “đương đọa Vô Gián địa ngục” (sẽ đọa vào địa ngục Vô Gián). “Nhược chư chúng sanh tác Ngũ Vô Gián, hoặc phạm trọng giới, hoặc Cận Vô Gián tánh tội” (Nếu các chúng sanh tạo tội Ngũ Vô Gián, hoặc phạm trọng giới, hoặc tánh tội Cận Vô Gián): Tội Cận Vô Gián, còn chưa phạm đại tội Ngũ Vô Gián. Tôi nêu thí dụ như sau: Giết người, nhưng chưa giết chết, [tức là] tuy người ấy bị giết, nhưng sau đó không chết, cái tội ấy là tội Cận Ngũ Vô Gián, vẫn chưa phải là tội Ngũ Vô Gián. Chẳng hoàn thành thì vẫn chưa kể là phạm giới căn bản. Nhưng tỳ-kheo có ác hạnh ấy đã là tỳ-kheo phá giới. “Thiện nam tử! Như thị phá giới ác hạnh bật-sô, tuy tác như thị việt pháp trọng tội” (Này thiện nam tử! Bật-sô ác hạnh, phá giới như thế tuy tạo trọng tội vượt pháp như vậy), kẻ đó đã tạo loại trọng tội ấy, tội Vô Gián ấy, nhưng do kẻ đó nương theo pháp của ta cạo bỏ râu tóc, khoác mặc ca-sa, oai nghi cử chỉ vẫn giống bậc hiền thánh. Quốc vương đối với tỳ-kheo ác hạnh, cũng có quốc vương thiện lương, chẳng hoàn toàn là quốc vương mang tánh ác. Ác tánh quốc vương có cùng một thể với kẻ đó (tỳ-kheo phá giới), đương nhiên sẽ chẳng giết kẻ đó, chẳng hại kẻ đó, vì nghĩ hắn làm đúng. Quốc vương thiện lương, đối với gã ác tánh tỳ-kheo ấy, tuy hắn chẳng thể vâng theo chánh pháp, hoặc là gã tỳ-kheo ấy trộm cắp, hoặc là gã tỳ-kheo ấy giết người, đáng phải đền mạng. Chiếu theo chánh pháp [của thế tục], phải đoạn dứt sanh mạng của gã tỳ-kheo ấy, điều này chớ nên! Vì hắn đã thị hiện tướng trạng giống như bậc hiền thánh, là Tăng Bảo có thiện căn thọ giới, hãy còn thế lực sót lại của thiện pháp. Thế lực ấy chưa tiêu hết sạch, [cho nên] chẳng thể đoạn mạng hắn, huống hồ [xử trí theo] phi pháp ư? Dẫu hợp pháp, cũng chẳng thể làm như vậy, vâng theo phi pháp thì càng chẳng thể được!

Therefore, “kings, ministers, false laymen, weakly trying to test things, taking advantage of a great sin” (kings, ministers, lay people, if they do this, they will commit a great sin): If you do this to a monk who breaks the precepts, that means punishing that person, you will commit a great sin. “Deciding to be born in the Infinite Hell” (Deciding to be born in the Infinite Hell), is equivalent to having killed a living being. Shouldn't we be punished like that for those who break the precepts and conduct such bad deeds, let alone [such a punishment for] those who keep the precepts and conduct genuine good deeds? For a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts, it is impossible to do so, as for a practitioner, a Bhikkhu who truly upholds the Precepts, a Bhikkhu who propagates the Dharma, and even a Bhikkhu who actually maintains the Dharma, it is even more impossible to do so. By doing so, the crime becomes even greater!

The four precepts “killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying”, whoever breaks any of them, are called “Bhikkhus breaking the precepts, evil deeds”, but the precepts that have been transmitted from the teaching body in harmony with the Sangha are still not broken. That person has not completely lost or broken the precepts of the precepts that he has received. Even for Thi La who had studied, although the Bhikkhu broke the precepts, that evil action was completely abandoned and he no longer studied, but he still had the scent of pure Dharma. The residual power of the incense world still lingers, [for example] the sandalwood has been burned, the smoke is no longer there, but you have been in that house for a long time, your body still has the scent, there is also the smell of sandalwood, or the smell of agarwood, has such a meaning.

“Kings, ministers, and lay people, who have no rules and regulations, should not be contemptuous” (Kings, ministers, lay people who do not have rules and regulations, should not be disdainful): King, ministers, you yourself have not received precepts and have no rules and regulations, how can you look down on that person? What's more, they're still being punished! “Such as a Buddha, even though it is not a Dharma weapon, he withdraws from the holy Dharma, impures the holy Dharma, impures the Dharma activities of all monks in the four directions, but if his body and teachings are in harmony with the Sangha, he attains the rules and rituals, he does not let go.” (Such an O-Sup is not a Dharma weapon, he withdraws from the Holy Dharma, impures the pure Sangha, destroys the Dharma activities of all monks, and is not allowed to receive the Dharma activities of all monks from the four directions. but because he did not abandon the rules and rituals that were transmitted from the teaching body in harmony with the Sangha). Because at first he received the precepts and learned the Vinaya from his Teacher, that person has not yet completely abandoned the discipline that was transmitted by the Sangha. Therefore, that person is still superior to all white-clothed people at home. Having violated the basic precepts, “committing a sinful nature, the highest level of acceptance is like this” ([for] those who commit a sinful nature, it should still be like that). For a [bhikkhu] who violates the basic precepts, a layman with white robes, or the king should not even look down on that person, nor should he be punished. Even if a Bhikkhu breaks the precepts and commits a small crime, he should not do it, that is, he should not be punished.

If the king, ministers, and lay people despise and punish [a monk who breaks the precepts], it is not right! Don't blame or despise that person. Having said that, it seems that the Buddha was very protective of his disciples, who even broke the precepts and still protected them like that! Absolutely not because of this reason. It's not about protecting them, it's about protecting you, protecting the lay people who slander them, fearing that you will bury your merits and fall into hell. Isn't it about protecting that [precept-breaker]! If we observe incorrectly, [we will think] the Buddha protects his disciples who break the precepts, just like we lay people protect our own children, or like a company protects its own officials. Using that concept to understand the Buddha is a mistake! Why say so? Because the Buddha protects you so you don't commit crimes, it's not at all protecting Bhikkhus who break that precept. Whoever defames that person, whatever that person does, that person must be punished, but if you defame that person, you will be guilty. This is to protect you, don't do that.

(Sutra) Why is it fake? Good man! In the past, there was the king of Ca Xa with the name Pham Tho, the color of Chien-do-la: "There is a great king, named Thanh Lien Muc, with six teeth, residing in the Tuyet mountain border, if he can pass away, he can take advantage of the future. If he is not successful, if he is like the five people, he will be inactive." During, Chien-dà-la protects the life of the body, upholds bows and arrows, flies off the chain, disguises himself as a majestic monk in the form of a monk, visits the Snow Mountain border, and reaches the king's image. At that time, the mother statue of Dao saw Nhan Lai, grasped the bow and arrow, the sutra of Ba Ba Tu, Nghe Tuong Vuong So, said: "Dai Thien! Kim saw the right person to open the palace, the bow and arrow, from the action to the siam, the beast to the ego, the future to the concubine, the desire to take the skin?" The statue of the king of literature, with the purpose of seeing the world except cultivating, in front of Ca-sa Nhan, that is, the mother statue, recited and wrote: "If you are degraded by the old age, all Buddhas and dharmas are filled with signs, contemplate and abandon all evils, and certainly do not harm sentient beings." At, the mother statue chanted and wrote in response: "Even though I am obeyed by the Dharma, I hold on to bows and arrows, look at the Lamb-dala, mock evil, and have no compassion." During, the great statue of King Phuc recited and wrote: "Seeing the one form of Ca-sa, knowing the original compassion, testing all Buddhas, mindfully reciting sentient beings. Doubting things, doubts quickly take hold of the mind, being tested by the forensic pathologist, saving the sea of ​​birth and death."
(Sutra: Why is that so? Good man! In the past, there was a country named Ca Xa, a king named Pham Tho, the edict of Chien-do-la: “There is a great elephant king, named Thanh Lien Muc, with six tusks, next to Tuyet mountain. You should go there and break the tusks back. If you cannot get it, the five of you should not expect to live anymore!” At that time, Chien-do-la, in order to preserve his life, grabbed a bow and arrow, wore a red scarf, and pretended to show his majesty and appearance. monk, came to the Snow Mountain, to the king's elephant. At that time, the female elephant saw someone coming from afar, holding a bow and arrow, so she was frightened and ran to the king's elephant, saying: “Dai Thien! Now I see someone holding a bow, nocking an arrow, walking leisurely and looking at us, isn't it because he wants to take our lives?" The king elephant heard, Raising his eyes, he immediately saw the person shaving off his beard and hair, putting on the robe, and immediately recited a chant for the female elephant: “The person who wears the Dharma field, of the Buddhas of the Constant Saṃsa Buddhas, considering that he is far from all evil, will not harm sentient beings”At that time, the female elephant chanted in verse: “Even though he knows how to wear Dharma clothes, but holding a bow and arrow is evil. At that time, the great statue king again spoke verses and chanted: “Seeing the appearance of ca-sa, knowing that he is inherently compassionate, he will return to Buddha, thinking of compassion for sentient beings. You should quickly take heart, the person wearing this dharma robe, wants to cross the sea of birth and death”).

This is the Buddha himself giving an example: There was a great king elephant named Thanh Lien Muc (eyes like blue lotus). A white elephant with six tusks is a precious elephant. Where is it? On the side of Snow Mountain. In the past, there was a country named Ca Xa La, whose king was named Pham Tho. The king looked for a few evil people of the Lamb-dala, that is, evil people of the Lamb-dala nature. The king told them: "There is a great king elephant named Thanh Lien Muc, with six tusks, on the Snow Mountain. His tusks are precious. You go there, break his tusks for me. If you can't break his tusks, I will kill all of you." Those five Lambs had no choice but to protect their own lives, so they went and killed that elephant. They knew that if they used their own strength, they would definitely be trampled to death by that elephant. Because elephants have great power, what do they do? They immediately took their bows and arrows, stayed far away from the elephant, dressed as monks, shaved their hair, found red robes, and pretended to assume the majesty and appearance of monks. “Vang Tuyet mountain border, the king's image” (To the side of Snow mountain, to the king's elephant). That king elephant has a female elephant; From afar, the female elephant saw someone holding a bow and arrow coming to this place, she was very frightened, ran to the king's elephant to report, praised the king's elephant, praised the great heavens: "The golden ants are holding bows, shooting arrows, from action to siem" (Now I see someone holding bows, nocking arrows, walking leisurely to look around). He said: "I'm just afraid they'll come and hurt us. As they go, they search and search." “Self-level hybrid beast” means coming to us, doesn't it mean to destroy our lives? Are we going to die?

After listening, the elephant king looked, immediately saw the person shaving off his beard and hair, applying a ka-sa, and then spoke verses and chanted to the female elephant: "Fallen by the old age, the Buddhas of the Dharma-field, contemplating the separation from all evil beings, must not harm sentient beings" (He wears the form of the Dharma-garden, of the Buddhas of the Constant Saṅgha, contemplates them leaving evil things, will not harm sentient beings). It said: "You are wrong. These people, wearing robes, have planted good roots in Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. The clothes they wear are the dharma fields of all Buddhas. These are robes. They have left evil, how can they harm living beings?" The elephant king said so. The female elephant replied: "Even though we know they wear Dharma clothes, they hold bows and arrows, that is, they are evil Lamb-dala, love to do evil, have no compassion." Because they cannot be compassionate, they will like to do evil things. Those people are all evil Lambo-la. Even though he wears legal clothes, how can he hold a bow and arrow? They're pretending!

The elephant king still spoke, and used verses to chant: "Seeing ca-sa's one form, knowing the original compassion" (Seeing the appearance of ca-sa, knowing that it is inherently compassionate): The elephant king said: "Let them go! Just seeing ca-sa, will be full of compassion. The person wearing ca-sa is basically compassionate, definitely compassionate." compassion for all living beings”. “If one tries to return to Buddha” (That person will definitely return to Buddha), he is definitely a disciple of Buddha. “Mindfulness for all sentient beings” (Pity for all sentient beings): Compassion, compassion for all sentient beings. “Don't harbor doubts” (Don't harbor doubts), meaning: Don't be too suspicious. “If you have doubts, quickly capture your mind” (You should quickly capture your mind): Collect your mind, stop thinking like that! A person wearing a ka-sa wants to cross the sea of ​​birth and death, how can he harm living beings?

(Sutra) Time, Fried-dala-i> Because of the poison arrow, the arrow shot from the bow and arrow and hit the king's heart. The mother statue saw the branch, moving in a clear, sad manner, reciting the words: "The person who was tested by the dharma doctor, doubts that he has returned to the Buddha, his dignity is quiet, but he is filled with evil thoughts, the eagle quickly tramples on the body, the soul's life and roots are cut off, the spirit of resentment is destroyed, and the body of the heavens is destroyed." At, the great king replied by reciting: "Quickly abandoning one's life and life, without giving birth to evil thoughts, despite being persistent and deceitful, it is from the Buddha's disciples. The wise do not pay for their lives, when they are destroyed, they purify their minds, for the sake of saving sentient beings, and often practice the Bodhi practice." At, the great elephant king's heart was filled with compassion, and he wrote: "What do you practice?" The benefactor replied and wrote: "Duc cultivating." The king of the statue rejoiced, that is, he gave alms to Chien-do-la, and then recited and wrote: "I have no anger, no hatred, no attachment. Pprayer to try to give blessings and become a Buddha, destroy all sentient beings' afflictions and diseases."
(Sutra: At that time, Chien-do-la immediately used a poisoned arrow to draw the bow, aim and shoot, hitting the elephant's heart The female elephant saw it, roared loudly, mourned, and choked up, chanting in verses: “This person wearing dharma robes, should take refuge in Buddha, majestic and calm, but embracing evil, quickly tramples on their bodies, in order to destroy their lives, destroy all this resentment, dares to shoot the body of the great thousand”. At that time, the great elephant king replied in verses: “It is better to quickly let go of one's life and life than to give rise to evil thoughts. Even though their minds are deceitful, they are still like Buddha's disciples. Wise people do not destroy their lives for the sake of their lives, but their minds are pure. To save sentient beings, they often practice Bodhicitta"At that time, the great statue king had a compassionate mind and leisurely asked those people: “What do you need? What?” Those people replied: “Want your ivory”. The elephant king was happy, pulled out the ivory himself, gave it to Chien-do-la, and recited verses: “Now use the white ivory to give to you, without anger, without hatred, without regret. I pray that this blessing will become a Buddha and eliminate your diseases and afflictions sentient beings”).

Right while the [elephant king] was speaking, the evil Lambu-la drew his bow and shot a poisonous arrow that hit the elephant's heart. “The mother statue sees the chi, carries the clear trenches, laments the hardships, recites the words: - Being tested by the ca-sa, doubts that she will return to Buddha, her majesty is still quiet, her heart is full of malice” (The female elephant sees it, roars loudly, mourns, chokes up, uses verses to recite: - This person wearing the ca-sa, should take refuge in the Buddha, majestic and quiet, but holding a cruel heart). Their majesty looks so good, but their hearts are so evil! “Quickly step on their bodies” (Quickly step on their bodies): The female elephant said, I will kill them. “The spirit of life is cut off” (To end their lives). Killing means ending the life base. “Destroy the spirit of resentment” (Destroy all this resentment): This resentful spirit, I will not destroy them, I will not be willing! Only by destroying them will my hatred disappear, all my resentment will be gone. The Great Elephant King did not approve, and used verses to tell the female elephant: "Quickly let go of one's life and life, but without giving rise to evil thoughts" (It is better to quickly let go of one's life and life, and not give rise to evil thoughts): Big advice to the female elephant, don't let go of evil thoughts a thousand times, I will give up my life and that's enough. “Even though they are deceitful in mind, they are disciples of Buddha” (Even though they are deceitful in heart, they are still like disciples of Buddha): Even though they are not real disciples of Buddha, they are deceitful, but they are similar. Why? They wear the clothes of Buddhist disciples. “Wise people do not care for their lives” (Wise people do not care for their lives): People with absolute wisdom do not protect their own lives, “the pure mind” (but destroys the pure mind): Destroying our pure mind. It's okay to sacrifice your life! Cannot destroy a pure mind. “For the sake of saving sentient beings, often practice the Bodhi practice” (For the sake of saving sentient beings, often practice the Bodhi practice): Must generate the cause of Bodhi, practice the Bodhi practice. Having a pure mind is the practice of Bodhi, one can definitely attain Bodhi.

“At that time, the great elephant king had compassion” (At that time, the great elephant king had compassion): To the person who shot it, not only did it not hurt, but on the contrary, it also pitied them. “Tu asks people to write” (Loosely ask them): “Tu” is slow, gentle, kind. “Nhu Ha So Tu?” (What do you need?): Ask why you have to shoot me, what do you need? They replied, that is, those Lamb-dala guys replied: "Duc tu tu tu tu tu tuh!" meaning "want to have your tusks". After hearing this, the elephant king was very happy and personally pulled out the ivory for the Lamb and gave alms to them. "I have no anger, no hatred, no greed" (The white ivory is now given to you, no anger, no hatred, no greed): I have no greed, I have no greed for my own body, I have no regrets either. You shoot me, I don't hate you, I don't resent you. My purpose is to give you this ivory as alms. Because of this merit of giving, you will become a Buddha. In the future, we can definitely become a Buddha, and we can also use this merit to destroy all the diseases and afflictions of sentient beings. I vow to destroy the afflictions and suffering of all sentient beings.

(Sutra) Good man! Contemplating the image of a king in the past, although he has lived in the body of an endless animal, he seeks Anuttara Sammyu and Sambodhi, and has the energy to sacrifice his life without cheating. He is respectful and respectful to people, but even though he has committed a grudge, he will not be punished. Of course, in the future world,, there are Kshatriyas, kings, officials, lay people, wealthy people, monks, Brahmins of the Chongdala level, who are truly foolish, always clever and arrogant, arrogant, hypocritical, deceitful, when they are caught up in the world, without any knowledge, without fear of the suffering consequences of the future. If you return to the Dharma Nhi and become a monk, the disciples are weak in the Dharma weapon, weak in the Dharma weapon, and their minds are confused. They may be forced to die, and the staff will be forced to die. If the Buddhas of the past, future, or present must commit all the great sins, they must decide to enter the Uninterrupted Hell, destroy their good roots, and burn the continuity, and the wise must depart.
(Sutra: Good man! You should contemplate the elephant king in the past like that, even though your life is not easy. In the path of rebirth, because of the pursuit of Supreme Enlightenment, one can abandon one's life and life without any regret, respecting and respecting the person who wears the ka-sa robe. Even though that person causes resentment and does not take revenge, in the future there will be King Sat-de-li Chien-tà-la, officials, lay people, monks, and Brahmins who are truly foolish, conceited, clever, flattering, and brahmin people. Therefore, lying, deceiving the world, without seeing or fearing the consequences of suffering in the next life, if the disciples who have become monks rely on my dharma, whether it is a dharma weapon or not a dharma weapon, their minds are disturbed, they are scolded, they are scolded, or they are using whips or sticks to beat their bodies, or they are imprisoned in prison, until the end of their lives. That person commits the great sins of all past, future, and present Buddhas, and will definitely enter the Hell of No Interruption, destroying their roots. good, burning continuously, all wise people are far away).

That elephant king was originally an animal, took on the body of an animal, that is, animal life. “If you seek Anuttara Sammyak Sambodhi, you will be able to let go of your life without regret” (For the sake of seeking Supreme Enlightenment, you can let go of your body and life without being stingy): Letting go of your body and life without regret or resentment, you can revere and respect the person wearing the ka-sa, and respect the person wearing the ka-sa. Kāṣāya is patience. Ca-sa has many meanings. "Even though he caused resentment, he did not retaliate" (Even though that person caused resentment but did not take revenge): That person shot him to death, he should have held grudges, had to hold grudges, but he did not take revenge. If we use the king's elephant's strength to take revenge, those five men will no longer have a life!

“Of course, in the future, there will be Kshatriya-kings, ministers, laymen, wealthy people, monks, Brahmins of the Chongla-class, who are truly foolish, too clever and arrogant, delusional, deceitful, when they are attached to the world, without any knowledge, without fear of the suffering of the future consequences. "But in the future there will be King Sat-de-li Chien-tà-la, ministers, lay people, wealthy people, monks, Brahmins who are Choi-dà-la guys, truly stupid, conceited to be intelligent, deceitful, deceitful, deceiving the world, not seeing, not afraid of the suffering in the next life, for those who take refuge in the Dharma I am ordained, even though is a dharma weapon, or not a dharma weapon): “Dharma weapon” is a disciple who maintains the precepts, “non-dharma weapon” is a disciple who breaks the precepts. Regardless of the dharma weapon, or the non-dharma aura, a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts is considered superior to all worldly people, whether kings, ministers, or commoners. “Red color” is red, but when the Buddha was in the world, his robe was always dyed with discoloration, not bright red. For example, the lama's clothes are all red mixed with purple (Maroon color), the yellow robe is not bright yellow. After [Buddhism] spread to China, our clothes turned bright red and bright yellow. That's because the king at that time, also King Sat-di-loi, wanted to do so, in order to show respect, [so] the monks all corrected it. But we monastics wear this outfit, a square-flashed, round-neck ao dai, which is the clothing of the Han Dynasty people.

Furthermore, pagodas and temples are called Tu, which is the name of the Han dynasty mandarin's palace, that is, the workplace, or the government's gate. At that time, [national guests] coming from abroad, or from India, were brought to Hong Lo Tu[74], equivalent to the reception place of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. There are many rooms to entertain them. Therefore, a temple was built, not called a temple, nor called Sangha-lam, but called a Temple. The temple was originally the Hong Lu Temple of the Han Dynasty. The halls and institutes of the government are all called Tu. It's okay to know the meaning of this. Now the meaning contained in this passage is slightly different. “Xich ca-sa” is a red ca-sa shirt. Y ca-sa translates as “liberation garment”, [implying] wearing that garment will liberate. But currently there is no liberation, wearing robes still does not liberate, just like in the previous section we said: There are many Bhikkhus who break the precepts, the Buddha still allows you to make offerings, you still have to support that person, do not allow harm to that person. What does that mean? Due to the meaning: That person can still make others see the Bhikkhu's appearance and create merit fields for others. Nowadays, there are times when even a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts cannot see it. This section includes many Rakshasa mothers and children and their relatives as mentioned above "arising from the mind". “Due to the test of fate, people admired Duc, the shop converted to King Thiem Bo Chau” (Due to that cause, everyone who admired Duc gradually turned to the king's teachings in Thiem Bo Chau): Because King Thang Quan did so, establishing this type of law, exempting the death penalty, exempting death penalty, is not for All people, but for monks, must be respectful, must worship, and must pay homage. “Regulation” is as everyone knows, once you come to Canada, you have to become a citizen. That is called “regularization”. You have to take an oath, you still have to swear. When I was in New York, after taking the oath, a fellow monk came back and said to me: "Today the examiner asked me: Suppose we fought with China, fought with the Chinese. We sent you to fight the enemy, would you go or not?" I asked: "How did you answer?" He replied: "Let's go! Of course we go." I said: "If you answer like that, you are not a disciple of Buddha!" He was very surprised and asked: "How should I answer?" I said: "You should answer, I hope you don't start a war. You sent me to fight, I won't go, if I don't become a naturalized citizen then that's it!" Because the Demon Mother of Rakshasa wants you to be converted, do you also submit and be willing to be taught by them? Everyone, think about it, you may not be asked that question, but you may also be asked this question!

Anything that causes harm to others, I will not do it. [Things that are harmful to] animals, I wouldn't do it! If we want to kill animals, we don't kill animals. No matter what nationality you enter, if it sends you to kill your own people, can you make that wish or not? Pay attention, don't miss out on a lot of happiness in the future because of immediate benefits. If you think it's empty talk, no problem! Oh my! Don't think it's just talk, when you take the oath of naturalization, it's not a vow, it's an oath. After taking the oath, if you don't do it, it will be a lie; If you do, you will hurt others, not even animals!

“Good man! Contemplate like the past Rakshasa, even though you have an endless life of hungry ghosts and beasts” (Hey good man! That is because of past karma, or because karma causes obstacles. There's no way, it's a small thing! Be brave and diligent and you can do it! “Infinite Eight, Ten Perfections”[77]: It is impossible to wish for such a human body!

Let's take myself as an example. I was in prison for several decades. I wanted to learn Buddhism, worship, and repent but I couldn't, I didn't have that opportunity. That is called “inferior”. You want your body to be perfect, it's very difficult! They were originally a Rakshasa ghost, were idle, and were hungry ghosts. They can see that person and not eat meat, which is very rare! That person commits great sins against all past, future, and present Buddhas, destroys good roots, burns continuously, all wise people are separated, and will be reborn in the Hell of No Intermittent.

Those Lambo-la guys did evil things that were even worse than Rakshasa and Duoc Xoa. “Foolish and arrogant”, without wisdom. I have no wisdom and am still very arrogant. "Destroying the good roots. “Continuous burning” (Continuous burning): This is a visual way of speaking. Therefore, stop killing, the king will rule over Thiem Bo Chau. Good man, you should contemplate the drunken elephant in the past like that, even though your life is not leisurely in the realm of life, but respect the ca-sa, do not create bad karma.

This is telling old stories. Old stories will inspire us to develop faith. In the past, there was a king named Sieu Phuoc Duc who committed a crime. “The crime is merciful, the king is merciful, does not want to destroy his life” (The crime deserves to die, the king is merciful, does not want to end his life): The king does not want to kill that sinner, does not want to end his life, which means he wants to exempt him from the death penalty. Although he committed a very serious crime and deserved the death penalty, they attempted to exile him. “One great minister, many wise people” means that there is a great minister who is very wise and has strategies. "Deeply respecting and admiring that person. Good men, you should contemplate the drunken elephant in the past like that, even though your life will not be leisurely in the path of rebirth; In the above part it is the hungry ghost, here it is the animal, the sentient beings in the three evil realms all have such great reverence towards the sinner wearing the red ka-sa. “I respect ca-sa, do not create bad karma” (Respect ca-sa, do not create bad karma), but humans are not like that.

When is “Futuristic”? It could be our present time! Currently called Dharma Ending. Is current society really like that? Just like where we are in a place where Buddha Dharma is, we still know what the Three Jewels are, but where there is no Buddha Dharma, we basically don't understand what the Three Jewels are! The Great Brahma King also protects and upholds the Buddha Dharma, requests the Dharma, and specializes in upholding the Buddha Dharma.

I have seen a few monks in America. They go to work, earn money, earn money to a certain level, then go to the retreat center to do a retreat: Hand over ten thousand dong to do a retreat for three years, three months, or three days. There was a person who worked half a day and studied the Dharma half a day. Currently, there are still more countries without the Three Jewels. For example, if Mainland China and Taiwan have the Three Jewels, do [the masses] respect monks or not? Most people are respectful, but there are still some people who are not. As for Bhikkhus who break the precepts, or Bhikkhus and Bhikkhunis who do not practice, they will be defamed.

If you read the Mahabodhi Sutra with confidence, you will be able to [have a] slightly better attitude. If you don't believe it, keep it that way. That's what Buddha said. Those people, even the king, mandarins, and people "are always cruel" (embrace cruelty), are not compassionate, keep doing exactly that, even more fierce than an evil elephant getting drunk, losing its good roots.

For the disciples who rely on the Buddha's Dharma to become monks, whether it is a Dharma weapon, or not a Dharma weapon, shaving off hair and beard, wearing Dharma clothes, they are not respectful, do not have a heart of reverence, are just confused, scolding, cursing, even using whips and sticks to beat them and put them in prison. This happened quite a lot at the time of the founding of the People's Republic of China. At that time, monastics in temples and pagodas were forced to renounce their religion and return to secular life. It was not until 1980 that, according to religious policy, they restored and returned the pagodas and temples to the monks. When the policy was implemented, if you wanted to find monks, you couldn't find them, so you had to look for monks who had returned to the secular world and got married. In the beginning, from 1980 to 1983, the situation was like that, [those monks who had returned to secular life] wore lay clothes to go to work, went to temples and shrines to work, and then put on their robes. If you have something to do, you put it on, when you're done, you get off work, hang up your robe, and go home. Nowadays it's not like that anymore. Since 1983, the policy has been implemented further. Sangha after Sangha, pagoda after pagoda, from then on the original state was restored!

Stealing the pagoda's fields and gardens, plundering the pagoda's rooms, if you have committed such a crime, you must receive retribution. “Male and female pure people” is like this: In temples and shrines [if they are nuns, the pure people] are all women.
