After Thien Tang Dai Pham finished speaking this mantra, he wished the World-Honored One and the assembly to be happy. The Buddha then told his great disciple Maudgalyayana and Bodhisattva Maitreya. Maitreya Bodhisattva is a great disciple among the Bodhisattvas, Maudgalyayana is a great disciple among the Shravakas. Maitreya Bodhisattva was born in India, manifesting a physical body, unlike Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara). Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is not in this world, He appears. The Buddha told Maudgalyayana and Maitreya Bodhisattva: "You should all receive and uphold the National Protection of the Non-Returning Mind Dharani Mantra spoken by Thien Store Maha Pham, so that in the future life, in this Buddha land, the person who has a mind that truly seeks liberation, will become a good person, so that a king of the Kshatriya nature like that will accept it himself. At the same time, because he leads the people in the country, he will cause everyone to accept it. Thus, It will bring benefits and happiness to that country. Because of him, the Dharma can always exist and the Dharma wheel will always turn. At the same time, the king's reputation will also be high and majestic.

In such a country, wrong knowledge and wrong views will be reduced, establishing a type of right knowledge and right view. That is due to the blessing power of this mantra. Due to the blessing of this mantra, it protects the dharma eye. The Dharma eye is the Dharma that abides in the world, just like the eyeballs. Only people with eyes can see. Without eyesight, nothing can be seen. Only then will the Three Jewels last forever in the world, and they will also be able to shine brightly and never be cut off. If there is a dharma, it will be possible to mature immeasurable, boundless sentient beings. All sentient beings who listen to the dharma will be able to achieve liberation and attain salvation.

When we preach the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, it is to make you achieve faith. The Bodhisattva who arose in that sutra was called Kien Tinh Tin. Now our faith is like a feather in the air, swaying in the wind. When we encounter a realm, we are blown to that place. It is neither steadfast nor pure. Steadfast faith seems so easy! If you can have faith, you can become a Buddha. That is the cause, becoming Buddha is the result. Cultivating pure faith takes ten thousand great eons, it is very difficult! What we are practicing in the present is to make our faith pure, always solid, unshakable! When we encounter a realm, we are immediately shaken. If so, if you hope to attain Buddhahood, it will not be possible! If you want to practice the Six Paramitas, you can't! It is necessary to have pure faith, the Six Paramitas will be complete. Without pure faith, whatever you do is mixed with impurities and impurities! For example, today we also practice giving and also practice renunciation, but your practice of renunciation is not pure! For example, when it's winter, we have extra clothes so we let loose a bit. With what mind do you dispose of the extra clothes? This has huge implications. Have pure faith, respect others, don't consider others as beggars!

We are teaching the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma again. In the Ksitigarbha Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva asked the Buddha, why after giving alms, some people enjoy blessings for one life, some people enjoy blessings for ten lifetimes, some people enjoy blessings for hundreds of lifetimes, thousands of lifetimes, and some people enjoy immeasurable blessings? Why do we both practice almsgiving in the same way, give the same things as alms [yet we enjoy such different blessings?] It is due to the discriminating mind. If you respect others, you will have a heart of offering. If you practice giving alms [with the mind of offering], it will be like offering to the Buddha, offering to the Dharma, offering to the Sangha.

In all the sutras, almost [all teach to give alms like] offerings to the Buddha, offerings to the Dharma, offerings to the Sangha. Respecting all living beings, he makes offerings to all living beings. Making offerings to the Buddha, making offerings to the Dharma, making offerings to the Sangha, and also making offerings to all sentient beings, that is, to demons and gods, treating them as sentient beings, are all Bodhisattvas. Use that mind to make offerings to everything, to the end of space, to the entire dharma realm, infinitely, endlessly, then your merit will be great. Although the material donation is not much, the generosity is enormous. When we repent, it's the same. Although it is said that "doing evil is not great", but day and night continuously, if the mind is strong, that evil will be great, that evil will spread throughout the dharma realm. Why do we still refuse to leave, unable to fully attain Buddhahood? Due to such reasons. You must use your heart to repent. Only then can we reach the end!

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - During the Thien Tang Dai Pham period, asked the two With the Sun, benefiting all sentient beings, mocking and cultivating Concentration, chanting, blessings, understanding the king of wisdom, becoming dharma, ascending to advancement, falling into the world? To practice the three things, to eliminate them Or not to retreat? The World-Honored One blasphemed, if one violates the conduct of Non-Importance, even though the enlightenment of wisdom is powerful, the child will be in the Infinite Hell. Unleashing the truth, mocking the Ten Evil Wheels, destroying good roots, and speeding up the path to hell. Concentrate on eliminating afflictions and chanting meritorious karma. Trying hard to seek Nirvana, always practicing Tinh Lu. Having wisdom, being diligent, protecting oneself in the Dharma, due to faith in ka-sa, one can overcome the sea of ​​afflictions, ridding oneself of idleness, far from creating others of the same kind, respectfully upholding the precepts and cultivating concentration, saving the sea of ​​beings. Universal faith in the three vehicles, upholding the true Dharma, respectfully wearing the robe, attaining the ocean of merit.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One wanted to reveal this meaning again, so he recited verses: "When Thien Store Maha Brahma asked the Two Perfect Ones, sentient beings with good faculties, like to practice Concentration, chanting, blessings, the king penetrates wisdom into dharma, ascends or descends? Of the three things that have been practiced, which dharma will eliminate Or, causing the attainment of non-regression? The World-Honored One told him: If one violates Non-Yāhāna, even though one's enlightenment is strong, one will still go to the prison of Non-Recurrence. Not truly proficient in wisdom, one likes to do the ten evil cycles, destroy good roots, quickly enter hell. Concentration eliminates afflictions, does not Therefore, when praying for Nirvana, one should often practice Tranquility. If one has wisdom, diligently and diligently upholds the Buddha's Dharma, one will overcome the sea of afflictions, prefer to live in a quiet place, stay away from others, practice Concentration, and will cross the sea of three realms, and prosper in the Buddha's Dharma.

This passage of the sutra belonging to the chapter on Non-Yāhāhna was basically about to be completed, the Buddha then repeated the meanings contained in it once again. In this verse, [Buddha recalls the story of] Thien Tang Dai Pham asking, repeating his question. Thien Tang Dai Pham came to "interrogate the Tathagata" (ask the Blessed One). This is the Blessed One speaking the verse. recitation, is not Thien Tang Dai Pham speaking? Because, after having finished saying this meaning, the Buddha repeated it a little. Why? In the Buddha's sermon hall, not all of the audience were present from the beginning, there were also people who had not heard the passage, the Buddha repeated it, but did not say it in such detail Among the Bodhisattvas and Sravakas, there are often those who have to go very far due to their career of transformation. In this Mahayana practice, without waiting for them to return, the Buddha used the verses to repeat them all in one go. [Just] briefly speaking, they will understand clearly, sometimes the verses are very long, sometimes very simplified says one thing, but the verse recited here summarizes the meanings [in this sutra].

Thien Tang Dai Pham asked: "Practicing concentration, cultivating blessings, chanting sutras, which dharma is good? Of these three dharmas, which dharma is supreme? Is there an order or not?" Because when he asked, the Buddha taught three types of karma, namely cultivating Concentration karma, reciting karma, and creating meritorious karma. The World-Honored One told him, that is, “false words”, all three of those subjects were good. If you commit Non-Conformity, that is, Non-Acts, then your practice actions will not be able to produce merit, will not be able to give birth to merit. By cultivating Vo Y Hanh, the deeds they have done will be Void Hanh. Not relying on the Three Jewels, even doing things against the religion, means not listening to the teachings of the Tathagata. Even though that person is very intelligent, has enlightenment wisdom and is also very strong and sensitive, but that person has committed Non-Yh Hanh, or the ten evil wheels mentioned in the previous section, if there is one evil wheel, what that person practices will not be accomplished. No matter how smart you are, no matter how wise you are, you will still fall into the Hell of No Interruptions. Why? Because that person's wisdom and intelligence are not genuine, [that is the meaning of the sentence] “non-truthful and wise”. What would true wisdom and intelligence look like? Do not do the ten evil things! Just like with the ten evil wheels in the previous section, if the person does not have any of them, he will have true wisdom. Now that we have learned the Ten Evil Wheels, we can compare ourselves a bit to see if we have committed the Ten Evil Wheels or not?

For example, the issue of vegetarianism and non-vegetarianism makes many people very confused. There are people who want to leave the world, who also hate birth and death, who are tired of leaving the suffering in the world, and also want to recite the Buddha's name to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, but in the East (Sa Ba) eating meat and drinking wine, that person cannot let go! Some people think that if they have to be vegetarian, it will be very difficult, indeed it is very difficult, because of the practice from beginningless time until now, they will encounter difficulties. If that person sees monks, some monks still eat salty food, that person will choose to eat salty food. Eating salty food makes you want to become a Buddha in the West, but still eating meat in the East. If you say it like that, psychologically, this is no problem, it depends on whether you are liberated or not? But because the psychology has been violated, that is not truly having wisdom!

Also, as for clothes, are we wearing clothes properly or not? I think we should pay attention to clothes. In the summer you have to dress a little thinner and stay a little cooler, in the winter you have to stay warmer. Clothes are intended to protect our bodies. Nowadays it's gone wrong, wearing clothes is for others to see! In the current era, focusing on fashion and wearing clothes for others to see is a sin for yourself. The body is tight and very uncomfortable. For example, in the US, there are companies that stipulate that [women] must wear skirts to work. In such a cold winter, so many degrees below zero, she looked very beautiful in a dress, letting her thighs show out. Women's thighs [due to not being kept warm] cause many diseases. Especially for women, it will lead to irregular menstruation and all kinds of diseases in the lower body. She would rather sacrifice her life and still have to dress a little prettier, afraid that if she is not beautiful, she won't make others like her. You see, whether you wear lipstick or makeup, the point is to let others see you and like you, not for yourself, but for others. That's not necessary!

Once upon a time, there was an old monk who received an offering from a benefactor. The entire family, ever since the Master began practicing the Way, has been enthusiastic about making offerings. Over the past two or three generations, they have all made offerings to the Master. The old monk lived a long time, practicing in the mountains. One time, when there was a happy event in that family, the old monk came there to change the fate and come to receive rice. The monk stood outside the door and saw that the house was planning a party, so he cried loudly. Others asked the Master: "Old monk! Today we have a great joy, you came here, why did you come to announce the funeral, what are you crying about?" The monk said: "Poor my old benefactor, pity the suffering sentient beings, my grandson marries his grandmother!" The monk said: "This is what I see for myself. She was reborn as a human again, as a bride for her grandson." “The monk sits on the throne, the six-bodied oa ly chu” (Pigs and goats sit on the feast, the six-bodied cooks in the pot).

When grandmother got married, all six relatives turned into pigs and goats. Now the grandchild is getting married, the pigs and goats are sitting at a feast, and the six relatives from back then are being cooked in a pot. The monk has supernatural powers and can see clearly. This has the meaning of a book scene. Why do we have to liberating living beings (life release)? We must save sentient beings and repent of our sins. Releasing life eliminates karma the fastest. You don't want to get sick, so it's okay to liberating living beings (life release). Making others live happily, makes your life happy too. A person who destroys good roots and practices the ten evil cycles will not fall into hell? Of course it's hell! Buddha said: “Concentration can cut off afflictions, not by practicing chanting and creating merit”. So Concentration is not the merit of listening and studying the sutras, because that blessing can belong to the worldly blessings, which has such a meaning. If you wish for Nirvana, you must constantly practice Concentration and Tinh Lu. Tinh Lu is not necessarily Zen meditation, Tinh Lu means your mind must always observe. Or observe with Chi. Just observing is Concentration, or the wisdom of observing. Observing Hue is cultivating Hue, which is also applying both Samatha and Contemplation, which has the same meaning! If you have wisdom and still have the courage to practice diligently, how can you practice? Protecting the Buddha's Dharma, protecting the Dharma is practicing.

“Due to the faith of ca-sa”: Believe in that robe. Because in the previous section, many examples were given, such as the Rakshasa demon seeing a piece of red casa, not eating that person's flesh because of respect. Respect gives rise to pure faith, don't discount it. “The sea of ​​afflictions” (Able to cross the sea of ​​afflictions): With such faith, one can cross the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death. Next, don't look for a bustling place, find a deep, quiet forest, not interacting with evil people, until you are far away from the hustle and bustle of society. Only by cultivating Concentration can you practice successfully. Only when you practice precepts can you maintain them firmly. Until “respectfully keep the precepts, cultivate Concentration” (respectfully keep the precepts, cultivate Concentration) in that place, external objective circumstances do not cause you to commit crimes, the opportunity to commit crimes is very small. In the state of Concentration, the mind of greed does not arise, especially when sitting in the poetry room[89], you see that every moment a corpse is brought in, it will rot after death, and as soon as you see it, a mind of boredom arises. You are the same, your own body will be the same.

Therefore, in this illusory human world saving sentient beings, he does not see sentient beings as real, only sees them as dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. If all sentient beings are true, the Bodhisattva will be filled with great compassion all day long. I am afraid that even I will suffer and die. They were not swayed by the scene, realizing that it was an illusion. If we do not have such concentration, nor do we have many good roots, we can only stay away and not go to noisy places, only then can we cross the sea of ​​“Beings” (twenty-five Beings, the three worlds).

“Universal faith in the three vehicles” (Complete faith in the three vehicles): With regard to the three vehicles, no distinction arises. It's the same with the Shravaka Vehicle, it's the same with the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, it's the same with the Bodhisattva Vehicle, only then can we "prosperize our true Dharma". “Respectfully wearing fake robes, you will achieve ocean of merit” (Respecting those wearing dyed clothes, you will achieve ocean of merit): If you seek merit, make many offerings to the monks, seclusion and purity. You should not distinguish whether this person is a holy monk or not, or whether that person is a violator or not. In your mind, there is basically no such idea, you are all Buddhists.

(Sutra) Ability to overcome difficulties to control the mind, not to turn away from sins. By cultivating the holy seed, you will become the Two Perfect Venerable. Far away from evil, close to the holy land. Not practical Increase things, quickly attain great Bodhi. The three realms are peaceful and peaceful, and the stage is born from the Three Jewels. Trying to pray for peace and happiness, often making offerings to the Three Jewels. Chien-dà-la is king, equal to the evil party. When the Three Jewels arise, they quickly fall into the Infinite Hell. Ten times of wandering, the most despicable of sexual immorality. The wisdom of the ten sects of sexual immorality is the first class of the crime of alcoholism. Tri is the top 10 worst offenders, the worst ward. The wisdom of the ten wards, the crime is the king of the highest rank. The king of truth and goodness, upholding the righteous Dharma, making offerings to the three vehicles, attaining the ocean of merit. The seven treasures fulfill the Thien Bodhisattva, serving the Buddha to bring the Sangha, gathering blessings, and protecting the Buddha Dharma. The Buddha and the Sangha create their own words, are equal to the fourteen continents, and are able to gather blessings, not like protecting the Buddha Dharma. Creating a good-pouring-three Buddha, equal to the three heavenly realms, gathering blessings at the base, is not like protecting the Buddha Dharma. Resolving Arhat's blessings, cultivating and making offerings to all races, unobstructing the true Dharma, allowing blessings to prevail. In the middle of the celestial kalpa, the wise person needs to cultivate Concentration, so that enlightenment can be born, not like the dharma that protects the self. The true good king is at the level of the king, abandoning the ten evil cycles, protecting the self and upholding the Dharma, and facing the false ca-sa. Not destroying the teachings of self, the three vehicles of dharma, the cause, the universal hearing and writings, offerings, protecting the teachings of the dharma, not damaging the Three Jewels, not obstructing before ca-sa, always glassy air, non-airy, blessings overcome immorality.
Lưỡng Túc Tôn. Xa lìa bật-sô ác, thân cận chỗ thánh hạnh. Chẳng ăn, dùng Tăng vật, mau chứng đại Bồ Đề. An lạc trong tam giới, đều do Tam Bảo sanh. Nên người cầu an lạc, thường cúng dường Tam Bảo. Bọn vua Chiên-đồ-la, cùng ác tăng kết đảng. Phạm lỗi với Tam Bảo, mau đọa ngục Vô Gián. Tội mười máy ép dầu, bằng tội một nhà thổ. Lập ra mười nhà thổ, bằng tội một tiệm rượu. Tội mở Ten wine shops, by setting up ten slaughterhouses, the crime is equal to that of a king and mandarin, practicing one evil practice. A good king, making offerings to all three vehicles, will become a sea of ​​merit throughout the Thiem Bodhisattva, and giving alms to the Buddha and Sangha, is not as big as protecting the Buddha's teachings, as big as fourteen continents, he is not as big as building a tower to worship the Buddha That person attains a mass of blessings, not equal to protecting the Buddha's teachings. Untying the bonds of Arhats, making offerings to the Buddha in all ways, and not hindering the Buddha's Dharma, that blessing is far superior. In a thousand kalpas, a wise person who diligently cultivates Samadhi and attains superior enlightenment is not as good as a good king who stays away from the ten evil realms, protects the Buddha's Dharma, and who wears the karma, does not blaspheme the three vehicles, as I have spoken, and does not blaspheme those who practice it one who preaches the Dharma, does not harm the Three Jewels, does not hinder those who become monks, is always respectful and neutral, and has incomparable blessings.

“It is difficult to tame the mind” (Able to subdue a mind that is difficult to tame): Tame your mind well. That mind is difficult to tame. You believed in Buddha, listened to two sutras, listened and immediately changed. However, greed is very difficult to control, more difficult to control than any other thing! There is a Dharma friend who says: "Whenever I sit still, there are so many false thoughts." It is through quiet meditation that you can recognize false thoughts. Without sitting still, how can you recognize false thoughts, because you are in false thoughts! To Dong Pha has a poem: "Hanh Khanh becomes cold, Trac becomes wind. Far near, high and high dikes are all different. Unconsciously, Lo Son's true face is blind, only fate is in the middle of the mountain" (Looking horizontally into a ridge, vertically into a peak. High, low, near and far, completely different. I don't know Lo Son's true face, because the body is still in this mountain). If you are in affliction, you will not see affliction. Because you practice Concentration, or listen to the sutras and compare them, like this is affliction, like that is affliction. If not, how will you know? Because after listening to the sutra, you sit still here and have false thoughts. After half an hour that false thought disappears, you move on to the false thought. Suppose you don't study Buddhism, don't do anything, then within half an hour, within twenty-four hours, you will be turned around by false thoughts. How can you recognize it? When I'm awake, I'm moved by delusional thoughts, but at night when I sleep, I'm still haunted by delusional thoughts. There's absolutely no time to control it! There are times when a great virtuous person cannot master it. Not yet a Bodhisattva ascending to the Bodhisattva level (at least having attained the First Stage), or the position of the Three Sages (Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications), there will also be times when he cannot master it!

Arahant has also cut off the Thoughts and Ordeals. When he does not enter Concentration, he cannot be the master. Why does He “sweat the body and wisdom” mean he has to burn this body? Regardless of whether he had supernatural powers, the upper part of his body caught fire, the lower part of his body gushed out water, eighteen magical powers changed, he burned himself, there was no longer this physical body, he had ended it, he truly entered Nirvana. When he reaches a certain level, he will undergo transformation, it's not that simple. If you study Arhats, [you will see] there are many types of Arhats, and there are also regressed (regressed) Arhats. He does not advance, does not save sentient beings, does not benefit the world. Before becoming a Buddha, if you have not yet reached the Eighth Bodhisattva Grounds, that is, the Unmoving Ground, you will not be able to retreat. Non-regression has Non-Regression Taste and Non-Regression Thought. Reciting Non-Regression is very difficult, understanding this principle is enough!

For all dharmas, one must know enough. “Cultivating the holy seed, you will become Two-Supported Venerable” (You need to know enough, that is the seed of the saint, will become Two-Supported Venerable): Mainly for greed, especially when we circulate in birth and death because of desire, that is, craving. That is the basis of our birth and death. “Stay away from evil bhikkhus, stay close to the holy place of conduct” (Stay away from evil bhikkhus, stay close to the holy ones): Stay close to good bhikshus, do not stay close to evil bhikshus. In the previous section, I told you not to differentiate. That is to say, when you make offerings, don't make distinctions. When you practice, you have to choose who is good and who is evil? If you have the power to convert evil people like the Bodhisattvas Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteshvara, and Ksitigarbha, they do not distinguish between good and evil, the more evil they are, the more they save that person. We don't have that power, ordinary people don't have that power, the Buddha immediately taught us: Be less close to those evil monks, be close to monks who are holy and worthy of respect.

Furthermore, do not use things that belong to the Sangha or Sangha [here referred to as the Sangha] in temples and shrines. Whenever the Sangha is mentioned, it is talking about the Sangha, the Sangha is not one person. One cannot be called a Sangha. Only those who become monks are called monks. [Speaking of Sangha], it must be three or more. “Monks” are belongings to the Sangha of three or more monks, please do not use them! If that's the case, you should be close to good friends, don't abuse things that belong to permanent residence, it will be very easy to achieve Bodhi. Since this is equivalent to not stealing, being close to good friends will be like respecting the Sangha. When you meet evil monks, you will be harmed, but when you make offerings to them, it is not because they are evil that you criticize them. Therefore, in the previous section, it was said many times, to respect the red kasaya, worn by that person, [so] you respect the Sangha of that person. Thus, in the three worlds, you can achieve peace, causing the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to arise, "often make offerings to the Three Jewels". That is Existence. The reason for Non-existence is because that person is not close to the Three Jewels, so Non-existence. In the next chapter is Existence, what that person has done is close to the Three Jewels; That's called Huu Y.

“Chien-dala kings, equal to the evil party, the Three Jewels have arisen too much, quickly fall into the Infinite Hell" (Chiefa kings, ganging up with evil monks, violating the Three Jewels, quickly falling into the Infinite Hell): A lot has been said in the previous section. Bhikkhus today still worship brothers; I have seen a lot. In India (Indonesia) and Singapore, there are a few people, all middle-aged, in their fifties or sixties. Bhikkhus currently still worship each other as brothers, do you say this is right or wrong? I think anyone who hears it will feel it's not right, it's called "pulling factions together". Those are evil Bhikkhus. They often commit crimes against Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and they will fall into hell very quickly!

In the previous section, it was said that “the ten crimes of wandering around are crimes, the most vile crimes of prostitution.TTrí are the ten crimes of sexual immorality, the first class of crimes of alcoholism are. The crime of ten oil presses is equal to the crime of one brothel. Opening ten brothels, the crime is equal to one tavern. Setting up ten taverns, the crime is equal to one slaughterhouse. Establishing ten slaughterhouses, the crime is equal to that of kings and mandarins, achieving one cycle of evil): The crime of a king of evil nature is equal to the sin of ten wine shops[90]. If you are a king, if you commit one crime, it will be equal to the crime of ten liquor stores. Because the king has great power, his crimes are also great. Cultivating great good deeds, creating great sins, "True and good kings are at the same level, promoting the dragon and self of the righteous dharma, making offerings to the three vehicles" (True good kings, flourishing Buddha's righteous dharma, making offerings to all three vehicles), without giving rise to the choice of the three vehicles, "will achieve the ocean of merit" (will achieve the ocean of merit), if such offerings are made, merit will be achieved very quickly.

“Seven treasures full of Thiem Bo Chau” (Seven treasures filled throughout Nam Thiem Bo Chau): Seven treasures filled Thiem Bo Chau, this was mentioned in the previous section. “Offering alms to the Buddha and the Sangha brings blessings to the Sangha, not equal to protecting the Buddha Dharma” (Offering alms to the Buddha and Sangha, gaining a mass of blessings, is not equal to protecting the Dharma): Providing material things is limited and also has an end. If you uphold the Buddha Dharma, it will cause many people to attain salvation in the future, and your merit will be immeasurable. “Buddha, The creates a temple, the amount is equal to fourteen continents” (Because Buddha and Sangha build a temple, the amount is equal to fourteen continents): This meaning has already been said in the previous section. Here is repetition. “The accumulation of blessings is not as great as protecting the Buddha Dharma” (They gain a lot of blessings, but it is not as great as protecting the Buddha Dharma), the merit is not as great as protecting the Buddha Dharma. “Create a Buddha as good as three thousand worlds, the amount of which is equal to the three thousand worlds” (Create a tower to worship the Buddha, the amount is equal to the great thousand world): Creating a very large pagoda, the pagoda is as big as the three thousand great thousand worlds, the blessings achieved are also “not as good as protecting the Buddha's dharma” (not equal to protecting the Buddha's dharma). “Unleashing the Arahant's blessings, cultivating and making offerings, not obstructing the true Dharma, the blessing will overcome the stubbornness” (Untying the Arhats, making offerings to all kinds of things, not obstructing the Buddha's Dharma, that blessing is far superior): This is also the protector of the dharma. In the previous section, it was said that someone tied up Arhats, or wanted to persecute them, so he saved them and freed them. After that, he also made offerings to them in all kinds of ways. That merit is still not equal to the merit of upholding the Dharma, the merit of not obstructing the Dharma. The merits of the latter far surpass the merits of the former.

“For thousands of kalpas, wise people need to cultivate Concentration, which gives birth to superior wisdom, not like protecting the ego” (In a thousand kalpas, a wise person diligently cultivates Concentration, giving birth to superior wisdom, not equal to protecting Buddha Dharma): Personally, you practice for a thousand lifetimes, even if you have wisdom, cultivating Concentration like that gives birth to enlightenment. victorious, but still not as great as my merit of upholding the Dharma. That's just for yourself, not for the benefit of sentient beings. As long as the Buddha Dharma eye exists, all sentient beings in the future will attain salvation, so everyone must propagate the Buddha Dharma, and not make excuses: "I don't have education, I don't know how to propagate it." You advise others to recite Amitābha Buddha's verse, that is to propagate Buddhism. You tell others a set of the Vajra Prajna Paramita Sutra, a set of the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, or a set of the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma. They hear these names, all of which are to propagate Buddha Dharma and sow good roots. [Therefore], everyone can propagate the Dharma.

Therefore, disciples of the Three Jewels, bhikkhus, bhiksunis, upasakas, and upasakas should all propagate the Dharma. We even often preach the Three Refuges to them in front of animals. You say: "Does it understand or not?" Don't think it doesn't understand! If you really talk to it, it will be saved. The smaller the living beings, the more ants there are. Doesn't your house have cockroaches? Isn't there a mouse? Don't hurt them, tell them the Three Refuges. You say: "It's not right for you to stay here. I will move you. Please leave. Because I can hurt you very easily. If others see that you are not pure, they will beat you to death. Please leave." You say the Three Refuges, preach the Dharma to them, try it! Don't give rise to afflictions, don't hurt them.

“The true good king, far from the ten evil wheels, protects the true Dharma of self, facing the false ca-sa” (The true good king, far away from the ten evil wheels, protects my dharma, and the one who wears the saffron): Not only protect the dharma, but also protect the Sangha, do not blaspheme the three vehicles as I have spoken and those who practice the three dharmas redundant. “Hearing all the texts, making offerings, protecting those who preach the Dharma” (Hearing all over, making offerings, protecting those who preach the Dharma): Makes you protect those who preach the Dharma. Don't say anything else, just recite Amitābha Buddha's verse and it's good advice to everyone. But you should never slander. All the dharmas spoken by the Buddha and the words the Buddha taught are not blasphemous. The Sravaka Dharma, the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, the Bodhisattva Dharma, as long as it is any Dharma spoken by the Buddha, you will not slander it. As for the protector, that is, the person who preaches the Dharma, you must listen completely. As long as that person speaks Buddha Dharma, he will often listen, and he will also have to make offerings. Protect those who preach the Dharma, or whoever preaches the Dharma, must protect that person.

Next, do not damage anything belonging to the Three Jewels. You should not destroy things belonging to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. “Often respecting dharma weapons, non-dharma weapons” (Usually respecting dharma weapons and non-dharma weapons): Being dharma tools is the same, but not being dharma tools is the same. The Dharma weapon is a pure Bhikkhu, the non-Pharma weapon (not a Dharma weapon) is a Bhikkhu who breaks the precepts, or is pure near men, pure near women. Whoever accepts the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, that person is pure. After receiving the Three Refuges, [the ordination teacher] will tell you: “If you take refuge in Buddha, you will not take refuge in pagans, heavenly demons, etc.…”, you will not bow to ghosts and spirits, or pray to ghosts and spirits for blessings. In any situation, don't do it, even if you lose your life [don't do it]. After taking refuge in Buddha, do not take refuge in ghosts or ghosts. Take the Three Refuges, take refuge in the Dharma, and do not take refuge in the books of pagans. Take refuge in the Sangha, do not take refuge in the evil groups of pagans. That is called the pure Tam Quy. There are many people who are not pure in the Three Refuges, not to mention the Five Precepts and the Bodhisattva Precepts! The Three Refuges are not pure, you should pay attention to this. That is a very important thing.

“Blessed victory over immorality” (Blessed victory, incomparable): If we can do so, regardless of purity or not, we will treat them equally. Not even pointing out their mistakes. How do we know if they are pure or not? Because you listen to other people's discussions, or you participate in discussions, you will know whether they are pure or not. Use the holy teachings to evaluate them. There's no need to do that, they have their retribution!

(Sutra) Like the five suns are pure and clear, the great ocean is dry exhausted. Nvoid protects the ego, can dry up afflictions. Just as the wind and disaster arise, all the mountain stages disperse. Nvoid protects the self and can eliminate afflictions. Like the beginning of a water disaster, the great earth phase is destroyed. Such as protecting the ego, the ability to destroy and non-love results. Like the wish-fulfilling jewel, according to one's wishes, the three vehicle dharmas can be fulfilled, and can fulfill the wishes of sentient beings. Such as enlightenment, attaining peace, eliminating poverty, attaining wealth and happiness. Nthe false enlightenment of Buddha Dharma, eliminating Orcism, achieving Bodhi. Like fifteen nights of the moon, illuminating the entire void. Like the guardian of the dharma, the wisdom pearl of the dharma realm. Like nothingness and equality, the heron has no form. That same year, he followed Dharma Master Dai Dung from Sichuan to Tibet to study Buddhism. From 1928 to 1940, the Master went to Tibet many times to study Tantric Dharma. Following the teachings of Master Khang Tat (Khangsar Rinpoche), he received the Dharma transmission and became the 28th generation son of the Gelugpa Sect. After successfully studying, the Master returned to Chengdu, established Can Tu Pagoda to specialize in translating and publishing Buddhist scriptures, trained many disciples, and was honored with the beautiful title "Tong Kha Ba reincarnated". After the establishment of Communist China, he was forced to serve as vice president of the Chinese Buddhist Association, National Assembly delegate, and member of the administrative committee of Shanxi province. In 1966, Mao Zedong launched the Cultural Revolution. At that time, the Master was at Thien Tai cave in Ngu Dai Son. He was charged by the Red Guards with spreading reactionary and revisionist ideas, seducing the masses, as well as a series of crimes against the government. He was humiliated and brutally tortured by the Red Guards, but he still endured it, believing that they were eliminating his karma. All monks in the pagoda were forced to return to secular life, or concentrate on re-education at the pagoda, if they refused to leave. Every day, monks were forbidden to chant, had to study politics constantly, and their food rations were cruelly reduced. On the evening of December 31, 1966, the Master told his students that it was time for him to leave because the fate of salvation had ended. That night, the Master asked Dharma Master Thanh Tong to ask him to take a day off from studying politics tomorrow because he was not feeling well. At dawn on January 1, 1967, Dharma Master Tham Duc entered his room and invited him to have breakfast porridge. He saw the Dharma Master wearing robes, sitting cross-legged, and had passed away at the age of 81. The Master's remains were buried at Thanh Luong Kieu in Ngu Dai Mountain. It was not until 1973 that his remains were brought back to be buried at Bao Thap mountain and a worship tower was built.

[86] In the Shurangama mantra, at the end of the fifth assembly, after the word Tadyathā is “san, a na le, bhi sera de, pedestal ra tat ra ra da ri, ban da, ban da ear, ta dh ra ban ni pollen, tiger rose do ro cancer pollen, sa ba ha” (Auṃ, anale, viśade, vīra vajra-dhare, bandha, bandhane vajra-paṇe, phaṭ phaṭ hūṃ trūṃ phaṭ svāha). But the Shurangama mantra is said to be Siddhartha Bat Dat Ra because when saying this mantra, the Buddha emitted light from the humerus on the top of his head and said it, and this mantra has the full name of the Great Buddha Emphasis on Shurangama. Siddhartha Bat Dat Ra translated means Dai Bach Tan Cai (white parasol) made up of two words Sita (white) and Atapatrā (umbrella, parasol). In Esoteric Buddhism, this is a Buddha's Name, the specific body of Buddha's wisdom, with the name Great White Buddha's Name (Uṣṇīṣasitātapatrā). This person is especially revered in the Buddhist Tradition. This Buddha's Name is often shaped as a female Bodhisattva, with three faces and six arms, or three faces and eight arms, sometimes up to a thousand arms, a thousand faces, a thousand legs, and a million eyes, to strongly represent the destruction of afflictions in the three thousand great thousand worlds. Typical Dharma objects are the Dharma wheel and the white parasol. Commentators believe that the five assembly of the Shurangama mantra corresponds to the five wisdoms of the Tathagata, and all the mantras before the word Dat-die-datha-tha are the reverential praise of the names of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, vajra, kings of light, dharma protectors, and demons and gods in each of the Five Orders.
